Schemes: PMKVY (outcome-based and certification, with reward money), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS, 2016), the SANKALP programme with World Bank help, STRIVE for ITIs, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKK), Udaan and Himayat for J&K, Nai Manzil for minorities, and the Skill Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion (SANKALP). The 2009 policy targeted 500 million skilled people by 2022, while the 2015 policy reset this as 400 million. The Skill India Digital Hub and the Skill India portal give digital access. UPSC may ask about the founding year, ministry, features of each scheme, the PPP shareholding in NSDC, the NSQF levels, and the related bodies' roles.

ocr: Which one of the following statements is not correct ? 104. (a) In India, Right to Education seeks to ensure that every child with special needs is’ provided with quality education. (b) All children are provided free textbooks up to Class V under the Right to Education Act. 105. (c) Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat Scheme focuses on foundational learning. (d) Under Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan, children of age group 6 — 18 years are motivated to engage in science and mathematics. =e) Which of the following is not a Vector Image Storage Format ? (a) CGM (b) SUG (c) JPEG (dq) SWF
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The RTE Act, 2009 came into force on 1 April 2010 after the 86th Constitutional Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A, which makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6-14 years. Elementary education means Classes I-VIII, so free entitlements (textbooks, uniforms, stationery under various state schemes, no fees, no capitation) apply up to Class VIII, not Class V. Statement (b) is therefore wrong because it restricts the entitlement to Class V. The Act also requires 25% reservation for economically weaker and disadvantaged children in private unaided schools (Section 12(1)(c)), bans detention and expulsion until completion of elementary education, bans corporal punishment, and sets pupil-teacher ratios. Children with disabilities are covered by the 2012 amendment, and Samagra Shiksha supports inclusive education for children with special needs (CWSN), which supports (a). Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat is the sub-programme for early reading, writing and arithmetic (foundational learning) in Classes I-II, which supports (c). Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (2015) motivates children aged 6-18 towards science, mathematics and technology, which supports (d). Elimination: only (b) misstates the Class limit.
explanations: Correct statement. The RTE framework and Samagra Shiksha provide for inclusive, quality education for children with special needs (CWSN), so it is not the answer.
Incorrect statement, hence the answer. Free education, including textbooks, under RTE extends to all of elementary education, Classes I-VIII (ages 6-14), not just up to Class V.
Correct statement. Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat, a sub-programme of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, focuses on foundational learning: early reading, writing and mathematics in Classes I-II.
Correct statement. Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (RAA) targets children aged 6-18 years to build interest in science and mathematics, so it is not the answer.
keyfact: RTE (Art. 21A) guarantees free and compulsory education for ages 6-14, i.e. Classes I-VIII, not just up to Class V.
option_notes: Inclusive education for CWSN: RTE (amended 2012) treats children with disabilities as children with disadvantage and allows home-based education for severe disabilities. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 guarantees inclusive education and a 5% reservation in higher education. Samagra Shiksha (2018) integrates SSA, RMSA and teacher education and has a dedicated inclusive education component with aids, appliances, therapy and resource teachers for CWSN.

Free textbooks: under RTE Section 3, children aged 6-14 can study free in a government or aided school until Class VIII, with no fee or charge. Section 2(d) and Section 8 specify free entitlements such as books and uniforms. Elementary education covers Classes I-VIII, so Class V is wrongly given as the limit in this option. Primary means Classes I-V, upper primary VI-VIII.

Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat (PBBB) was launched in 2014 as a sub-programme of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan for children in Classes I and II. It has two parts: early reading and writing, and early mathematics. It aims to build foundational literacy and numeracy. It was later followed by the NIPUN Bharat Mission (2021) under NEP 2020, which targets foundational literacy and numeracy by Grade 3 by 2026-27.

Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (RAA) was launched in 2015 by MHRD (now Ministry of Education). It is meant to motivate and engage children aged 6-18 in science, mathematics and technology through activities, using both school and community resources. Its stated aim is to build a scientific temperament, make learning fun, and encourage observation, experimentation and application rather than rote learning.
related: Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment (2002), makes education a Fundamental Right for ages 6-14.
RTE Act, 2009 came into force on 1 April 2010.
RTE Section 12(1)(c): 25% reservation for EWS and disadvantaged children in private unaided schools.
Elementary education = Classes I-VIII; primary = I-V; upper primary = VI-VIII.
Article 51A(k) makes it a parental duty to educate children aged 6-14.
Padhe Bharat Badhe Bharat focuses on foundational learning in Classes I-II.
Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (2015) covers ages 6-18 for science and maths.
NEP 2020 introduced the 5+3+3+4 school structure.
summary: The answer is (b). The Right to Education Act, 2009 guarantees free and compulsory education for ages 6-14 (Classes I-VIII), not free textbooks only up to Class V. Section 3 entitles every child to free elementary education, which covers Classes I-VIII, and Section 8 obliges the appropriate government to provide it. The other three statements are correct.
topic_notes: Right to Education: the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 inserted Article 21A (free and compulsory education for ages 6-14), changed Article 45 to early childhood care for children under 6, and added Article 51A(k), a fundamental duty of parents to provide education opportunities to children aged 6-14. The RTE Act was passed in 2009 and came into force on 1 April 2010. Main features: neighbourhood schools, no screening or capitation fee, no detention or expulsion up to Class VIII, a prohibition on physical punishment and mental harassment, 25% reservation for disadvantaged and EWS children in private unaided schools with reimbursement by the state, a pupil-teacher ratio of 30:1 for primary and 35:1 for upper primary, and School Management Committees with parents as members. Teachers need minimum qualifications (TET). Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation was prescribed. The 2019 amendment removed the no-detention policy up to Class VIII, allowing states to hold back students after re-examination in Classes V and VIII. Related schemes: Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (2001), Mid-Day Meal (now PM POSHAN), RMSA (2009), Samagra Shiksha (2018), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015), PM SHRI schools, NIPUN Bharat (2021), DIKSHA platform and NEP 2020, which proposes the 5+3+3+4 structure and extends RTE coverage from age 3 to 18 as a goal. Possible future angles: Article numbers, age groups, reservation percentages, scheme launch years and the ministry responsible.

question: The equivalent decimal value of the product of two binary numbers 11111 and 1010 is:
subject: Computers
detail: To find the decimal value of a product of binary numbers, convert each to decimal and multiply, or multiply in binary and then convert. 11111 (binary) = 16+8+4+2+1 = 31, which is also 2^5 − 1. 1010 (binary) = 8+2 = 10. The product is 31 × 10 = 310. Cross-check by binary multiplication: 11111 × 1010 = 11111×1000 + 11111×10 = 11111000 + 111110 = 100110110. Reading this in decimal weights: 256+32+16+4+2 = 310. Hence 310 is correct. Elimination: 300 is 30×10, which comes from wrongly reading 11111 as 30. 301 and 309 are near-miss values that no standard error produces. Only 310 matches. A useful shortcut is that a string of n ones equals 2^n − 1, so 11111 = 31. Multiplying by 1010 (decimal 10) is straightforward. Note that the provided official-key text reads 'b or b or c', which is ambiguous. The arithmetic here clearly points to 310, which is option (c).
explanations: (a) 300 is wrong. It would result from treating 11111 as 30 instead of 31.
(b) 301 is wrong. It does not equal 31 × 10, and the key text is ambiguous between b and c. Direct computation does not support 301.
(c) 310 is correct. 31 × 10 = 310, and the binary product 100110110 also converts to 310.
(d) 309 is wrong. It is one less than 310 and has no basis in the calculation.
keyfact: 11111₂ = 31 and 1010₂ = 10, so the product is 310 (binary 100110110), option (c).
option_notes: 300 in decimal is 100101100 in binary (256+32+8+4). It is a round number and a distractor here, equal to 30×10. It would be the answer if the first number were 11110 (30). In number-system questions, off-by-one errors in converting strings of ones are the typical trap that produces values like this.

301 in decimal is 100101101 in binary (256+32+8+4+1). It is an odd number, but the product of 31 and 10 must be even, since 1010 ends in 0 and so the product ends in binary 0. This parity check alone eliminates 301 and 309 quickly.

310 in decimal is 100110110 in binary (256+32+16+4+2). It equals 31×10, where 31 = 2^5−1 = 11111 in binary and 10 = 1010 in binary. It is an even number, consistent with the multiplier ending in 0 in binary. It is the correct result of the multiplication asked.
309 in decimal is 100110101 in binary (256+32+16+4+1). It is odd, so it cannot be a multiple of binary 1010, which is even. It is a distractor one less than the correct answer, 310.
related: A string of n ones in binary equals 2^n − 1.
Binary 1010 = decimal 10; binary 1111 = decimal 15.
Hexadecimal uses digits 0-9 and letters A-F, with F = 15.
1 byte = 8 bits; 1 nibble = 4 bits.
Binary 1+1 = 10 (sum 0, carry 1).
2's complement is used to represent negative numbers in computers.
NAND and NOR are universal logic gates.
Binary multiplication by 10 (binary 2) shifts the digits left by one place.
summary: The answer is (c) 310. 11111 in binary is 31 and 1010 is 10, so the product is 31 × 10 = 310 in decimal. The note says the official answer is given as 'b or b or c', but the computation gives 310, which is option (c).
topic_notes: Number systems in computers are a standard topic. Binary is base 2 and uses the digits 0 and 1. Octal is base 8, decimal is base 10, and hexadecimal is base 16, using 0-9 and A-F. To convert binary to decimal, add the powers of 2 for each position that holds a 1. To convert decimal to binary, divide repeatedly by 2 and read the remainders from bottom to top. Octal groups binary digits in threes and hexadecimal groups them in fours. Binary addition rules: 0+0=0, 0+1=1, 1+0=1, and 1+1=10 (carry 1). Binary multiplication works like decimal long multiplication, but with only 0 and 1 partial products. Subtraction commonly uses 1's complement or 2's complement. 2's complement is the standard way computers represent negative numbers. A string of n ones equals 2^n − 1 (for example 1111 = 15 and 11111 = 31). A bit is a single binary digit, a nibble is 4 bits, and a byte is 8 bits. ASCII uses 7 bits (128 characters), extended ASCII uses 8 bits, and Unicode supports a much larger set of characters. Hexadecimal FF = 255 and binary 1111 1111 = 255. Likely questions are: convert a number between bases, binary arithmetic, complement representation, the number of bits needed to represent a value, and the logic gates (AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR). NAND and NOR are called universal gates.

question: Which one of the following is a small, fast and expensive memory that stores the copies of the data that needs to be accessed frequently from the main memory ?
subject: Computers
detail: Cache memory works on the principle of locality of reference. Temporal locality means recently used data is likely to be used again. Spatial locality means data near recently used data is likely to be needed soon. When the CPU needs data, it first checks the cache. If the data is found, it is a cache hit. If not, it is a cache miss, and the data is fetched from RAM and copied into the cache. Cache is built from SRAM, which is faster but costlier than the DRAM used for main memory. The hierarchy runs from registers, then L1, L2 and L3 cache, then main memory (RAM), then secondary storage (HDD/SSD), then tertiary or archival storage. Speed and cost per bit fall as you move down, while capacity rises. Elimination: magnetic tape, CD-ROM and secondary memory are all slow, cheap, high-capacity, non-volatile storage devices. None of them is a small, fast, expensive memory holding copies of main-memory data. Only cache fits the description.
explanations: Wrong. Magnetic tape is a sequential-access, very slow, cheap, high-capacity medium used for backup and archival. It does not hold copies of frequently used RAM data.
Wrong. CD-ROM is a read-only optical disc with slow access and fixed content. It is neither small and fast nor expensive memory.
Correct. Cache memory is a small, high-speed, costly SRAM-based memory between the CPU and RAM. It stores copies of frequently accessed data and instructions from main memory.
Wrong. Secondary memory (HDD, SSD, optical discs, tape) is large, slower, cheaper and non-volatile. It is used for permanent storage, not as a fast copy of main memory.
keyfact: Cache memory = small, fast, costly SRAM between CPU and RAM that stores copies of frequently used data.
option_notes: Magnetic tape is a sequential-access storage medium made of magnetically coated plastic tape on reels or cartridges. It is cheap per bit, has very large capacity and is slow because data must be read in order. It is used for backups, archives and data warehousing (for example LTO cartridges). It is non-volatile and counts as secondary or tertiary storage.

CD-ROM (Compact Disc Read-Only Memory) is an optical disc whose data is written during manufacture and cannot be altered by the user. Capacity is about 650-700 MB. A laser reads it. Variants are CD-R (write once) and CD-RW (rewritable). DVD and Blu-ray are higher-capacity successors. It is a secondary storage device with slow access.

Cache memory is a small, very fast, expensive memory built from SRAM. It sits between the CPU and RAM and stores frequently used data and instructions. L1 is the smallest and fastest and is on the CPU core. L2 is larger, and L3 is shared among cores. Terms: hit, miss, hit ratio, write-through, write-back. It is volatile and not directly addressable by programmers.

Secondary memory is non-volatile auxiliary storage that holds programs and data permanently. Examples are hard disks, SSDs, pen drives, optical discs and magnetic tape. It has a large capacity, lower cost per bit and slower access than RAM. The CPU does not access it directly. Data is first loaded into main memory before processing.
related: Cache is built from SRAM; main memory (RAM) is built from DRAM.
Fastest memory in a computer: CPU registers, then cache.
Cache hit means the data is found in the cache; a miss means it must be fetched from RAM.
Cache mapping types: direct, fully associative, set-associative.
RAM is volatile; ROM, HDD, SSD and tape are non-volatile.
EPROM is erased by UV light; EEPROM is erased electrically; flash is a form of EEPROM.
Virtual memory uses part of the hard disk as an extension of RAM.
Magnetic tape is sequential access; disks are direct access.
summary: The answer is (c) Cache memory. Cache is a small, very fast and costly memory placed between the CPU and main memory (RAM) that holds copies of frequently accessed data and instructions, which reduces average access time.
topic_notes:
Computer memory is organised as a hierarchy that trades off speed, cost and capacity. At the top are CPU registers, which are the fastest and smallest. Next are cache memory (L1, L2, L3) built from SRAM, then main memory or primary memory (RAM), built from DRAM. Below these is secondary storage (HDD, SSD, optical discs, tape), followed by tertiary or offline storage. Moving down the hierarchy, access time and cost per bit rise toward the top while capacity grows toward the bottom.

Primary memory includes RAM and ROM. RAM is volatile and read-write. It comes as SRAM (faster, no refresh, used in cache) and DRAM (needs periodic refresh, used as main memory). ROM is non-volatile and comes as PROM, EPROM (erased with UV light) and EEPROM (electrically erasable). Flash memory is a type of EEPROM. Virtual memory uses disk space to extend RAM, and paging and swapping are involved. Units of storage: bit, nibble (4 bits), byte (8 bits), KB, MB, GB, TB, PB.

Cache mapping techniques are direct, associative and set-associative. Replacement policies include LRU, FIFO and random. Write policies are write-through and write-back. Locality of reference, both temporal and spatial, is the principle that makes caching effective. Other angles UPSC could ask about include volatile versus non-volatile memory, access methods (sequential, direct, random), the order of memory by speed, buffer versus cache, and registers such as the program counter, accumulator and instruction register.

ocr: In mesh technology, if we have 4 computers, how many links must be there ? (a) 2 (b) 4 ea (d) 6 MS-Access is used to : (a). Create a database (b) Edit graphics (c) Publish documents in PDF file (d) Create a document
subject: Computers
detail: In a full mesh topology every device has a dedicated point-to-point link to every other device. For n devices the number of links is n(n-1)/2, and each device needs n-1 I/O ports. With n = 4, links = 4×3/2 = 6, and each computer has 3 ports. Check by counting pairs: A-B, A-C, A-D, B-C, B-D, C-D, which gives 6. Elimination: 2 links could not even connect 4 nodes into one network. 4 links can form a ring, which is a ring topology and not a full mesh. 5 links would leave one pair unconnected, which is a partial mesh. Only 6 gives the full mesh the question describes. The same formula gives 3 links for 3 nodes, 10 for 5 nodes, 15 for 6 nodes and 45 for 10 nodes. Advantages of mesh are dedicated links with no traffic problems, robustness, privacy and easy fault identification. Disadvantages are heavy cabling, high cost and complex installation, so full mesh is used mainly in backbone networks. In the second question in the image, MS-Access is a relational DBMS in the Microsoft Office suite, so (a) is correct. Because neither question in the image has (c) as its correct answer, the key given should be checked.
explanations: (a) 2 links: wrong. Two links can connect at most 3 computers in a line, so 4 computers cannot even be fully connected in a network.
(b) 4 links: wrong. Four links would form a ring or a similar partial layout, not a full mesh, where every pair is directly connected.

(c) 5 links: does not satisfy n(n-1)/2, which gives 6. It would leave one pair unconnected (a partial mesh). This is the option the supplied key marks as correct, but it conflicts with the standard formula. Option (c) is also incorrect in the MS-Access question shown.
(d) 6 links: correct by the formula 4×3/2 = 6, and by listing the six pairs AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD. Every computer connects directly to the other three.
keyfact: Full mesh links = n(n-1)/2, so 4 computers need 6 links (option d). The supplied key (c) conflicts with this, so verify it.
option_notes: Option (a), 2 links, is the link count for a minimal line of 3 nodes. In a bus or line arrangement, n nodes need n-1 links, so 2 links connect only 3 nodes. It is not a mesh. A tree or star with 4 nodes needs 3 links. Students should remember n-1 links for a star, bus (segments) or tree, versus n(n-1)/2 for a full mesh.

Option (b), 4 links, equals the number of links in a ring topology with 4 nodes, because a ring has n links. Each device connects to exactly two neighbours and data travels in one direction or both. A single break can disrupt a simple ring, which is why FDDI and Token Ring used dual or controlled rings. A ring is not a mesh.

Option (c), 5 links, is what a partial mesh with 4 nodes could look like, with some but not all pairs directly connected. For example, a ring plus one diagonal gives 5 links. In a partial mesh only some nodes have multiple connections, giving some redundancy at lower cost than a full mesh. It does not satisfy the full-mesh formula.

Option (d), 6 links, is the full-mesh count for 4 nodes, from n(n-1)/2 = 6. Each node has 3 dedicated links and needs 3 ports. A full mesh gives dedicated, private, robust connections and easy fault isolation, but cabling and cost grow quadratically. It is used in backbone and critical networks, for example WAN routers.
related: Full mesh links = n(n-1)/2; ports per device = n-1.
Star topology has a central hub or switch as its single point of failure.
Ring topology with n nodes has n links.
Bus topology uses a single backbone cable with terminators at both ends.
MS-Access is a relational DBMS; its file extension is .accdb.
Token Ring is IEEE 802.5; Ethernet is IEEE 802.3.
Partial mesh connects only some nodes redundantly, so it costs less than a full mesh.
summary: For a full mesh of 4 computers the number of links is n(n-1)/2 = 4×3/2 = 6, which is option (d). The supplied official key (c) = 5 does not match this formula, and option (c) is also wrong for the MS-Access question in the image (the answer there is (a) Create a database). The key may refer to a different question number or a different paper version, so please verify it against the official answer sheet.
topic_notes: Network topology is the physical or logical arrangement of devices in a network. Bus: a single backbone cable with terminators; it is cheap, but a backbone fault brings the network down and collisions are common. Star: every node connects to a central hub or switch; it is easy to manage and a single cable failure affects only one node, but the central device is a single point of failure. Ring: each node connects to two neighbours, giving n links; a token is often used (Token Ring, IEEE 802.5). Mesh: every node connects to every other, with n(n-1)/2 links and n-1 ports per node; it is the most reliable and the costliest. Partial mesh connects only some nodes redundantly. Tree (hierarchical) combines star and bus. Hybrid combines two or more topologies. Quick numbers for a full mesh: 3 nodes need 3 links, 4 need 6, 5 need 10, 6 need 15, 8 need 28 and 10 need 45. LAN covers a building or campus, MAN a city and WAN a country or the world. Ethernet is IEEE 802.3 and Wi-Fi is IEEE 802.11. MS-Access, from the second question, is Microsoft's desktop relational DBMS. It is used to create databases with tables, queries, forms and reports, and its files have the extension .accdb (earlier .mdb). Other Office tools are Word for documents, Excel for spreadsheets, PowerPoint for presentations and Publisher for publishing. Adobe Acrobat creates PDFs, and graphics editing is done in Paint or Photoshop. Likely future angles are the formula for mesh links, ports per node in a mesh, the topology with a single point of failure (star) and the topology that uses a token (ring).

note: This image may contain more than one question. Answer Q104.
ocr: In mesh technology, if we have 4 computers, how many links must be there ? (a) 2 (b) 4 ea (d) 6 MS-Access is used to : (a). Create a database (b) Edit graphics (c) Publish documents in PDF file (d) Create a document
subject: Computers
detail: Mesh topology is a network layout in which each device has a dedicated point-to-point link to every other device. For n devices, the number of links is the number of distinct pairs, n(n-1)/2. For 4 computers the pairs are AB, AC, AD, BC, BD and CD, which makes 6 links. Each device also needs n-1 = 3 I/O ports. The formula for duplex links is n(n-1)/2. If the links were counted as simplex (one direction each), it would be n(n-1) = 12 channels. Advantages of mesh are that it needs no traffic sharing, is robust (one link failing does not bring the network down), is private and secure, and makes faults easy to identify. Disadvantages are heavy cabling, many ports, and high cost and installation complexity. That is why full mesh is used mainly in backbones, and partial mesh is common elsewhere. Elimination: 2 and 4 are too few. Even a ring of 4 computers has 4 links, and a mesh needs more than a ring. 5 would be a partial mesh and does not connect every pair. Only 6 covers all pairs.
explanations: (a) 2 is wrong. Two links cannot connect four computers, let alone join every pair directly.
(b) 4 is wrong. Four links is the count for a ring topology of 4 nodes, which is not a full mesh. Each node would then have only 2 connections.
(c) 5 is wrong. It would be a partial mesh. A full mesh with 4 nodes needs 4C2 = 6 links, so one pair would be left unlinked.
(d) 6 is correct. n(n-1)/2 = 4×3/2 = 6, so each of the 6 computer pairs has a dedicated link.
keyfact: Full mesh with n nodes has n(n-1)/2 links, so 4 computers need 6 links.
option_notes: 2 links: this is the number of links in a bus or line of just 3 devices, or the minimum links needed to connect 3 nodes in a chain. Each link is a point-to-point cable between two devices. A network of 4 computers needs at least 3 links to be connected at all (a tree or line). Two links cannot join 4 nodes, so this value has no standard topology meaning here.

4 links: this is the link count of a ring topology with 4 nodes, since a ring has n links. In a ring each device connects to exactly two neighbours and data travels in one direction or both. It is also the number of cables in a star topology of 4 leaf nodes with a central hub. Ring and star are cheaper than mesh but depend on one path or on the hub.

5 links: this would be a partial mesh with 4 nodes, which is a full mesh (6 links) with one link missing. Partial mesh connects some nodes to all others and other nodes only to a few. It is a compromise between the cost of full mesh and its reliability, and it is used in WAN backbones and the Internet. It does not satisfy the 'must be' condition for a full mesh.

6 links: this is the full mesh count for 4 devices, n(n-1)/2 = 6. Each node has n-1 = 3 ports. Full mesh gives dedicated, secure, fault-tolerant links but is costly. Examples include backbone networks and wireless mesh networks. The count grows quickly: 5 nodes need 10 links, 6 nodes need 15, and 10 nodes need 45.
related: Full mesh links = n(n-1)/2; each device needs n-1 ports.
Star topology uses a central hub or switch, and failure of the hub fails the network.
Ring topology of n nodes has n links.
Bus topology uses a single backbone cable with terminators at both ends.
Partial mesh is used in the Internet and WAN backbones.
Tree topology is a hierarchy of star networks connected to a bus backbone.
10 nodes in a full mesh need 45 links and 9 ports each.
MS-Access (the second question in the image) is a DBMS used to create databases.
summary: The answer is (d) 6. In a full mesh topology every computer is directly connected to every other computer, so the number of links is n(n-1)/2. For n = 4 this gives 4×3/2 = 6.
topic_notes:
Network topology is the physical or logical arrangement of devices in a network. The main types are bus, ring, star, mesh, tree and hybrid.

Bus: all devices share a single backbone cable. It is cheap, but a break in the backbone fails the whole network and collisions are common. It needs terminators.

Ring: each node connects to two neighbours. Data flows in one direction, as in Token Ring, or in two directions, as in FDDI. A single break can stop the network unless the ring is dual.

Star: all nodes connect to a central hub or switch. It is easy to add nodes and to find faults, but the hub is a single point of failure. It is the most common LAN layout (Ethernet). Links = n-1 for n-1 end nodes.

Mesh: full mesh needs n(n-1)/2 links and n-1 ports per device. Partial mesh needs fewer links. Mesh offers high reliability and privacy, and is costly and complex to install.

Tree: a hierarchy of star networks joined on a bus. Hybrid: a combination of two or more topologies.

Other angles UPSC may ask: the number of cables in each topology, the failure impact of each topology, which topology is used in LANs, the difference between physical and logical topology, and the role of hubs, switches and routers. Links are also counted differently for simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex. For full-duplex mesh the link count stays n(n-1)/2. For simplex channels it is n(n-1).

note: This image may contain more than one question. Answer Q105.
ocr: In mesh technology, if we have 4 computers, how many links must be there ? (a) 2 (b) 4 ea (d) 6 MS-Access is used to : (a). Create a database (b) Edit graphics (c) Publish documents in PDF file (d) Create a document
subject: Computers
detail: Microsoft Access is a desktop RDBMS from Microsoft, first released in 1992 and bundled with the Professional and higher editions of Microsoft Office. It stores data in related tables made of rows (records) and columns (fields). Tables are linked through primary and foreign keys. The main objects are Tables (store data), Queries (retrieve or modify data, usually with SQL), Forms (data entry and display), Reports (formatted printed output) and Macros/Modules (automation, with VBA). Access databases are saved as .accdb files (the older format is .mdb). Access suits small and medium databases for a single user or a small workgroup. Elimination: editing graphics is done with Paint, Photoshop or CorelDRAW, so (b) is wrong. Publishing PDF documents is done with Adobe Acrobat, or with Word and Publisher's 'Save as PDF' export, so (c) is wrong. Creating a document is the job of MS-Word, so (d) is wrong. Only (a) matches Access. Remember the Office mapping: Word = documents, Excel = spreadsheets, PowerPoint = presentations, Access = databases, Outlook = email.
explanations: Correct. MS-Access is a relational DBMS used to create, store, manage and query databases, and to build forms and reports on them.
Wrong. Editing graphics is done with image editors such as Paint, Photoshop or GIMP. Access is not a graphics tool.
Wrong. Access does not publish documents. PDFs are produced by Adobe Acrobat or by the export feature of Office applications. Access can export reports to PDF, but that is not its main purpose.
Wrong. Creating a document (letters, reports) is the function of a word processor such as MS-Word.
keyfact: MS-Access = Microsoft's RDBMS for creating and managing databases (.accdb); Word = documents, Excel = spreadsheets.
option_notes: Creating a database: a database is an organised collection of related data stored electronically. MS-Access is Microsoft's desktop RDBMS, using tables, queries, forms and reports. It uses SQL and the Jet/ACE database engine, and saves files as .accdb (from Access 2007) or .mdb (earlier). It is suited to small-scale and single-user applications. Large enterprise databases use Oracle, MySQL or SQL Server instead.

Editing graphics: this is done with image or graphics software. Raster editors include MS-Paint and Adobe Photoshop. Vector editors include CorelDRAW and Adobe Illustrator. Common formats are JPEG, PNG, GIF, BMP and SVG. In MS-Office, only limited picture formatting is possible, in Word and PowerPoint. This option does not describe Access.

Publishing documents in PDF: PDF (Portable Document Format) was created by Adobe in 1993 and is now an ISO standard (ISO 32000). It keeps the layout the same on any device. It is created or edited with Adobe Acrobat, and Office programs can export to it through 'Save As' or 'Export'. MS-Publisher is Microsoft's desktop publishing tool. None of this is the main purpose of Access.

Creating a document: this is the function of word-processing software, mainly MS-Word, whose files have the extension .docx (earlier .doc). Other word processors are Google Docs, LibreOffice Writer and WordPad. Word handles typing, formatting, mail merge and templates. It is not a database tool, so it is not the use of Access.
related: MS-Access is an RDBMS; its default file extension is .accdb (older .mdb).
A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a table and cannot be null or duplicate.
Access objects: Tables, Queries, Forms, Reports, Macros, Modules.
MS-Excel is for spreadsheets (.xlsx); MS-Word for documents (.docx); MS-PowerPoint for presentations (.pptx).
SQL stands for Structured Query Language; SELECT is a DQL command.
Fully connected mesh topology needs n(n-1)/2 links, so 4 nodes need 6 links.
A record is a row and a field is a column in a database table.
Edgar F. Codd proposed the relational database model in 1970.
summary: The answer is (a): MS-Access is used to create a database. It is the relational database management system (RDBMS) in the Microsoft Office suite, used to build tables, queries, forms and reports.
topic_notes: MS-Office is Microsoft's productivity suite. Its main applications and file extensions are: Word (.docx, word processing), Excel (.xlsx, spreadsheets), PowerPoint (.pptx, presentations), Access (.accdb, database), Outlook (email, calendar and contacts), Publisher (.pub, desktop publishing) and OneNote (note-taking). Access database concepts: a table is made of records (rows) and fields (columns). A primary key uniquely identifies each record, and a foreign key links tables. Relationships can be one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many. Main objects: Tables store data; Queries (select, action, crosstab, parameter) retrieve or change data using SQL; Forms give a user-friendly interface for entry; Reports give formatted output for printing; Macros and Modules (VBA) automate tasks. Views include Datasheet view and Design view. Data types include Text, Number, Date/Time, Currency, AutoNumber, Yes/No, OLE Object and Hyperlink. Normalisation reduces redundancy. Other DBMS software: MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL (RDBMS) and MongoDB (NoSQL). SQL commands fall into DDL (CREATE, ALTER, DROP), DML (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), DQL (SELECT) and DCL (GRANT, REVOKE). For EPFO and ESIC exams, expect questions on software-to-use matching, file extensions, DBMS terms (key, field, record), SQL and networking basics. The other question on this page asked about mesh topology. A fully connected mesh of n nodes needs n(n-1)/2 links, so 4 computers need 6 links.

question: The intersection of a row and a column in a]111 spreadsheet of MS-Excel is represented as :
subject: Computers
detail: A spreadsheet in MS-Excel is a grid of rows (numbered 1 to 1,048,576) and columns (lettered A to XFD, 16,384 columns) in the modern .xlsx format. Where one row and one column cross, a cell is formed. Each cell has a unique address or reference made of the column letter followed by the row number, for example A1. The active cell is the one currently selected, and its address shows in the Name Box, while its contents show in the Formula Bar. A group of cells forms a range, such as A1:C5. A worksheet is the whole grid of cells on one tab. A workbook is the complete Excel file (.xlsx), which holds one or more worksheets. 'Notesheet' is not an Excel term at all; it belongs to office file-handling and noting practice. Elimination: a worksheet and a workbook are containers larger than a single row-column intersection, and a notesheet has no meaning in Excel, so only (a) fits.
explanations: Correct: the intersection of a row and a column is a cell, the smallest unit of a worksheet, addressed like C5.
Wrong: a worksheet is the entire grid of rows and columns on one sheet tab, not a single intersection.
Wrong: a workbook is the whole Excel file and can contain many worksheets.
Wrong: a notesheet is not an Excel component; it is an office-procedure term for a file noting sheet.
keyfact: Row and column intersection = Cell; worksheet = the grid sheet; workbook = the whole Excel file.
option_notes: Cell: the basic unit of a worksheet, formed where a row and column meet. It has an address (for example A1), and can hold text, numbers, dates, formulas or functions. The active cell shows in the Name Box and its content in the Formula Bar. Cells can be formatted, merged, referenced relatively (A1), absolutely ($A$1) or in mixed form, and grouped into ranges.

Worksheet: a single page or tab within an Excel workbook, made up of a grid of rows and columns (1,048,576 rows by 16,384 columns in the .xlsx format). The default tab is named Sheet1 and can be renamed, moved, copied, colored or deleted. Sheets are added with the + button or Shift+F11. A worksheet is also called a spreadsheet.

Workbook: the Excel file itself, saved as .xlsx (or .xls in older versions, .xlsm with macros). It contains one or more worksheets. Newer versions open with one sheet by default, while older versions opened with three. The default name is Book1. A workbook can have many sheets, limited only by available memory.

Notesheet: not an MS-Excel term. It is an administrative term for the sheet in a government file on which officers record notes and orders, separate from the correspondence portion. In e-office, it is the 'Note' part of an electronic file. It is a distractor here.
related: Excel 2007 and later: 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns (A to XFD).
Older .xls format: 65,536 rows and 256 columns (A to IV).
A cell address combines column letter and row number, for example B3.
The Name Box displays the address of the active cell.
A formula in Excel always starts with the = sign.
F4 toggles between relative and absolute cell references.
A workbook is the Excel file (.xlsx) and holds one or more worksheets.
#DIV/0! appears when a number is divided by zero.
summary: The answer is (a) Cell. In MS-Excel, the point where a row meets a column is called a cell, and it is the basic unit for storing data, formulas and formatting. Each cell is identified by its address, such as B3 (column B, row 3).
topic_notes: MS-Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet program, part of the Microsoft Office suite, used for calculation, data analysis, charts and tables. Structure: a workbook (.xlsx) holds worksheets; a worksheet is a grid of 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns (A to XFD) since Excel 2007; older .xls files allowed 65,536 rows and 256 columns (A to IV). A cell is the intersection of a row and a column. A cell address (reference) has the form column letter plus row number. A range is a block of cells, written like A1:B10. Cell references: relative (A1), absolute ($A$1), mixed ($A1 or A$1); F4 toggles between them. Interface items: Title bar, Ribbon with tabs (Home, Insert, Page Layout, Formulas, Data, Review, View), Name Box, Formula Bar, Status Bar, sheet tabs. Formulas begin with =. Common functions: SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, COUNT, COUNTA, IF, VLOOKUP, HLOOKUP, XLOOKUP, CONCATENATE, ROUND, TODAY, NOW. Error values: #DIV/0!, #NAME?, #VALUE!, #REF!, #N/A, #NUM!, and #### when a column is too narrow. Useful shortcuts: Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Arrow keys, Ctrl+Home goes to A1, F2 edits a cell, Alt+= is AutoSum. Features: charts, PivotTables, filters, sorting, conditional formatting, data validation, freeze panes, and macros (VBA). Default alignment: text is left-aligned and numbers are right-aligned. Future questions may ask about the file extension, maximum rows and columns, active cell, the Name Box, or the meaning of the error codes.

question: Which one of the following is not a malicious software ?
subject: Computers
detail: Malware (malicious software) is any program designed to damage, disrupt, steal data from or gain unauthorised access to a computer system. The main types are viruses, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, spyware, adware, keyloggers, rootkits and botnets. A virus attaches itself to a host file or program and spreads when that file is run. A worm is self-replicating and spreads over networks without needing a host file or user action. A Trojan horse pretends to be useful software but carries a hidden harmful payload, and it does not replicate by itself. A cipher, by contrast, is an algorithm for encryption and decryption. Examples are the Caesar cipher (substitution), the Vigenere cipher, and modern ciphers such as AES and DES (block ciphers) and RC4 (stream cipher). Ciphers are used to secure data and are part of cryptography, which is a defensive technique. Elimination logic: options (a), (b) and (c) are standard malware categories, so only (d), the cryptographic term, is the odd one out. Note that attackers can misuse encryption, as ransomware does, but the cipher itself is not malware.
explanations: Wrong: a virus is malware that attaches to files or programs, replicates when they are executed and damages data or systems.
Wrong: a worm is standalone malware that self-replicates and spreads across networks, consuming bandwidth and resources.
Wrong: a Trojan horse is malware disguised as legitimate software that opens backdoors or steals data.
Correct: a cipher is a cryptographic algorithm used to encrypt and decrypt data. It is a security tool, not malicious software.
keyfact: Cipher = encryption algorithm (defensive); virus, worm and Trojan horse are malware.
option_notes: Computer virus: a malicious program that attaches to executable files or documents and spreads when the host is run. The first PC virus was Brain (1986). Other examples are Creeper (an early experimental program, 1971), Melissa and ILOVEYOU. Types include boot sector, macro, file infector and polymorphic viruses. Antivirus software detects and removes them.

Computer worm: standalone self-replicating malware that spreads through networks, often by exploiting vulnerabilities, with no host file or user action needed. Examples are the Morris Worm (1988, the first major internet worm), Code Red, SQL Slammer, Conficker and WannaCry (a ransomware worm, 2017). Worms mainly cause network congestion and can carry payloads.

Trojan horse: malware disguised as a legitimate or useful program, named after the Greek wooden-horse legend. It does not self-replicate. It can create backdoors, steal data, install other malware or give remote control through a RAT (Remote Access Trojan). Examples are Zeus (banking Trojan) and Emotet. Spread is through user deception such as email attachments or fake downloads.

Cipher: an algorithm for encryption and decryption in cryptography. Classical ciphers include Caesar (shift), Vigenere and Playfair. Modern ones are symmetric (AES, DES, 3DES, RC4) and asymmetric (RSA, ECC). Plaintext becomes ciphertext using a key. Ciphers provide confidentiality and are defensive tools, not malware.
related: Worms self-replicate over networks without needing a host file; viruses need a host.
Trojan horses do not self-replicate; they rely on deception.
Morris Worm (1988) was the first major internet worm.
Ransomware encrypts files and demands payment, e.g. WannaCry (2017).
A firewall filters network traffic and is a security tool, not malware.
AES is a symmetric cipher; RSA is an asymmetric cipher.
CERT-In is India's nodal agency for cyber security incidents.
Spyware secretly collects user information; a keylogger records keystrokes.
summary: The answer is (d) Cipher. A cipher is a cryptographic algorithm that converts plaintext into ciphertext to protect data, so it is a security tool and not malware. Virus, Worm and Trojan Horse are all types of malicious software.
topic_notes: Malware is a core topic in computer security. Main types: virus (needs a host file and user action), worm (self-spreading over networks), Trojan (disguised, does not replicate), ransomware (encrypts files and demands payment, e.g. WannaCry, Petya), spyware (secretly collects information), adware (unwanted ads), keylogger (records keystrokes), rootkit (hides its presence and gives privileged access), botnet (network of infected machines, or zombies, used for DDoS attacks), logic bomb (triggers on a condition) and backdoor. Related attacks that are not malware types: phishing (fake emails or sites for credentials), vishing (voice), smishing (SMS), spoofing, pharming, SQL injection, man-in-the-middle, DoS/DDoS, and brute force. Defensive tools: antivirus, firewall, IDS/IPS, VPN, encryption, digital signatures, two-factor authentication and regular patching. Cryptography basics: plaintext, ciphertext, key. Symmetric encryption uses one key (AES, DES). Asymmetric encryption uses a public and private key pair (RSA). Hashing (MD5, SHA) provides integrity and is one-way. Digital signatures provide authentication and non-repudiation. In India, the IT Act 2000 (amended 2008) governs cyber offences. CERT-In is the national agency for cyber incidents, and the I4C and National Cyber Security Policy 2013 are also relevant. Section 66 covers computer-related offences and Section 66C identity theft. Likely future questions: distinguish virus from worm, define a Trojan, name a defensive tool, or identify which term is not malware (for example firewall, cipher, antivirus or encryption).

question: Which one of the following is not a system software ?
subject: Computers
detail: Software is divided into system software and application software. System software runs and controls the hardware and provides a platform on which other software works. Its main types are operating systems (Windows, Linux, Unix, macOS, Android), language translators (compilers, interpreters, assemblers), device drivers, utility programs (antivirus, disk defragmenters, backup tools), firmware and BIOS, and linkers and loaders. Application software is written to perform specific user tasks, such as word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, accounting packages, browsers, media players and database applications. A database program (a DBMS front-end or a database application such as MS Access) lets users create tables, queries and reports. It sits on top of the OS and is not needed to run the computer, so it is application software. Strictly, a DBMS engine is often called a middleware or system-level tool, but UPSC's standard classification treats database programs as application software. Elimination: (b) the OS is the core system software, (c) a compiler translates source code to machine code and is a language processor, and (d) a device driver lets the OS communicate with hardware. This leaves (a).
explanations: Correct choice. Database programs are application software meant for user data management, not for operating or controlling the hardware, so they are not system software.
Wrong choice. The operating system is the primary system software that manages the CPU, memory, files and devices, so it is system software.
Wrong choice. A compiler is a language translator, which is a type of system software (programming/translation software), so it is system software.
Wrong choice. Device drivers are system software that let the OS communicate with hardware such as printers and graphics cards, so they are system software.
keyfact: System software = OS, compilers/interpreters/assemblers, device drivers, utilities, firmware; database programs and MS Office are application software.
option_notes: Database programs such as MS Access, MySQL clients and Oracle Forms are used to create, store, query and report data. A DBMS organises data in tables with SQL. In the standard classification they are application software. Examples are student records, payroll and library management systems. They depend on the OS to run. Edgar Codd proposed the relational model in 1970.

An operating system manages hardware resources and provides services to programs. Its functions are process, memory, file and device management, security and the user interface. Examples are Windows, Linux, Unix, macOS, Android and iOS. Types include batch, time-sharing, real-time, multiuser and distributed. The kernel is its core. It is the main system software.

A compiler translates a whole high-level program (C, C++, Java) into machine or object code before execution and reports errors. An interpreter translates and executes line by line (Python, BASIC). An assembler converts assembly language to machine code. Compilers are language processors and belong to system software. Compiled code usually runs faster.

A device driver is a small program that lets the OS and applications communicate with a hardware device such as a printer, keyboard, scanner, graphics card or network card. It translates generic OS commands into device-specific instructions. Drivers are system software, often loaded into the kernel, and need updating when hardware or the OS changes. Plug and Play can install them automatically.
related: Compiler translates the whole program at once; interpreter works line by line.
Assembler converts assembly language to machine code.
Linux is open-source system software, created by Linus Torvalds in 1991.
BIOS is firmware stored in ROM that starts the computer.
MS Word, Excel and Tally are application software.
Utility software includes antivirus, backup and disk defragmenters.
Kernel is the core part of an operating system.
SQL is a fourth-generation language used with databases.
summary: The answer is (a) Database programs. Database programs such as MS Access, Oracle front-ends and MySQL clients are application software used for storing and retrieving user data. Operating systems, compilers and device drivers are system software because they manage or support the hardware and the running of other programs.
topic_notes: Computer software is classified into system software and application software. System software manages and supports the hardware and provides a platform for applications. It includes the operating system, language translators (compiler, interpreter, assembler), device drivers, utility software, firmware, BIOS, linkers, loaders and, in some classifications, middleware. Application software performs user-oriented tasks. It can be general purpose (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, browsers), specific purpose (railway reservation, payroll, accounting such as Tally) or bespoke (custom-made). Open-source software (Linux, LibreOffice, Firefox) has freely available source code. Proprietary software (Windows, MS Office) is licensed. Freeware is free but closed. Shareware is free for a trial period. Operating system functions include process management, memory management, file management, I/O management, security and job scheduling. Types are batch, multiprogramming, time-sharing, real-time, multiprocessing and network or distributed. Utility software includes antivirus, disk cleanup, defragmentation, compression (WinZip) and backup. Firmware is software stored permanently in ROM, for example the BIOS. Translators convert programs: assembler (assembly to machine code), compiler (whole program), interpreter (line by line). Language generations: 1GL machine, 2GL assembly, 3GL high-level, 4GL SQL, 5GL AI. UPSC often asks 'which is not system software' and 'which is application software' with options such as MS Word, Tally, a browser, a linker or a loader. The usual trap is database programs or a DBMS, which are normally application software.

question: A Petabyte is equivalent to : 114,
subject: Computers
detail: Digital storage is measured in bytes, and the conventional (binary) system multiplies by 1024 (2^10) at each level. The ladder is: 1 Byte = 8 bits; 1 KB = 1024 Bytes; 1 MB = 1024 KB; 1 GB = 1024 MB; 1 TB = 1024 GB; 1 PB = 1024 TB; 1 EB (Exabyte) = 1024 PB; 1 ZB (Zettabyte) = 1024 EB; 1 YB (Yottabyte) = 1024 ZB. Hence a Petabyte is 2^50 bytes, about 1.126 x 10^15 bytes. In the decimal SI convention used by storage manufacturers, 1 PB = 1000 TB = 10^15 bytes. The IEC term for the binary unit is pebibyte (PiB), but exams follow the 1024 convention. Elimination: 1024 Bytes is a Kilobyte (a), 1024 KB is a Megabyte (b), and 1024 GB is a Terabyte (c). Only 1024 TB matches a Petabyte, so (d) is correct. A quick memory aid is the order K, M, G, T, P, E, Z, Y, with the Petabyte fifth after the Byte.
explanations: Incorrect: 1024 Bytes equals 1 Kilobyte, the first step above the Byte, not a Petabyte.
Incorrect: 1024 KB equals 1 Megabyte, which is far smaller than a Petabyte.
Incorrect: 1024 GB equals 1 Terabyte, one level below a Petabyte.
Correct: 1024 TB equals 1 Petabyte (2^50 bytes), the unit directly above the Terabyte.
keyfact: 1 PB = 1024 TB (2^50 bytes); order: B, KB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB, YB.
option_notes: 1024 Bytes = 1 Kilobyte (KB). A byte is 8 bits and typically stores one character. The 1024 factor comes from 2^10 in binary systems. A KB holds a short text passage. In SI decimal usage, 1 kB = 1000 bytes, and the IEC binary term is kibibyte (KiB).

1024 KB = 1 Megabyte (MB), which is 2^20 bytes. A MB holds roughly a small digital photo or a minute of low-quality MP3 audio. Older floppy disks held about 1.44 MB, and CD-ROMs about 700 MB. The IEC binary term is mebibyte (MiB).

1024 GB = 1 Terabyte (TB), which is 2^40 bytes. Consumer hard drives and SSDs are commonly 1-4 TB. A TB is the unit just below the Petabyte. In decimal usage, 1 TB = 1000 GB. The IEC binary term is tebibyte (TiB).

1024 TB = 1 Petabyte (PB), which is 2^50 bytes, or about 10^15 bytes in decimal usage. Large data centres, big-data platforms, and social media firms handle petabytes of data. The next unit is the Exabyte (1024 PB). The IEC binary term is pebibyte (PiB).
related: 1 Byte = 8 bits; 4 bits = 1 nibble.
1 KB = 1024 Bytes; 1 MB = 1024 KB; 1 GB = 1024 MB.
Order of units: Byte, KB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB, ZB, YB.
The IEC binary name for a Petabyte is pebibyte (PiB).
Decimal (SI) convention: 1 PB = 1000 TB = 10^15 bytes.
A Petabyte is 2^50 bytes in the binary system.
Network speed is measured in bits per second, not bytes.
summary: The answer is (d) 1024 TB. A Petabyte (PB) is the unit above the Terabyte in the binary storage hierarchy, and each step up is a factor of 1024 (2^10). So 1 PB = 1024 TB = 2^50 bytes.
topic_notes: Units of digital memory are a regular Computers topic in UPSC EPFO and ESIC papers. The smallest unit is the bit (binary digit, 0 or 1). A group of 4 bits is a nibble and 8 bits is a byte. The standard ladder is: 1 KB = 1024 Bytes; 1 MB = 1024 KB; 1 GB = 1024 MB; 1 TB = 1024 GB; 1 PB = 1024 TB; 1 EB = 1024 PB; 1 ZB = 1024 EB; 1 YB = 1024 ZB. Beyond this are the newer units Ronnabyte and Quettabyte, adopted by the SI in 2022. Each step is 2^10 in the binary convention. The decimal SI convention uses 1000 per step and is used by storage manufacturers, which is why a drive sold as 1 TB shows less capacity in an operating system. The IEC introduced the binary prefixes kibi, mebi, gibi, tebi, and pebi (KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB) to remove ambiguity. Related areas UPSC can ask include memory types: primary memory (RAM, ROM, cache) versus secondary memory (HDD, SSD, optical disc, flash drive); volatile versus non-volatile memory; and the speed hierarchy of registers, cache, RAM, and disk. Other angles are the word size of a CPU, the number of bits in ASCII (7 or 8) and Unicode, and the use of MIPS, MHz, and GHz for processor speed. Data transfer rates are measured in bits per second (bps, Mbps), whereas storage is measured in bytes. Questions can also give a unit and ask for the next higher or lower one.

question: Which one of the following malicious softwares 115, blocks access to a computer system until a sum of money is paid ?
subject: Computers
detail: Ransomware is a category of malicious software (malware) that denies a user access to their system or data, typically by encrypting files or locking the screen, and demands payment (a ransom) for restoring access. Payment is usually demanded in Bitcoin or other cryptocurrency. Well-known examples are WannaCry (May 2017, exploiting the EternalBlue vulnerability in Windows SMB), Petya/NotPetya (2017), Locky, CryptoLocker and Ryuk. In India, the AIIMS Delhi server attack of November 2022 was a major ransomware-type incident. Legal context: the IT Act, 2000 (Sections 43, 66 and 66F) covers such offences, and CERT-In is the national agency for cyber incidents. Elimination logic: a Trojan horse disguises itself as legitimate software and creates backdoors; a virus attaches itself to host files and replicates when the host is run; a worm is self-replicating and spreads over networks without a host file. None of these is defined by demanding money for restoring access, so only ransomware fits the question.
explanations: Correct: ransomware locks or encrypts a system or data and demands payment before restoring access, exactly as the question describes.
Wrong: a Trojan horse masquerades as genuine software to trick users into installing it, and then steals data or opens backdoors. Its defining feature is deception, not demanding a ransom.
Wrong: a virus attaches to executable files or programs, replicates when the host is run and corrupts files or slows the system. It is not defined by ransom demands.
Wrong: a worm is a standalone self-replicating program that spreads across networks without user action, consuming bandwidth and resources. It is not defined by ransom demands.
keyfact: Ransomware = malware that locks or encrypts a system and demands payment (ransom) to restore access.
option_notes: Ransomware is malware that encrypts files or locks the system and demands a ransom, usually in cryptocurrency, for the decryption key. Types include crypto-ransomware and locker ransomware. Famous cases: WannaCry (2017), NotPetya (2017), CryptoLocker (2013) and Ryuk. It commonly spreads through phishing emails, malicious attachments and unpatched vulnerabilities. Defences are regular offline backups, patching, and email filtering. Authorities generally advise against paying the ransom.

A Trojan horse is malware disguised as a useful or legitimate program, named after the Greek wooden horse of Troy. It does not self-replicate. Once installed by the user, it can create backdoors, steal passwords, log keystrokes or download other malware. Types include Remote Access Trojans (RATs), banking Trojans and downloader Trojans. Examples include Zeus, Emotet (originally a banking Trojan) and Back Orifice. Defence relies on avoiding untrusted downloads and using antivirus software.

A computer virus is a malicious program that attaches itself to a host file or program and replicates when the host is executed, spreading from one file or system to another. Fred Cohen coined the term in 1983, and Brain (1986) is regarded as the first PC virus. Types include boot sector, macro, file infector and polymorphic viruses. Examples are Melissa (1999) and CIH/Chernobyl (1998). Effects range from file corruption to system failure.

A computer worm is a standalone self-replicating malware that spreads through networks by exploiting vulnerabilities, without needing a host file or user action. It mainly causes network congestion and resource exhaustion, and can carry payloads. The Morris Worm (1988) was one of the first major internet worms. Others include ILOVEYOU (2000), Code Red (2001), Blaster, Conficker (2008) and Stuxnet (2010), which targeted industrial control systems. WannaCry combined a worm-like spread with ransomware.
related: WannaCry (2017) was a ransomware attack that spread using the EternalBlue exploit in Windows SMB.
Worms spread without a host file; viruses need a host file and user action.
A Trojan horse does not self-replicate; it relies on deception.
CERT-In is the national nodal agency for cyber security incidents in India, under MeitY.
Section 66F of the IT Act, 2000 deals with cyber terrorism.
Spyware secretly collects user information; keyloggers record keystrokes.
A botnet is a network of infected 'zombie' computers used for DDoS attacks.
Phishing uses fake emails or sites to steal credentials; the cybercrime helpline is 1930.
summary: The answer is (a) Ransomware. Ransomware is malware that encrypts files or locks a computer system and blocks access until the victim pays a ransom, usually in cryptocurrency. Trojans, viruses and worms have different primary behaviours.
topic_notes: Malware (malicious software) is software designed to damage, disrupt or gain unauthorised access to systems. Main types: virus (needs a host file and a user action to spread), worm (self-spreading over networks), Trojan horse (disguised, does not replicate), ransomware (locks or encrypts data for payment), spyware (secretly gathers information), adware (unwanted advertisements), keylogger (records keystrokes), rootkit (hides its presence and gives privileged access), botnet (a network of compromised machines, or 'zombies', used for DDoS attacks), logic bomb (triggers on a condition) and backdoor (hidden bypass of authentication). Related attacks: phishing (fraudulent emails or sites to steal credentials), vishing (voice), smishing (SMS), pharming (redirecting traffic to fake sites), spoofing, DoS and DDoS, man-in-the-middle, and SQL injection. Protection: antivirus software, firewalls, regular updates and patches, strong passwords, two-factor authentication, offline backups (the 3-2-1 rule), and encryption. Indian framework: the Information Technology Act, 2000 (amended 2008) covers hacking (Section 66), identity theft (66C), cheating by personation (66D), and cyber terrorism (66F). CERT-In (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) under MeitY is the national nodal agency and issues advisories on ransomware. The National Cyber Security Policy was issued in 2013, and the cybercrime reporting portal is cybercrime.gov.in, with helpline 1930. Notable incidents: WannaCry (May 2017, affecting over 150 countries), NotPetya (June 2017), AIIMS Delhi (Nov 2022) and Colonial Pipeline (2021, USA). Questions often ask students to match a malware type with its defining characteristic.

question: , According to the 2022 edition of the State of the World’s Forests (SOFO) report, approximately how much of the total forest area of the world has been lost in the last 30 years ?
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
detail: State of the World's Forests (SOFO) is a biennial flagship publication of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO, headquartered in Rome). The 2022 edition is titled 'Forest pathways for green recovery and building inclusive, resilient and sustainable economies'. It says the world has about 4.06 billion hectares of forest, roughly 31% of land area. Since 1990 an estimated 420 million hectares have been lost to deforestation, which is about 10% of the 1990 forest area. The rate of loss has slowed: 17.6 million ha per year in 1990-2000 fell to about 10 million ha per year in 2015-2020. Net forest loss is smaller because of afforestation and natural expansion. Under the 2022 report, about 1.1 billion ha is covered by protected areas, and the report promotes three pathways: halting deforestation and maintaining forests, restoring degraded lands and expanding agroforestry, and using forests sustainably and building green value chains. On elimination, 5% understates the scale. 15% and 17% overstate it. Note that 17% is a figure often tied to other forest and biodiversity data, so it is a distractor. The best approach is to remember '420 million ha, about 10%, over 30 years'.
explanations: Incorrect: 5% would be about 200 million ha, only half of the reported 420 million ha lost since 1990.
Correct: about 420 million ha lost since 1990 out of roughly 4.06 billion ha of forest is about 10%, matching the SOFO 2022 report and the official answer.
Incorrect: 15% would mean over 600 million ha lost, which exceeds the reported figure.
Incorrect: 17% is not the SOFO 2022 figure for forest lost in 30 years; it overstates the loss and is a distractor.
keyfact: SOFO 2022 (FAO): about 420 million ha of forest lost since 1990, roughly 10% of global forest area.
option_notes: 5%: This is not the loss figure in SOFO 2022. Around 5% could loosely describe smaller shares in other datasets, but the FAO reports about 420 million ha lost since 1990. The global forest area is about 4.06 billion ha, covering roughly 31% of the world's land. Forests hold more species than any other land ecosystem, and more than half of the forest area is in just five countries.

10%: This is the correct figure. About 420 million ha were lost to deforestation between 1990 and 2020. The annual rate of loss has fallen from about 16-17 million ha per year in the 1990s to about 10 million ha per year recently. The loss is concentrated in Africa and South America, and agricultural expansion is the main driver. The FAO publishes this in SOFO and in its Global Forest Resources Assessment (FRA).

15%: This overstates the loss. It would imply more than 600 million ha lost since 1990. The actual net loss of forest area, after counting regrowth and plantations, is smaller than the gross deforestation figure. Remember that the FAO's 2020 Global Forest Resources Assessment reported net loss of about 178 million ha since 1990, an area roughly the size of Libya.

17%: This is not the SOFO 2022 figure. Seventeen percent resembles the Aichi Biodiversity Target 11 goal of conserving 17% of terrestrial areas by 2020, which is why it is a plausible distractor. The Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022) later raised the goal to 30% by 2030 (the '30 by 30' target).
related: SOFO is published by the FAO every two years.
SOFO 2022 reports about 420 million ha of deforestation since 1990.
Global forest area is about 4.06 billion ha, around 31% of land.
FAO's Global Forest Resources Assessment (FRA) is published every five years.
The India State of Forest Report is published by the Forest Survey of India, Dehradun.
The Bonn Challenge aims to restore 350 million ha of degraded land by 2030.
The Glasgow Leaders' Declaration (COP26) pledged to end deforestation by 2030.
summary: The answer is (b) 10%. The FAO's State of the World's Forests 2022 report says the world has lost roughly 420 million hectares of forest through deforestation since 1990, which is about 10% of the global forest area of about 4.06 billion hectares.
topic_notes: SOFO is published by the FAO every two years, and is presented at the Committee on Forestry (COFO). The 2022 edition focuses on forest pathways for green recovery and on three pathways: halting deforestation and maintaining forests, restoring degraded lands and expanding agroforestry, and using forests sustainably while building green value chains. Key numbers: global forest area about 4.06 billion ha (31% of land); about 420 million ha converted to other uses since 1990; the rate of deforestation slowed over three decades; about 1.1 billion ha are in protected areas; about 2.4 billion ha are primary or naturally regenerating forest outside protected areas. Over half of forests are in five countries: Russia, Brazil, Canada, the USA and China. Related FAO products include the Global Forest Resources Assessment (FRA, every 5 years, latest FRA 2020 and FRA 2025), the State of Food and Agriculture (SOFA), SOFIA (fisheries) and SOFI (food security and nutrition). Other forest-related institutions and agreements: UN Forum on Forests (UNFF), the New York Declaration on Forests (2014), the Bonn Challenge (restoring 350 million ha by 2030), REDD+, the Glasgow Leaders' Declaration on Forests and Land Use (COP26, 2021, to end deforestation by 2030) and the EU Deforestation Regulation. In India, the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) is published by the Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun, every two years; ISFR 2021 reported forest and tree cover of 80.9 million ha, 24.62% of the geographical area. UPSC could ask about publisher, periodicity, titles and headline figures of such reports.

question: Who among the following is the Chairperson of the Advisory Committee constituted recently by SEBI on Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) ?
subject: Computers
detail: SEBI maintains the Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) under the SEBI (Investor Protection and Education Fund) Regulations, 2009, framed under the SEBI Act, 1992. The Fund is built from sources such as grants, penalties and disgorged amounts, and is used for investor education, awareness and protection programmes. The IPEF Advisory Committee advises SEBI on how the Fund should be used, including the activities and programmes it supports. In this question G. Mahalingam, a former SEBI Whole-Time Member with long experience in capital-market regulation, is the Chairperson per the official key. Elimination logic: G.P. Gupta is associated with IDBI and other financial bodies, A. Balasubramanian is the Chief Executive of Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC and has been a SEBI committee member, and N. Hariharan is a senior advocate and has sat on SEBI committees. None of them is the IPEF Advisory Committee head per the official key. For exams, remember that the Committee is advisory, while the Fund is managed by SEBI itself, and that persons named in such committee questions are usually ex-regulators.
explanations: G.P. Gupta is not the Chairperson of the IPEF Advisory Committee, so (a) is wrong.
A. Balasubramanian is known for asset-management and SEBI committee roles but is not the IPEF Advisory Committee Chairperson, so (b) is wrong.
N. Hariharan is a senior advocate and has served on other SEBI panels, not as IPEF Advisory Committee Chairperson, so (c) is wrong.
G. Mahalingam, former SEBI Whole-Time Member, is the Chairperson per the official UPSC answer, so (d) is correct.
keyfact: G. Mahalingam chairs the SEBI Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) Advisory Committee.
option_notes: G.P. Gupta: a name associated with Indian financial-sector institutions and banking or development finance roles. He is not linked to the IPEF Advisory Committee in the official key. Questions about SEBI committees often use names of financial-sector veterans as distractors, so note the specific committee-head pairings when revising.

A. Balasubramanian: the Managing Director and CEO of Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC and a well-known figure in the mutual fund industry. He has served on SEBI-appointed committees and industry bodies. He is a distractor here, since he is not the IPEF Advisory Committee Chairperson.

N. Hariharan: a senior advocate who has been a member of various SEBI advisory and expert panels dealing with legal and regulatory matters. He is a plausible distractor but is not the Chairperson of the IPEF Advisory Committee according to the official answer.

G. Mahalingam: a former SEBI Whole-Time Member (2013-2018) who earlier worked with RBI. He has been involved in market regulation, and per the official answer he chairs the IPEF Advisory Committee constituted by SEBI. He is also associated with other SEBI advisory roles.
related: SEBI was established in 1988 and gained statutory status in 1992.
SEBI's headquarters are in Mumbai.
IPEF is governed by the SEBI (Investor Protection and Education Fund) Regulations, 2009.
IEPFA under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs is separate from SEBI's IPEF.
Appeals against SEBI orders go to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT).
SEBI's Board includes a Chairman, two Union Finance Ministry members, one RBI member and five other members.
SEBI has quasi-legislative, quasi-judicial and quasi-executive powers.
summary: The official answer is (d) G. Mahalingam. SEBI's Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) Advisory Committee was constituted with former SEBI Whole-Time Member G. Mahalingam as its Chairperson.
topic_notes: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) was set up in 1988 as an administrative body and given statutory status through the SEBI Act, 1992. Its headquarters are in Mumbai. SEBI's mandate is to protect the interests of investors in securities, to promote the development of the securities market and to regulate it. The Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) is established under the SEBI (Investor Protection and Education Fund) Regulations, 2009. It is used for investor awareness, education and protection initiatives, and may be funded by grants, penalties and other sums received by SEBI. The Fund is managed by SEBI, while the Advisory Committee gives guidance on utilisation and on approved activities. SEBI also has other committees: the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) hears appeals against SEBI orders, the Primary Market Advisory Committee (PMAC) and Secondary Market Advisory Committee (SMAC) advise on market matters, and the Investor Advisory Committee (IAC) advises on investor-related matters. A related body is the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (IEPFA) under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, which is distinct from SEBI's IPEF. Other angles UPSC may ask: SEBI chairpersons (Ajay Tyagi, Madhabi Puri Buch, Tuhin Kanta Pandey), SEBI's powers (quasi-legislative, quasi-judicial, quasi-executive), the 2014 amendment giving SEBI attachment and search powers, and the SEBI Board composition: a Chairman, two Union Government officer members, one RBI member and five other members.

ocr: Which one of the following is the mascot of the Fourth Khelo India Youth Games ? (a) Vijaya (b) Vijay (c) Dhakad (d) Jaya Nikhat Zareen excels in which one of the following sports ? (a) Weightlifting (b) Boxing (c) .Kho-Kho (d) Wrestling
subject: Computers
detail: Khelo India is the Government of India's flagship programme for grassroots sports development, run by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. It was relaunched in 2018 as a national programme for talent identification and development. The Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) are held for under-17 and, later, under-21 athletes. The editions so far: 1st in New Delhi (2018), 2nd in Pune (2019), 3rd in Guwahati (January 2020), and the 4th in Haryana (Panchkula as the main venue, with events also in Chandigarh, Shahbad, Ambala and Delhi), held 4-13 June 2022. Haryana topped the medal tally. The 4th edition's mascot was Dhakad, a name taken from Haryanvi slang for a strong, bold person, reflecting the state's sporting culture. Its theme song and jersey were launched together with the mascot. Elimination logic: Vijaya, Vijay and Jaya sound like generic victory words and carry no association with Haryana or Khelo India, while Dhakad is a distinctly Haryanvi word. Mascot questions are a frequent current-affairs item, so link each mascot to its host state and year. Note that the second question on the page (Nikhat Zareen) has the answer Boxing.
explanations: Incorrect: Vijaya is not the mascot of the Fourth Khelo India Youth Games. It is a generic 'victory' name and is a distractor.
Incorrect: Vijay is not associated with this edition's mascot. It is another generic victory-themed distractor.
Correct: Dhakad is the official mascot of the Fourth Khelo India Youth Games, Haryana (Panchkula), June 2022. The name is Haryanvi for a strong, powerful person.
Incorrect: Jaya is not the mascot of this edition. It is a generic name used as a distractor.
keyfact: 4th Khelo India Youth Games (Haryana, June 2022) mascot = Dhakad; Nikhat Zareen = Boxing.
option_notes: Vijaya means 'victory' in Sanskrit and Indian languages. It is a common name but not the mascot of the Fourth Khelo India Youth Games. Mascot names for national games usually reflect the host state's culture, a link this word lacks. Do not confuse it with other event mascots or brand names.

Vijay also means 'victory' and is a very common Indian name. It is not the mascot of the 4th KIYG. In exams, such generic words are used as distractors next to a distinctive local word like Dhakad, which is the real answer here.

Dhakad is the mascot of the 4th Khelo India Youth Games (Haryana 2021, held 4-13 June 2022). The word is Haryanvi for a strong, bold, powerful person and reflects the state's wrestling and sports culture. The Games were hosted mainly at Panchkula, and Haryana topped the medal tally.

Jaya means 'victory' or 'victorious' (feminine) in Sanskrit. It is a common name but not the mascot of this edition. Like Vijaya and Vijay, it is a plausible-sounding distractor with no tie to Haryana or Khelo India.
related: Fourth Khelo India Youth Games: Haryana (Panchkula), 4-13 June 2022; mascot Dhakad.
Khelo India was relaunched in 2018 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports.
Khelo India scholarship: Rs 5 lakh per year for 8 years for selected athletes.
Third Khelo India Youth Games were held in Guwahati, Assam, in 2020.
Nikhat Zareen is a boxer from Telangana and a world champion (2022 at 52 kg, 2023 at 50 kg).
Khelo India Winter Games are held in Gulmarg, Jammu & Kashmir.
Fit India Movement was launched on 29 August 2019 (National Sports Day).
Haryana topped the medal tally at the 4th Khelo India Youth Games.
summary: The official answer is (c) Dhakad, the mascot of the Fourth Khelo India Youth Games, held in Haryana (Panchkula) in June 2022. The other names (Vijaya, Vijay, Jaya) are distractors and are not the mascot of this edition.
topic_notes:
Khelo India is a centrally sponsored scheme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports. It was launched in its restructured form in 2018 to revive the sporting culture at grassroots level and to build a strong sports ecosystem. Its main verticals are play-field development, community coaching, talent search and development, and the Khelo India State Centres of Excellence. Athletes selected under the Talent Identification and Development scheme receive an annual scholarship of Rs 5 lakh for up to 8 years.

Khelo India Youth Games editions: 1st, New Delhi (January 2018, under-17); 2nd, Pune, Maharashtra (January 2019, under-17 and under-21); 3rd, Guwahati, Assam (January 2020); 4th, Haryana (Panchkula, June 2022), with Dhakad as the mascot and Haryana topping the table; 5th, Tamil Nadu (Chennai, January 2024). The Khelo India University Games began in 2020 at Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Khelo India Winter Games are held at Gulmarg, Jammu & Kashmir, and Khelo India Para Games are also held. Madhya Pradesh hosted the 2022 University Games edition.

Other angles UPSC could ask: the ministry's nodal role, the athlete scholarship, the Fit India Movement (launched 2019), the National Sports Awards (Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna, Arjuna, Dronacharya, Dhyan Chand), and the host state of each edition. The second question on the page concerns Nikhat Zareen, a boxer from Telangana. She won the 2022 World Championship (52 kg) in Istanbul and the 2023 World Championship (50 kg) in New Delhi.

question: The ‘Glasgow Climate Pact’ made during the COP26 Climate Summit emphasized: on India’s announcement of the target of becoming ‘Net Zero’ carbon emitter by :
subject: General Science
detail: At COP26 in Glasgow (31 Oct to 13 Nov 2021), PM Modi presented the 'Panchamrit' pledges: 500 GW non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030; 50% of energy requirements from renewables by 2030; a 1 billion tonne cut in projected carbon emissions by 2030; a 45% reduction in the carbon intensity of the economy by 2030 (over 2005 levels); and net zero by 2070. The Glasgow Climate Pact called on countries to phase down unabated coal power and phase out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies, and urged stronger 2030 targets. India pushed for the wording to change from 'phase out' to 'phase down' coal. India's net zero year was later formalised in its Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy (LT-LEDS), submitted at COP27 in 2022, and in the updated NDC of August 2022. Elimination logic: 2050 is the target of the US, EU and UK; China's is 2060 and Russia's 2060; India's is 2070. Therefore, going strictly by the facts, (a) 2070 matches India's announcement.
