Demo-2 (May 2020) was the first crewed orbital launch from US soil since 2011
Starlink is SpaceX's LEO satellite internet constellation
Starship is SpaceX's fully reusable super-heavy launch system
IN-SPACe is India's space-sector regulator and promoter, set up in 2020
Orion is NASA's crew spacecraft for Artemis
statements: 1 — Correct: SpaceX is the popular name of Space Exploration Technologies Corp. It was founded in 2002 by Elon Musk with the goal of reducing launch costs and enabling Mars colonisation. It is headquartered at Hawthorne, California. It became the first private company to put a liquid-fuel rocket into orbit (Falcon 1, 2008) and to send a spacecraft to the ISS (Dragon, 2012). It operates Starlink and is developing Starship. It is a major NASA contractor and launches both commercial and government payloads.

2 — Incorrect: Falcon is indeed a SpaceX rocket family (Falcon 1, Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy), but Dragon is also a SpaceX spacecraft, not NASA's. Dragon flies on Falcon 9 and has cargo and crew versions. NASA funded it through COTS and Commercial Crew but did not develop it. Crew Dragon first carried NASA astronauts in May 2020 (Demo-2). Missions include Crew-1 onward, Axiom-4 (2025, with India's Shubhanshu Shukla) and Inspiration4 (2021, the first all-civilian orbital mission). NASA's own spacecraft include Orion and the Space Shuttle.
summary: The answer is (a) 1 only. Statement 1 is correct because Space Exploration Technologies Corp. is commonly called SpaceX. Statement 2 is wrong because both Falcon (launch vehicles) and Dragon (spacecraft) were developed by SpaceX, not NASA.
topic_notes: SpaceX was founded in 2002 by Elon Musk. Falcon 1 became the first privately developed liquid-fuel rocket to reach orbit in 2008. Falcon 9 first flew in 2010 and is partially reusable; the first orbital-class booster landing came in December 2015. Falcon Heavy, with three Falcon 9 cores, first flew in February 2018, carrying a Tesla Roadster. Dragon is the capsule: Cargo Dragon first docked with the ISS in May 2012. Crew Dragon flew its first crewed mission, Demo-2, in May 2020, and Inspiration4 in 2021 was the first all-civilian orbital flight. Axiom-4 in 2025 carried Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla of India to the ISS. Starship is the fully reusable super-heavy vehicle intended for Moon (NASA Artemis HLS) and Mars missions. Starlink is a low-Earth-orbit broadband constellation with thousands of satellites. Other private space firms: Blue Origin (New Shepard, New Glenn), Rocket Lab (Electron), Virgin Galactic, and Boeing's Starliner. In India, Skyroot (Vikram-S, 2022) and Agnikul (Agnibaan) are private launch firms, supported by IN-SPACe, which was set up in 2020 as the regulator and promoter. NASA's own programmes include Artemis, the Space Launch System and Orion. ISRO vehicles include PSLV, GSLV and LVM3.

question: Which of the following statements relating to 2026 FIFA Men’s Football World Cup is/are correct ? le USA, Mexico and Canada will jointly host the event. 2. 48 teams shall participate in the event. Select the answer using the codes given below :
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The 23rd FIFA Men's World Cup is scheduled for 11 June to 19 July 2026. It is the first World Cup hosted by three nations. The joint bid, called 'United 2026', beat Morocco's bid in the FIFA Congress vote in Moscow on 13 June 2018. Mexico becomes the first country to host or co-host the tournament three times (1970, 1986, 2026), and Canada hosts for the first time. The USA hosted in 1994. The tournament expands from 32 to 48 teams, a change approved by FIFA in January 2017 for 2026. There are 104 matches, up from 64. The 48 teams are drawn into 12 groups of 4. The top two from each group plus the 8 best third-placed teams advance to a Round of 32, followed by the knockout rounds. The opening match is at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City, and the final is at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Elimination logic: statement 1 is true, so options (b) and (d) go. Statement 2 is also true, so option (a) goes. That leaves (c).
explanations: Incorrect: this would mean statement 2 is false, but the tournament does have 48 teams.
Incorrect: this would mean statement 1 is false, but the three-nation joint hosting is true.
Correct: both the joint hosting by USA, Mexico and Canada and the 48-team format are accurate.
Incorrect: both statements are factually correct.
keyfact: 2026 FIFA World Cup: co-hosted by USA, Mexico and Canada, with 48 teams and 104 matches, the first of its kind.
option_notes: Statement 1 only: this would mean joint hosting is correct but the 48-team format is wrong. The joint hosting is real, but the expansion to 48 teams is also confirmed, so this option is wrong. The 2026 tournament is the first with three hosts and the first with 48 teams. The 2022 World Cup in Qatar used 32 teams.

Statement 2 only: this would mean the 48-team format is correct but the joint hosting is wrong. The 48-team field is real, but the three-country hosting is also true, so this option is wrong. The expansion from 32 teams was approved by FIFA in 2017 and takes effect in 2026.

Both 1 and 2: this is the correct option. The USA, Mexico and Canada co-host the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and 48 teams take part for the first time. The tournament runs from 11 June to 19 July 2026 and has 104 matches across 16 host cities.

Neither 1 nor 2: this is wrong because both statements are accurate. A student would only choose it by confusing the 2026 edition with earlier tournaments. The 2022 World Cup was in Qatar with 32 teams, and the 2030 edition has a different hosting arrangement.

The 2026 event is the first World Cup with 48 teams and three co-hosts

Select the answer using the codes given below : (a) Lonly (b) 2only (c) Both 1 and2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2 118.
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The 23rd FIFA World Cup (men's) will be held from 11 June to 19 July 2026. The hosts are the United States, Canada and Mexico, which makes it the first World Cup with three host nations. FIFA chose them through the 'United 2026' bid, which beat the Morocco bid at the FIFA Congress in Moscow on 13 June 2018. Elimination logic: both statements are factually correct, so options (a), (b) and (d) are ruled out and only (c) remains.
explanations: (a) Wrong: it accepts only statement 1, but statement 2 is also correct because the field expands to 48 teams.

(c) Correct: both statements are accurate, since there are three co-hosts and 48 participating teams.

question: Prime Minister Paetongtarn Shinawatra was removed by Thailand’s Constitutional Court in the year 2025 over a leaked phone call with a senior statesperson of which neighbouring country ?
subject: Indian Polity
detail: In June 2025 a Thai-Cambodian border dispute flared after a clash in the disputed Emerald Triangle area, where a Cambodian soldier was killed. Paetongtarn phoned Hun Sen, who had been Cambodia's PM for nearly four decades until handing over to his son Hun Manet in 2023 and now serves as Senate President. She addressed him as 'uncle' and criticised a Thai army commander. Hun Sen leaked the recording. Her coalition partner Bhumjaithai quit the government, and petitions reached the Constitutional Court, which suspended her in July 2025. On 29 August 2025 the Court ruled 6-3 that she had violated the ethical standards required of ministers under the Constitution, and removed her. She was the second Shinawatra PM removed by a court, after Srettha Thavisin in 2024 (Move Forward was dissolved the same year). Her father Thaksin and aunt Yingluck were earlier ousted. Elimination: Myanmar, Laos and Vietnam were not involved in the call. Cambodia is the neighbour with the border dispute and the Hun Sen link, and Hun Sen is the senior statesperson.
explanations: Incorrect: Myanmar is a Thai neighbour but had no part in the leaked call.
Correct: the leaked call was with Hun Sen of Cambodia, and it led to her removal by the Constitutional Court.
Incorrect: Laos borders Thailand but was not involved in this episode.
Incorrect: Vietnam does not share a land border with Thailand and was not involved in the call.
keyfact: Thailand's PM Paetongtarn was removed in August 2025 over a leaked call with Cambodia's Hun Sen.
option_notes: Myanmar: Thailand's western and northwestern neighbour, with a long border of about 2,400 km. It has been under military rule since the February 2021 coup, led by Min Aung Hlaing. It is a member of ASEAN and BIMSTEC, and its capital is Naypyidaw. India and Thailand are both linked to it via the Trilateral Highway.

Cambodia: A kingdom in Southeast Asia with its capital at Phnom Penh. King Norodom Sihamoni is head of state. Hun Manet has been PM since August 2023, and his father Hun Sen is Senate President. It has long-running border disputes with Thailand, including the Preah Vihear temple, which the ICJ awarded to Cambodia in 1962 and 2013. It is an ASEAN member.

Laos: A landlocked communist state with its capital at Vientiane. It borders Thailand along the Mekong River. It is an ASEAN member, joined in 1997, and is known as the 'battery of Southeast Asia' for its hydropower. Its currency is the kip. It is part of the Mekong-Ganga Cooperation grouping with India.

Vietnam: A socialist republic with its capital at Hanoi. It does not share a land border with Thailand, since Laos and Cambodia lie in between. It joined ASEAN in 1995. The leader of the Communist Party is To Lam (General Secretary since 2024). It is part of the Mekong-Ganga Cooperation and has a comprehensive strategic partnership with India.
related: Paetongtarn Shinawatra was removed on 29 August 2025 by a 6-3 Constitutional Court verdict.
The leaked call was with Hun Sen, Cambodia's Senate President and former PM.
Anutin Charnvirakul became Thailand's PM in September 2025.
Srettha Thavisin was removed by the Constitutional Court in August 2024.
Hun Manet has been Cambodia's PM since August 2023.
The ICJ awarded the Preah Vihear temple to Cambodia in 1962.
Move Forward Party was dissolved by Thailand's Constitutional Court in August 2024.
summary: The answer is (b) Cambodia. Thailand's PM Paetongtarn Shinawatra was removed by the Constitutional Court (August 2025) over a leaked June 2025 phone call with Cambodia's former PM and Senate President Hun Sen, in which she was found to have breached ethical standards.
topic_notes: Thailand is a constitutional monarchy under King Maha Vajiralongkorn (Rama X), with a bicameral National Assembly. Paetongtarn Shinawatra, born 1986, daughter of Thaksin Shinawatra, became PM in August 2024 at age 37, the youngest PM in Thai history. She succeeded Srettha Thavisin, who was removed by the Constitutional Court over the appointment of a minister with a criminal record. Her party is Pheu Thai. The Constitutional Court has repeatedly shaped Thai politics: it dissolved Thai Raksa Chart in 2019 and Move Forward in 2024. After her removal, Anutin Charnvirakul of Bhumjaithai was elected PM by parliament in September 2025. The Thai-Cambodian border dispute has older roots. The Preah Vihear temple was awarded to Cambodia by the ICJ in 1962, and the ruling was reaffirmed in 2013. In 2025 border clashes escalated into deadly fighting in July, followed by a ceasefire mediated by Malaysia, the ASEAN chair, with US involvement. Other points: Thailand is an ASEAN founding member (1967), a BIMSTEC member, and a Mekong-Ganga Cooperation member. India's Act East Policy links with Thailand through the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway. Bangkok is the capital, and the currency is the baht.

question:
Which of the following statements relating to the ‘Scheme for Promotion of Registration of Employers and Employees (SPREE) 2025’ is/are correct ? 109%
1. SPREE is approved by the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC).
2. SPREE provides a one-time opportunity for unregistered employers and employees — including contractual and temporary workers. Select the answer using the codes given below :
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
detail: SPREE 2025 is a one-time registration campaign of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), the statutory body under the Ministry of Labour & Employment that runs the ESI Act, 1948 scheme. The scheme was approved by the Corporation in its meeting chaired by the Union Labour Minister and was operationalised from 1 July 2025 for a limited window (to 31 December 2025). Employers who were covered under the Act but had not registered themselves or their employees can register voluntarily without facing inquiry or demand for contributions for the past period, and without penal action for earlier non-compliance; contributions are payable only from the date of registration. Benefits to newly registered employees start from the date of registration or coverage. It covers all eligible workers, including contractual, casual and temporary staff, within ESI coverage rules (wage ceiling Rs 21,000 per month, Rs 25,000 for persons with disability; 10+ employees threshold for establishments). Since statement 1 (approval by ESIC) and statement 2 (one-time opportunity incl. contractual and temporary workers) both match the scheme's design, options (a), (b) and (d) are eliminated. Remember the parallel EPFO scheme, ELI/ELI-linked drives and the earlier EPFO's Employees' Enrolment Campaign 2025 to avoid confusion.
explanations: Wrong: statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is also correct, so 'only 1' is incomplete.
Wrong: statement 2 is correct but statement 1 is also correct, so 'only 2' is incomplete.
Right: ESIC approved SPREE 2025 and it is a one-time registration opportunity covering contractual and temporary workers.
Wrong: at least one, in fact both, statements are correct.
keyfact: SPREE 2025: ESIC-approved, one-time registration amnesty (1 Jul-31 Dec 2025) covering contractual and temporary workers, with no past-dues inquiry.
option_notes: Option (a) '1 only' would mean that only the approval by ESIC is accurate. ESIC is the statutory body under the ESI Act, 1948 that administers health insurance and cash benefits for workers earning up to Rs 21,000 per month. It has its headquarters in New Delhi and is chaired by the Union Labour Minister. It includes representatives of employers, employees, states, Parliament and medical profession.

Option (b) '2 only' would mean that only the one-time opportunity description is accurate. SPREE is indeed a limited-period amnesty-type drive that waives scrutiny of past periods. It targets unregistered employers and employees, including contractual, temporary and casual workers. It is an administrative scheme and not a new Act, and operates through the ESIC online portal during its notified window in 2025.

Option (c) 'Both 1 and 2' is the correct choice. It reflects that ESIC, the nodal statutory authority, approved SPREE 2025 and that the scheme gives a one-time chance to register. ESIC's approach to widening coverage includes this drive, the ESI coverage threshold for establishments of 10 or more employees, and wider coverage of gig and platform workers under the Code on Social Security, 2020.

Option (d) 'Neither 1 nor 2' is wrong because both statements match the scheme's official design. Choosing this would imply SPREE was approved by another body, such as EPFO or the Ministry alone, or that it excluded contractual and temporary workers. Both are untrue; EPFO runs a different scheme, the Employees' Enrolment Campaign 2025, for PF coverage.
related: ESIC was set up under the ESI Act, 1948 and is chaired by the Union Labour Minister.
ESI wage ceiling is Rs 21,000 per month (Rs 25,000 for persons with disabilities).
ESI contribution rates: employer 3.25%, employee 0.75%, total 4% of wages.
SPREE 2025 ran from 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2025.
SPREE gives registration without inquiry for past periods; contributions are due from registration date.
Atal Bimit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana is ESIC's unemployment allowance scheme.
The Code on Social Security, 2020 subsumes nine labour laws including the ESI Act and EPF Act.
EPFO's parallel drive was the Employees' Enrolment Campaign 2025.
statements: 1 — Correct: SPREE 2025 was approved by the ESIC. ESIC is the statutory body created under the ESI Act, 1948, with the Union Labour Minister as chairperson. Its decisions on coverage, benefits and campaigns are taken in Corporation meetings. SPREE came out of such a decision (196th meeting, Dec 2024) and was rolled out from 1 July 2025 through ESIC's regional and sub-regional offices and the online portal.

2 — Correct: SPREE offers a one-time, time-bound opportunity for employers and employees not yet registered under the ESI Act to register. It covers contractual, temporary and casual workers if they meet eligibility criteria (wages up to Rs 21,000 per month). Registration under the scheme avoids inspection or recovery of past dues for the period before registration, and contributions are due only from the registration date. Window: 1 July to 31 December 2025, with registration through the ESIC portal and Shram Suvidha.
summary: Both statements are correct, so the answer is (c). SPREE 2025 was approved by the ESIC (at its 196th meeting, Dec 2024) and launched as a limited-period amnesty/special drive from 1 July 2025 to 31 Dec 2025 to bring unregistered employers and employees under ESI coverage.
topic_notes: The ESI Act, 1948 is a major social security law providing medical, sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants' and funeral benefits. The scheme is run by ESIC, a corporate body with headquarters in New Delhi, with the Union Labour and Employment Minister as chairperson and the Union Minister of State as vice-chairman; the Director General is the chief executive. The Medical Benefit Council and Standing Committee assist it. Coverage: factories and notified establishments with 10 or more persons (20 in some states earlier), employees earning up to Rs 21,000 per month (Rs 25,000 for persons with disabilities). Contributions: employer 3.25% and employee 0.75% of wages, total 4%. Employees earning up to Rs 176 per day are exempt from the employee contribution. Contribution periods are April-September and October-March, with benefit periods that follow. SPREE 2025 is a special registration drive that began on 1 July 2025 and was meant to run until 31 December 2025, offering employers a clean slate for registration without penal or past liabilities. The Code on Social Security, 2020 subsumes the ESI Act, EPF Act and others and extends the definition to gig and platform workers, and allows ESI coverage across all establishments, and hazardous occupations even with a single employee. ESIC also runs schemes such as Atal Bimit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana (unemployment allowance), Rajiv Gandhi Shramik Kalyan Yojana, and the ESIC's Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY tie-up for treatment. Related EPFO schemes include ELI (Employment Linked Incentive), Employees' Enrolment Campaign 2017 and the 2025 drive, and EDLI and EPS.

question: Zero Defect, Zero Effect’ is an initiative of 120. which one among the following Ministries of the Government of India ?
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
subject: Indian Economy
detail: The phrase 'Zero Defect, Zero Effect' was given by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in his Independence Day speech of 15 August 2014, as part of the Make in India campaign. The Ministry of MSME then built the ZED Certification Scheme, launched in 2016 and later revamped, to make MSMEs adopt quality manufacturing, cleaner production, energy efficiency, waste reduction and safe use of resources. 'Zero Defect' means products without flaws, so exports are not rejected in global markets. 'Zero Effect' means production without harming the environment. The scheme is implemented through the Quality Council of India (QCI), which developed the ZED Maturity Assessment Model. Certification has levels such as Bronze, Silver, Gold, then Diamond and Platinum in the revamped version, with subsidies for MSMEs, with higher rates for micro enterprises and for women-owned or SC/ST-owned units. Elimination: the Ministry of Heavy Industries deals with large industry, automobiles and capital goods (FAME, PLI for auto). The Ministry of Education deals with schools and higher education. The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship deals with Skill India and PMKVY. Only MSME deals with quality and sustainability for small manufacturers.
explanations: Incorrect: Heavy Industries handles schemes like FAME and auto PLI, not ZED certification for MSMEs.
Incorrect: The Ministry of Education handles education policy such as NEP 2020, with no link to manufacturing quality certification.
Incorrect: Skill Development and Entrepreneurship runs Skill India and PMKVY. ZED concerns quality and environmental standards in manufacturing, not skilling.
Correct: ZED Certification is run by the Ministry of MSME with the Quality Council of India, and promotes defect-free, eco-friendly manufacturing.
keyfact: Zero Defect, Zero Effect (ZED) = Ministry of MSME certification scheme with QCI; slogan from PM Modi, 15 Aug 2014.
option_notes: The Ministry of Heavy Industries oversees large and medium industries, including automobiles, heavy electrical equipment, machine tools and capital goods. It runs schemes like FAME India for electric vehicles and PLI for automobiles and advanced chemistry cell batteries. It also oversees many central public sector enterprises such as BHEL. Its administrative focus is on large industry, not small enterprise certification.

The Ministry of Education was renamed from the Ministry of Human Resource Development in July 2020 after NEP 2020. It has the Department of School Education and Literacy and the Department of Higher Education. It oversees bodies such as UGC, AICTE, NCERT and CBSE, and schemes like Samagra Shiksha, PM POSHAN and PM SHRI.

The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was created in November 2014. It runs Skill India Mission, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme. It also oversees ITIs and entrepreneurship promotion, but not ZED certification.

The Ministry of MSME promotes micro, small and medium enterprises. It runs schemes such as PMEGP, the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE), the MSME Champions scheme and ZED certification. It also oversees KVIC, NSIC and the Udyam registration portal. MSME classification was revised in 2020 using combined investment and turnover limits.
related: ZED slogan was given by PM Modi on 15 August 2014.
ZED Certification is implemented with the Quality Council of India (QCI).
QCI was set up in 1997 and comes under DPIIT.
Udyam Registration is the online MSME registration since 2020.
MSME classification (2020) combines investment and turnover criteria.
PMEGP is implemented by KVIC under the Ministry of MSME.
MSME Samadhaan addresses delayed payments to MSMEs.
summary: The answer is (d), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. 'Zero Defect, Zero Effect' (ZED) is a MSME initiative that encourages manufacturers to produce goods with no defects and no adverse environmental or ecological effect.
topic_notes: ZED stands for Zero Defect, Zero Effect. The slogan was coined by PM Modi on 15 August 2014 and tied to Make in India. The Ministry of MSME launched the ZED Certification Scheme in 2016, implemented with the Quality Council of India (QCI). The scheme aims to build quality consciousness, reduce waste, improve energy and resource efficiency, and prepare MSMEs for exports. The ZED Maturity Assessment Model covers areas such as manufacturing processes, quality, environment, safety and customer satisfaction. Certification levels are Bronze, Silver and Gold, with Diamond and Platinum in the revamped scheme. Subsidies are higher for micro enterprises, women-owned units, and units owned by SC/ST entrepreneurs or located in the North East and aspirational districts. Related MSME facts: classification since 1 July 2020 is Micro (investment up to Rs 1 crore and turnover up to Rs 5 crore), Small (up to Rs 10 crore and Rs 50 crore) and Medium (up to Rs 50 crore and Rs 250 crore). Udyam registration is online. Key schemes are PMEGP (credit-linked subsidy through KVIC), SFURTI (clusters for traditional industries), CGTMSE (collateral-free credit), MSME Samadhaan (delayed payments) and the Public Procurement Policy, which reserves 25 percent of government purchases from MSMEs. Other quality-related initiatives include the Lean Manufacturing Competitiveness Scheme and the Technology Centre Systems Programme. QCI was set up in 1997 as a non-profit with the Government and industry associations, and is under DPIIT.

question:
Which of the following statements relating to the recent steps taken by the “Employees? Provident Fund Organization (EPFO)” is/are correct ?
1. EPFO has enhanced member services by increasing the auto-settlement limit for advance claims from the existing = 1 lakh to 3 lakh.
2. EPFO first introduced auto-settlement of advance claims during the COVID-19 pandemic. Select the answer using the codes given below :
subject: Social Security
detail: EPFO's auto-settlement facility lets certain claims be processed by the IT system without human intervention, so money reaches the member's bank account in about 3 days. It began in April 2020 for the COVID-19 advance (non-refundable withdrawal under Para 68L), and was then extended in 2021 to illness, education, marriage and housing advances. The auto-settlement limit for advance claims was first Rs 50,000 (2020), then raised to Rs 1 lakh (2024). In May 2025 the Central Board of Trustees/EPFO raised it from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh, which is the recent step. Statement 1 states Rs 3 lakh, so it is wrong on the figure. Statement 2 is right on the origin during the pandemic. Elimination: since statement 1 has a wrong number, options (a) and (c) fall. Statement 2 is true, so (d) falls. Only (b) remains. Always check numbers carefully in current-affairs statements, because UPSC alters the figures.
explanations: Wrong, because statement 1 gives Rs 3 lakh while the actual enhanced limit is Rs 5 lakh, and statement 2 is also correct, so 'statement 1 only' is incorrect on both counts.
Correct, because only statement 2 is accurate: auto-settlement was first introduced during COVID-19 in 2020, while the Rs 3 lakh figure in statement 1 is wrong.
Wrong, because statement 1 does not hold. The limit was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh.
Wrong, because statement 2 is true, so the claim that neither is correct fails.
keyfact: EPFO auto-settlement began in 2020 (COVID-19); the limit was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh in 2025, not Rs 3 lakh.
option_notes: Option (a) says statement 1 only. It would be right only if the limit was raised to Rs 3 lakh, but the real figure is Rs 5 lakh (May 2025), and the 2020 origin makes statement 2 true as well.

Option (b) says statement 2 only. This matches the facts: auto-settlement began in 2020 under COVID-19 conditions, and the recent limit enhancement was Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh. Auto-settlement uses IT-based checks of KYC, Aadhaar seeding and bank details, and the claim is usually paid in about 3 days.

Option (c) says both statements are correct. It fails because of the wrong figure in statement 1. Rs 3 lakh is not the enhanced limit, which is Rs 5 lakh. Auto-settlement has been extended in steps: Rs 50,000 in 2020, Rs 1 lakh in 2024 and Rs 5 lakh in 2025.

Option (d) says neither is correct. It fails because statement 2 is true. EPFO started auto-settlement in the COVID-19 period in 2020 to reduce the time taken to process claims. The facility was later extended to many claim categories and higher limits, so the statement on its origin is valid.
related: Auto-settlement of advance claims began in 2020 with the COVID-19 advance.
Auto-settlement limit: Rs 50,000, then Rs 1 lakh (2024), then Rs 5 lakh (2025).
EPFO is administered through the Central Board of Trustees, chaired by the Union Labour Minister.
EPF Act was enacted in 1952; EPS in 1995; EDLI in 1976.
EPF interest rate for 2024-25 is 8.25%.
The COVID-19 advance was under Para 68L of the EPF Scheme, 1952.
Wage ceiling for compulsory EPF coverage is Rs 15,000 per month.
Employer's 12%: 8.33% to EPS and 3.67% to EPF.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: The limit was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh, not Rs 3 lakh. Auto-settlement means the system settles eligible claims without manual intervention, usually within about 3 days. It was introduced in 2020 for the COVID advance at Rs 50,000, and the limit was raised to Rs 1 lakh in 2024 (covering illness, education, marriage and housing). In May 2025 it was raised to Rs 5 lakh for these advance claims, which cut the pending workload and the processing time for members.

2 — Correct: Auto-settlement was first rolled out in April-May 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. At the time it covered the COVID-19 advance, a non-refundable withdrawal under Para 68L of the EPF Scheme, 1952, allowing 75% of the balance or three months' basic wage plus DA, whichever is lower. The first limit was Rs 50,000. In 2020 the facility was initially used for illness claims, then in 2021 it was extended to education, marriage and housing advances. Later it was extended further to cover other claim types too.
summary: The answer is (b): only statement 2 is correct. EPFO introduced auto-settlement of advance claims in April-May 2020 during COVID-19, but the recent limit enhancement was from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh (May 2025), not Rs 3 lakh.
topic_notes: EPFO is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, set up under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. It administers three schemes: the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme 1952 (EPF), the Employees' Pension Scheme 1995 (EPS) and the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme 1976 (EDLI). Its apex decision-making body is the Central Board of Trustees (CBT), chaired by the Union Labour Minister. The Central Provident Fund Commissioner is the chief executive officer. Recent member-service reforms include: auto-settlement of advance claims, first launched in 2020 and expanded step by step (Rs 50,000, then Rs 1 lakh, then Rs 5 lakh in 2025); the Universal Account Number (UAN) and UAN activation; Aadhaar-based and face-authentication technology for UAN generation; the joint declaration facility for correcting member details; EPFO 3.0, a digital upgrade of the IT system; and simplification of partial withdrawal rules. The EPF interest rate for 2023-24 was 8.25%, and the rate for 2024-25 was 8.25% as well. Other angles for future questions: the wage ceiling for compulsory coverage is Rs 15,000 per month; the employee contribution is 12% of basic wage plus DA; the employer's 12% is split into 8.33% to EPS and 3.67% to EPF; the Employees' Pension Scheme has a pensionable salary ceiling of Rs 15,000; and the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) scheme and the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (launched 2025) are connected to EPFO registration. Also recall the Code on Social Security, 2020, which subsumes the EPF Act.

question:
Which of the following statements relating to the recent steps taken by the Government of India under the ‘Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme’ is/are correct ?
1. ELI Scheme has an outlay of about = 1 lakh crore.
2. Establishments registered with the EPFO are required to hire at least two additional employees (with fewer than 50 employees) or five additional employees (with 50 or more employees), on a sustained basis for at least six months, to avail benefits under the ELI Scheme. Select the answer using the codes given below :
subject: Current Affairs
detail: The ELI Scheme was approved by the Union Cabinet on 1 July 2025 and is linked to the Budget 2024-25 package of employment and skilling schemes. It is also referred to as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana. Its outlay is ₹99,446 crore, about ₹1 lakh crore. It covers jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027, and it aims to support about 3.5 crore jobs, of which roughly 1.92 crore are first-time employees. Part A (employees) gives first-time EPFO-registered employees one month's wage, up to ₹15,000, in two instalments after 6 and 12 months of service. Salary up to ₹1 lakh is eligible, and a financial literacy module must be completed. Part B (employers) gives employers up to ₹3,000 per month for each additional employee for 2 years, extended to years 3 and 4 for the manufacturing sector. The employee must be on the job for at least 6 months. Eligible employers must be EPFO-registered. Those with fewer than 50 employees must add at least 2 additional employees, and those with 50 or more must add at least 5. These hires must be sustained for at least six months. Payments are made through DBT (Aadhaar Bridge Payment System) for employees and PAN-linked accounts for employers. Since both statements match the scheme, options (a), (b) and (d) are eliminated.
explanations: Wrong: statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 is also correct, so '1 only' is incomplete.
Wrong: statement 2 is correct, but statement 1 is also correct, so '2 only' is incomplete.
Right: the outlay is about ₹1 lakh crore (₹99,446 crore), and the hiring thresholds of 2 and 5 additional employees sustained for 6 months are correct.
Wrong: both statements accurately describe the ELI Scheme.
keyfact: ELI Scheme: ₹99,446 crore (about ₹1 lakh crore); employers must add 2 hires (under 50 staff) or 5 (50+ staff) for 6 months; employees get up to ₹15,000.
option_notes: Option (a) 1 only: it would be correct only if the hiring condition were wrong. Here the outlay of about ₹1 lakh crore is correct, but the option ignores the employer hiring condition, which is also accurate.
Option (b) 2 only: it would be correct only if the outlay figure were wrong. The employer condition is accurate, but the outlay of ₹99,446 crore is also correct, so this option is incomplete.

Option (c) Both 1 and 2: this is the correct answer. The scheme has an outlay of about ₹1 lakh crore. Establishments must add 2 (under 50 employees) or 5 (50 or more) additional employees, retained for at least 6 months, to claim the employer incentive.
Option (d) Neither 1 nor 2: this is wrong because both statements match the Cabinet-approved scheme, announced on 1 July 2025.
related: ELI Scheme outlay: ₹99,446 crore, approved by Cabinet on 1 July 2025
ELI period: jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027
Part A: first-timers get up to ₹15,000 (one month's wage) in two instalments
Part B: employers get up to ₹3,000 per month per additional employee for 2 years (4 years for manufacturing)
Employer threshold: 2 additional hires if under 50 employees, 5 if 50 or more, sustained for 6 months
Target: 3.5 crore jobs, including 1.92 crore first-time employees
Scheme was launched as Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on 15 August 2025
Predecessor schemes: PMRPY and ABRY, which paid employer EPF contributions
statements: 1 — Correct: the outlay is ₹99,446 crore, about ₹1 lakh crore. The Cabinet approved the scheme on 1 July 2025. It is funded by the Centre and is meant to generate about 3.5 crore jobs over two years. It applies to jobs created from 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027. It was announced in the Union Budget 2024-25 as one of the PM's package schemes (Scheme A: first-timers; Scheme B: manufacturing job creation; Scheme C: support to employers). The Ministry of Labour and Employment implements it, with EPFO as the delivery agency. The scheme was later branded Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, launched around 15 August 2025.

2 — Correct: an EPFO-registered establishment with fewer than 50 employees must hire at least 2 additional employees, and one with 50 or more must hire at least 5. These additional hires must be sustained for at least 6 months. This is the employer-side Part B. Incentives go up to ₹3,000 per month per additional employee, tiered by wage: up to ₹10,000 wages gets ₹1,000, ₹10,000-20,000 gets ₹2,000, and ₹20,000-1 lakh gets ₹3,000. Incentives run for 2 years, and for manufacturing the benefit extends to the 3rd and 4th years. Payments go to the employer's PAN-linked account, and the employees must be EPFO-registered with a UAN generated through the Face Authentication Technology (FAT).
summary: Answer: (c) Both 1 and 2. The Union Cabinet approved the ELI Scheme (renamed 'Employment Linked Incentive Scheme') on 1 July 2025 with an outlay of about ₹99,446 crore, which is roughly ₹1 lakh crore. Employers must hire the stated minimum number of additional employees and retain them for at least six months, so both statements are correct.
topic_notes: The Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) Scheme was announced in Budget 2024-25 as part of the PM's package for employment and skilling, with a central outlay of ₹2 lakh crore over five years. The Union Cabinet approved the ELI Scheme on 1 July 2025 with an outlay of ₹99,446 crore. It covers jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027, with a target of 3.5 crore jobs, of which 1.92 crore are first-time employees. It was later launched as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on 15 August 2025. Part A is for first-time employees registered with EPFO. They get one month's EPF wage, up to ₹15,000, paid in two instalments after 6 and 12 months of service. Wages up to ₹1 lakh are eligible. Part of the amount is held in a savings instrument or deposit account for a time, and a financial literacy programme is required. Part B is for employers. It gives up to ₹3,000 per month for each additional employee for 2 years, and the benefit extends to years 3 and 4 for the manufacturing sector. Wage slabs: up to ₹10,000 gets ₹1,000; ₹10,000-20,000 gets ₹2,000; ₹20,000-1 lakh gets ₹3,000. Hiring thresholds are 2 additional employees for establishments with fewer than 50 employees and 5 for those with 50 or more, all sustained for at least 6 months. The Ministry of Labour and Employment implements the scheme and EPFO operates it. Payments to employees go by DBT through the Aadhaar Bridge Payment System, and employers receive payments in PAN-linked accounts. The scheme replaces the earlier Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) and the ABRY (Atmanirbhar Bharat Rozgar Yojana), under which the government paid the employer's EPF contribution for new employees. Related ideas include the Universal Account Number (UAN) and Face Authentication Technology for UAN generation.

question: The Union Cabinet had approved a new Framework on Currency Swap Arrangement with which regional bloc for the period 2024 — 2027 ?
options: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
detail: The RBI's SAARC Currency Swap Facility was first launched in 2012 and revised in 2019. It is a standby facility that gives SAARC members short-term liquidity support for balance of payments problems. The Framework for 2024-27 was approved in 2024, and the RBI issued it on 18 February 2024. Under it, the total swap amount is US$2 billion. Within that total, US$1 billion is available in US dollars or euros, and a separate rupee window of up to Rs 250 billion is available. Swaps are drawn in tranches, and the RBI offers the facility to members as a standby arrangement, with its own terms and conditions. India has used this facility to help neighbours such as Sri Lanka and the Maldives during financial stress. The elimination logic is that the facility is explicitly named after SAARC. India has no such RBI-run standing framework with the African Union or the EU as blocs. ASEAN is a different case: India has bilateral swap arrangements with some individual countries, such as Japan, but not an ASEAN-wide framework of this kind. The SAARC option is therefore the only one that fits.
explanations: Correct. The Cabinet approved the RBI's SAARC Currency Swap Framework for 2024-27, offering a swap facility to SAARC members.
Incorrect. India has no such RBI swap framework with the African Union. Its engagement with Africa runs through other channels, such as lines of credit and the India-Africa Forum Summit.

Incorrect. ASEAN has no such facility with India. The swap facility is meant for South Asian neighbours. ASEAN has its own Chiang Mai Initiative Multilateralisation (CMIM) with China, Japan and South Korea, and India is not a part of it.
Incorrect. India has no currency swap framework with the EU as a bloc. The EU is linked to India mainly through trade negotiations and the euro-denominated swap window within the SAARC framework.
keyfact: The RBI's SAARC Currency Swap Framework for 2024-27 offers US$2 billion in dollars or euros, plus an INR window of Rs 250 billion.
option_notes: SAARC was founded in 1985 in Dhaka and has its secretariat in Kathmandu. It has 8 members: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, the Maldives and Afghanistan. Its summits have been stalled since 2014 (Kathmandu), and the 2016 Islamabad summit was postponed. The RBI's swap facility for SAARC members was started in 2012 and has been renewed since then. Its current framework runs 2024-27.

The African Union was launched in 2002 as the successor to the Organisation of African Unity (OAU, 1963). It is headquartered in Addis Ababa and has 55 member states. The G20 granted it permanent membership at the 2023 New Delhi summit, an initiative pushed by India. It has no currency swap framework with the RBI.

ASEAN was formed in 1967 through the Bangkok Declaration. It is headquartered in Jakarta and has 10 members, with Timor-Leste admitted as the 11th member in 2025. India is a dialogue partner and has an FTA in goods with ASEAN (AITIGA), which is under review. India has no ASEAN-wide currency swap framework.

The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 member states, as the UK left in 2020 (Brexit). Its headquarters are in Brussels. Its single currency is the euro, used by 20 countries (21 with Bulgaria joining in 2026). India and the EU have been negotiating an FTA, and the EU is one of India's largest trading partners. There is no RBI swap framework with the EU.
related: The SAARC swap facility was launched in 2012 and revised in 2019.
The 2024-27 framework carries a total of US$2 billion, plus an INR window of Rs 250 billion.
SAARC was founded in 1985 and its secretariat is in Kathmandu.
The SAARC member count is 8, including Afghanistan, which joined in 2007.
India-Japan bilateral swap arrangement: up to US$75 billion.
The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement is a US$100 billion pooled facility.
summary: The answer is (a) SAARC. The Union Cabinet approved the RBI's SAARC Currency Swap Framework for 2024-27, which lets SAARC member countries draw on a swap facility in US dollars, euros or Indian rupees to meet short-term foreign exchange needs.
topic_notes: A currency swap is an agreement under which two central banks exchange currencies at an agreed rate and reverse the exchange later. It gives the borrower short-term foreign exchange liquidity without drawing down reserves. The RBI runs the SAARC Currency Swap Facility under a framework first issued in 2012 and revised in 2019, and the current one covers 2024-27. Key features: a total of US$2 billion, with US$1 billion in dollars or euros and a separate INR window of Rs 250 billion. Each swap draw has a fixed tenor, and members apply to the RBI. Beneficiaries have included Sri Lanka, the Maldives, Bhutan and Bangladesh. Other angles for UPSC: India has bilateral swap lines, for example with Japan (up to US$75 billion), and uses local-currency settlement with countries such as the UAE. The RBI has also allowed rupee vostro accounts for settling trade with other countries since 2022. The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (US$100 billion) is a multilateral pooled facility. The Chiang Mai Initiative is the East Asian one, and the IMF is the global lender of last resort. Other related points are the SAARC Development Fund and the BIMSTEC grouping, and India's push for rupee internationalisation, which includes the UPI link with Singapore, the UAE and others.

detail: The Allahabad Pillar inscription, composed by Harishena, glorifies Samudragupta's conquests. The Aihole inscription, composed by the poet Ravikirti in Sanskrit, records Pulakeshin II's victory over Harsha and is dated to 634 CE. The Mandasor inscription of the Malava era 493/529 CE records the construction of a Sun temple by a silk-weavers guild during the reign of Kumaragupta I with Bandhuvarman as the local ruler. The Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri hills near Bhubaneswar in Brahmi script is that of Kharavela of the Mahameghavahana dynasty (Chedi). Gautamiputra Satakarni is known from Nashik inscription of his mother Gautami Balasri. Elimination: spotting the single wrong pair gives 'only three'.
explanations: Wrong: three pairs are correct.
Wrong: more than two pairs are correct.
Correct: pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched.
Wrong: pair 4 is mismatched.
keyfact: Hathigumpha = Kharavela; Aihole = Pulakeshin II; Allahabad = Samudragupta.

summary: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct; pair 4 is wrong because the Hathigumpha inscription belongs to Kharavela of Kalinga, not Gautamiputra Satakarni. Hence only three pairs are correct.

detail: The pH scale is logarithmic: pH = -log[H+]. A fall of one pH unit means a tenfold rise in H+ concentration, so pH 3 has ten times the H+ of pH 4. Sodium carbonate is a salt of a strong base (NaOH) and a weak acid (carbonic acid); it hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution that turns red litmus blue. The ionic product of water Kw rises with temperature, so at higher temperatures pure water has [H+] greater than 10^-7 M and pH below 7, yet it remains neutral because [H+] = [OH-]. Elimination: statement 3 is false, which removes options b, c and d, leaving a.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are true and statement 3 is false.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is false because neutral pH varies with temperature.
Wrong: it includes statement 3 and excludes statement 2, which is true.
Wrong: statement 3 is false, so not all three are correct.
keyfact: Neutral pH equals 7 only at 25°C; each pH unit is a tenfold change in H+ concentration.
question:

Human blood pH is about 7.35 to 7.45.

statements: 1 — Correct: pH is logarithmic, so each unit change means a tenfold change in H+ concentration.
2 — Correct: Na2CO3 undergoes basic hydrolysis and gives an alkaline solution (washing soda).
3 — Incorrect: Kw depends on temperature; neutral pH is 7 only at 25°C. Pure water at 100°C has pH of about 6 but is still neutral.
subject: General Science
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the ionic product of water changes with temperature, so neutral pH is 7 only at 25°C.

detail: The MPC is a statutory body created by the Finance Act 2016, which amended the RBI Act 1934. It has six members: three from the RBI (the Governor as ex-officio Chairperson, the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, and one officer nominated by the Central Board) and three external members appointed by the Centre. The Governor votes like every other member and has a second, casting vote when votes are tied. External members hold office for four years and cannot be reappointed. The numerical inflation target is notified by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI, and the MPC works to achieve it. Elimination: statements 3 and 4 are both wrong, so options (c) and (d) fall away. Statement 1 is a well-known provision, so option (a) falls away.
explanations: Incorrect: this would require only one correct statement, but statements 1 and 2 are both correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.
Incorrect: statements 3 and 4 are wrong, so three cannot be correct.
Incorrect: statements 3 and 4 are factually wrong.
keyfact: MPC: 6 members (3 RBI + 3 external), Governor has a casting vote, external members serve 4 years with no reappointment, and the Centre sets the inflation target.

detail: Section 14 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 provides for recognition of a sole negotiating union. A trade union with the support of 51% or more of workers on the muster roll is recognised as the sole negotiating union. If no union has 51%, the employer constitutes a negotiating council. The council includes representatives of every union that has the support of at least 20% of workers on the muster roll. The aim is to give a single, representative voice for negotiation with the employer, and the status is valid for three years. Elimination: 10% is too low and would fragment the council, while 25% and 33% are plausible but not the statutory figure. The 20% figure is the threshold to remember.
explanations: Incorrect. 10% is not the statutory threshold for membership of the negotiating council.
Correct. Unions with at least 20% support on the muster roll are represented in the negotiating council.
Incorrect. 25% is a distractor and not in the Code.
Incorrect. 33% is a distractor and not in the Code.
keyfact: IR Code: 51% gives a sole negotiating union; otherwise a negotiating council of unions with at least 20% support.
options: 10 per cent of the workers on the muster roll

related: A sole negotiating union needs the support of 51% or more of workers on the muster roll.

The Code's trade union provisions replaced the Trade Unions Act, 1926.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is 20 per cent. A trade union with at least 51% support becomes the sole negotiating union. If none has that support, the negotiating council is made up of representatives of unions with at least 20% support.

detail: Under the ESI Act, the standard sickness benefit is a periodical cash payment of about 70 per cent of the average daily wage. It is available for up to 91 days in any two consecutive benefit periods, subject to the contribution conditions. Extended sickness benefit is a different benefit for certain long-term diseases such as tuberculosis. It is paid at a higher rate of 80 per cent and for up to 124 days. The question asks about the standard benefit, so the numbers must match that benefit alone. Options (a), (b) and (c) each mix in the 80 per cent or 124-day figures from the extended benefit. Only option (d) pairs the correct rate and period for the standard benefit.
explanations: Incorrect: 80 per cent is the rate for extended sickness benefit, and 91 days is the limit for the standard benefit, so the pairing is wrong.
Incorrect: the rate is correct, but 124 days is the period for extended sickness benefit.
Incorrect: both figures belong to the extended sickness benefit for specified long-term diseases.
Correct: standard sickness benefit is 70 per cent of wages for a maximum of 91 days in two consecutive benefit periods.
keyfact: ESI standard sickness benefit is 70% of wages for 91 days; extended sickness benefit is 80% for up to 124 days.
question: Under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, the standard sickness benefit payable to an insured person is paid at the rate of ___ of the average daily wages, for a maximum of ___ days in any two consecutive benefit periods.
related: Extended sickness benefit is paid at 80 per cent for up to 124 days for specified diseases.
Enhanced sickness benefit at 100 per cent of wages is paid for sterilisation (vasectomy or tubectomy).
ESI maternity benefit is paid at 100 per cent of wages for 26 weeks.
Dependants' benefit for employment injury death is payable at 90 per cent of wages.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The answer is 70 per cent for a maximum of 91 days in any two consecutive benefit periods. The 80 per cent and 124 days figures belong to the separate extended sickness benefit.

detail: Chandrayaan-3 soft-landed on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to do so near the south polar region. The Government declared 23 August as National Space Day, and it was first celebrated in 2024. The International Astronomical Union ratified the name Shiv Shakti Point for the landing site. Names of other Indian lunar sites are a common trap. Tiranga Point is the Chandrayaan-2 Vikram impact site, and Jawahar Sthal is the Chandrayaan-1 Moon Impact Probe site. To eliminate options, first fix the date: 23 August matches the landing, so option (c) fails. Then separate the three site names by mission: Chandrayaan-1 (Jawahar Sthal), Chandrayaan-2 (Tiranga Point) and Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti).
explanations: Correct: the Chandrayaan-3 landing site is Shiv Shakti Point, and 23 August is National Space Day.
Incorrect: Jawahar Sthal is the Chandrayaan-1 Moon Impact Probe site, not the Chandrayaan-3 landing site.
Incorrect: the site name is right, but 15 August is Independence Day, not National Space Day.
Incorrect: Tiranga Point is the Chandrayaan-2 impact site, although the date is right.
keyfact: Chandrayaan-3 landed on 23 Aug 2023 at Shiv Shakti Point; 23 August is National Space Day.
question: Which one of the following correctly identifies the name given to the Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander's touchdown site near the lunar south pole, and the date on which India now observes National Space Day?
related: Chandrayaan-3 was launched on 14 July 2023 on an LVM3-M4 rocket.
India is the fourth country to achieve a soft landing on the Moon, after the USSR, the USA and China.
Chandrayaan-2 (2019) carried the Vikram lander, which crashed, and the Pragyan rover.
First National Space Day was observed in 2024.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: The Chandrayaan-3 landing site is called Shiv Shakti Point, and National Space Day is observed on 23 August. The date marks the day in 2023 when Vikram soft-landed near the lunar south pole.

detail: The mandative subjunctive is used in a that-clause after verbs such as insist, demand, recommend, suggest, propose, require and request, and after adjectives like essential, vital and imperative. The verb takes its base form regardless of the subject's number or the sentence's tense, for example 'The committee recommended that he resign.' Here, 'insisted that the register be maintained' follows the pattern. Option (a) 'is' is an indicative form and does not suit the demand sense. Option (b) 'was being' is a progressive past and does not express the required obligation. Option (d) 'would have been' is a conditional perfect and does not fit. Learn the trigger verbs and the base-form rule.
explanations: Incorrect: indicative mood, which does not convey a demand in standard usage.
Incorrect: progressive past form, which does not fit the mandative pattern.
Correct: base form 'be' is required in the subjunctive after 'insisted that'.
Incorrect: conditional perfect form, which is grammatically unsuitable here.
keyfact: After insist, demand, suggest or recommend, a that-clause uses the base-form verb (subjunctive).
question:
Choose the option that correctly fills the blank:

"The auditor insisted that the register ______ maintained in the prescribed format."
related: It is essential that every employee be informed.
I suggest that he apply immediately.
If I were you (hypothetical subjunctive).
The board demanded that the report be submitted.
subject: General English
summary: After verbs of insistence, suggestion or demand, a 'that' clause takes the subjunctive, using the base form of the verb. So 'be maintained' is correct.

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 is the first Indian labour statute to define 'gig worker', 'platform worker' and 'aggregator'. It lets the Central Government frame schemes covering life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, old age protection and similar matters for these workers. Aggregators fund the schemes through a contribution fixed by the Central Government. The contribution must fall between 1 and 2 per cent of annual turnover, and it cannot exceed 5 per cent of the amount the aggregator pays or owes to such workers. To eliminate options: b, c and d use ranges and ceilings that do not appear in the Code. Option d also drops the payment-linked ceiling, which is an essential feature. Candidates should remember both limbs, the turnover band and the payment cap.
explanations: Correct. The band is 1 to 2 per cent of annual turnover, with a cap of 5 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers.
Incorrect. A 3 to 5 per cent band and a 10 per cent cap are not what the Code provides.
Incorrect. A 0.5 to 1 per cent band and a 2 per cent cap understate the statutory limits.
Incorrect. The band is wrong, and the Code does contain a ceiling tied to payments made to workers.
keyfact: Aggregator contribution: 1-2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers.
options: 1 to 2 per cent of the aggregator's annual turnover, subject to a ceiling of 5 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig workers and platform workers
3 to 5 per cent of the aggregator's annual turnover, subject to a ceiling of 10 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig workers and platform workers
0.5 to 1 per cent of the aggregator's annual turnover, subject to a ceiling of 2 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig workers and platform workers
2 to 4 per cent of the aggregator's annual turnover, with no ceiling linked to payments made to workers
question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, the Central Government may notify a scheme for gig workers and platform workers that is funded in part by contributions from aggregators. Within which limits may the aggregator's contribution be fixed?
related: The Code on Social Security, 2020 defines aggregator, gig worker and platform worker.
Gig and platform workers are registered on a portal so that scheme benefits can reach them.
The Code provides for a Social Security Fund to finance schemes for unorganised, gig and platform workers.
The four Labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is option a. The Code lets the Central Government fix the aggregator's contribution at 1 to 2 per cent of annual turnover, capped at 5 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers.
topic: Code on Social Security - Gig and Platform Workers

detail: Females are XX and males are XY. Every egg carries an X chromosome, while sperm carry either X or Y, so the father's contribution decides the child's sex. Humans have 46 chromosomes arranged in 23 pairs: 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes. Colour blindness (red-green) is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome. Males have only one X, so one defective allele produces the trait, whereas females need two copies. Since all three statements hold, option d is the answer.
explanations: Incorrect: it leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
Incorrect: it leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
Incorrect: it leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
keyfact: The father's gamete (X or Y) determines the sex of the child.
question:
Consider the following statements about genetics and heredity in humans:
1. The sex of a child is determined by the type of sex chromosome contributed by the father.
2. Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, including one pair of sex chromosomes.
3. Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait, so it is more common in males than in females.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

Haemophilia is also X-linked recessive.

Mendel worked on pea plants.
statements: 1 — Correct: eggs always carry X, while sperm carry X or Y.
2 — Correct: 22 autosome pairs plus one sex chromosome pair give 23 pairs.
3 — Correct: males are hemizygous for X-linked genes, so the recessive trait shows more often in them. Haemophilia is another example.
subject: General Science
summary: All three statements are correct. The father's gamete (X or Y) determines the child's sex, humans have 23 chromosome pairs, and X-linked recessive traits appear more often in males.

detail: National income accounting links production-side aggregates through the tax and subsidy wedge. GDP at market prices equals GVA at basic prices plus product taxes minus product subsidies. Product taxes, such as GST and customs duties, are levied per unit of a good or service, so they are excluded from basic prices. Other taxes on production, such as property tax and land revenue, are not tied to the volume of output. They remain in basic prices, net of other production subsidies. For the national aggregates, GNP is GDP plus net factor income from abroad (NFIA), where NFIA is factor income received from abroad minus factor income paid abroad. Net National Product is GNP minus depreciation (consumption of fixed capital). To eliminate options, note that statements 1 and 2 are standard and consistent with each other. Statement 3 is a classic reversal, so 'Only two' is the answer.
explanations: Incorrect. Two statements, not one, are correct.
Correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is wrong.
Incorrect. Statement 3 reverses the sign of NFIA, so not all three are correct.
Incorrect. Statements 1 and 2 are accurate.
keyfact: GVA at basic prices + net product taxes = GDP at market prices; GNP = GDP + NFIA.
question:
With reference to the measurement of national income in India, consider the following statements:
1. Gross Value Added at basic prices equals GDP at market prices minus taxes on products plus subsidies on products.
2. Basic prices include other taxes on production, such as property tax, net of other subsidies on production.
3. Gross National Product at market prices equals GDP at market prices minus net factor income from abroad.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies.
GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad.
NNP = GNP − depreciation (consumption of fixed capital).
Product taxes include GST and customs duties; production taxes include property tax.
statements: 1 — Correct: GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes − product subsidies, so the rearranged form is right.
2 — Correct: Basic prices exclude product taxes but include other production taxes net of other production subsidies.

3 — Incorrect: GNP = GDP + NFIA, not GDP − NFIA. Facts: NNP at market prices = GNP − depreciation. India's headline growth is reported as real GDP and GVA, and the difference between them is net product taxes.
subject: Economy
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is (b). Statement 3 reverses the relationship, because GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad.

detail: Epigraphy questions in UPSC often test script, direction, language, and region. Brahmi is the ancestor of most Indian scripts and was written left to right. James Prinsep deciphered it in the 1830s, helped by the bilingual Indo-Greek coins used for Kharosthi and by the repeated formulae of Ashokan edicts. Kharosthi was used in the north-west, in places such as Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, and was written right to left, like Aramaic, from which it derives. Ashoka's inscriptions at Kandahar include Greek and Aramaic versions, which shows he adapted language and script to local audiences. To eliminate options, spot that statement 3 uses the absolute word 'all' and 'only', which is a typical trap. Once 3 is rejected, options (b) and (d) go. Confirming either statement 1 or 2 then narrows the answer to (c).
explanations: Incorrect: it omits statement 2, which is also correct.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3, which is false, and omits statement 2.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate and statement 3 is false.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false because Greek and Aramaic inscriptions exist in Afghanistan.
keyfact: Brahmi was deciphered by James Prinsep, and Kharosthi runs right to left.
question:
With reference to the scripts and inscriptions of ancient India, consider the following statements:
1. The Brahmi script was deciphered in the 1830s through the work of James Prinsep.
2. The Kharosthi script was written from right to left.
3. All the Ashokan inscriptions found in present-day Afghanistan are in the Prakrit language written only in the Brahmi script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts are in Kharosthi.
The Kandahar inscriptions include Greek and Aramaic.
Brahmi is written left to right and is the ancestor of most Indian scripts.
Prinsep served in the Asiatic Society of Bengal.
statements: 1 — Correct: Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in the 1830s, which made it possible to read Ashokan edicts.
2 — Correct: Kharosthi ran right to left and was used in the north-west.

3 — Incorrect: Ashokan inscriptions at Kandahar and elsewhere in Afghanistan include Greek and Aramaic versions, so they are not only in Prakrit in Brahmi. The Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts in Pakistan are in Kharosthi.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statement 3 is incorrect. Ashoka's edicts in Afghanistan include Greek and Aramaic versions, so they are not only in Prakrit in Brahmi.

detail: The Marxist perspective holds that the employment relationship is exploitative because of the divergent interests of capital and labour. Conflict is therefore structural and unions are instruments of class struggle, aiming at transformation of society. The unitary perspective sees the organisation as one team with shared goals, treating conflict as pathological and unions as unnecessary. The pluralistic perspective accepts multiple interest groups, treating conflict as manageable through collective bargaining. The trusteeship perspective, associated with Gandhi, holds that owners are trustees of wealth for society, and emphasises cooperation and moral obligation. Matching the key words conflict, class struggle and social change leads directly to the Marxist perspective.
explanations: Correct: it sees conflict as structural, and unions as part of the class struggle.
Incorrect: the unitary view treats conflict as abnormal and unions as unnecessary.
Incorrect: the pluralistic view accepts conflict as manageable through bargaining, not as grounds for overthrowing the system.
Incorrect: the trusteeship view is Gandhian and stresses cooperation and moral duty.
keyfact: Marxist/radical perspective: conflict is structural, rooted in class struggle.
question: Which one of the following perspectives of industrial relations regards conflict as inherent in the employment relationship and sees trade unions as a result of the capitalist system's class structure, aiming at fundamental change in society?
related: Unitary perspective: the organisation is a team with one source of authority.
Pluralistic perspective: multiple interest groups and collective bargaining.
Trusteeship perspective: Gandhian, owners as trustees.
Marxist perspective is also called the radical perspective.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: Option (a) is correct. The Marxist (radical) perspective views industrial conflict as rooted in class struggle under capitalism, and sees unions as vehicles for broader social change.

detail: Invasive alien species are non-native species that spread aggressively and harm native biodiversity, livelihoods or ecosystems. Lantana camara, from tropical America, was introduced as an ornamental and now overruns forests and degrades habitats. Mikania micrantha, called the 'mile-a-minute' weed, comes from Central and South America and smothers vegetation in the north-east and Western Ghats. Eichhornia crassipes (water hyacinth) comes from South America and chokes water bodies and depletes oxygen. Prosopis cineraria is the native khejri tree of Rajasthan and the arid north-west, and is the State tree of Rajasthan. Its look-alike, Prosopis juliflora, is the invasive one. The trap is the similar genus name. Once you know that khejri is native, options containing 2 are eliminated, which leaves (a).
explanations: Correct. Lantana, Mikania and water hyacinth are all invasive aliens in India.
Incorrect. It includes Prosopis cineraria, which is native, and leaves out water hyacinth.
Incorrect. It includes the native khejri and leaves out two invasive species.
Incorrect. It includes the native Prosopis cineraria.
keyfact: Khejri (Prosopis cineraria) is native, whereas Prosopis juliflora is the invasive species.
question:
Consider the following plants:
1. Lantana camara
2. Prosopis cineraria
3. Mikania micrantha
4. Eichhornia crassipes
Which of the above are invasive alien species in India?
related: Prosopis juliflora (from Central and South America) is invasive in dry regions.
Parthenium hysterophorus (congress grass) is an invasive weed from tropical America.
Prosopis cineraria is the State tree of Rajasthan.
The Biological Diversity Act 2002 has provisions on invasive alien species through the 2023 amendment.
Invasive alien species are a major direct driver of biodiversity loss.
subject: Environment
summary: Lantana camara, Mikania micrantha and Eichhornia crassipes are all invasive aliens in India, so the answer is (a). Prosopis cineraria (khejri) is native to the arid parts of India.

detail: Surface salinity peaks in the subtropics, around 20 to 30 degrees latitude, where evaporation is high and rainfall is low. At the equator, heavy rain lowers salinity. The Baltic Sea is brackish because of large river inflow, low evaporation in cool latitudes and limited exchange with the open ocean. The Dead Sea is not part of the ocean at all. It is an inland hypersaline lake with salinity roughly ten times the average ocean value, near 340 parts per thousand, against about 35 for the ocean. Elimination: spotting statement 3 as wrong removes options (c) and (d), and statement 1 is a well-known fact, which confirms option (b).
explanations: Wrong, because statement 2 is also correct.
Correct, because statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 is not.
Wrong, because statement 3 is incorrect.
Wrong, because statement 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: Ocean surface salinity peaks in the subtropics, not at the equator; the Dead Sea is a hypersaline lake.
question:

2. The Baltic Sea has lower salinity than the open ocean average because of high freshwater inflow and low evaporation.
3. The Dead Sea is an ocean basin with salinity close to the oceanic average.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Average ocean salinity is about 35 per mille.
Lake Van in Turkey is a highly saline soda lake.

statements: 1 — Correct: Evaporation exceeds precipitation in the subtropics.

The average ocean salinity is about 35 parts per thousand.
subject: Geography
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is wrong. The Dead Sea is a landlocked hypersaline lake, far saltier than the ocean.

detail: The FRBM Review Committee chaired by N.K. Singh (2017) recommended using the debt-to-GDP ratio as the primary fiscal anchor, with a target of 60% for the general government (40% for the Centre and 20% for States) by 2023, and the fiscal deficit as the operating target, with a path to 3% of GDP. It also proposed a fiscal council, which has not been established. The Finance Act 2018 amended the FRBM Act to incorporate the debt anchor; the Act retains an escape clause allowing deviation for specified grounds such as national security, war, national calamity and a sharp fall in real output. Option b is wrong because the revenue deficit was not the principal target. Option c is wrong because the escape clause was retained and broadened to include a sharp fall in output. Option d is invented.
explanations: Correct: the debt anchor with the fiscal deficit as the operating target reflects the N.K. Singh recommendations.
Wrong: the revenue deficit was not made the principal target, and the debt target covers the general government.
Wrong: the escape clause remains in the framework.
Wrong: there is no such requirement to eliminate the primary deficit in three years.
keyfact: The N.K. Singh Committee: the debt-to-GDP ratio is the anchor (60% for the general government) and the fiscal deficit is the operating target.
options: It prescribes a debt-to-GDP target for the general government and treats the fiscal deficit as the operational target
It prescribes a debt-to-GDP target for the Central Government and treats the revenue deficit as the principal target
It abolished the escape clause that permits deviation from fiscal targets
It requires the Central Government to eliminate the primary deficit within three years
