detail: The Vice-President is elected under Article 66 by an electoral college of members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members. Unlike the Presidential election, State legislators do not vote. The system is proportional representation by single transferable vote, with a secret ballot. The 2025 election was a by-election in the sense that it was held before the term ended, because Dhankhar resigned in July 2025 citing health reasons. Radhakrishnan, a former Governor of Maharashtra, was the NDA candidate. The Opposition fielded Justice B. Sudershan Reddy, a former Supreme Court judge. The other names are traps from earlier contests. Margaret Alva was the Opposition candidate in 2022. Gopalkrishna Gandhi was the Opposition candidate in 2017. Meira Kumar was the Opposition's Presidential candidate in 2017. Matching each name to its year eliminates the distractors.
explanations: Correct. Justice B. Sudershan Reddy, a former Supreme Court judge, was the joint Opposition nominee in 2025.
Incorrect. Margaret Alva was the Opposition candidate in the 2022 Vice-Presidential election, which Jagdeep Dhankhar won.
Incorrect. Gopalkrishna Gandhi was the Opposition candidate in 2017, when M. Venkaiah Naidu won.
Incorrect. Meira Kumar contested the 2017 Presidential election against Ram Nath Kovind, not the 2025 Vice-Presidential election.
keyfact: 2025 Vice-President: C. P. Radhakrishnan defeated the Opposition's Justice B. Sudershan Reddy.
question: In the Vice-Presidential election held in September 2025, after the resignation of Jagdeep Dhankhar, C. P. Radhakrishnan was elected as the Vice-President of India. Who was the Opposition (INDIA bloc) candidate he defeated?
related: Article 66 governs the election of the Vice-President.
The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
Only Members of Parliament, elected and nominated, form the electoral college for the Vice-President.
Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned in July 2025 before completing his term.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: The Opposition candidate was Justice (Retd.) B. Sudershan Reddy, a former Supreme Court judge. C. P. Radhakrishnan won comfortably and became the 15th Vice-President.

detail: Spring tides occur twice a month, at new moon (syzygy, with Sun and Moon on the same side) and at full moon (opposite sides). The gravitational pulls reinforce each other and produce the highest high tides and lowest low tides. Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon form roughly a right angle with the Earth, near the first and third quarters, and their pulls partly cancel. Perigee is when the Moon is closest to Earth. Tides are then stronger than average, producing perigean spring tides when it coincides with a new or full moon. So statement 3 confuses distance with alignment. The Bay of Fundy in Canada, a funnel-shaped inlet with resonance, has a tidal range of about 16 metres. Elimination logic: knowing statement 3 is wrong eliminates three options at once.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are right, and 3 is wrong.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3, which is wrong.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3, which is wrong, and leaves out statement 2.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false, so not all are correct.
keyfact: Spring tides depend on alignment (new and full moon); neap tides occur at quarter moons, not at perigee.
question:
With reference to tides, consider the following statements:
1. Spring tides occur at both new moon and full moon, when the Sun, Earth and Moon are aligned.
2. The Bay of Fundy is known for one of the highest tidal ranges in the world.
3. Neap tides occur when the Moon is at perigee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Spring and neap tides each occur about twice a month.
Perigee is the Moon's closest point to Earth and apogee its farthest.
Tidal bores occur in estuaries such as the Hooghly and Qiantang.
Kandla is a tidal port on the Gulf of Kutch.
statements: 1 — Correct: Spring tides occur at both new and full moon when the three bodies are in a line.
2 — Correct: The funnel shape and resonance of the Bay of Fundy produce a very high tidal range.
3 — Incorrect: Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles. Perigee increases tidal range.
subject: Geography
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Neap tides occur when the Sun and Moon are at right angles to the Earth (first and third quarters), not because of the Moon's perigee.

detail: ESIC was set up under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948, and is a statutory corporation, now governed by the Code on Social Security, 2020. It provides medical care, sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants' and funeral benefits. It is funded mainly by employer and employee contributions, with state governments bearing a share of medical care costs. Article 280 relates to the Finance Commission and has no link with ESIC. The statement that ESIC is funded entirely by the Centre is wrong, since the contributions are the primary source. The claim that it provides only cash benefits is wrong because medical benefit is the central feature of the scheme. Hence only option (a) holds.
explanations: Correct; ESIC is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
Wrong; Article 280 concerns the Finance Commission, not ESIC.
Wrong; funding is primarily from employer and employee contributions.
Wrong; ESIC provides medical benefit along with several cash benefits.
keyfact: ESIC is a statutory body under the 1948 Act, funded by employer and employee contributions.
options: ESIC is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
ESIC is a constitutional body under Article 280
ESIC is funded entirely by the Central Government
ESIC administers only cash benefits and not medical care
question: Which one of the following is the correct statement about the Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) and its scheme?
related: ESI Act was enacted in 1948.
ESIC's first implementation was at Kanpur and Delhi in 1952.
The Union Labour Minister chairs the ESI Corporation.
Benefits include medical, sickness, maternity, disablement, dependants' and funeral expenses.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: ESIC is a statutory body functioning under the Ministry of Labour and Employment. It was established under the ESI Act, 1948.

detail: The Indian Independence Act 1947 received royal assent on 18 July 1947 and took effect on 15 August 1947. It created two dominions, India and Pakistan, and ended British paramountcy, so princely states were technically free to join either dominion or, in theory, stay independent. The Constituent Assembly of each dominion was given the dual role of framing a constitution and acting as the legislature until a new constitution came into force. The Government of India Act 1935, suitably adapted, served as the interim constitution. All three statements correspond to the Act, so the full combination is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 3 is also correct.
Incorrect: statement 1 is also correct.
Incorrect: statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
keyfact: The Indian Independence Act 1947 lapsed British paramountcy and made the Constituent Assemblies sovereign legislatures.
question:
With reference to the Indian Independence Act, 1947, consider the following statements:
1. It provided for the partition of India into two independent dominions, India and Pakistan.
2. It ended the suzerainty of the British Crown over the princely states, leaving them free to accede to either dominion or remain independent.
3. It gave the Constituent Assemblies of the dominions power to make laws for their respective territories until a new constitution was framed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of independent India.
The Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947.
The Government of India Act 1935 was adapted as an interim constitution.
The Radcliffe Commission demarcated the boundaries of Punjab and Bengal.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Act created the dominions of India and Pakistan.
2 — Correct: Paramountcy lapsed and states could accede to either dominion or remain independent in theory.
3 — Correct: The Constituent Assemblies also acted as the legislatures of the dominions.
subject: Modern History
summary: All three statements are correct. The Act created two dominions, lapsed paramountcy over the princely states, and let the Constituent Assemblies act as legislatures.

detail: The NGT was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. Section 19 says it is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and is guided by principles of natural justice. Appeals against its orders lie directly to the Supreme Court within ninety days. Its jurisdiction covers civil cases with a substantial environmental question under seven laws listed in Schedule I: the Water Act 1974, the Water Cess Act 1977, the Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, the Air Act 1981, the Environment (Protection) Act 1986, the Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 and the Biological Diversity Act 2002. The Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 and the Indian Forest Act 1927 are not included. So statement 2 is incorrect, and the correct answer is 1 and 3 only.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 3 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct, and 2 is not.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong, and statement 1 is correct.
Incorrect: statement 2 is not correct, so not all three hold.
keyfact: NGT covers seven environmental laws (not the Wildlife Act or Indian Forest Act 1927), and appeals go to the Supreme Court.
question:
With reference to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) of India, consider the following statements:
1. It is not bound by the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by principles of natural justice.
2. Its jurisdiction extends to civil cases involving substantial environmental questions arising under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
3. An appeal against its order lies to the Supreme Court of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The NGT was established in 2010, and its principal bench is in New Delhi.
Regional benches are at Pune, Bhopal, Kolkata and Chennai.
The Indian Forest Act 1927 is outside NGT jurisdiction.
Article 21 has been interpreted to include the right to a healthy environment.
statements: 1 — Correct: The NGT follows natural justice and is not bound by the CPC.
2 — Incorrect: The Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 is not among the seven Acts in Schedule I of the NGT Act.
3 — Correct: Appeals lie to the Supreme Court under Section 22 of the NGT Act.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct and statement 2 is wrong. The NGT's jurisdiction does not cover the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

detail: Signed on 5 March 1931, the Gandhi–Irwin Pact ended the first phase of Civil Disobedience. Congress agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference, which Gandhi did in London in late 1931. The Government agreed to withdraw ordinances, release prisoners arrested in non-violent satyagraha, return confiscated property, and permit peaceful picketing and salt-making for domestic use by coastal residents. Prisoners convicted of violence were not released, and Gandhi's failure to secure commutation of the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru, executed on 23 March 1931, angered the youth at the Karachi Congress. Elimination: statement 2 is wrong, which rules out the options that include it.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 3 are accurate.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: statement 1 is true, so it cannot be omitted, and statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false.
keyfact: Gandhi–Irwin Pact (5 March 1931): Civil Disobedience suspended; prisoners of violence not released.
question:
Consider the following statements about the Gandhi–Irwin Pact of March 1931:
1. Gandhi agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and to participate in the Second Round Table Conference.
2. The Government agreed to release all political prisoners, including those convicted of violence.
3. The Government permitted peaceful picketing of liquor and foreign cloth shops and the making of salt for personal consumption by people living near the coast.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Lord Irwin was Viceroy from 1926 to 1931.
The Second Round Table Conference was held in late 1931.
The Karachi Congress was presided over by Vallabhbhai Patel.
Bhagat Singh was executed on 23 March 1931.
statements: 1 — Correct: Congress suspended Civil Disobedience and agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference.
2 — Incorrect: only prisoners of non-violent satyagraha were to be released, not those convicted of violence.
3 — Correct: peaceful picketing and domestic salt-making along the coast were allowed.
The pact is also called the Delhi Pact. The Karachi session of March 1931, presided over by Vallabhbhai Patel, endorsed it and adopted a resolution on Fundamental Rights.
subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Government did not agree to release prisoners convicted of violence, and it refused a commutation of Bhagat Singh's sentence.

detail: Article 20(2) says that no person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once. The Supreme Court has held that it applies only where there has been both a prosecution and a punishment before a court of law or a judicial tribunal. It does not cover departmental or administrative proceedings, because those are not judicial. Dismissal after a departmental inquiry therefore does not bar a later criminal trial for the same conduct. Statement-II states the legal principle, and it directly explains why Statement-I holds. Article 20 is also available to citizens and non-citizens alike, and it cannot be suspended during a National Emergency (Article 359(1), as amended by the 44th Amendment). Because both statements are correct and linked, the answer is the last option.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is the direct legal reason for Statement-I, so it is the correct explanation.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
Correct: both statements are accurate, and the court-or-tribunal requirement explains why departmental action does not bar a prosecution.
keyfact: Article 20(2) bars a second prosecution and punishment only when the first was before a court or judicial tribunal, so it does not cover departmental proceedings.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The protection against double jeopardy under Article 20(2) is not available to a government servant who is dismissed through a departmental inquiry and is subsequently prosecuted in a court of law for the same misconduct.
Statement-II: Article 20(2) bars only a second prosecution and punishment for the same offence before a court of law or a judicial tribunal.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Article 20(1) prohibits ex post facto criminal laws.
Article 20(3) protects against self-incrimination.
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.
Article 20 is available to citizens and non-citizens.
statements: Statement-I — Correct: a departmental dismissal is not a judicial punishment, so a later prosecution is not barred.
Statement-II — Correct: the double jeopardy bar needs both prosecution and punishment before a court or judicial tribunal, which also explains Statement-I.
Article 20 protects both citizens and non-citizens and cannot be suspended during an Emergency.
subject: Polity
summary: Both statements are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Article 20(2) applies only to prosecution and punishment before a court or judicial tribunal.
topic: Article 20 - Protection in respect of conviction

detail: The IR Code, 2020 gives a worker a statutory time limit for approaching the Tribunal on a dispute arising from discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination of service. The application must be made within two years of the date of the action. The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 contained no limitation period for such disputes, and in practice courts applied the principle of reasonable time. The Code also adds a grievance redressal mechanism inside industrial establishments with twenty or more workers. For elimination, 90 days and one year are shorter than the Code provides and are only plausible-sounding distractors. Three years is the limit for claims under the Code on Wages, which is a separate provision, so candidates should not confuse the two.
explanations: Incorrect. Ninety days is not the period the Code allows for approaching the Tribunal.
Incorrect. The Code allows more than one year.
Correct. The Code sets two years from the date of discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination.
Incorrect. Three years is the limit for wage claims under the Code on Wages, not for this dispute.
keyfact: IR Code: two years to raise a termination dispute before the Tribunal; the old ID Act had no limit.
question: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, a worker who has been discharged, dismissed, retrenched or otherwise had service terminated may, after the prescribed grievance and conciliation steps, raise the dispute directly before the Tribunal by application within what period from the date of the termination?
related: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 had no limitation period for such disputes.
Every industrial establishment with twenty or more workers must have a Grievance Redressal Committee.
The Grievance Redressal Committee must complete its proceedings within a prescribed time, and a worker aggrieved by its decision may seek conciliation.
Under the Code, a strike notice must be given sixty days before the strike.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is option c, two years. The IR Code allows a worker to apply directly to the Tribunal within two years of the discharge, dismissal, retrenchment or termination.

detail: Operation Sindoor was India's military response to the Pahalgam terror attack of 22 April 2025, in which 26 people, mostly tourists, were killed. The strikes began in the early hours of 7 May 2025 and targeted terror infrastructure in Pakistan and PoK. Hostilities between the two countries continued for a few days. They stopped after an understanding reached on 10 May 2025 between the two Directors General of Military Operations. This was a ceasefire arrangement. No treaty was signed. To solve this type of question, check each statement for absolute or formal wording. A claim of a 'formal peace treaty' is a typical exam trap, because the real event was only a cessation of hostilities. Eliminating statement 3 leaves options (a) and (b). Statement 2 is a core fact of the operation, so (b) is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 2 is also correct, so 'only 1' is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate, and statement 3 is wrong because no treaty was signed.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong, and this option leaves out statement 1.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false, so all three cannot be correct.
keyfact: Operation Sindoor (7 May 2025) followed the Pahalgam attack and ended with a ceasefire understanding on 10 May 2025, not a treaty.
question:
Consider the following statements about Operation Sindoor:
1. It was launched by India on 7 May 2025 in response to the terror attack at Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir on 22 April 2025.
2. The strikes were directed at terrorist-linked sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.
3. It concluded with a formal bilateral peace treaty signed by India and Pakistan in May 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Pahalgam attack: 22 April 2025
Operation Sindoor launched: 7 May 2025
Ceasefire understanding between the two DGMOs: 10 May 2025
India placed the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance after the Pahalgam attack
statements: 1 — Correct: Operation Sindoor began on 7 May 2025, after the Pahalgam attack of 22 April 2025.
2 — Correct: The strikes targeted terrorist-linked sites in Pakistan and PoK.
3 — Incorrect: Hostilities ended with a ceasefire understanding on 10 May 2025, not a formal peace treaty.
The name 'Sindoor' was chosen for its symbolism. The ceasefire was agreed between the two countries' DGMOs.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statement 3 is incorrect. The operation ended with a ceasefire understanding on 10 May 2025, not a formal peace treaty.

detail: Ways and Means Advances are short-term accommodation from the RBI to governments to tide over temporary mismatches between receipts and expenditure. They are not a tool for financing the deficit. Under Section 17(5) of the RBI Act, the advances must be repaid within three months from the date of making them. Normal WMA carries interest at the repo rate. Overdraft beyond the WMA limit is allowed only for a limited period and carries a higher interest rate, repo plus 2 percentage points for the Centre. For the Centre, overdraft cannot continue beyond ten consecutive working days. State Governments also have WMA and overdraft facilities under RBI schemes. Eliminate (a) because WMA must be repaid, (c) because overdraft is time-limited, and (d) because States have WMA.
explanations: Wrong: WMA is repayable and is not a permanent financing source for the deficit.
Correct: WMA is a temporary facility, repayable within three months under Section 17(5) of the RBI Act.
Wrong: overdraft is limited in duration, for the Centre to ten consecutive working days.
Wrong: State Governments also have WMA and overdraft facilities from the RBI.
keyfact: WMA is temporary and repayable within three months. It is not a source of deficit financing.
options: WMA is a permanent source of financing the fiscal deficit that need not be repaid
WMA is a temporary facility to bridge mismatches in receipts and payments and must be repaid within three months of the advance
Once the WMA limit is exhausted, the Centre may overdraw from the RBI for an unlimited period
WMA facilities are available only to the Centre and not to State Governments
question: With reference to Ways and Means Advances (WMA) extended by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government of India, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Since the FRBM framework took effect in 2006, the RBI cannot subscribe to primary issues of government securities, except in exceptional circumstances.
Normal WMA interest is at the repo rate, and overdraft carries a higher rate.
The RBI acts as banker and debt manager to the Centre and State Governments.
Cash Management Bills are short-term instruments used by the Centre to manage temporary cash mismatches.
subject: Economy
summary: Option (b) is correct. WMA is meant only for temporary cash-flow mismatches and, under Section 17(5) of the RBI Act, must be repaid within three months.

detail: The Aihole inscription (634-35 CE) is a Sanskrit prashasti composed by the court poet Ravikirti. It records the achievements of Pulakeshin II, including the check on Harsha's southward advance, generally placed on the Narmada. Pulakeshin II also fought the Pallavas under Mahendravarman I. Later, around 642 CE, the Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman I invaded and captured Vatapi, and assumed the title Vatapikonda. Both statements are true. The test is whether the second explains the first. It does not, because the inscription was written earlier and is not the cause of the Pallava conquest. Options (c) and (d) fail because each denies a true statement. Between (a) and (b), the absence of a causal link decides it.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is true but is not an explanation of what the inscription says.
Correct: both statements are factual and unrelated causally.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Aihole inscription (634-35 CE): Ravikirti's prashasti of Pulakeshin II; Narasimhavarman I later took Vatapi.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Consider the following two statements:
Statement-I: The Aihole inscription, composed by Ravikirti, is a major source for the reign of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II and refers to his success against Harsha.
Statement-II: Pulakeshin II's capital Vatapi was later captured by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Ravikirti is described in the inscription as a Jaina poet comparable to Kalidasa and Bharavi.
Pulakeshin II assumed the title Parameshvara.
The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built under the Chalukya queen Lokamahadevi.
Mahendravarman I authored the Sanskrit play Mattavilasa Prahasana.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Aihole prashasti of Ravikirti is the chief source on Pulakeshin II and his success against Harsha.
2 — Correct: Narasimhavarman I captured Vatapi around 642 CE and took the title Vatapikonda, but this is not an explanation of the inscription's content.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. The Aihole prashasti by Ravikirti records Pulakeshin II's reign, while the Pallava capture of Vatapi is a separate later event.

detail: Article 249 is a device that lets Parliament legislate on State List matters in the national interest when the Rajya Sabha so resolves by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting. The resolution remains in force for a period not exceeding one year, which can be extended by one year at a time by further resolutions. The law ceases to have effect six months after the resolution lapses. Article 250 concerns legislation on State List matters while a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation. Article 252 enables Parliament to legislate for States with their consent, when two or more State legislatures pass resolutions. Article 356 deals with President's Rule in a State. Distinguishing these by trigger is the key.
explanations: Correct: Art. 249 is triggered by a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by two-thirds of members present and voting.
Wrong: Art. 250 applies when a Proclamation of Emergency is in operation.
Wrong: Art. 252 requires resolutions of two or more State legislatures requesting Parliament to legislate.
Wrong: Art. 356 relates to failure of constitutional machinery in a State.
keyfact: Art. 249: Rajya Sabha two-thirds resolution lets Parliament legislate on a State List subject in the national interest.
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India empowers Parliament to make laws on a matter in the State List if the Rajya Sabha has passed a resolution, supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting, declaring that it is necessary in the national interest?
related: A resolution under Art. 249 lasts up to one year and can be renewed.
Laws under Art. 249 cease to operate six months after the resolution ceases.
Art. 253 gives Parliament power to legislate to implement international treaties.
Art. 250 applies during a National Emergency.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: The answer is Article 249. It allows Parliament to legislate on a State List subject once the Rajya Sabha passes such a resolution by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

detail: The SDR is an international reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969 to supplement members' official reserves. It is neither a currency nor a claim on the IMF itself. It is a potential claim on the freely usable currencies of IMF members, and members can exchange SDRs for such currencies. The basket has five currencies: the US dollar, euro, renminbi (added in October 2016), yen and pound sterling. Statement 3 is the trap. SDRs are held only by IMF member countries, their central banks and other prescribed official holders, such as certain international institutions. Private banks and corporates cannot hold them or use them for trade settlement. Since statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is wrong, only option (b) fits.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate, and statement 3 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 3 is false because private entities cannot hold SDRs.
Wrong: statement 3 is false, so not all three are correct.
keyfact: SDR is a reserve asset held only by official holders, backed by a five-currency basket.
question:
With reference to the Special Drawing Right (SDR) of the International Monetary Fund, consider the following statements:
1. SDR is a potential claim on the freely usable currencies of IMF members.
2. The SDR valuation basket currently comprises the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling.
3. Private commercial banks and corporates can hold SDRs and use them for settling international trade transactions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: SDR was created in 1969 under the Bretton Woods system.
The Chinese renminbi joined the SDR basket in October 2016.
SDR allocations to members are proportional to their IMF quotas.
SDR is not a currency and has no circulation among the public.
The IMF reviews the SDR basket composition roughly every five years.
statements: 1 — Correct: SDR is a potential claim on freely usable currencies, not a currency itself.
2 — Correct: The basket has five currencies, with the renminbi added in 2016.
3 — Incorrect: Only members, central banks and prescribed official holders may hold SDRs, not private entities.
Facts: SDRs are allocated in proportion to members' IMF quotas. Their value is a basket-based unit of account. The IMF reviews the basket roughly every five years.
subject: Economy
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is '1 and 2 only'. SDRs can be held only by IMF members, central banks and a limited set of prescribed official holders, not by private entities.

detail: Article 6 of the Paris Agreement creates voluntary cooperation to meet NDCs. Article 6.2 lets Parties engage bilaterally or in small groups and transfer ITMOs. Parties must apply 'corresponding adjustments' to avoid double counting, but there is no central approval for each deal, only reporting and technical review. Article 6.4 creates the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM), a centralised market mechanism supervised by a Supervisory Body under the authority of the CMA. It is widely seen as the successor to the Kyoto Protocol's CDM. Article 6.8 recognises non-market approaches, such as finance, technology transfer and capacity building, with no trading of credits. Statement 1 is the odd one out, so it eliminates options (a), (c) and (d).
explanations: Wrong. Statement 1 is false and statement 2 is true.
Correct. Statements 2 and 3 are accurate, and statement 1 wrongly claims central approval for each transfer.
Wrong. It includes the false statement 1 and omits the true statement 2.
Wrong. Statement 1 is false.
keyfact: Article 6.2 = decentralised bilateral ITMOs with corresponding adjustments; 6.4 = centralised, successor to CDM; 6.8 = non-market approaches.
question:
With reference to Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 6.2, every bilateral transfer of Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs) requires prior approval from a central supervisory body of the UNFCCC.
2. Article 6.4 establishes a mechanism, supervised by a body under the authority of the Parties, that is often seen as the successor to the Clean Development Mechanism.
3. Article 6.8 provides a framework for non-market approaches to cooperation among Parties.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Article 6.2: bilateral or cooperative approaches involving ITMOs.
Article 6.4: the Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism, often called the successor to the CDM.
Article 6.8: non-market approaches.
The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21 in 2015 and entered into force in November 2016.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: Article 6.2 is decentralised. Parties apply corresponding adjustments and report, but each bilateral transfer does not need central UNFCCC approval.
2 — Correct: Article 6.4 sets up a centralised mechanism under a Supervisory Body, seen as the CDM's successor.
3 — Correct: Article 6.8 is a framework for non-market approaches.
Facts: Corresponding adjustments prevent double counting. The CMA is the Conference of the Parties serving as the meeting of the Parties to the Paris Agreement.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Article 6.2 is a decentralised, bilateral approach with 'corresponding adjustments', not subject to approval by a central UNFCCC body for each transfer, so statement 1 is wrong.

detail: India's boundary with Myanmar is about 1,643 km long. It runs along four northeastern States. Arunachal Pradesh has the longest stretch in the north, followed by Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland. Mizoram also borders Bangladesh, and Mizoram's boundary with Myanmar is long. Assam, despite being the gateway to the northeast, has no border with Myanmar, because Nagaland and Manipur lie between. Its international borders are with Bhutan and Bangladesh. Tripura is almost surrounded by Bangladesh and has no Myanmar border. Counting States 1, 3, 4 and 5 gives four, so the correct option is d.
explanations: Wrong: four States, not two, share the border.
Wrong: Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland make four.
Wrong: Assam and Tripura do not touch Myanmar, so five is too many.
Correct: Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Mizoram and Nagaland share the border.

detail: India distinguishes FDI from FPI mainly by the 10 per cent equity threshold. If a single FPI along with its investor group holds 10 per cent or more of a company's paid-up equity on a fully diluted basis, the holding must be reclassified as FDI, which is subject to the sectoral FDI policy and routes, or it must be reduced within a stipulated time. FPIs are registered with SEBI through designated depository participants under the SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, 2019. The investment instruments are governed by the FEMA (Non-debt Instruments) Rules. In the Balance of Payments, FDI and FPI are both part of the capital account (financial account), while the current account covers trade in goods and services, primary income and secondary income. A candidate can eliminate options (b), (c) and (d) by spotting that statement 3 is wrong.

Incorrect: statement 3 is not correct.
keyfact: An FPI holding of 10 per cent or more in a company is treated as FDI. FPI is recorded in the capital account.

detail: The Montreal Protocol (1987) originally controlled ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs and HCFCs. HCFCs were widely replaced by HFCs, which contain no chlorine or bromine and so do not deplete ozone, but they are very potent greenhouse gases. The Kigali Amendment (adopted in 2016, in force from 1 January 2019) therefore added HFCs to the Protocol's control regime, using the Protocol's own institutions and Multilateral Fund. It is a climate measure implemented through an ozone treaty. Parties are split into groups with different schedules. India is in Group 2, with a baseline of 2024-26, a freeze in 2028 and a first 10% cut in 2032, reaching an 85% cut by 2047. To eliminate options, spot that statement 2 is wrong, since the Amendment is not under the Kyoto Protocol. That leaves 'Only one' or 'Only two', and statement 3 is accurate, so the answer is 'Only two'.

summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'. The Kigali Amendment belongs to the Montreal Protocol, not the Kyoto Protocol.

detail: Section 70 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 lays down conditions precedent to retrenchment of a worker who has been in continuous service for not less than one year. The employer must give the worker one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons, or pay wages for the notice period in lieu of such notice. The worker must be paid, at the time of retrenchment, compensation equivalent to fifteen days' average pay for every completed year of continuous service or any part thereof in excess of six months. Notice must also be served on the appropriate Government or the authorised authority. Chapter X establishments (300 or more workers, threshold which States may raise) need prior permission instead. detail: In humans, the zygote receives its cytoplasm, and with it nearly all its mitochondria, from the oocyte. Paternal mitochondria that enter with the sperm are generally marked and degraded, so they do not persist. As a result, mtDNA follows the maternal line. This is why mtDNA is used to trace maternal ancestry and why mitochondrial diseases typically pass from mothers to offspring. Rare exceptions have been reported but do not change the general rule. detail: Lichens are a symbiosis between a fungus (mycobiont) and an alga or cyanobacterium (photobiont). They have no roots and no waxy cuticle, so they absorb moisture and dissolved nutrients directly from air, rain and dew across the whole thallus. Pollutants such as sulphur dioxide are absorbed in the same way, and they damage chlorophyll and cell membranes. Sensitive species, especially fruticose and foliose forms, therefore decline or vanish in polluted areas, while crustose species tolerate more pollution. This is why lichen distribution is used to map air quality and the 'lichen desert' around industrial cities. Because the mechanism in Statement-II directly causes the sensitivity in Statement-I, option (a) is correct. Options (b), (c) and (d) fail because both statements are factually true.

detail: Taxes are classified by how the rate varies with the tax base. In a progressive tax, the average rate rises with income, so higher earners pay a larger share. India's personal income tax with slab rates is the classic example. In a proportional tax, a constant rate applies at all income levels. In a regressive tax, the burden falls proportionally more on lower incomes; indirect taxes on necessities often have this effect because the same rupee amount takes a larger share of a poor household's income. A specific tax is levied as a fixed amount per physical unit, not as a percentage of value. Hence the description matches progressive taxation only.

Wrong: the rate stays constant at all incomes.

keyfact: Progressive tax: the average rate rises with income, as with income tax slabs.

subject: Indian Economy
summary: Progressive taxation raises the average tax rate as income rises. Income tax slabs in India are the standard example.

detail: The term, popularised by John Preskill, denotes a milestone where a quantum device completes a well-defined computational task in a time that classical supercomputers cannot match in practice. Google claimed this in 2019 with its Sycamore processor on a random circuit sampling problem. options: The use of quantum cryptography to make communication completely unhackable

subject: Science & Tech
summary: Quantum supremacy refers to a quantum computer performing a specific task far faster than any classical computer feasibly could. It does not mean general superiority or unbreakable communication.

detail: The Lorenz curve plots the cumulative percentage of population, ordered from poorest to richest, on the horizontal axis against the cumulative percentage of income (or consumption) on the vertical axis. The 45-degree diagonal is the line of perfect equality. The more the curve sags away from the diagonal, the greater the inequality. The Gini coefficient is the ratio of the area between the diagonal and the Lorenz curve to the total area under the diagonal. It ranges from 0, which is perfect equality, to 1, which is maximum inequality. Statement 2 reverses the relationship, because proximity to the diagonal means a more equal distribution. Statements 1 and 3 are accurate, so exactly two are correct.
explanations: Wrong: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct, and statement 2 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect.
Wrong: statements 1 and 3 are correct.
keyfact: Gini coefficient: 0 is perfect equality, 1 is maximum inequality. A Lorenz curve closer to the diagonal means less inequality.

detail: Water has a specific heat of about 4200 J/kg/K, much higher than land materials. It absorbs a lot of heat with a small temperature rise and releases it slowly, so coastal areas have milder temperatures and a smaller diurnal range than inland regions. In fluids the main mode of heat transfer is convection, where the moving fluid carries the heat; conduction occurs mainly in solids. The Sun's heat reaches the Earth by radiation, which needs no medium, because space is nearly a vacuum. Dark, rough surfaces are good absorbers and good emitters of radiation, which is why black-bodies are ideal absorbers. Elimination: a, b and d each reverse the correct physical principle.
explanations: Incorrect: convection is the main mode in fluids, and conduction is mainly in solids.
Incorrect: solar heat reaches Earth by radiation, which does not need a medium.
Correct: high specific heat capacity of water moderates coastal climates.
Incorrect: dark, rough surfaces are good absorbers and good emitters.
keyfact: Water's high specific heat capacity moderates coastal climates; the Sun's heat reaches Earth by radiation.
options: Conduction is the main mode of heat transfer in fluids such as water and air

subject: General Science
summary: The correct answer is option c. Water's high specific heat capacity means it heats and cools slowly, which moderates the climate of coastal regions.

detail: For a transformation y = ax + b, the new mean is a × (old mean) + b. The new standard deviation is |a| × (old SD), because adding or subtracting a constant (change of origin) shifts all values equally and does not change their spread. Here a = 3 and b = -5. New mean = 3 × 20 - 5 = 55. New SD = 3 × 4 = 12. Variance would become 9 times the old variance, which is 144. Elimination: any option showing the SD as 7 or 17 wrongly applies the subtraction or addition of 5 to the SD. Mean 60 forgets to subtract 5. Only mean 55 with SD 12 is consistent with both rules.
explanations: Correct: mean = 3 × 20 - 5 = 55 and SD = 3 × 4 = 12.
Incorrect: it wrongly subtracts 5 from the SD (12 - 5 = 7). Change of origin does not affect SD.
Incorrect: it forgets to subtract 5 from the mean, giving 60 instead of 55.
Incorrect: it wrongly adds 5 to the SD. Change of origin does not affect SD.
keyfact: Under y = ax + b: new mean = a·mean + b, new SD = |a|·SD.

summary: The new mean is 55 and the new SD is 12. The mean follows the full transformation, but the SD is affected only by the multiplication.
topic: Statistics (Effect of change of origin and scale)

detail: India's national accounts divide GVA into agriculture and allied (primary), industry (mining and quarrying, manufacturing, electricity, gas, water supply and other utility services, and construction) and services (trade, hotels, transport, communication, financial, real estate, professional, public administration, defence and other services). Note that in the national accounts mining is grouped under industry, though in the classical Clark-Fisher classification it is primary. Since the question asks for the tertiary sector, only option c lists services. Elimination: option a lists mining and electricity (industry in national accounts); option b lists manufacturing, construction and gas supply (industry); option d lists the primary sector.

Developed countries are urged to take the lead on contributions, but contributions are voluntary, and other countries are encouraged to contribute. There is no assessed contribution system, as under UN budget scales. So statement 3 is wrong. The words 'solely' and 'mandatory' signal an overstatement. With statements 1 and 2 correct and 3 incorrect, the answer is 'Only two'.

keyfact: The Loss and Damage Fund was agreed at COP27, operationalised at COP28, with voluntary contributions.

detail: Section 13 of the Code on Wages, 2019 provides that where an employee works in an establishment for more than the number of hours that constitute a normal working day, he is entitled to overtime wages at a rate not less than twice the rate of his normal wages. This mirrors the rate in the Factories Act, 1948 and keeps the premium unchanged for most workers. Other rates such as one and a half times or two and a half times are plausible distractors but have no basis in the Code. Overtime at the normal rate would give no premium at all and cannot be correct. Note that the Code fixes the minimum premium, and the appropriate Government may notify the normal working hours for different classes of employment.
explanations: Incorrect: one and a half times is below the statutory minimum.

detail: The nephron filters blood at the glomerulus (Bowman's capsule), and most glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule, so normal urine has no glucose. Urea is made in the liver through the ornithine (urea) cycle from ammonia and carbon dioxide, then carried by blood to the kidneys; the kidney does not synthesise it. ADH, released from the posterior pituitary (made in the hypothalamus), makes the collecting duct more permeable to water, concentrating urine; its deficiency causes diabetes insipidus. Because statements 3 and 4 are false, only option a survives.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are true.
Wrong: statement 3 is false because urea is made in the liver.
Wrong: both 3 and 4 are false.
Wrong: statement 4 is false; ADH increases reabsorption.
keyfact: Urea is made in the liver; the nephron reabsorbs glucose in the proximal tubule; ADH conserves water.

detail: The OSH Code, 2020 consolidated the Factories Act, 1948 and several other safety laws. Its welfare thresholds are lower than the old Factories Act thresholds. Under the Factories Act, a canteen was needed for more than 250 workers, a crèche for more than 30 women workers, and a Welfare Officer for 500 or more workers. The Code requires a canteen for 100 or more workers, a crèche for 50 or more workers, and a Welfare Officer for 250 or more workers. Options (b), (c) and (d) each contain at least one old Factories Act figure, so they are wrong. A candidate who remembers the new figures lowers the thresholds and can eliminate the options with the old numbers.

Incorrect. The canteen threshold of 250 is the old figure.

detail: A tropical cyclone needs several conditions. Sea surface temperature should be above roughly 26.5°C to a depth of about 50 m. The atmosphere should be unstable, with high mid-level humidity. There should be a pre-existing low-level disturbance and low vertical wind shear. Finally, the Coriolis force must be strong enough, which in practice means beyond about 5° of latitude. At the equator the Coriolis force is zero. Air flowing towards a low-pressure centre there is not deflected enough to develop a cyclonic spiral, so the pressure gradient simply fills the low. Equatorial seas are among the warmest in the world, which makes Statement-II false. So Statement-I is true and Statement-II is false.
explanations: Incorrect. Statement-II is factually wrong, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Incorrect. Statement-II is not correct at all, so this option fails.
Correct. Statement-I is true, and Statement-II is false because equatorial seas are warm.
Incorrect. The truth values are reversed.
keyfact: Weak Coriolis force, not cold water, prevents cyclone genesis within about 5° of the equator.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

related: Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal are more frequent than in the Arabian Sea.

statements: Statement-I — Correct: genesis is rare within about 5° of the equator because of the negligible Coriolis force.
Statement-II — Incorrect: equatorial seas are very warm, often above 28°C, so temperature is not the limiting factor.
Cyclone formation needs a sea surface temperature above about 26.5°C and a sufficient Coriolis effect. The Coriolis force is zero at the equator and increases towards the poles.
subject: Geography
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. Cyclones are rare near the equator because the Coriolis force is too weak to start rotation, not because the sea is cold.

detail: Corals live in symbiosis with zooxanthellae, which give them colour and most of their energy. Under thermal or other stress the corals expel the algae and turn white, which is bleaching. Corals are weakened but still alive and can regain algae and recover if stress eases, so statement 2 is wrong. The word 'exclusively' in statement 4 is the trap, because cold-water corals occur at depth in cold seas, even at high latitudes, without sunlight or zooxanthellae. India's four major reef areas are the Gulf of Mannar, the Gulf of Kachchh, Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Eliminating statements 2 and 4 leaves 1 and 3 only.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 3 are accurate, and 2 and 4 are not.
Incorrect: statements 2 and 4 are both false.
Incorrect: statement 4 uses 'exclusively', which is wrong because cold-water corals exist.
Incorrect: statements 2 and 4 are false.
keyfact: Bleaching is expulsion of zooxanthellae, which is reversible, and cold-water corals exist beyond the tropics.

detail: The Congo basin is centred on the Equator. The river rises south of the Equator, flows north across it near Boyoma (Stanley) Falls, then curves west and south and crosses it again near Mbandaka. As a result it has rain-fed flow in both hemispheres, and its discharge stays steady through the year. This makes it the deepest river in the world and second only to the Amazon in discharge. The Nile flows north from the Equator region to the Mediterranean. The Niger lies wholly north of the Equator, in West Africa. The Amazon's main stem lies just south of the Equator, and its mouth meets the Atlantic near it. So the Congo is the correct answer.
explanations: Incorrect. The Nile's sources are near or south of the Equator, and it then flows north without a second crossing.
Correct. The Congo crosses the Equator twice and so has a steady year-round flow.
Incorrect. The Amazon's main stem lies largely south of the Equator and does not cross it twice.
Incorrect. The Niger lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere.
keyfact: The Congo is the only major river that crosses the Equator twice, giving it a near-constant discharge.
question: Which one of the following rivers crosses the Equator twice in its course?
related: The Congo is Africa's deepest river and second largest in the world by discharge.

The Nile is traditionally listed as the longest river, flowing into the Mediterranean.
The Niger has an inland delta in Mali and a large delta in Nigeria.
subject: Geography
summary: The Congo (Zaire) crosses the Equator twice, once in its upper loop and again in its lower course. The Nile, Niger and Amazon do not cross it twice.

detail: Section 17 of the Code on Wages, 2019 deals with the time limit for payment of wages. For employees on daily wages, payment is at the end of the shift. For weekly wages, it is on the last working day of the week before the weekly holiday. For fortnightly wages, it is before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight. For monthly wages, it is before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding wage period. Where an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigns, the wages must be paid within two working days of such removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation. Option (a) is the rule for monthly-rated employees in the ordinary course, so it is a plausible but wrong distractor. Options (b) and (c) are not found in the Code.

Incorrect. The Code does not allow a fifteen-day period for settling wages on termination.

Correct. Section 17 of the Code requires payment within two working days of removal, dismissal, retrenchment or resignation.
keyfact: Code on Wages, 2019: wages on termination or resignation are payable within two working days.

detail: Under the tinkathia system, European planters forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land (3 kathas per bigha). Rajkumar Shukla, a local peasant, persuaded Gandhi to visit in 1917. Gandhi was served an order to leave the district but chose to disobey it, and the charges were withdrawn. A government inquiry committee, on which Gandhi served, recommended abolition of the system, and the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 followed. Gandhi's associates included Rajendra Prasad, Mazharul Haque, J.B. Kripalani and Mahadev Desai. Since each statement matches the historical record, only the option containing all three is correct. Be careful not to confuse this with the Kheda (1918) and Ahmedabad mill strike (1918) movements.

Incorrect: it omits statement 1, which is also correct.
Incorrect: it omits statement 2, which is also correct.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
keyfact: Champaran (1917): Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, against tinkathia; Agrarian Act 1918.

detail: The International Booker Prize honours a work of fiction translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland. The prize money is divided equally between author and translator. Deepa Bhasthi translated it from Kannada, making her the first Indian translator to win. It was the first short story collection to win the prize. Geetanjali Shree's Tomb of Sand, translated from Hindi by Daisy Rockwell, won in 2022. Elimination: option b is the 2022 winner. Option c gives the wrong language, since the stories are in Kannada. Wrong, because Tomb of Sand won the International Booker in 2022.

Wrong, because Flesh won the 2025 Booker Prize for fiction in English, not the International Booker.
keyfact: Heart Lamp (Banu Mushtaq, translated by Deepa Bhasthi) was the first Kannada winner of the International Booker, in 2025.

detail: The IBC consolidated India's insolvency laws and set a time-bound process. For companies and LLPs, the Adjudicating Authority is the NCLT, with appeals going to the NCLAT. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India is the regulator. The Committee of Creditors is made up of financial creditors, such as banks and bondholders, and only they vote on the resolution plan. Operational creditors, such as suppliers and employees, may attend meetings in certain cases but have no vote. Section 29A, inserted in 2017, disqualifies persons such as wilful defaulters, those with non-performing accounts above a stated period, and certain related parties from bidding. The aim is to stop promoters from regaining control cheaply. To eliminate options, note that statement 2 is wrong because of the voting rule. That removes options (c) and (d) and leaves (a) and (b). Statement 3 is correct, so (b) is the answer.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 3 is also correct, so 1 only is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct, and statement 2 is incorrect.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong, since operational creditors do not vote in the CoC.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong, so not all three are correct.
keyfact: Under the IBC, only financial creditors vote in the CoC, and Section 29A bars wilful defaulters from bidding.

statements: 1 — Correct: The NCLT is the Adjudicating Authority for corporate persons under the IBC.
2 — Incorrect: Only financial creditors have voting rights in the Committee of Creditors.
3 — Correct: Section 29A disqualifies wilful defaulters from submitting a resolution plan.
Individuals and partnership firms fall under the Debt Recovery Tribunal. The IBBI is the regulator for insolvency professionals.

summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so the answer is (b). The NCLT adjudicates corporate insolvency, and Section 29A bars wilful defaulters from submitting resolution plans. Operational creditors do not vote in the Committee of Creditors.

detail: Article 39A (42nd Amendment, 1976) provides equal justice and free legal aid. Article 43B (97th Amendment, 2011) directs the State to promote cooperative societies. Article 48 directs the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines, including prohibiting slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle. Article 45 originally spoke of free and compulsory education until age fourteen. The 86th Amendment (2002) moved that guarantee into Article 21A as a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14. It also recast Article 45 to cover early childhood care and education for children below six years. Pair 3 is therefore the odd one out.
explanations: Wrong: three pairs are matched correctly, not one.
Wrong: pairs 1, 2 and 4 are also correct, which makes three.
Correct: pairs 1, 2 and 4 are right, and pair 3 is wrong.
Wrong: pair 3 is not correct after the 86th Amendment.
keyfact: Article 45 now covers early childhood care and education below six years; Article 21A covers ages 6 to 14.

detail: India's WPI, compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser in DPIIT, tracks the prices of goods at the wholesale level and excludes services. The CPI (Combined) is compiled by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation. The CPI for Industrial Workers, along with the CPI for Agricultural Labourers and Rural Labourers, is compiled by the Labour Bureau under the Ministry of Labour and Employment. The inflation-targeting framework under the RBI Act sets a target of 4 per cent with a band of 2 to 6 per cent, based on CPI-Combined. Statement 2 is the trap, since the CPI-IW is not an NSO index. That eliminates options b and d. Statement 1 is correct, which leaves option c.

Incorrect. It wrongly includes statement 2.
keyfact: CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau. The RBI targets 4% CPI-Combined inflation with a ±2% band.

detail: The conditions at least 2 men and at least 2 women in a committee of 5 allow only two splits: 3M+2W and 2M+3W. For 3M+2W: C(7,3) × C(5,2) = 35 × 10 = 350. For 2M+3W: C(7,2) × C(5,3) = 21 × 10 = 210. Total = 560. Check by complement: the total number of committees is C(12,5) = 792. The invalid ones are 5M (21), 4M+1W (35×5 = 175), 1M+4W (7×5 = 35) and 5W (1), which total 232. Then 792 − 232 = 560. Elimination: the answer must be below 792, and 616 is too large because it would require an additional invalid split to be counted.
explanations: Correct: 35×10 + 21×10 = 560, confirmed by 792 − 232.
Incorrect: 582 does not match any combination of valid cases.
Incorrect: 525 is not the sum of the two valid cases.
Incorrect: 616 overcounts and is not the sum of the two valid cases.
keyfact: For 'at least' conditions, list the valid splits or subtract the invalid cases from the total.
question: A 5-member committee is to be formed from 7 men and 5 women so that it contains at least 2 men and at least 2 women. In how many ways can this be done?

Arrangements of n distinct objects = n!.

subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: The answer is 560. The valid splits are 3 men and 2 women, or 2 men and 3 women, giving 350 + 210 = 560.

detail: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) of sugarcane is the minimum price payable by sugar mills to cane growers. It is fixed under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966 on the basis of CACP recommendations, after consulting State Governments and other stakeholders, and is approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs. It replaced the earlier Statutory Minimum Price. States such as Uttar Pradesh and Punjab announce a State Advised Price (SAP), which is generally higher than the FRP. The FRP is a price that mills pay, not a government procurement price like the MSP of wheat and paddy. FCI does not procure sugarcane. To eliminate, (b) reverses the roles of the Centre and States, (c) confuses FRP with procurement, and (d) wrongly links it to APMC Acts.
explanations: Correct: the Centre announces the FRP on CACP's recommendation, and mills must pay at least this price.
Wrong: the roles are reversed, since the Centre fixes the FRP and States may announce the State Advised Price.
Wrong: FCI does not procure sugarcane, and the FRP is a price paid by mills.
Wrong: the FRP is set under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, not under APMC Acts.
keyfact: FRP is the Centre-announced minimum price that sugar mills must pay for sugarcane, and it is not a government procurement price.
options: The Fair and Remunerative Price is announced by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices and is the minimum price sugar mills must pay to cane growers
The Fair and Remunerative Price is determined by State Governments, while the Central Government fixes the State Advised Price
The Fair and Remunerative Price is the price at which the Food Corporation of India directly procures sugarcane from farmers
The Fair and Remunerative Price is fixed under State Agricultural Produce Market Committee Acts and varies across States

subject: Economy
summary: The answer is (a). The Centre announces the FRP on CACP's recommendation, and it is the minimum price mills must pay for sugarcane. Some States additionally announce a higher State Advised Price.

detail: A negative externality in production, such as pollution, imposes costs on third parties. The producer decides output where price equals private marginal cost, which ignores this external cost. Social marginal cost equals private marginal cost plus marginal external cost, so it lies above the private curve. The socially optimal output is where price equals social marginal cost, which is a lower quantity. The market therefore overproduces and sells at a price that is too low relative to the true cost. Statement-I describes this result. Statement-II gives the mechanism, which is the gap between private and social costs. A Pigouvian tax equal to the marginal external cost closes the gap by internalising the externality. Since Statement-II is the direct cause of Statement-I, option (a) is correct, and options (b), (c) and (d) wrongly deny the link or the truth of a statement.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true, and the cost gap in Statement-II causes the overproduction in Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is the actual explanation for Statement-I, not an unrelated truth.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Negative externality means private cost is below social cost, so the market overproduces.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: In a perfectly competitive market where production causes a negative externality, the market equilibrium output exceeds the socially optimal output.
Statement-II: The private marginal cost of producers is lower than the social marginal cost because producers do not bear the external cost imposed on others.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: A Pigouvian tax equals the marginal external cost and internalises the externality.
Social marginal cost equals private marginal cost plus marginal external cost.
A positive externality, such as education, leads to under-provision by the market.
The Coase theorem says that, with low transaction costs and clear property rights, private bargaining can solve externalities.
Carbon taxes and emission trading are market-based tools for negative externalities.
statements: 1 — Correct: With a negative production externality, market output is above the socially optimal level.
2 — Correct: Private marginal cost is lower than social marginal cost, and this gap explains the overproduction.
Facts: Social marginal cost equals private marginal cost plus marginal external cost. A Pigouvian tax equals the marginal external cost. Positive externalities lead to under-provision.
subject: Economy
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Because private marginal cost falls short of social marginal cost, producers supply more than the socially efficient quantity.

detail: Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission within two years of the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the end of every fifth year, or earlier if necessary. It consists of a Chairman and four other members. It recommends the distribution of net tax proceeds between the Union and States and the principles governing grants-in-aid. Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts of India and the States. Article 275 deals with grants from the Union to certain States, and the Finance Commission's recommendations guide these grants. Article 292 deals with borrowing by the Government of India. Remember that Article 280 is the establishing article.
explanations: Incorrect: Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts.
Incorrect: Article 275 deals with grants-in-aid to States, not the constitution of the Commission.
Correct: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission.
Incorrect: Article 292 deals with borrowing by the Union Government.
keyfact: Article 280 establishes the Finance Commission, constituted every fifth year.
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of the Finance Commission?
related: The Finance Commission has a Chairman and four other members.

Article 281 requires its recommendations to be laid before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum.
Article 270 deals with taxes levied and distributed between the Union and States.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, which the President constitutes every fifth year or earlier. It recommends the distribution of tax proceeds between the Union and the States.

detail: After the Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander touched down on 23 August 2023, the Government of India declared 23 August as National Space Day to commemorate the achievement. The first National Space Day was celebrated in 2024. India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon, and the first to land near the lunar south polar region. The landing site was named Shiv Shakti Point, and the Chandrayaan-2 impact site was named Tiranga Point. To answer such Statement I/II questions, first check the truth of each statement, then ask whether the second is the cause of the first. Here the day was chosen because of the landing, so Statement-II directly explains Statement-I, which rules out option (b).

topic: Space: Chandrayaan-3 and National Space Day

detail: Article 312 allows Parliament to create a new All-India Service by law if the Rajya Sabha resolves, by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest. Article 249 allows Parliament to legislate on a State List matter if the Rajya Sabha passes a similar resolution. Such a resolution under Article 249 lasts up to one year and can be renewed for further periods of up to one year each. Both provisions reflect the Rajya Sabha's role as the House of the States. They are separate special powers and neither is the reason for the other. To eliminate options, verify that both statements match the text of the Articles, which rules out c and d. Then see that Article 249 does not explain why Article 312 needs a Rajya Sabha resolution, which rules out a.
explanations: Incorrect: the two powers are independent, so II does not explain I.
Correct: both statements are true and are separate Rajya Sabha powers.
Incorrect: Statement-II is true under Article 249.
Incorrect: Statement-I is true under Article 312.
keyfact: Articles 249 and 312 both need a Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds of members present and voting.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Parliament can create a new All-India Service common to the Union and the States only after the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
Statement-II: Parliament can make laws on a matter in the State List if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting declaring that it is necessary in the national interest.

The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House and is not subject to dissolution.

statements: I — Correct: Article 312 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds of members present and voting before Parliament creates a new All-India Service.

II — Correct: Article 249 allows Parliament to legislate on a State List matter after such a Rajya Sabha resolution. Facts: the Article 249 resolution lasts one year and can be renewed, and laws made under it cease six months after the resolution lapses.
subject: Polity
summary: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II is not the explanation for Statement-I. Each describes a separate special power of the Rajya Sabha, under Article 312 and Article 249 respectively.
topic: Special powers of Rajya Sabha (Articles 312 and 249)

detail: Matching a monument with its patron dynasty is a standard UPSC pattern. The Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho is a Nagara-style monument of the Chandelas. The monolithic Kailasanatha temple at Ellora (Cave 16) was begun under the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I. The Konark Sun Temple was built by the Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I in the 13th century. The Modhera Sun Temple in Gujarat belongs to the Solanki (Chaulukya) dynasty, c. 1026-27 CE, in the reign of Bhima I. The Paramaras are linked with Malwa, with the Bhojshala and with Raja Bhoja. detail: India's economic data is produced by different bodies, so matching them is a standard UPSC theme. The Labour Bureau, under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, compiles the CPI for Industrial Workers and the CPI for Agricultural and Rural Labourers. detail: The ISS orbits at roughly 400 km, which is small compared with Earth's radius of about 6,400 km. Gravitational acceleration there is therefore about 8.7 m/s², close to 90 per cent of its value at the surface. Gravity is what keeps the station in orbit. Weightlessness, or microgravity, arises because the station and the astronauts are falling around the Earth together with the same acceleration. As a result there is no normal reaction force, and the astronauts feel no weight. A similar sensation occurs in a freely falling lift. Elimination logic: any option that accepts Statement-I is wrong, because gravity is not negligible there. Statement-II is correct, which leaves only option (d).
explanations: Incorrect: Statement-I is false, because gravity is not negligible at the ISS altitude.
Incorrect: Statement-I is false, so the pairing of two correct statements fails.
Incorrect: Statement-I is not correct, and Statement-II is correct, which is the reverse of this option.
Correct: Statement-I is false and Statement-II correctly describes free fall as the cause of weightlessness.
keyfact: Weightlessness in orbit is caused by free fall, not by absence of gravity.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct

Consider the following statements:
