statements: 1 — Correct: Article 67(b) requires an effective majority in the Rajya Sabha and agreement by the Lok Sabha.

3 — Correct: Article 65(3) gives the acting President the President's powers, immunities, emoluments and privileges.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so two are correct. Statement 2 is wrong because the Vice-President must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha, which is not the same as being qualified as a member, but the key problem is that Article 66 and 67 read differently on removal. Careful re-reading shows statement 2 is also correct, so see the detail.

detail: The Union Cabinet approved the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) scheme in July 2025, and it was launched as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on 15 August 2025. It covers jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027. First-time employees registered with the EPFO receive up to Rs 15,000 in two instalments. Employers get incentives for each additional employee who is retained. EPFO registration is the gateway for both benefits, so the scheme promotes formalisation. Elimination: (b) PMKVY is a skilling scheme. (c) PM Vishwakarma supports traditional artisans. (d) Atmanirbhar Bharat Rozgar Yojana (2020) was an earlier EPFO-linked scheme that subsidised contributions during COVID-19, so it does not match the launch date or the 15,000 first-job benefit.
explanations: Correct. This scheme, the ELI scheme, was launched on 15 August 2025 with this benefit structure.
Incorrect. PMKVY is a skill training and certification scheme, not an employment incentive.
Incorrect. PM Vishwakarma supports traditional artisans and craftspeople.
Incorrect. ABRY was a 2020 scheme that subsidised EPF contributions, and it does not match this launch or benefit.
keyfact: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (ELI), launched 15 August 2025, gives first-time EPFO-registered employees up to Rs 15,000.
options: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana
question: Which one of the following schemes, launched on 15 August 2025, gives a one-month wage incentive of up to Rs 15,000 to first-time employees registered with the EPFO, with incentives for employers for additional jobs created?
related: The scheme uses EPFO registration to identify eligible first-time employees.

subject: Current Affairs
summary: The answer is (a). The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana, the Employment Linked Incentive scheme, was launched on 15 August 2025. It gives first-time EPFO-registered employees up to Rs 15,000 and also supports employers who create jobs.

detail: Under Section 4 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, a trade union of workers can be registered only if at least ten per cent of the workers employed in the establishment or industry it represents, or one hundred workers, whichever is less, are members on the date of application. The membership must also never be below seven. This differs from the older Trade Unions Act, 1926, where any seven members could apply for registration. The Code therefore adds a representativeness test, which prevents a flood of tiny unions in large establishments. Elimination: 'whichever is more' would make registration very hard in large establishments, so option (b) is wrong. Fifteen per cent and a minimum of ten have no basis in the Code. Option (d) describes the repealed 1926 Act position.
explanations: Correct: ten per cent or 100 workers, whichever is less, subject to a minimum of seven.
Incorrect: it says 'whichever is more', but the Code says 'whichever is less'.
Incorrect: the Code does not prescribe fifteen per cent or a minimum of ten members.
Incorrect: this was the position under the Trade Unions Act, 1926, but the Code adds the percentage test.
keyfact: IR Code registration: 10% of workers or 100, whichever is less, with a minimum of seven members.
options: Not less than ten per cent of the workers or one hundred workers, whichever is less, subject to a minimum of seven
Not less than ten per cent of the workers or one hundred workers, whichever is more, subject to a minimum of seven
Not less than fifteen per cent of the workers or one hundred workers, whichever is less, subject to a minimum of ten
Any seven members, irrespective of the number of workers employed in the establishment
question: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the minimum membership required for an application for registration of a trade union is:
related: The Trade Unions Act, 1926 is subsumed in the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
The Registrar of Trade Unions registers unions under the Code.
The Code provides for a negotiating union or council for recognition as sole negotiating union.
A sole negotiating union needs the support of at least 51 per cent of workers on the muster roll.
Registration under the Code can be cancelled on grounds specified in the Code.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: Option (a) is correct. The Code requires an application backed by ten per cent of the workers or one hundred workers, whichever is less, and in any case at least seven. The other options change the percentage, the threshold or the minimum.
topic: Trade unions - registration under the IR Code

detail: The Stockholm Convention (adopted 2001, in force 2004) aims to eliminate or restrict the production and use of persistent organic pollutants. Annex A chemicals are to be eliminated, Annex B chemicals restricted, and Annex C chemicals have unintentional releases reduced. DDT sits in Annex B with an acceptable purpose of disease vector control, particularly malaria, under WHO guidelines. Option a is wrong because the exemption exists. Option c is wrong because DDT is actively restricted. Option d is wrong because the Basel Convention deals with hazardous waste movements, not the status of DDT as a POP.
explanations: Wrong: DDT is in Annex B and has an exemption for disease vector control.
Correct: Annex B restricts DDT but allows its use for disease vector control.
Wrong: DDT is subject to actual restriction on use, beyond monitoring.

keyfact: DDT is in Annex B of the Stockholm Convention, and its use is allowed for disease vector control.
options: It is listed for complete elimination with no exemptions of any kind
It is listed for restricted use, with production and use allowed for disease vector control such as malaria

related: Annex A means elimination, Annex B means restriction, and Annex C means unintentional production.
The Stockholm Convention entered into force in 2004.
The Basel Convention controls transboundary movement of hazardous wastes.
The Minamata Convention deals with mercury.
subject: Environment
summary: DDT is listed in Annex B (restriction) of the Stockholm Convention. Its use remains permitted for disease vector control, in line with WHO guidelines, until suitable alternatives are available.

detail: According to legend, the Gordian knot was an intricate knot that no one could untie. Whoever untied it was said to be destined to rule Asia. Alexander is said to have cut it with his sword. The idiom therefore means resolving a tangled problem through a forceful, unconventional solution rather than patient effort. Option (b) reverses the meaning, since it describes creating complexity. Option (c) suggests giving up, whereas the idiom is about success. Option (d) involves mutual concession, but cutting the knot is a unilateral and decisive act. Always link the origin story to the meaning when learning idioms.
explanations: Correct: a bold stroke that resolves a complex problem.
Wrong: this is the opposite, as the idiom is about removing complexity.
Wrong: the idiom denotes success, not giving up.
Wrong: it is a decisive act, not a compromise.
keyfact: Cutting the Gordian knot = solving a hard problem by decisive, bold action.
options: To solve a difficult problem by a bold, decisive stroke
To create a complicated situation deliberately
To abandon a task midway out of fear
To settle a dispute by compromise
question: Select the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom 'To cut the Gordian knot':

Pandora's box means a source of unforeseen troubles.
subject: General English
summary: The idiom means to solve a seemingly impossible problem by a bold, direct action. It comes from Alexander the Great's legendary slicing of the knot.

detail: Article 368 prescribes a special majority: a majority of the total membership of each House and at least two-thirds of members present and voting. Bills can be introduced in either House, and Article 108 joint sitting applies only to ordinary Bills (and not to Money or Constitution Amendment Bills). Matters in the proviso to Article 368(2), such as the election of the President, the Seventh Schedule, the representation of States in Parliament, the Supreme Court and High Courts, and Article 368 itself, need ratification by half of the State legislatures. The 24th Amendment made Presidential assent obligatory. So the elimination logic is that statement 3 fails, which removes options (c) and (d), and statement 2 is true, which removes (a).
explanations: Incomplete, because it omits statement 2, which is correct.
Correct, because statements 1 and 2 are right and statement 3 is wrong.
Wrong, because statement 3 is incorrect and statement 1 is omitted.
Wrong, because statement 3 is incorrect: the President must give assent.
keyfact: Article 368: either House can initiate, no joint sitting, the President must assent, and the federal proviso needs half the States.
question:
With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements regarding the amendment procedure under Article 368:
1. A Constitution Amendment Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament, and there is no provision for a joint sitting to resolve a deadlock over it.
2. An amendment to the Seventh Schedule requires, in addition to a special majority in Parliament, ratification by the legislatures of not less than one-half of the States.
3. The President may withhold assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill that has been duly passed by Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The 24th Amendment (1971) made assent compulsory.
Kesavananda Bharati (1973) laid down the basic structure doctrine.
The 42nd Amendment tried to bar judicial review of amendments, and Minerva Mills (1980) struck that down.
Ratification by States is by a simple majority of each State legislature.
statements: 1 — Correct: A Bill can originate in either House, and no joint sitting exists for it.
2 — Correct: The Seventh Schedule falls under the federal proviso to Article 368(2), so half the States must ratify.
3 — Incorrect: Since the 24th Amendment (1971), the President shall give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill.
Ratification by States needs only a simple majority in each State legislature, and no time limit is prescribed. The Bill does not go to the States for ordinary subjects.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A Bill under Article 368 may originate in either House and no joint sitting is available, and Seventh Schedule changes need ratification by half the States. The President must give assent, so statement 3 is wrong.

detail: This is conditional probability, so the sample space shrinks to the outcomes with at least one 2. There are 6 + 6 − 1 = 11 such outcomes. A sum that is a multiple of 4 can be 4, 8 or 12. Sum 4 with a 2 present: (2,2) only, since (1,3) and (3,1) contain no 2. Sum 8 with a 2 present: (2,6) and (6,2). Sum 12 needs (6,6), which has no 2. That gives 3 favourable outcomes, so the probability is 3/11. Option (d) comes from using 9 favourable outcomes out of 36, ignoring the condition. Always recount within the restricted sample space.
explanations: Correct. Favourable outcomes are (2,2), (2,6) and (6,2), out of 11 outcomes.
Incorrect. It misses one of the three favourable outcomes.
Incorrect. It counts an extra outcome such as (1,3) that contains no 2.
Incorrect. 1/4 = 9/36 is the unconditional probability of a sum divisible by 4.
keyfact: In conditional probability, count favourable outcomes only inside the restricted sample space.
question: Two fair six-faced dice are thrown together. Given that at least one of the dice shows the number 2, what is the probability that the sum of the numbers on the two dice is a multiple of 4?
related: P(A|B) = P(A∩B) / P(B).
Two dice have 36 equally likely outcomes.
The sum of 7 is the most probable, with probability 1/6.
P(at least one 2 on two dice) = 11/36.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: The probability is 3/11. Eleven outcomes contain at least one 2, and exactly three of them have a sum that is a multiple of 4.

detail: Announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 and approved by the Cabinet in July 2025, the Pradhan Mantri Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana is modelled partly on the Aspirational Districts approach. It covers 100 districts chosen on the basis of low productivity, low cropping intensity and below-average credit access. It runs for six years from 2025-26 and relies on convergence of 36 existing schemes across departments, together with state and private partnerships, to raise productivity, promote crop diversification and sustainable practices, improve post-harvest storage and expand credit. Elimination: the programme is about agriculture, so the nodal ministry is Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, not Rural Development. That rejects statement 4, and 'All four' goes. detail: The Tenth Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985), provides for disqualification on grounds of voluntarily giving up party membership or defying the party whip in a vote. A nominated member may join a party within six months of taking his seat without disqualification; joining later attracts it. Paragraph 6 made the Presiding Officer's decision final, but Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) held the bar on jurisdiction invalid for the Paragraph 7 portion, so the decision is subject to judicial review on grounds such as mala fides and perversity. An expelled member continues as an unattached member of the House and is not disqualified for being expelled. Hence option (a).
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are right and 3 is wrong.
Incomplete: statement 1 is also correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect, as expulsion is not a ground.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect so all three cannot be right.
keyfact: Expulsion from a party is not a ground for disqualification under the Tenth Schedule; the Presiding Officer's decision is judicially reviewable.
question:
With reference to the Anti-Defection Law under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. A nominated member of a House who joins a political party after the expiry of six months from the date on which he takes his seat becomes liable to disqualification.
2. The decision on a question of disqualification is made by the Presiding Officer of the House, and such decision is subject to judicial review.
3. A member is disqualified if a political party expels him from the party.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Tenth Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act, 1985.
The 91st Amendment, 2003 omitted the provision on splits.
A merger is protected if two-thirds of the legislature party agree to it.
Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992) upheld the validity of the Tenth Schedule.
Disqualification of the Presiding Officer's own party-related matters is decided by the House or a member elected by it.
statements: 1 — Correct: Paragraph 2(3) disqualifies a nominated member who joins a party after six months from taking his seat.
2 — Correct: Presiding Officer decides under Paragraph 6, but the decision is subject to judicial review per Kihoto Hollohan (1992).
3 — Incorrect: Expulsion by the party is not a ground for disqualification; the expelled member remains an unattached member.

subject: Indian Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is incorrect. A nominated member must join a party within six months of taking his seat, and the Presiding Officer's decision is subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan, 1992). Expulsion by a party does not by itself disqualify a member.

detail: Gravitational waves are ripples in the fabric of spacetime, predicted by Einstein's general theory of relativity. They are produced by accelerating masses with changing quadrupole moments, such as merging black holes or neutron stars. They are not electromagnetic waves. Electromagnetic waves come from accelerating charges and are oscillations of electric and magnetic fields. LIGO uses laser interferometry with kilometre-scale arms to detect changes in length far smaller than a proton's width. The first detection, GW150914, was observed on 14 September 2015 and announced in 2016. It came from the merger of two black holes. India's LIGO-India is a planned detector at Hingoli, Maharashtra, in collaboration with the US LIGO Laboratory. It is run by the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Science and Technology. To eliminate options, spot statement 2 as false, which removes every option containing it. Statements 1 and 3 are both true, leaving option (a).
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 3 are true and statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false, and statements 1 and 3 are true and are left out.
Incorrect: it includes the false statement 2 and leaves out the true statement 3.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false because gravitational waves are not electromagnetic.
keyfact: Gravitational waves are spacetime ripples, not electromagnetic waves, and LIGO-India is planned at Hingoli, Maharashtra.
question:
With reference to gravitational waves and the LIGO-India project, consider the following statements:
1. LIGO-India is planned to be located in the Hingoli district of Maharashtra.
2. Gravitational waves are a form of electromagnetic radiation produced only by accelerating charged particles.
3. The first direct detection of gravitational waves, made in 2015 by the LIGO detectors in the United States, came from the merger of two black holes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: GW170817 was a neutron star merger observed in both gravitational waves and light.
LISA is a planned space-based gravitational wave observatory led by ESA.
LIGO-India would be the fifth detector in the global network.
Gravitational waves travel at the speed of light in vacuum.
statements: 1 — Correct: LIGO-India is planned at Aundha in Hingoli district, Maharashtra, and was approved by the Union Cabinet in 2023.
2 — Incorrect: Gravitational waves are spacetime distortions, not electromagnetic radiation, and any accelerating mass can produce them.
3 — Correct: GW150914 was detected in September 2015 and came from a binary black hole merger.
Facts: LIGO has detectors at Hanford and Livingston in the US. Virgo is in Italy and KAGRA is in Japan. The 2017 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for the LIGO detection.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: The correct answer is 1 and 3 only. LIGO-India is planned for Hingoli, and the 2015 first detection was a binary black hole merger. Gravitational waves are ripples in spacetime, not electromagnetic radiation.

detail: The Standing Deposit Facility was introduced in 2022 and replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the liquidity adjustment corridor. Its rate is set 25 basis points below the policy repo rate. It lets banks park surplus liquidity with the RBI, and the RBI does not need to give collateral in return. The Marginal Standing Facility rate is the ceiling of the corridor, set 25 basis points above the repo rate. Under the SDF, banks do not pledge any securities, unlike the earlier reverse repo, where the RBI provided government securities. Statement-II reverses this. To eliminate, once you know the SDF is the floor, Statement-I is correct and options d is out. Statement-II is wrong because it is the RBI that would otherwise have to give collateral, so options a and b are out.
explanations: Incorrect. Statement-II is false, so it cannot be the explanation for Statement-I.
Incorrect. Statement-II is not correct, since the SDF is collateral-free.
Correct. Statement-I is accurate, and Statement-II is wrong because no collateral is involved.
Incorrect. Statement-I is accurate.
keyfact: SDF is the floor of the LAF corridor at repo minus 25 bps, and it is collateral-free. MSF is the ceiling at repo plus 25 bps.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Consider the following statements:

related: The SDF was introduced in April 2022.

The MSF rate is 25 basis points above the repo rate and is the ceiling of the corridor.
The SDF replaced the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor of the corridor.
The Bank Rate is aligned with the MSF rate.
subject: Economy
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. The SDF rate is the floor of the LAF corridor, and the facility needs no collateral from banks.

detail: Gandhi began the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati with 78 followers and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) saw the Congress suspend the movement, while the government released political prisoners not guilty of violence and permitted salt making for personal consumption along the coast. Gandhi then represented the Congress at the Second Round Table Conference in London in late 1931. The First Round Table Conference (November 1930-January 1931) was held while Congress leaders were in jail and Congress did not attend, which makes statement 3 incorrect. Hence only 1 and 2 hold, and the answer is (b).

summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Congress boycotted the First Round Table Conference (1930) and took part only in the Second (1931) after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

detail: India holds many named bilateral exercises, and UPSC often tests the pairing of exercise and country. The usual army series are Nomadic Elephant (Mongolia), Ekuverin (Maldives), Dustlik (Uzbekistan), Ajeya Warrior (United Kingdom), Shakti (France), Yudh Abhyas (USA), Dharma Guardian (Japan), Harimau Shakti (Malaysia), Garuda Shakti (Indonesia), Mitra Shakti (Sri Lanka) and Khanjar (Kyrgyzstan). The efficient method is to confirm the pairs you are sure of and then spot the one that is wrong. Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Pair 3 is wrong because the India-France army exercise is Shakti. detail: Under Article 316, the President appoints the Chairman and members and determines the number of members, since the Constitution fixes no number. A member holds office for six years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. Under Article 319, the Chairman on ceasing to hold office is not eligible for further employment under the Government of India or any State. A member can become Chairman of the UPSC or of a State Public Service Commission, but not take other government employment. Under Article 320, the UPSC advises on recruitment and disciplinary matters, but its advice is not binding on the Government. Elimination: statement 3 is false, which rules out options b and c. keyfact: UPSC tenure is six years or age 65, whichever is earlier, and its advice under Article 320 is not binding on the Government.

question:

detail: India's flexible inflation targeting framework, in place since 2016, uses CPI-Combined as the nominal anchor, with a target of 4% and a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%. The CPI is compiled by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI. In contrast, the WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (Ministry of Commerce and Industry), and covers only goods, not services. Hence (a) is wrong because MoSPI does not compile WPI, (c) is wrong because WPI excludes services, and (d) is wrong since the target is in CPI terms.
explanations: Incorrect: WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
Correct: CPI-Combined from NSO is the RBI's inflation target measure.
Incorrect: WPI covers only goods, not services.
Incorrect: the MPC target is defined with CPI, not WPI.
keyfact: RBI's inflation target uses CPI-Combined (NSO), not WPI.
options: The WPI is compiled and released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
CPI (Combined) is released by the National Statistical Office and is the main measure used by the RBI for its inflation target
WPI includes services along with goods in its basket
The Monetary Policy Committee's inflation target is set in terms of WPI
question: Which one of the following statements about the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) in India is correct?
related: Inflation target is 4% with a ±2% band.

MPC has six members, three from RBI and three external.
CPI-Industrial Workers is compiled by the Labour Bureau.
subject: Indian Economy
summary: CPI (Combined), released by the NSO under MoSPI, is the anchor for the RBI's flexible inflation targeting. WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, and covers only goods.

detail: Shankaradeva (15th-16th century) preached devotion to Krishna through naam-kirtan, the Ekasarana Dharma, and composed borgeets and plays (Ankiya Nat). Nizamuddin Auliya, disciple of Baba Farid, was the major Chishti saint of Delhi, whose disciples included Amir Khusrau. Bahauddin Zakariya of Multan was a leading Suhrawardi saint, and the Suhrawardis, unlike the Chishtis, accepted state contacts and gifts. Since all three are accurate, option d is correct. Candidates who doubt any one statement may wrongly choose a two-statement option.

detail: In a von Neumann machine the program counter holds the address of the next instruction. The control unit fetches the instruction from memory into the instruction register, and the program counter is incremented. The decoder interprets the opcode and identifies the operands. The ALU or other units then execute the operation, and the result is stored or written back. The cycle repeats continuously. Elimination: an instruction cannot be decoded before it has been fetched, and it cannot be executed before it has been decoded, which rules out every other ordering.
explanations: Correct: the natural order is fetch from memory, decode the opcode, then execute.
Incorrect: decoding needs the instruction to be fetched first.
Incorrect: execution cannot precede decoding.
Incorrect: execution cannot begin before the instruction is fetched.
keyfact: Instruction cycle: Fetch → Decode → Execute.
question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the phases of the instruction cycle in a basic von Neumann computer?
related: The program counter holds the address of the next instruction.
The instruction register holds the current instruction.
The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
The control unit directs the flow of operations.
subject: Computers
summary: The correct answer is Fetch, Decode, Execute. The CPU first fetches the instruction from memory, then decodes it, then executes it.

detail: Burzahom, near Srinagar, is a Neolithic site known for pit dwellings and the burial of domestic dogs with their owners, so pair 1 is correct. Mehrgarh in Balochistan, near the Bolan pass, is one of the earliest farming and herding settlements in South Asia, so pair 2 is correct. Daimabad lies in Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra on the Pravara river. It is famous for bronze sculptures such as the chariot, rhinoceros and elephant, and it shows Late Harappan and Jorwe-culture phases, so pair 3 is wrong. Ahar (Banas culture) in Rajasthan is a copper-using chalcolithic site on the Banas basin, so pair 4 is correct. Elimination: once Daimabad is known to be in Maharashtra, 'all four' is ruled out, and two further correct pairs rule out the smaller counts.
explanations: Wrong: three pairs are correct, not one.
Wrong: pairs 1, 2 and 4 are all correct, so the count is three.
Correct: pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct; Daimabad is on the Pravara.
Wrong: pair 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: Daimabad is on the Pravara in Maharashtra and is known for its bronze sculptures.

3 — Incorrect: Daimabad is on the Pravara in Maharashtra, not on the Narmada.

Daimabad's bronzes are among the most notable metal sculptures from protohistoric India.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Only three pairs are correct. Daimabad is in Maharashtra on the Pravara (a Godavari tributary), not in the Narmada valley.

detail: Surface salinity is controlled mainly by the balance between evaporation and precipitation, with additional effects from river inflow, ice melt and currents. Under the subtropical high-pressure belts (about 20°–30°), skies are clear, winds are dry and descending, and evaporation far exceeds rainfall, so salinity is highest. At the equator, the Doldrums bring convectional rain, high humidity and thick cloud, which lowers net evaporation and freshens the surface. Salinity therefore forms a double-humped profile with latitude, with a dip at the equator and a further decline towards the poles. To eliminate options, check Statement-I first, since it is the standard observed pattern. Statement-II gives the physical cause of the equatorial dip, which is the contrast that Statement-I describes, so it is a valid explanation. Options (b), (c) and (d) each wrongly reject one of the two statements or the link between them.
explanations: Correct: Both statements are accurate, and the equatorial rainfall and cloud cover in Statement-II explain the subtropical maximum and equatorial dip in Statement-I.
Incorrect: Statement-II is directly the explanation for the pattern in Statement-I, so the link is not absent.
Incorrect: Statement-II is factually correct, since the equatorial belt is wet, humid and cloudy.
Incorrect: Statement-I is correct, because the salinity maximum lies in the tropics and subtropics rather than at the equator.
keyfact: Open-ocean surface salinity is highest around 20°–30° latitude, not at the equator.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: In the open oceans, the highest surface salinity is generally found in the subtropical belts around 20°–30° latitude rather than at the equator.
Statement-II: The equatorial belt receives heavy rainfall and has high humidity and cloud cover, which reduces net evaporation and dilutes surface waters.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The Atlantic is the saltiest ocean, and the Arctic Ocean has relatively low salinity.
The Dead Sea has very high salinity because of intense evaporation and closed drainage.
The Baltic Sea has low salinity because of heavy river inflow and low evaporation.
Isohalines are lines joining places of equal salinity.
Salinity is measured in parts per thousand or practical salinity units.
statements: Statement-I — Correct: Salinity peaks in the subtropics (about 35–37 psu in the Atlantic) and is lower at the equator and at high latitudes.

Statement-II — Correct and explanatory: Equatorial rain and cloud cover reduce net evaporation, and this explains why the subtropics, not the equator, are the saltiest belts. Evaporation exceeds rainfall under the subtropical highs.
subject: Geography
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Surface salinity peaks in the subtropics, where evaporation exceeds precipitation, and dips at the equator, where heavy rain and cloud cover dilute the water.

detail: Section 13 of the Code on Wages, 2019 provides that where an employee works for more than the normal working hours fixed by the appropriate Government for the establishment, the employer must pay overtime at a rate not less than twice the normal rate of wages. The Code thus retains the double-rate principle found in the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 (which used the same standard) and the Factories Act, 1948. Option (a) is a common international standard but not the Indian statutory minimum. Option (c) understates the rate. Option (d) overstates it, as the Code sets only a minimum of twice and does not set triple. Candidates should recall that the word is 'not less than', so a higher contractual rate is permitted.
explanations: Incorrect. One and a half times is not the Indian statutory minimum under the Code.
Correct. Section 13 requires overtime at not less than twice the normal rate of wages.
Incorrect. A 25% premium is far below the statutory minimum.
Incorrect. The Code prescribes a minimum of twice, not three times.
keyfact: Code on Wages, Section 13: overtime at not less than twice the normal wage rate.

Not less than twice the normal rate of wages

Not less than three times the normal rate of wages
question: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, where an employee works in an employment for more than the number of hours fixed as normal working hours per day or per week, the employer is bound to pay overtime wages at a rate which is:
related: Section 6 of the Code on Wages prescribes that wages shall not be paid below the minimum wage.
Section 9 deals with floor wage fixed by the Central Government.
The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumes four Acts, including the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 and the Minimum Wages Act, 1948.
The Code fixes a limit of eight hours for normal working day only as appropriate Government notifies; the Code itself leaves hours to the appropriate Government.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is that overtime must be paid at not less than twice the normal rate of wages. Section 13 of the Code on Wages, 2019 fixes this minimum rate for work beyond normal hours.

detail: Pyramids of biomass show the standing crop at one point in time. On land, producers such as trees accumulate large biomass, so the pyramid is upright. In aquatic systems the producers are mostly microscopic phytoplankton that are eaten almost as fast as they grow. At any instant their standing biomass is small, yet they reproduce within days, so their productivity (the rate of biomass production) is high. Zooplankton and fish live longer and accumulate biomass, so the consumer biomass can exceed the producer biomass and the pyramid becomes inverted. This is the causal link between the two statements. The pyramid of energy, in contrast, is always upright, because energy is lost at every trophic level. The pyramid of numbers can be inverted in a tree-parasite system. A candidate who confuses standing crop with productivity would wrongly reject Statement-II.
explanations: Correct. Both statements are true, and the high turnover of phytoplankton is the reason for the inverted biomass pyramid.
Incorrect. Statement-II is not merely a related fact; it is the direct explanation.
Incorrect. Statement-II is also correct.
Incorrect. Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Aquatic biomass pyramids are often inverted because phytoplankton have low standing crop but high turnover; energy pyramids are never inverted.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: In many pond and open-ocean ecosystems, the pyramid of biomass is inverted.
Statement-II: Phytoplankton have a very small standing crop but a very high turnover rate, so they sustain a larger biomass of zooplankton and fish.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The pyramid of energy is always upright.
Gross primary productivity minus respiration equals net primary productivity.
The 10% law of energy transfer was proposed by Lindeman.
A pyramid of numbers in a single tree supporting many insects is inverted.
statements: Statement-I — Correct: pond and sea biomass pyramids are commonly inverted.
Statement-II — Correct: low standing crop combined with rapid turnover explains the inversion.
Facts: energy pyramids are always upright, while pyramids of numbers and biomass can be inverted.
subject: Environment
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Producers with a small standing crop but rapid reproduction can support a larger consumer biomass at any one time.

detail: Article 108 provides a mechanism to resolve a deadlock on an ordinary Bill after the Houses disagree on amendments, one House rejects it, or six months pass without the other House passing it. The President summons the joint sitting, and the decision is by a majority of the total members present and voting. A Money Bill or a Constitution Amendment Bill cannot be sent to a joint sitting, because the former is decided finally by the Lok Sabha and the latter needs special majorities in each House. The Speaker presides. If the Speaker is absent, the Deputy Speaker presides, then the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, and then any person decided by the members present. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha never presides, since he is not a member of either House. Joint sittings have taken place on three Bills: the Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill (1978) and the POTA Bill (2002). Elimination: statements 2 and 3 are wrong, which leaves only option (a).
explanations: Correct: only statements 1 and 4 are correct.
Wrong: statements 2 and 3 are both false.
Wrong: statement 3 is false because the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha never presides.
Wrong: statements 2 and 3 are false.
keyfact: Joint sitting (Art 108) excludes Money and Constitution Amendment Bills; only 3 have been held.
question:
With reference to a joint sitting of the two Houses of the Parliament of India under Article 108 of the Constitution, consider the following statements:
1. The President may summon a joint sitting for an ordinary Bill when the Houses disagree on it or when more than six months elapse without the other House passing it.
2. A joint sitting can be summoned for a Constitution Amendment Bill if the Rajya Sabha rejects it.
3. If the Speaker, the Deputy Speaker and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are all absent, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides over the joint sitting.
4. The Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1960, the Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill, 1977 and the Prevention of Terrorism Bill, 2002 were passed at joint sittings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: A Money Bill is not subject to a joint sitting; the Lok Sabha has the final say.
The Speaker presides over a joint sitting, and the Rules of Lok Sabha apply with adaptations.
Joint sittings have been held only three times: 1961, 1978 and 2002.
The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides if the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent.
Decisions at a joint sitting are by a majority of members present and voting.
statements: 1 — Correct: These are the Article 108 triggers for a joint sitting on an ordinary Bill.
2 — Incorrect: Constitution Amendment Bills require separate special majorities in each House under Article 368.
3 — Incorrect: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha never presides over a joint sitting. After the Deputy Chairman, a person agreed by members present presides.
4 — Correct: These Bills were passed at joint sittings in 1961, 1978 and 2002.
The Rules of Procedure give the Lok Sabha Speaker the chair. The joint sitting can consider only amendments made by one House and not accepted by the other, plus those occasioned by delay.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. A joint sitting does not apply to Constitution Amendment Bills, and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha never presides over it.

detail: CRR and SLR are often confused. The CRR is the share of net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that banks keep as cash balances with the RBI, and no interest is paid on it. The SLR is the share of NDTL that banks must hold in their own custody in the form of cash, gold or unencumbered approved securities, which include government securities and state development loans. A higher SLR forces banks to park more funds in these assets, so less is available for lending, which makes Statement-I correct. Statement-II confuses SLR with CRR, which makes it wrong. Since Statement-II is wrong, options (a), (b) and (d) are eliminated. The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 sets the legal framework for SLR, and the RBI sets the rate within the statutory limits.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is factually incorrect.
Correct: Statement-I is true, and Statement-II wrongly describes CRR rather than SLR.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct, since higher SLR reduces lendable funds.
keyfact: CRR is cash with the RBI; SLR is held by banks themselves in cash, gold or approved securities.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: An increase in the Statutory Liquidity Ratio reduces the lendable resources available with commercial banks.
Statement-II: Statutory Liquidity Ratio has to be maintained by banks in the form of cash balances kept with the Reserve Bank of India.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: CRR is maintained with the RBI as cash and earns no interest.
SLR assets include cash, gold and unencumbered approved securities.
Both CRR and SLR are expressed as a percentage of NDTL.
A lower CRR increases the loanable funds of banks.
SLR acts as a captive market for government securities.
statements: 1 — Correct: A higher SLR locks more of NDTL in liquid assets, leaving less for loans.
2 — Incorrect: Cash balances with the RBI constitute CRR; SLR is held by banks themselves in cash, gold or approved securities.
Fact: CRR balances earn no interest, while SLR securities earn returns.
Fact: Both CRR and SLR are computed as a percentage of NDTL.
subject: Economy
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. SLR is held by banks themselves in liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities, not as balances with the RBI. Balances with the RBI are the CRR.

detail: When atmospheric CO2 dissolves in seawater it forms carbonic acid, which releases hydrogen ions. These ions combine with carbonate ions, so carbonate availability falls. Calcifying organisms such as corals, pteropods and molluscs need carbonate to build shells and skeletons of aragonite or calcite. Aragonite is more soluble than calcite, so it is the first to be affected. Gas solubility rises as temperature falls, so cold polar waters take up more CO2. They also naturally have lower carbonate ion concentrations. This makes the aragonite saturation state in these waters fall towards undersaturation sooner than in warm tropical waters, which is why the Southern Ocean and Arctic are early warning regions for pteropods. Statement-II gives the physical reason for Statement-I, so option (a) is right. Options (c) and (d) wrongly reject one correct statement. Option (b) accepts both statements but ignores the causal link.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true and the temperature-dependent solubility of CO2 explains the earlier undersaturation at high latitudes.
Incorrect: Statement-II is the direct explanation for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Incorrect: Statement-II is a correct physical fact.
Incorrect: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Cold water dissolves more CO2, so polar oceans reach aragonite undersaturation first.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Polar and sub-polar seawater is expected to become undersaturated with respect to aragonite earlier than tropical surface seawater as ocean acidification progresses.
Statement-II: The solubility of carbon dioxide in seawater is higher at lower temperatures.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Ocean acidification is often called the 'other CO2 problem'.
Aragonite is more soluble than calcite, so aragonite organisms such as corals and pteropods are more vulnerable.
Surface ocean pH has fallen by about 0.1 units since pre-industrial times.
Warm water dissolves less CO2, which is why tropical oceans release CO2 to the atmosphere in upwelling zones.
Pteropods are used as indicator species for acidification in polar seas.
statements: Statement-I — Correct: High-latitude waters have lower carbonate ion concentration and take up more CO2, so aragonite undersaturation is expected there first.
Statement-II — Correct: Gas solubility increases as water temperature decreases, so cold water holds more dissolved CO2. This is the cause behind Statement-I.
subject: Environment
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Cold water dissolves more CO2, which lowers carbonate ion concentration and the aragonite saturation state faster in high latitudes.

detail: Basel III requires banks to hold capital against risk-weighted assets. The global minimum total capital is 8 per cent, but the RBI prescribes 9 per cent for Indian banks. In addition, the Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) of 2.5 per cent must be held entirely in Common Equity Tier 1, which brings the effective requirement to 11.5 per cent. Common Equity Tier 1 consists of paid-up equity capital, statutory reserves and other disclosed free reserves, so these are the highest-quality capital. Tier 2 capital is supplementary and includes items like subordinated debt and revaluation reserves. Statement 3 therefore mixes up the tiers. Since statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 is wrong, only option (a) fits.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect and statement 2 is correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect, so not all three are correct.
keyfact: RBI minimum CRAR is 9% (plus 2.5% CCB in CET1 = 11.5%), above the Basel global 8%.
question:

2. The Capital Conservation Buffer of 2.5 per cent of risk-weighted assets is required to be maintained in the form of Common Equity Tier 1 capital.
3. Equity share capital and disclosed reserves form part of Tier 2 capital.

related: The RBI minimum CET1 ratio is 5.5 per cent of RWA.
With the CCB, the effective minimum total capital is 11.5 per cent.
Tier 2 capital includes subordinated debt and revaluation reserves.
Basel norms are set by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, hosted at the BIS.
statements: 1 — Correct: the RBI minimum is 9 per cent against the Basel III global minimum of 8 per cent.

3 — Incorrect: equity capital and disclosed reserves are CET1, which is Tier 1 capital, not Tier 2.
subject: Economy
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Equity share capital and disclosed reserves are Common Equity Tier 1 (Tier 1) capital, not Tier 2.

detail: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended a new monetary policy framework centred on flexible inflation targeting, which led to the amended RBI Act in 2016 and the Monetary Policy Committee. The Nachiket Mor Committee (2013) on comprehensive financial services for small businesses and low-income households proposed universal bank accounts and differentiated banks, which led to payments banks and small finance banks. The P. J. Nayak Committee (2014) reviewed governance of bank boards and recommended reducing government shareholding in public sector banks and creating a Bank Investment Company. The Malegam Committee (2011) examined the microfinance sector and recommended measures such as the NBFC-MFI category, margin caps and lending limits. Since pair 3 swaps the Malegam and Nayak subjects, exactly three pairs are correct.
explanations: Incorrect: three pairs, not one, are correct.
Incorrect: it counts only two pairs, but pairs 1, 2 and 4 are all correct.
Correct: pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correct, and pair 3 is wrong.
Incorrect: pair 3 is mismatched.
keyfact: Urjit Patel: monetary policy framework. Nachiket Mor: financial inclusion. Malegam: microfinance. P. J. Nayak: bank board governance.

The Nachiket Mor Committee's ideas contributed to payments banks and small finance banks.
The P. J. Nayak Committee suggested a Bank Investment Company for public sector banks.

statements: 1 — Correct: the Urjit Patel Committee, 2014, recommended the monetary policy framework and flexible inflation targeting.
2 — Correct: the Nachiket Mor Committee, 2013, proposed differentiated banks for financial inclusion.
3 — Incorrect: the Malegam Committee, 2011, examined microfinance, not bank boards.

subject: Economy
