detail: The Ilbert Bill, introduced in 1883 by the law member C. P. Ilbert during Ripon's viceroyalty, aimed to remove racial discrimination by allowing Indian district magistrates and sessions judges to try European offenders. Europeans in India organised a fierce agitation, and the government gave way. A compromise in January 1884 gave European accused the right to be tried by a jury of which at least half had to be Europeans. The episode showed Indians that the British would not accept racial equality, and it taught them the value of organised agitation, which helped the setting up of the Indian National Congress in 1885. detail: Splicing joins an old index series to a new one with a different base by using an overlapping link year, here 2019. On the old base, 2019 is 250, which means prices have risen 2.5 times since 2011. On the new base, 2023 is 120, which means prices are 1.2 times the 2019 level. Converting to the old base gives 250 × 1.2 = 300. Equivalent form: old-base index = new index × old index at link year / 100. The value 370 results from wrongly adding 250 and 120. The value 220 is the result of an incorrect subtraction (250 − 30), and 208.3 comes from dividing 250 by 1.2, which moves the series in the wrong direction. Always multiply when converting a new-base figure to the old base.

keyfact: Splicing: old-base value = new-base value × (old index at link year / 100).

summary: The 2023 index on the old base is 300. Splicing multiplies the new-series value by the old-series index at the link year divided by 100: 120 × 250/100 = 300.
topic: Index Numbers: Splicing and Base Shifting

detail: The Narmada and Tapi are the two major west-flowing rivers of peninsular India. They flow through rift valleys, or fault troughs. The Narmada flows between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges, and the Tapi flows south of the Satpura range. The Narmada rises near Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh. The Tapi rises near Multai in Betul district of Madhya Pradesh. Both fall into the Arabian Sea, the Narmada in the Gulf of Khambhat and the Tapi near Surat. They form estuaries because they flow through hard rock in narrow channels with a steep gradient and carry little sediment. The east-flowing rivers form deltas. So statement 3 is wrong, and only 1 and 2 hold.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is false because they form estuaries.
Correct: only statements 1 and 2 are correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is false.
keyfact: The Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries, not deltas.

detail: Old shares: X = 3/5, Y = 2/5. Z's share is 1/5 = 10/50, taken equally, so each of X and Y sacrifices 1/10 = 5/50. X's new share = 3/5 - 1/10 = 6/10 - 1/10 = 5/10 = 1/2 = 25/50. Y's new share = 2/5 - 1/10 = 4/10 - 1/10 = 3/10 = 15/50. Z = 1/5 = 10/50. So the ratio is 25:15:10 = 5:3:2. Hence option a is correct and the answer in the options marked b is wrong; this requires re-evaluation.

detail: The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced provincial autonomy: ministers responsible to legislatures ran provincial subjects, though Governors retained special responsibilities and discretionary powers. At the Centre the Act introduced dyarchy, with subjects such as defence, external affairs, ecclesiastical affairs and tribal areas reserved to the Governor-General. It also proposed an All-India Federation, which never materialised because princely states did not join. Statement-I is accurate in describing provincial autonomy with strong central control. Statement-II is also factually correct. But the explanation of central control lies in the Governor-General's special powers and the reserved subjects, together with the non-implementation of federation, not simply in the introduction of dyarchy. So Statement-II is true but does not properly explain Statement-I.

keyfact: 1935 Act: provincial autonomy plus dyarchy at the Centre; the federation never came into being.

detail: Article 74(2) says that the question whether any, and if so what, advice was tendered by Ministers to the President shall not be inquired into in any court. The bar covers the advice as such. In S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994), concerning Article 356, the Supreme Court held that the bar does not cover the material on which the advice is founded. The Union must produce that material, and the Court can examine whether it exists and is relevant, though it will not substitute its own satisfaction. Statement-II extends the bar to the underlying material, which makes it incorrect. Since Statement-I is correct, the answer is (c).

summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. Article 74(2) bars inquiry into the advice itself, but not into the material on which it was based. The Supreme Court held this in S.R. Bommai (1994).

detail: Lord Ripon is remembered as the most liberal Viceroy of the period. He repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1882, held the first regular census in 1881, and issued the Resolution on Local Self-Government in 1882, which is why he is called the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'. He also set up the Hunter Commission on education (1882) and brought in the Factory Act of 1881. The Ilbert Bill (1883) proposed to remove racial disqualification in trying Europeans. The European community protested strongly, and a compromise in 1884 gave Europeans the right to be tried by a jury at least half of whom were Europeans. So statement 2 fails. To eliminate options, you only need to be sure that statement 2 is wrong and that any one of 1, 3 or 4 is right. That removes (d), and certainty about two correct statements removes (a) and (b).

keyfact: Ripon: Father of Local Self-Government (1882), repealed the Vernacular Press Act, Ilbert Bill diluted in 1884.

detail: Air India Statutory Corporation v. United Labour Union (1996) had suggested that on abolition of contract labour, the principal employer must absorb the workers. In Steel Authority of India Ltd. v. National Union Waterfront Workers (2001), a Constitution Bench overruled that view on this point. It held that the CLRA contains no provision for automatic absorption, and that the contract labour can claim absorption only if the contract is found to be a sham or a camouflage, in which case the workers are treated as employees of the principal employer. Elimination: Gammon India dealt with the validity of the CLRA Act and its application provisions. Vegoils is a case about workmen and the meaning of 'workman' in the context of retrenchment. Bandhua Mukti Morcha is a bonded labour and PIL case about Article 21.

Incorrect: Bandhua Mukti Morcha concerns bonded labour and Article 21.
keyfact: SAIL (2001, Constitution Bench): no automatic absorption of contract labour on abolition of contract system.

detail: NISAR, the NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar, is the first Earth-observation satellite to carry dual-frequency radar. NASA supplied the L-band radar and ISRO the S-band radar. It was launched on 30 July 2025 aboard GSLV-F16 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. It orbits at about 740 km in a near-polar sun-synchronous orbit and images almost the entire land and ice surface of Earth repeatedly. It monitors ecosystems, ice sheets, land deformation and natural hazards. To eliminate options, recall that radar imaging of the whole globe needs a polar orbit, so geostationary is wrong. detail: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights, and this right is guaranteed in Part III itself. Dr Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution. The Supreme Court's writ power under Article 32 is therefore confined to Fundamental Rights. Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose, which makes their jurisdiction wider. The five writs are habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto. Elimination: once you know that Article 32 is in Part III and that Article 226 says 'any other purpose', statements 2 and 3 are certain. Statement 1 reflects the Article 32 limit, so all three hold.

keyfact: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, and Article 226 gives High Courts wider writ power.

subject: Indian Polity
summary: All three statements are correct, so the answer is (b). Article 32 limits the Supreme Court to Fundamental Rights, Article 226 gives High Courts wider reach, and Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right.

detail: A general average act is an extraordinary sacrifice or expenditure made voluntarily and reasonably for the common safety of the adventure. The loss is shared rateably by all parties to the adventure in proportion to their contributory values. The sacrificed interest also contributes by its own value, so its owner bears his own share of the loss. Here the contributory values are ship 50 + A 30 + B 20 + C 25 = Rs 125 lakh. The loss is Rs 25 lakh, so the rate is 20%. A pays 30 × 20% = Rs 6 lakh. B pays Rs 4 lakh, the ship pays Rs 10 lakh, and C bears Rs 5 lakh himself, so C receives Rs 20 lakh in all. Dividing by Rs 100 lakh, ignoring C's value, gives Rs 7.5 lakh, which is the common trap.
explanations: Wrong. Rs 5 lakh is the share that C, the owner of the sacrificed cargo, bears himself.
Correct. A's share is 30 × 25/125 = Rs 6 lakh.
Wrong. This divides by Rs 100 lakh and ignores the contributory value of the sacrificed cargo.
Wrong. This does not follow from any rateable basis; the rate is 20%, so 30 × 20% is Rs 6 lakh.
keyfact: General average is shared rateably by contributory values, and the sacrificed property is included in the base.
question: A vessel carrying cargo is in danger. To save the voyage, the master jettisons cargo of owner C worth Rs 25 lakh. The ship (Rs 50 lakh), cargo of owner A (Rs 30 lakh) and cargo of owner B (Rs 20 lakh) reach the destination safely. Assume the contributory values equal these values and that there are no other expenses. Under the principle of general average, what amount must the owner of cargo A contribute?
related: General average is a loss borne by all parties; particular average is borne by the owner of the damaged property alone.
A general average act must be voluntary, extraordinary and for the common safety.
The sacrificed interest contributes in proportion to its value.
The York-Antwerp Rules govern general average adjustment internationally.
subject: Insurance
summary: The answer is Rs 6 lakh. The general average loss of Rs 25 lakh is shared in proportion to contributory values, including the value of the sacrificed cargo, so the rate is 25/125 = 20%.

detail: Section 143(12) requires an auditor who has reason to believe that an offence involving fraud is being or has been committed against the company by its officers or employees to report it. The Board's report must then disclose the nature of the fraud, the amount, and the remedial action taken. Option (b) applies to frauds of ₹1 crore or more. Option (c) is not a procedure in the Act. detail: Section 139(6) provides that the first auditor of a company, other than a government company, is appointed by the Board within 30 days of the date of registration. If the Board fails to do so, it must inform the members, who then appoint the auditor at an extraordinary general meeting within 90 days. The auditor holds office until the conclusion of the first annual general meeting. For a government company, Section 139(7) provides that the first auditor is appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General within 60 days of registration. If the CAG does not appoint, the Board does so within the next 30 days, and if the Board also fails, the members appoint within the following 60 days. Elimination: options a, c and d name the wrong appointing authority for an ordinary company.
explanations: Members appoint the first auditor only if the Board fails to do so. This is not the primary rule.
Section 139(6) gives the Board the power to appoint within 30 days of registration. This is correct.
The Central Government does not appoint the first auditor of an ordinary company. The CAG appoints for a government company.
The Registrar of Companies has no power to appoint the first auditor.
keyfact: The Board appoints the first auditor within 30 days of registration, and the CAG does so for a government company within 60 days.
options: The first auditor is appointed by the shareholders in the first general meeting
The first auditor is appointed by the Board of Directors within 30 days of registration of the company
The first auditor is appointed by the Central Government
The first auditor is appointed by the Registrar of Companies
question: Under the Companies Act, 2013, which one of the following statements about the first auditor of a company (other than a government company) is correct?
related: Subsequent auditors are appointed at an AGM for a term of 5 years.
Appointment must be ratified at every AGM under the old rule, which was omitted by the 2018 amendment.
The CAG appoints the auditor of a government company within 180 days of the start of the financial year.
Section 141 lays down eligibility and disqualifications of auditors.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The correct answer is option b. Under Section 139(6), the Board appoints the first auditor within 30 days of registration. If the Board fails, members may appoint within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting.

detail: Partition took effect on 16 October 1905. Rabindranath Tagore led a Rakhi-tying procession, and fasting and hartal were observed. The Bengal National College was founded in 1906 with Aurobindo Ghosh as first principal, so option b is wrong on both date and presidency. Option c is misleading: the annulment and the capital shift were announced together at the 1911 Delhi Durbar, but Bengal became a Governor's province in 1912 as the new Presidency of Bengal, not 1920, so the combined claim fails. Option d is wrong because Swaraj was adopted as the goal at the Calcutta session of 1906 under Dadabhai Naoroji, not Benares 1905, which presided by Gokhale only endorsed Swadeshi and boycott in Bengal.
explanations: Correct: 16 October 1905 was observed as a day of mourning with Rakhi-bandhan for unity.
Incorrect: the Bengal National College was founded in 1906 and Aurobindo Ghosh was its first principal.
Incorrect: Bengal became a Governor's presidency in 1912, not 1920.
Incorrect: Swaraj was adopted at Calcutta in 1906, not Benares in 1905.
keyfact: The Partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905; Swaraj became the Congress goal at Calcutta in 1906.
options: The Partition took effect on 16 October 1905, which was observed as a day of mourning and Rakshabandhan was used to promote unity
The Bengal National College was founded in 1905 under the presidency of Rabindranath Tagore

The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911 and the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi in the same Delhi Durbar announcement, along with the creation of Bengal as a Governor's province in 1920
The Indian National Congress formally adopted Swaraj as its goal for the first time at the Benares session of 1905

detail: Article 94 provides that the Speaker vacates office on ceasing to be a member of the House. The Speaker may resign by writing to the Deputy Speaker, and may be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, with at least 14 days' notice. Article 94 also says that when the House is dissolved, the Speaker does not vacate office until immediately before the first meeting of the next House. Under Article 96, when a resolution for the Speaker's removal is under consideration, the Speaker may not preside but can speak and take part in proceedings. The Speaker can vote only in the first instance, not in case of a tie. In other situations, the Speaker has only a casting vote. The answer follows by rejecting statement 3, since continuity of the Speaker's office after dissolution is well established.
explanations: Wrong. Statement 3 is incorrect, so this combination fails.
Correct. Statements 1 and 2 are accurate and statement 3 is not.
Wrong. It includes incorrect statement 3 and omits correct statement 2.
Wrong. Statement 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: The Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution; the Speaker may vote in the first instance, not as a tiebreaker, on a removal resolution.
question:
With reference to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements:
1. The Speaker can be removed from office only by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House, after at least 14 days' notice.
2. While a resolution for the removal of the Speaker is under consideration, the Speaker can speak in the House and vote in the first instance, but not in the case of an equality of votes.
3. On the dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the Speaker vacates office immediately.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Speaker's resignation is addressed to the Deputy Speaker.
The Speaker has a casting vote in ordinary proceedings.
The Speaker decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill.
The Speaker's salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 94 requires a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members, with 14 days' notice.
2 — Correct: Article 96 lets the Speaker speak and vote in the first instance but not in a tie, while a removal resolution is pending.
3 — Incorrect: The Speaker continues in office after dissolution until immediately before the first meeting of the new House.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the Speaker continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the newly elected Lok Sabha.

detail: India's statutory social security began with the Workmen's Compensation Act of 1923, now the Employees' Compensation Act. The ESI Act of 1948 was the first major social insurance law of independent India. The Maternity Benefit Act of 1961 replaced the earlier State and mine-specific maternity laws. The Payment of Gratuity Act came in 1972, after the Employees' Provident Funds Act of 1952. To answer, place 1923 first. That removes options a and d, which start with 1. Then separate options b and c by the order of 1961 and 1972. Maternity Benefit comes before Gratuity, so b is correct.
explanations: Wrong: it puts the ESI Act before the 1923 Act.
Wrong: it places Gratuity (1972) before Maternity Benefit (1961).
Wrong: it places ESI first and Gratuity before Maternity Benefit.
keyfact: The sequence is 1923 (Workmen's Compensation), 1948 (ESI), 1952 (EPF), 1961 (Maternity), 1972 (Gratuity).
question:

2. Workmen's Compensation Act
3. Maternity Benefit Act
4. Payment of Gratuity Act

subject: Social Security
summary: The correct order is Workmen's Compensation Act 1923, ESI Act 1948, Maternity Benefit Act 1961, Payment of Gratuity Act 1972. This gives the sequence 2, 1, 3, 4.
topic: Evolution of social security legislation in India

detail: The Indian Ocean Dipole is the difference in sea surface temperature between the western (Arabian Sea) and eastern (off Sumatra) tropical Indian Ocean. In the positive phase, easterly winds strengthen along the equator, pushing warm water west and causing upwelling of cooler water in the east. Convection shifts towards the western Indian Ocean and East Africa, which gets heavy rain, while Indonesia and Australia turn drier. For India, a positive IOD usually boosts monsoon rainfall, as in 1997 and 2019. In the negative phase the pattern reverses. Option (a) describes the negative phase. Option (c) has no dipole because the temperatures do not differ. Option (d) is not a recognised IOD configuration.
explanations: Incorrect: this describes a negative IOD.
Correct: a positive IOD is warm in the west and cool in the east near Indonesia.
Incorrect: a dipole requires a west–east temperature contrast, not uniform warmth.
Incorrect: this is not the definition of the IOD, and it mixes in unrelated Pacific features.
keyfact: Positive IOD means warm west, cool east, and is usually good for the Indian monsoon.
options: Warmer than normal sea surface temperatures in the eastern Indian Ocean near Sumatra and cooler in the west
Warmer than normal sea surface temperatures in the western Indian Ocean and cooler than normal in the eastern Indian Ocean near Indonesia
Uniformly warm sea surface temperatures across the entire Indian Ocean basin
Cooler than normal sea surface temperatures in the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal together, with a stronger Walker cell over the Pacific
question: Which one of the following best describes a positive phase of the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)?
related: IOD is also called the Indian Niño
It is measured by the Dipole Mode Index
A positive IOD can offset El Niño's drying effect on the Indian monsoon
IOD events typically develop in May–June and peak in September–October
Positive IOD brings heavy rain to East Africa and drought to Indonesia and Australia
subject: Geography
summary: A positive IOD has warmer water in the western Indian Ocean and cooler water in the east near Indonesia. It generally favours the Indian summer monsoon, often offsetting the effect of El Niño.

detail: Fisher's ideal index is the geometric mean of the Laspeyres (base-weighted) and Paasche (current-weighted) indices, so it equals √(144 × 100) = √14400 = 120. The Drobisch–Bowley index is the arithmetic mean of the same two indices, which is (144 + 100)/2 = 122. The difference is 122 − 120 = 2. Since the arithmetic mean is always at least the geometric mean, the Drobisch–Bowley value is never below the Fisher value, and the two are equal only when L = P. Option c (22) is the gap between the Drobisch–Bowley index and Paasche index, and option d would hold only if L = P. Fisher's index is called ideal because it satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.
explanations: Wrong: 4 would result from mistakenly taking the difference as 124 − 120 or similar; the actual means are 122 and 120.
Wrong: 22 is the gap between the Drobisch–Bowley index (122) and the Paasche index (100), not the Fisher index.
Wrong: the AM and GM are equal only if L = P, which is not the case here.
keyfact: Fisher = GM of Laspeyres and Paasche; AM ≥ GM, so Drobisch–Bowley ≥ Fisher.
question: For a given pair of years, the Laspeyres price index is 144 and the Paasche price index is 100. By how much does the Fisher ideal index differ from the Drobisch–Bowley index (the arithmetic mean of the Laspeyres and Paasche indices)?
related: Fisher index = √(Laspeyres × Paasche); it satisfies both the time reversal and factor reversal tests.
Laspeyres uses base-year quantities; Paasche uses current-year quantities.
Laspeyres usually overstates and Paasche usually understates price changes.
Marshall–Edgeworth index uses the mean of base and current quantities as weights.
The Laspeyres and Paasche indices fail the time reversal test.
subject: Statistics
summary: Fisher's index is the geometric mean √(144 × 100) = 120. The Drobisch–Bowley index is (144 + 100)/2 = 122. The difference is 2.

detail: The Indian Councils Act of 1892 enlarged the non-official membership of the central and provincial legislative councils. Some non-official members were nominated by the Governor-General or Governors on the recommendation of bodies such as universities, district boards, municipalities and chambers of commerce. This was a limited, indirect form of representation, although the Act itself avoided the word 'election'. The Act also gave members the right to discuss the annual financial statement and to put questions to the executive, within limits. They could not vote on the budget, and they could not ask supplementary questions. Voting on parts of the budget came only with the Morley-Minto reforms of 1909. In elimination, check Statement-II first: since budget voting was not allowed in 1892, any option that accepts Statement-II falls.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is not correct, since members had no right to vote on the budget.
Correct: Statement-I is true, and Statement-II is false because the members could only discuss the budget.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct, so this option fails.
keyfact: 1892 Act: discussion of the budget and questions allowed, but no vote on the budget and no supplementary questions.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Indian Councils Act, 1892 introduced a limited element of indirect election in the legislative councils.
Statement-II: The Act of 1892 empowered the members of the legislative councils to vote on the budget.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The 1909 Act (Morley-Minto) introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
The 1892 Act allowed interpellation (questions) but not supplementary questions.
The 1861 Act began the association of Indians with legislation through nominated non-officials.
The 1909 Act allowed discussion and resolutions on the budget.
statements: Statement-I — Correct: The 1892 Act introduced a limited indirect element of election through recommendations of local bodies.
Statement-II — Incorrect: The members could only discuss the budget; they had no power to vote.
subject: Modern History
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. The 1892 Act allowed members to discuss the budget and put questions but gave them no power to vote on it.

detail: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 in Pune. Annie Besant launched her Home Rule League in September 1916 at Madras, shortly after Tilak's league at Poona in April 1916. Sir Syed founded the Scientific Society (1864) and the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh (1875), and later the Muhammadan Educational Conference. He was hostile to the Congress and died in 1898, years before the Muslim League was formed in 1906 under the leadership of the Aga Khan, Nawab Salimullah and others. So pair 4 is a fabricated link.
explanations: Wrong: three pairs are correct, not one.
Wrong: three pairs, not two, are correct.
Correct: pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched.
Wrong: pair 4 is incorrect.
keyfact: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan died in 1898, so he had no role in founding the Muslim League (1906).

detail: AS 2 states that inventories should be valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value (NRV). Comparison is ordinarily made item by item, or by groups of similar items, and not on the total of all stock. Item P: cost ₹60,000 (500×120) against NRV ₹55,000 (500×110), so the lower value is ₹55,000. Item Q: cost ₹24,000 (300×80) against NRV ₹28,500 (300×95), so the lower value is ₹24,000. Total = ₹79,000. Option (b) compares the aggregate NRV (₹83,500) with aggregate cost (₹84,000) and takes the lower, which is not item-wise. Option (c) is total cost. Option (d) takes the higher figure for each item, which is the opposite of the prudence principle.
explanations: Correct. P at NRV ₹55,000 plus Q at cost ₹24,000 gives ₹79,000.
Incorrect. This is the aggregate NRV, which ignores the item-wise comparison.
Incorrect. This is total cost, which ignores the NRV write-down on item P.
Incorrect. This takes the higher of cost and NRV for each item, contrary to AS 2.
keyfact: AS 2: inventory is valued at the lower of cost and NRV, compared item by item.
question: At the year end, a trader holds two items of stock. Item P has 500 units, with cost ₹120 per unit and net realisable value ₹110 per unit. Item Q has 300 units, with cost ₹80 per unit and net realisable value ₹95 per unit. Applying Accounting Standard 2 (Valuation of Inventories) on an item-by-item basis, which one of the following is the value at which closing inventory should be shown?
related: Cost of inventory includes purchase cost, conversion cost and other costs to bring it to present location and condition
AS 2 permits FIFO and weighted average cost; LIFO is not permitted
NRV = estimated selling price less estimated costs of completion and costs necessary to make the sale
Abnormal wastage and storage costs (unless necessary in production) are excluded from cost
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: Closing inventory is ₹79,000. AS 2 requires inventory to be valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value, applied item by item.

detail: Megasthenes, as preserved in later writers like Strabo and Arrian, describes the city administration of Pataliputra by six committees of five members each, handling industry, foreigners, births and deaths, trade, manufactured goods, and sales tax. In the Arthashastra, the Samaharta was the chief collector of revenue and the Sannidhata was the chief custodian of the treasury and storehouse, both among the high officials called tirthas or mahamatras. Because all three claims match the sources, the all-correct option is the answer. Candidates often confuse these with Adhyakshas such as Sitadhyaksha or Panyadhyaksha.
explanations: Wrong: statements 2 and 3 are also correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is also correct.
Wrong: statement 1 is also correct.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
keyfact: Samaharta collected revenue; Sannidhata kept the treasury; Megasthenes recorded six committees for Pataliputra.

detail: In life insurance, insurable interest must exist at the inception of the policy, because the contract is not one of indemnity. Once validly issued, the policy continues to be enforceable even if the interest later ceases, for example on divorce or when a debt is repaid. This contrasts with fire insurance, where interest must exist at the time of loss, and marine insurance, where it must exist at the time of loss. A person has unlimited interest in his own life, and a spouse is presumed to have interest in the other spouse's life. A creditor has an insurable interest in the debtor's life to the extent of the debt, so option d is wrong. Option a is wrong because relatives such as distant cousins do not automatically have an interest. Option c reverses the rule.
explanations: Incorrect: interest is not automatic or unlimited for every relative.
Correct: it must exist at inception, and need not exist at claim.
Incorrect: this reverses the rule, which applies to property and marine insurance.
Incorrect: a creditor has an insurable interest to the extent of the debt.
keyfact: Life insurance needs insurable interest at inception, not at the time of the claim.
options: A person has unlimited insurable interest in the life of any relative
Insurable interest must exist at the time of the proposal, and it need not exist at the time of the claim in life insurance
Insurable interest in life insurance exists only at the time of the claim
A creditor has no insurable interest in the life of a debtor
question: Which one of the following best describes the doctrine of insurable interest in life insurance, as understood in India?
related: Fire insurance requires interest at the time of loss
Marine insurance requires interest at the time of loss
A person has unlimited insurable interest in his own life
Insurable interest legally separates insurance from a wager
subject: Insurance
summary: The answer is option b. In life insurance, insurable interest must be present when the policy is taken out, and it is not required at the time of the claim.

detail: Karst landscapes develop where soluble rocks such as limestone and dolomite are dissolved by slightly acidic water, producing sinkholes, caves and underground drainage. Dripping water in caves precipitates calcium carbonate. Stalactites form on the ceiling and stalagmites on the floor, and they may merge into pillars or columns. Surface depressions form a size sequence: a doline (sinkhole) is a small funnel- or bowl-shaped hollow, an uvala is a larger depression formed when several dolines merge, and a polje is a very large, elongated, flat-floored basin, sometimes several kilometres across. A trap here is statement 3, which describes a doline and wrongly assigns it to a polje. Test this kind of question by remembering the size order: doline < uvala < polje.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct, and 3 is wrong because it describes a doline.
Incorrect: statement 3 misdefines a polje, so not all three are correct.
Incorrect: statements 1 and 2 are accurate.
keyfact: Karst depression size order: doline (small) < uvala (compound) < polje (large, flat-floored).
question:
With reference to karst topography, consider the following statements:
1. Stalactites grow downward from cave ceilings, whereas stalagmites build upward from cave floors, and the two may eventually join to form a column.
2. An uvala is formed by the coalescence of several adjacent sinkholes (dolines).
3. A polje is a small, deep, funnel-shaped depression that is smaller than a doline.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Karst gets its name from the Kras (Karst) plateau region of Slovenia and Italy.
Dolines are the commonest karst surface depressions.
Limestone dissolves in water containing carbonic acid.
Cave formations such as stalactites are called speleothems.
Indian karst examples include the Borra Caves in Andhra Pradesh and Mawsmai Cave in Meghalaya.
statements: 1 — Correct: Stalactites hang from ceilings and stalagmites rise from floors, and they can fuse into a column.
2 — Correct: An uvala is a compound depression created when neighbouring dolines coalesce.
3 — Incorrect: The description fits a doline. A polje is a large, flat-floored depression, often kilometres wide, with a steep margin.
Karst forms in soluble carbonate rocks. The size order of depressions is doline, then uvala, then polje.
subject: Geography
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statement 3 is incorrect. A polje is a large, flat-floored closed depression, not a small funnel-shaped one.

The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was a women's unit commanded by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal (Swaminathan). The INA trials were held at the Red Fort, Delhi, in 1945-46, before Independence. Elimination: (b) fails because the INA was reorganised under Bose; (c) fails because the regiment was of women; (d) fails because trials took place in 1945-46.
explanations: Correct: the government was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943.
Wrong: the INA was reorganised under Bose in 1943 after its first collapse, and it was not under Japanese officers' command.
Wrong: the Rani of Jhansi Regiment was a women's regiment.
Wrong: the Red Fort trials took place in 1945-46, before Independence.
keyfact: Subhas Chandra Bose proclaimed the Azad Hind Provisional Government at Singapore on 21 October 1943.
options: The Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) was proclaimed by Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore in October 1943.
The INA was first formed in 1942 under Rash Behari Bose as a force led by Japanese officers and was never reorganised.
The Rani of Jhansi Regiment was an all-male unit named after Lakshmibai.
The INA trials at the Red Fort began in 1948 after Independence.
question: With reference to the Indian National Army (INA) and the Azad Hind movement, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Mohan Singh raised the first INA in 1942.

Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon were tried at the Red Fort.
The INA slogan was 'Delhi Chalo' and the greeting was 'Jai Hind'.

detail: The Ilbert Bill was introduced in 1883 under Viceroy Ripon by Courtenay Ilbert, the Law Member. It sought to remove the disqualification that prevented Indian judges in the mofussil from trying Europeans. European residents, including planters, organised a fierce campaign, and the government compromised: European defendants were granted the right to be tried by a jury of which at least half the members were Europeans. The episode revealed racial attitudes in the colonial state and gave Indians a lesson in organised agitation, which contributed to the climate in which the Indian National Congress was founded in 1885. Statement-II supplies the factual basis for the interpretation in Statement-I, so option (a) holds.
explanations: Correct: Statement-II describes the bill and its dilution, which directly shows the unwillingness stated in Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is factually correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is a valid assessment.
keyfact: Ilbert Bill (1883): attempt to let Indian judges try Europeans; diluted by a jury compromise after European agitation.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883 exposed the unwillingness of the colonial government to concede equality between Europeans and Indians in the judicial sphere.
Statement-II: The Ilbert Bill proposed to empower Indian district magistrates and sessions judges to try European offenders in the mofussil, and the European community's agitation led to a compromise that diluted it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Lord Ripon was Viceroy from 1880 to 1884.
Ripon repealed the Vernacular Press Act in 1882.
Ripon's Resolution on Local Self-Government was passed in 1882.
The first Factory Act of 1881 was passed under Ripon.
Hunter Commission on education was appointed in 1882.
subject: Modern History
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. The bill tried to remove a racial disqualification in the courts, and the compromise showed how far the government would go in conceding equality.

detail: A not-for-profit organisation's Income and Expenditure Account follows the accrual basis, so only subscriptions belonging to the current year are credited. Start with the cash received of ₹4,00,000. Deduct the opening outstanding of ₹30,000, because it was received now but belongs to the previous year. Add the closing outstanding of ₹50,000, because it is earned but not yet received. Add the opening advance of ₹10,000, because it was received last year but belongs to this year. Deduct the closing advance of ₹20,000, because it belongs to next year. Result: 4,00,000 − 30,000 + 50,000 + 10,000 − 20,000 = ₹4,10,000. Errors usually come from reversing the treatment of advances. Remember that the outstanding and advance adjustments work in opposite directions, and that the opening and closing positions are also opposite.
explanations: Incorrect: this reverses the treatment of both advances, adding the closing advance and deducting the opening one.
Incorrect: this is simply the cash received and ignores accrual adjustments.
Incorrect: this deducts the opening advance and adds the closing advance, reversing the advance adjustments.
keyfact: Income and Expenditure Account = accrual basis: opening outstanding goes out, closing outstanding comes in, opening advance comes in, closing advance goes out.
question:

Received in advance at the beginning of the year (for the current year): ₹10,000
Received in advance at the end of the year (for the next year): ₹20,000

detail: Primary pollutants, such as CO, SO2, NO and particulates, are emitted directly from sources. Secondary pollutants form in the atmosphere through reactions among primary pollutants. Ground-level ozone forms when nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds react in the presence of sunlight. Other secondary pollutants include peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN) and the components of photochemical smog. This is why ozone levels peak on sunny afternoons and why it is controlled indirectly, by curbing NOx and VOC emissions. Statement-II reverses this and so is false. Options (a) and (b) fail because they accept Statement-II, and option (d) fails because it rejects the true Statement-I.

Correct: ozone is a secondary pollutant formed photochemically from NOx and VOCs.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct, so this option cannot hold.
keyfact: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed from NOx and VOCs in sunlight.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. Ground-level ozone forms in the air from photochemical reactions and is not emitted directly.
topic: Air pollution - Primary and secondary pollutants

detail: In 1928 the Bombay government enhanced the land revenue assessment in Bardoli taluka, Surat district, by about 22 per cent despite poor conditions. Peasants, organised by Vallabhbhai Patel with support from the Bardoli Satyagraha Patrika and women leaders such as Mithuben Petit, Bhaktiba and Sarda Mehta, refused to pay. Government confiscated land and cattle, but pressure led to the Maxwell-Broomfield inquiry, which found the enhancement unjustified, and the increase was reduced (to about 6 per cent). The Bardoli women are said to have given Patel the title 'Sardar'. Elimination: indigo relates to Champaran, salt tax to Dandi in 1930, and zamindar rent issues with Awadh Kisan Sabha, so only option a fits.

Incorrect: indigo cultivation grievance belongs to Champaran 1917.
Incorrect: the salt tax was the issue in the 1930 Salt Satyagraha; Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam march.
Incorrect: Baba Ramchandra led the Awadh peasant movement against zamindars, not Bardoli.
keyfact: Bardoli 1928: no-tax campaign under Vallabhbhai Patel, who became 'Sardar'.

subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: The Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) opposed a roughly 22 per cent hike in land revenue and was led by Vallabhbhai Patel. Its success earned him the title 'Sardar'.

detail: Dhrupad is among the oldest surviving genres of Hindustani classical vocal music, noted for its meditative, austere style that emphasises a long unmetered alap using syllables, followed by a composition with percussion. The pakhawaj, a barrel-shaped drum, is the traditional accompaniment, not the tabla. Therefore option b is accurate. detail: Gandhara art (Kushana period, north-west India) used grey-blue schist and stucco and shows Greco-Roman influence in wavy hair, drapery and realistic anatomy. Mathura art used spotted red sandstone from Sikri and developed indigenously, with Buddha images showing a shaved head, a muscular body and the usnisha, and it also made Jain and Hindu images. Amaravati art, by contrast, used white marble-like limestone and is known for narrative reliefs. Wrong: Statement-I is true.

detail: An ascetic renounces comfort and indulgence, usually for spiritual or disciplinary reasons. The three distractors are the opposite type: a hedonist pursues pleasure as the chief aim of life, an epicure takes refined enjoyment in food and drink, and a sybarite is devoted to luxury and sensual pleasure. The question is built so that all four options are 'person' words about attitude to pleasure; the key phrases 'indifferent to pleasure' and 'severe self-discipline' point to the one who denies themselves. Learn such words in opposing pairs (ascetic vs hedonist) because exam options often pair them.

Correct. An ascetic practises severe self-discipline and avoids indulgence.

detail: Habeas corpus ('to have the body') secures the release of a person unlawfully detained, and it can be directed against the State or a private individual. Quo warranto ('by what authority') tests a person's right to hold a substantive public office created by statute or the Constitution. It does not apply to private or purely ministerial offices. Mandamus ('we command') compels a public official to perform a public duty. It cannot be issued against the President or the Governor personally (Article 361), against a private individual or body unless it discharges a public duty, or to enforce a non-statutory departmental instruction with no statutory force. Elimination logic: statement 2 is wrong because 'private' offices are excluded, which removes options b and c. Statement 3 is wrong because of the presidential and gubernatorial immunity, which removes option d.
explanations: Correct: Statement 1 is right, and statements 2 and 3 are wrong.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect because quo warranto is confined to substantive public offices.
Wrong: both statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect because mandamus does not lie against the President or Governors personally.
keyfact: Quo warranto applies only to substantive public offices, while habeas corpus can run against private persons too.

2. A writ of quo warranto can be issued in respect of any office, whether public or private, if the incumbent lacks the necessary qualifications.
3. A writ of mandamus can be issued against the President of India or a Governor in respect of the exercise of their official powers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Certiorari quashes an order already passed, while prohibition stops proceedings that are still pending, and both are issued to lower courts or tribunals.
Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, whereas Article 226 is not.
Article 32 can be suspended only during a National Emergency under Article 359.
The Supreme Court in L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held that High Courts' writ jurisdiction forms part of the basic structure.
statements: 1 — Correct: Habeas corpus lies against any person, public authority or private individual, who illegally detains another.
2 — Incorrect: Quo warranto applies only to substantive public offices created by statute or the Constitution, not to private offices.

3 — Incorrect: Article 361 protects the President and Governors from being answerable to courts for the exercise of their official powers, so mandamus does not lie against them personally. Under Article 32 the Supreme Court can issue writs only for Fundamental Rights, while a High Court under Article 226 can do so for other purposes as well.
subject: Polity
summary: Only statement 1 is correct. Habeas corpus lies against both public authorities and private persons, whereas quo warranto is limited to substantive public offices and mandamus does not lie against the President or Governors personally.

detail: Find the pattern of 7^n modulo 100. 7^1 = 07, 7^2 = 49, 7^3 = 343 -> 43, 7^4 = 2401 -> 01. The cycle length is therefore 4. Now 2026 = 4 x 506 + 2, so 7^2026 = (7^4)^506 x 7^2, which ends in 01 x 49 = 49. Elimination: 07 would need the exponent to leave remainder 1, 43 would need remainder 3, and 01 would need remainder 0. Since 2026 divided by 4 leaves remainder 2, only 49 fits. The tempting wrong answer is 01 for those who compute 2026 mod 4 incorrectly, or 07 for those who use the 1-digit cycle of 7 (7, 9, 3, 1) wrongly.
explanations: Incorrect: 07 corresponds to exponents with remainder 1 mod 4, but 2026 leaves remainder 2.
Incorrect: 43 corresponds to remainder 3 mod 4.
Correct: remainder 2 mod 4 gives 7^2 = 49.
Incorrect: 01 corresponds to exponents divisible by 4, but 2026 is not.
keyfact: 7^4 ends in 01, so the last two digits of 7^n repeat every 4 powers.
question: What are the last two digits of 7^2026?
related: The unit digit of powers of 7 cycles as 7, 9, 3, 1.
7^4 = 2401, so 7^(4k) always ends in 01.
A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4.
By Euler's theorem, a^40 = 1 (mod 100) for a coprime to 100.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: The last two digits are 49. Since 7^4 = 2401 ends in 01, the cycle has length 4, and 2026 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 4.
topic: Number System - Cyclicity of Last Two Digits

detail: The traditional account gives four councils. The First, at Rajagriha shortly after the Buddha's death under Ajatashatru, was led by Mahakassapa, with Upali reciting the Vinaya and Ananda the Dhamma. The Second, at Vaishali about a century later, was led by Sabbakami (Sabakami) and dealt with disputed Vinaya practices. The Third, at Pataliputra under Ashoka, was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa and is associated with the compilation of the Kathavatthu and the Theravada tradition. The Fourth, in Kashmir (Kundalavana) under Kanishka according to northern tradition, was presided over by Vasumitra, with Ashvaghosha as his deputy. Upali and Upagupta are therefore wrongly assigned in pairs 3 and 4.
explanations: Wrong: two pairs are correct, not one.
Wrong: pairs 3 and 4 are mismatched, so only two are correct.
Wrong: pairs 3 and 4 are wrong.
Correct: only pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched.
keyfact: First Council: Mahakassapa; Second: Sabbakami; Third: Moggaliputta Tissa; Fourth: Vasumitra.

statements: 1 — Correct: Mahakassapa led the First Council at Rajagriha after the Buddha's death.
2 — Correct: Sabbakami is associated with leading the Second Council at Vaishali.
3 — Incorrect: The Third Council at Pataliputra was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa. Upali recited the Vinaya at the First Council.
4 — Incorrect: The Fourth Council, held during Kanishka's reign, was presided over by Vasumitra with Ashvaghosha as deputy. Upagupta was the teacher of Ashoka in tradition.
Facts: The Mahasanghika-Sthavira divide is linked to the Second Council, and the Kathavatthu is linked to the Third.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Only pairs 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is only two. The Third Council at Pataliputra was presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa, and the Fourth Council is linked with Vasumitra.

detail: The 15th Indian Labour Conference (1957) laid down the norms for a need-based minimum wage. These are three consumption units for one earner (the worker, his spouse and two children), 2,700 calories per adult consumption unit, 72 yards of cloth per person per year, rent for minimum housing under the Government's Industrial Housing Scheme, and fuel, lighting and miscellaneous items at 20 per cent of the total minimum wage. In Reptakos Brett (1991) the Supreme Court held that these norms left out important needs. It added 25 per cent weightage for children's education, medical requirement, minimum recreation including festivals and ceremonies, and provision for old age and marriage. Options a, c and d use items or figures that belong to the original 15th ILC package, or misstate them. Option a is the original 20 per cent, so it is not the Court's addition. Option d misstates the calorie norm, which was 2,700.
explanations: Incorrect. The 20 per cent for fuel, lighting and miscellaneous items was already part of the 15th ILC norms, so it is not the Court's addition.
Correct. This is the 25 per cent additional component added by the Supreme Court in Reptakos Brett.
Incorrect. Housing rent was already a 15th ILC norm, and the 10 per cent figure is invented.
Incorrect. The cloth norm of 72 yards is from the 15th ILC, but the calorie norm was 2,700, not 3,000. Neither is the Court's addition.
keyfact: Reptakos Brett added 25% of the minimum wage for education, medical needs, recreation, marriage and old age to the 15th ILC norms.
options: Fuel, lighting and other miscellaneous items, at 20 per cent of the total minimum wage
An additional 25 per cent of the minimum wage for children's education, medical requirements, minimum recreation, and provision for marriage and old age
Rent for minimum housing accommodation, at 10 per cent of the total minimum wage
Clothing at 72 yards per annum per person, and food at 3,000 calories per consumption unit

related: The Committee on Fair Wages (1948) recognised three levels of wage: living wage, fair wage and minimum wage.
The 15th ILC (1957) assumed a standard family of three consumption units.
Article 43 of the Constitution directs the State to secure a living wage for workers.
The Code on Wages, 2019 subsumed the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and three other wage laws.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is option b. In Reptakos Brett, the Supreme Court added 25 per cent of the minimum wage for children's education, medical needs, recreation and provision for marriage and old age, on top of the 15th ILC norms.
topic: Wage concepts and need-based minimum wage

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 extends social security to gig and platform workers. Aggregators contribute 1 to 2 per cent of annual turnover, with a cap of 5 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers; the rate is notified by the Central Government. Since statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 contradicts 2, only option (a) fits. Remember that the labour codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025.

detail: Section 45, as substituted by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015, protects policyholders against stale repudiation. Within three years from the policy's issuance, commencement of risk, revival, or rider (whichever is later), the insurer may call the policy in question on grounds of fraud, misstatement or suppression of material facts. The insurer must give written notice stating the grounds and materials relied on. After three years, a policy cannot be called in question on the ground of misstatement or suppression alone, and only fraud can be raised. The burden of proving fraud lies on the insurer. Option b is wrong because fraud is an exception and the period is three years, not two. Option c ignores the time limit entirely. Option d is wrong because the period can run afresh from revival.
explanations: Correct: this accurately states the three-year window, the later-of-dates rule, and the fraud exception after three years.
Incorrect: the period is three years, not two, and fraud remains a ground for repudiation even after the window.
Incorrect: Section 45 sets a time limit, so misstatement cannot be raised without limit.
Incorrect: the period is counted from the latest of issuance, commencement, revival or rider, so revival is relevant.
keyfact: Section 45: after three years, a life policy can be repudiated only for fraud, which the insurer must prove.

A life policy can never be repudiated by the insurer after the expiry of two years, even on the ground of fraud
The insurer may call in question a policy on grounds of misstatement at any time during the life of the policy, without any time limit

question: With reference to Section 45 of the Insurance Act, 1938, as amended in 2015, which one of the following statements regarding the repudiation of life insurance policies is correct?

Section 45 applies to life insurance, not to general insurance.
subject: Insurance
summary: The correct answer is option a. Section 45 sets a three-year contestability window. After it, a policy cannot be questioned for mere misstatement, and only fraud, proved by the insurer, can justify repudiation.

detail: The Code on Social Security 2020 formally recognises gig workers and platform workers as categories for social security.
