Between two and four per cent of annual turnover, subject to a ceiling of ten per cent of the amount paid or payable to such workers
Between one and two per cent of annual turnover, subject to a ceiling of ten per cent of the amount paid or payable to such workers
question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, an aggregator is required to contribute to the Social Security Fund for gig workers and platform workers. Which one of the following correctly states the permissible contribution?
related: The Code on Social Security defines an aggregator as a digital intermediary or marketplace for a buyer or user of a service.
A gig worker works outside a traditional employer-employee relationship.
A platform worker is a person engaged in or undertaking platform work.
The Central Government frames schemes for gig and platform workers covering life, disability, health and maternity benefits.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The answer is one to two per cent of annual turnover, capped at five per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers. The Central Government specifies the exact rate within this band.
topic: Gig and platform workers under the Code on Social Security, 2020

detail: In federated learning, a central coordinator sends a model to many participants, such as mobile phones or hospitals. Each participant trains it on local data and sends back only the updated parameters or gradients. The coordinator aggregates these updates, for example by federated averaging, to improve the global model. Raw data never leaves the device, which helps with privacy, data-protection compliance and bandwidth use. It is not a complete guarantee, because updates can still leak information, so it is often combined with techniques such as differential privacy or secure aggregation. Elimination: option (b) describes centralised storage, which is the opposite of federated learning. Option (c) describes synthetic-data training, or loosely a generative adversarial setup. Option (d) describes model compression or distillation, which is a different concept.
explanations: Correct. This is the standard definition: decentralised training, with only model updates shared.
Wrong. Federated learning avoids centralising data, whereas this option describes central storage.
Wrong. This describes synthetic data generation, not federated learning.
Wrong. This describes model compression or distillation, not federated learning.
keyfact: Federated learning moves the model to the data, not the data to the model.
options: a technique in which a model is trained across many decentralised devices or servers holding local data, with only model updates being shared rather than the raw data
a method of encrypting all training data so that it can be stored permanently on a single central cloud server
a process by which several AI models generate synthetic data to train one another without any real data
a technique of compressing a large AI model into a smaller one by removing its training data
question: In the context of artificial intelligence, 'federated learning', sometimes mentioned in discussions on data privacy, refers to
related: Federated averaging aggregates locally trained model updates.
Differential privacy adds calibrated noise to protect individuals' data.
Transformer models rely on a self-attention mechanism.
Retrieval-augmented generation grounds model output in external documents.
AI 'hallucination' means a model producing plausible but incorrect output.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Federated learning trains a shared model across decentralised devices or servers, with raw data staying local and only model updates being sent. This reduces privacy risk compared with pooling data centrally.

detail: Under SA 706, an Emphasis of Matter paragraph refers to a matter appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements that is of such importance that it is fundamental to users' understanding. An Other Matter paragraph refers to matters not presented or disclosed in the financial statements that are relevant to users' understanding of the audit, the auditor's responsibilities or the report. Modifications of opinion under SA 705 are of three types: qualified, adverse and disclaimer. A qualified opinion arises from material misstatement or inability to obtain evidence that is material but not pervasive. An adverse opinion arises when misstatements are material and pervasive. A disclaimer arises when the possible effects of undetected misstatement are material and pervasive.
explanations: Wrong: an Emphasis of Matter is not a qualification.
Correct: this is the SA 706 description.
Wrong: this describes a disclaimer of opinion under SA 705.
Wrong: this describes an adverse opinion under SA 705.
keyfact: Emphasis of Matter does not modify the audit opinion.
options: It is a qualification of the opinion because the auditor disagrees with the management

It is a paragraph referring to a matter already appropriately presented or disclosed in the financial statements that, in the auditor's judgement, is fundamental to users' understanding, and it does not modify the opinion
It is a disclaimer of opinion because the auditor could not obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence
It is an adverse opinion because the financial statements are materially misstated
question: Which one of the following best describes the 'Auditor's Report' on financial statements of a company with an 'Emphasis of Matter' paragraph under the Standards on Auditing?
related: SA 705 deals with modifications to the opinion.
SA 706 deals with Emphasis of Matter and Other Matter paragraphs.
SA 570 deals with going concern.
SA 700 deals with forming an opinion and reporting.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: An Emphasis of Matter paragraph draws attention to a matter already properly presented or disclosed in the financial statements that is fundamental to users' understanding. It does not modify the auditor's opinion.

detail: Under the WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement, dumping occurs when the export price of a product is lower than its normal value, usually the price in the exporter's domestic market or its cost of production. A country may levy anti-dumping duty only after investigation shows dumping, material injury to the domestic industry and a causal link. In India the Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) investigates and recommends, while the Finance Ministry imposes the duty. Option b describes an import quota, option c a subsidy, and option d an export ban.
explanations: Correct: this is the standard definition of dumping.
Incorrect: this describes an import quota.
Incorrect: this describes a farm subsidy, not dumping.
Incorrect: this describes an export prohibition.
keyfact: Dumping = exporting at a price below the home-market price or below cost; remedy is anti-dumping duty.
options: Selling goods in a foreign market at a price lower than the price in the exporter's home market or below cost
Imposing a ceiling on the quantity of imports allowed
Granting a subsidy to domestic farmers
Prohibiting the export of surplus goods
question: Which one of the following correctly describes 'Dumping' in international trade?
related: India's DGTR is under the Department of Commerce.
Anti-dumping duty is imposed by the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
The WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement governs such duties.
Countervailing duties offset subsidies, not dumping.
subject: Indian Economy
summary: Dumping is selling goods abroad at a price lower than in the home market or below cost of production. Importing countries may respond with anti-dumping duties under WTO rules.

detail: Nomination under Section 39 merely names a person to receive the policy money on the policyholder's death. Assignment under Section 38 transfers the policyholder's rights and interest in the policy to another person, with written notice to the insurer. An absolute assignment to anyone other than the insurer automatically cancels an earlier nomination. If the policy is assigned or transferred to the insurer in return for a loan, the nomination continues, but only to the extent of the insurer's interest. Option a contradicts this cancellation rule. Option b is wrong because nomination can be made in the policy itself, in the proposal, or by a later endorsement. Option c is wrong because assignment can be made to any person, including banks and financial institutions, as security for loans.
explanations: Incorrect: an absolute assignment to a third party cancels the earlier nomination.
Incorrect: nomination is made on the policy or the proposal form or by endorsement, not only by will.
Incorrect: assignment is not restricted to relatives, and banks and financial institutions commonly take assignments as loan security.
Correct: assignment transfers the rights, and an absolute assignment to a person other than the insurer cancels the nomination.
keyfact: An absolute assignment of a life policy cancels any earlier nomination (Section 39 read with Section 38).
options: A nomination remains fully effective even after the policy is absolutely assigned to a third party
A nomination can be made only by a will and cannot be made in the policy itself
An assignment can be made only in favour of a close relative and never to a bank or financial institution
Assignment transfers the policyholder's rights in the policy to the assignee, and a subsequent absolute assignment to a person other than the insurer cancels an earlier nomination
question: Under the Insurance Act, 1938, Section 38 deals with assignment and Section 39 with nomination of life insurance policies. Which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Section 38 governs assignment and Section 39 governs nomination.
Notice of assignment must be given in writing to the insurer.
Nomination can be changed or cancelled by endorsement or a written notice to the insurer.
Under Section 39, as amended in 2015, certain close family members named as nominees can be treated as beneficial owners of the policy money.
subject: Insurance
summary: The correct answer is option d. Assignment transfers the rights in the policy to the assignee, and an absolute assignment to anyone other than the insurer cancels an earlier nomination.

detail: The Bill follows the recommendations of the High-Level Committee on simultaneous elections chaired by former President Ram Nath Kovind. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 by the Law Minister, together with a companion Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill. After a division vote on introduction, it was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee. It aims to hold elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies simultaneously. Elimination: it was not passed by both Houses and has no assent. It was introduced in the Lok Sabha, not the Rajya Sabha, and no Article 143 reference was made. Local body elections were not the main object of the Bill. So (a) alone is correct.
explanations: Correct: introduced in the Lok Sabha on 17 December 2024 and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
Incorrect: it was not passed by both Houses or given assent in December 2024.
Incorrect: it was introduced in the Lok Sabha, and no Article 143 reference was made.
Incorrect: the Bill concerns simultaneous Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections, not just local body elections.
keyfact: The 129th Amendment Bill, 2024 on simultaneous elections was introduced in the Lok Sabha and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
options: It was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for examination
It was passed by both Houses of Parliament in December 2024 and received Presidential assent
It was introduced in the Rajya Sabha and referred to the Supreme Court for an advisory opinion under Article 143
It proposes to hold only Panchayat and Municipal elections simultaneously with Lok Sabha elections
question: Which one of the following statements about the Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-ninth Amendment) Bill, 2024, relating to simultaneous elections, is correct?
related: The High-Level Committee on One Nation One Election was chaired by Ram Nath Kovind.
The Bill was accompanied by a Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill.
A constitutional amendment affecting federal matters may require ratification by half of the States under Article 368.
The Bill inserts a new Article 82A on simultaneous elections.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: The correct answer is (a). The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 17 December 2024 and then sent to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for detailed scrutiny. It provides for simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
topic: Indian Polity - One Nation One Election

detail: Fundamental Duties are placed in Part IVA (Article 51A), not Part IV, which contains the Directive Principles. They were inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976 on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, originally ten in number. The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the eleventh duty, for a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child aged six to fourteen. Duties are non-justiciable and not directly enforceable by writs, though courts may use them in interpreting laws. So (b) fails on the Part, (c) on enforceability and (d) on the original list.
explanations: Correct: 42nd Amendment, 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.
Incorrect: Article 51A is in Part IVA, not Part IV.
Incorrect: Fundamental Duties are not directly enforceable by courts through writs.
Incorrect: this duty was added as the eleventh duty by the 86th Amendment, 2002.
keyfact: Fundamental Duties: Part IVA, Article 51A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976; the eleventh duty was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002.
options: They were added to the Constitution on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976
They are contained in Article 51A in Part IV of the Constitution
They are enforceable by the courts through writs under Article 32
The duty to provide opportunities for education to a child between the ages of six and fourteen years was included in the original list of ten duties
question: With reference to the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements regarding the Fundamental Duties is correct?
related: The original list had ten Fundamental Duties; there are now eleven
Part IVA contains only one Article, Article 51A
The Fundamental Duties were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR
The 86th Amendment also inserted Article 21A
subject: Indian Polity
summary: Option (a) is correct. The 42nd Amendment inserted Part IVA with Article 51A on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

detail: Section 14 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 deals with recognition of a negotiating union or negotiating council. If a single trade union has the support of at least fifty-one per cent of the workers on the muster roll, the employer must recognise it as the sole negotiating union. If no union has such support, the employer must constitute a negotiating council that consists of representatives of unions having at least twenty per cent of the workers on the muster roll as members. The number of representatives from each union is in proportion to its membership. The council must include the representatives of the employer too, and the number of employer representatives does not exceed the number of union representatives. For elimination: all unions regardless of membership is wrong because the threshold exists to keep the council workable. The highest-membership option is wrong because that union would only get recognition if it reached 51 per cent. Ten per cent is the trap taken from trade union registration criteria, which is a different threshold.
explanations: Incorrect. The Code sets a membership threshold, so not every union qualifies.
Incorrect. A single union gets recognition only with fifty-one per cent support; otherwise a council of eligible unions is formed.
Correct. Unions with at least twenty per cent of the workers on the muster roll as members are represented on the negotiating council.
Incorrect. Ten per cent is a registration-related benchmark, not the threshold for the negotiating council.
keyfact: Negotiating union needs 51 per cent; failing that, a negotiating council of unions with at least 20 per cent membership.
options: Every registered trade union in the establishment, irrespective of its membership
Only the trade union with the highest membership
Trade unions having at least twenty per cent of the total workers on the muster roll as their members
Trade unions having at least ten per cent of the total workers on the muster roll as their members
question: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, where no trade union has the support of fifty-one per cent of the workers on the muster roll for recognition as the sole negotiating union, the employer is required to constitute a negotiating council. Which of the following trade unions are entitled to be represented on that council?
related: Sole negotiating union: support of at least 51 per cent of workers on the muster roll.
Negotiating council: unions with at least 20 per cent membership, represented in proportion to membership.
Employer representatives on the council cannot exceed the number of union representatives.
The recognition is meant for negotiation with the employer on matters in the Code.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is unions with at least twenty per cent of the workers on the muster roll as members. These unions send representatives to the negotiating council in proportion to their membership.
topic: Recognition of negotiating union and negotiating council (IR Code, 2020)

detail: Market prices include the effect of indirect taxes, which raise prices, and subsidies, which lower them. To arrive at the income actually received by factors of production, the following adjustment is made: GDP at factor cost = GDP at market prices - indirect taxes + subsidies. Equivalently, GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost + net indirect taxes. Option (b) states this precisely. Option (a) describes the reverse of the adjustment. Option (c) describes nothing in particular and keeps market-price distortions. Option (d) wrongly says subsidies are also removed, whereas they are added back to the market price. Note that India currently reports GDP at constant market prices, plus Gross Value Added at basic prices, which equals GVA at factor cost plus production taxes less subsidies.
explanations: Incorrect: factor cost removes indirect taxes rather than including them.
Correct: factor cost = market price - indirect taxes + subsidies.
Incorrect: including indirect taxes would give a market-price measure, not factor cost.
Incorrect: subsidies are added back, not removed.
keyfact: GDP at factor cost = GDP at market prices - indirect taxes + subsidies.
options: It includes indirect taxes but excludes subsidies
It excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies
It includes both indirect taxes and subsidies
It excludes both indirect taxes and subsidies from the market value
question: Which one of the following is a feature of 'Gross Domestic Product at factor cost' as compared with 'GDP at market prices'?
related: GDP at market prices = GDP at factor cost + indirect taxes - subsidies.
Net Domestic Product = GDP - depreciation.
GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad.
India's GDP series uses a base year of 2011-12 (revision to a newer base year is underway).
subject: Indian Economy
summary: GDP at factor cost equals GDP at market prices minus indirect taxes plus subsidies. So it excludes indirect taxes and includes subsidies.

detail: Chandrayaan-3 was launched on the LVM3 rocket and landed on 23 August 2023 at about 69.37°S, near the lunar south polar region. The landing site was named Shiv Shakti Point. The rover Pragyan carried two payloads: LIBS and the Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer (APXS). LIBS detected sulphur along with other elements such as aluminium, calcium, iron, chromium and titanium. Pragyan was small and solar-powered, so it had no strong direct link to Earth. Its data went to the Vikram lander, which sent them on to the Indian Deep Space Network at Byalalu. Elimination: once statement 3 is recognised as false, options (b), (c) and (d) all fall away. Statement 3 is the most testable one because UPSC likes questions on the communication chain.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate and statement 3 is false.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is false, and leaves out statement 1, which is true.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is false, and leaves out statement 2, which is true.
Wrong: statement 3 is false because the rover communicated through the lander.
keyfact: Pragyan talked to Vikram, and Vikram talked to Earth; the rover had no direct link to Earth.
question:
With reference to India's Chandrayaan-3 mission, consider the following statements:
1. The touchdown location of the Vikram lander in August 2023 was subsequently named 'Shiv Shakti Point'.
2. The Pragyan rover's Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscope (LIBS) payload reported the presence of sulphur in the lunar soil near the landing site.
3. The Pragyan rover communicated directly with the Indian Deep Space Network on Earth, without using the lander as a relay.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Chandrayaan-3 was launched by LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III) from Sriharikota.
Vikram's ChaSTE payload measured the temperature profile of the lunar topsoil.
The propulsion module carried the SHAPE payload to study Earth's spectro-polarimetric signatures.
Chandrayaan-2's orbiter continued working and served as an additional communication link.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Vikram landing point was named Shiv Shakti Point. Chandrayaan-2's crash site was named Tiranga Point.
2 — Correct: LIBS on Pragyan confirmed sulphur in lunar soil near the south pole, along with several other elements.
3 — Incorrect: Pragyan transmitted data to the Vikram lander, which relayed them to the Indian Deep Space Network. The rover did not link directly to Earth.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: The answer is (a). Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because Pragyan communicated through the Vikram lander, not directly with Earth.

detail: The 2024 FIDE World Chess Championship was played in Singapore in November-December 2024 between the defending champion Ding Liren and challenger D. Gukesh, who had won the 2024 Candidates Tournament in Toronto. Gukesh won the match 7.5-6.5 by winning the final, 14th game, at age 18. He broke the record of Garry Kasparov, who became champion at 22. Gukesh is only the second Indian world champion after Viswanathan Anand. To eliminate options, note that Carlsen did not defend his title in this cycle and that Nepomniachtchi was Gukesh's Candidates-cycle rival, not the 2024 title opponent. Caruana was a Candidates rival, not the champion. Only Ding Liren was the reigning champion.
explanations: Correct: Gukesh beat Ding Liren in Singapore.
Incorrect: Carlsen was not part of the 2024 title match.
Incorrect: Nepomniachtchi did not play Gukesh in the final and the match was not in Chennai.
Incorrect: Caruana was a Candidates competitor, not the opponent in the title match.
keyfact: Gukesh (aged 18) beat Ding Liren in Singapore in December 2024 to become the youngest undisputed world champion.
options: Ding Liren of China, at Singapore
Magnus Carlsen of Norway, at Dubai
Ian Nepomniachtchi of Russia, at Chennai
Fabiano Caruana of the USA, at Singapore
question: In December 2024, D. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in history. Whom did he defeat in the title match, and where was it held?
related: Gukesh won the 2024 Candidates Tournament in Toronto.
Viswanathan Anand is the only other Indian world champion.
Gukesh broke Garry Kasparov's record as youngest champion.
The 2024 match was a 14-game classical match.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Gukesh defeated China's Ding Liren in the title match in Singapore, so the answer is (a). He won 7.5-6.5 after winning the 14th game.

detail: The Natyashastra, attributed to Bharata Muni, is the foundational Sanskrit text on performing arts. It covers stagecraft, acting (abhinaya), dance, music, and rasa. Its rasa sutra says rasa arises from the combination (samyoga) of vibhava (determinants), anubhava (consequents) and vyabhichari bhava (transitory states). The standard enumeration lists eight rasas, and shanta was later championed as a ninth by thinkers such as Abhinavagupta. In statement-type questions, first test each statement independently. Here both pass. Then ask whether II is the reason for I. It is not, because the text's age and scope are not caused by its rasa doctrine. That eliminates (a), and the correctness of both statements eliminates (c) and (d).
explanations: Wrong: the rasa doctrine is a content feature and does not account for the text being the earliest comprehensive treatise.
Correct: both statements are true, but II is not the explanation of I.
Wrong: Statement-II accurately states the rasa sutra's components.
Wrong: Statement-I is accurate; Bharata's work is the earliest surviving comprehensive treatise.
keyfact: Rasa arises from vibhava + anubhava + vyabhichari bhava (Natyashastra's rasa sutra).
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Natyashastra, attributed to Bharata Muni, is regarded as the earliest surviving comprehensive Indian treatise on dramaturgy, which also deals with music and dance.
Statement-II: According to its rasa theory, rasa is realised through the union of vibhava, anubhava and vyabhichari (sanchari) bhava.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The Natyashastra is attributed to Bharata Muni.
Abhinavagupta wrote the Abhinavabharati commentary on the Natyashastra.
The standard Natyashastra enumeration lists eight rasas.
Shanta is the rasa later accepted as the ninth.
The Natyashastra is often called the fifth Veda in tradition.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: Both statements are factually correct. Statement-II describes one doctrine within the treatise but does not explain why the Natyashastra is considered the earliest comprehensive work, so (b) is correct.

detail: In a digital signature scheme the sender computes a hash of the message and encrypts it with their own private key. Anyone can verify using the sender's public key, because only the holder of the private key could have produced the signature. This gives authentication, integrity and non-repudiation. By contrast, confidentiality uses the receiver's public key to encrypt, with the receiver's private key to decrypt. Option a reverses the keys, which would let anyone forge signatures. Option c describes symmetric cryptography, such as a MAC, which does not give non-repudiation. Option d is wrong because the sender never has the receiver's private key.
explanations: Incorrect: the keys are reversed; the public key cannot create a verifiable signature.
Correct: sign with the sender's private key, verify with the sender's public key.
Incorrect: a shared secret key is symmetric and cannot give non-repudiation.
Incorrect: the receiver's private key is never available to the sender.
keyfact: Sign with your private key, verify with your public key.
options: The sender signs the message hash with the sender's public key and the receiver verifies with the sender's private key
The sender signs the message hash with the sender's private key and the receiver verifies with the sender's public key
The same shared secret key is used for both signing and verification
The receiver's private key is used by the sender to encrypt the signature
question: Which one of the following is a characteristic of asymmetric (public-key) cryptography used in digital signatures?
related: Confidentiality: encrypt with the receiver's public key
RSA is a widely used asymmetric algorithm
AES is a symmetric block cipher
In India, digital signatures are recognised under the Information Technology Act, 2000
subject: Computers
summary: A digital signature is created with the sender's private key and verified with the sender's public key. This provides authentication, integrity and non-repudiation.

detail: The Pallava dynasty is a favourite of UPSC. Mahendravarman I (c. 600-630 CE) patronised Jainism early on, then embraced Shaivism under the influence of Appar (Tirunavukkarasar). His titles include Mattavilasa and Vichitrachitta. Narasimhavarman I Mamalla (c. 630-668 CE) defeated Pulakeshin II, captured Vatapi (Badami) around 642 CE and assumed the title Vatapikonda. Narasimhavarman II Rajasimha (c. 700-728 CE) built the Shore Temple at Mamallapuram and the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram. Because each statement is a standard, textbook-level fact, none can be eliminated, and the answer is all three.
explanations: Wrong: at least two statements are correct, and in fact all three are.
Wrong: no statement can be rejected, so two is too few.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
Wrong: the statements are all valid.
keyfact: Narasimhavarman I Mamalla took Vatapi (c. 642 CE) and the title Vatapikonda; Rajasimha built the Shore Temple.
question:
With reference to the Pallava rulers of Kanchipuram, consider the following statements:
1. Mahendravarman I was originally a Jaina who was converted to Shaivism by the Nayanar saint Appar.
2. The Shore Temple at Mamallapuram was built during the reign of Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha).
3. Narasimhavarman I defeated the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II and took the title Vatapikonda.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Mahendravarman I wrote the play Mattavilasa Prahasana.
The Pallava capital was Kanchipuram.
Rajasimha also built the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram.
Mamallapuram rathas were carved under Narasimhavarman I.
Pulakeshin II of the Chalukyas had earlier defeated Mahendravarman I.
statements: 1 — Correct: Mahendravarman I was a Jaina who turned to Shaivism under Appar.
2 — Correct: The Shore Temple is attributed to Rajasimha (Narasimhavarman II).
3 — Correct: Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakeshin II and took the title Vatapikonda. The Pallavas thus moved from Jaina patronage to Shaiva and Vaishnava temple building.
subject: Ancient History
summary: All three statements are correct. They reflect well-established facts about Mahendravarman I's religious change, Rajasimha's temple building and Narasimhavarman I's victory over Pulakeshin II.

detail: The 106th Amendment inserted Articles 330A, 332A and 334A. It reserves one-third of all seats, including those for SCs and STs, for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Legislative Assembly of Delhi. Within the SC and ST seats, one-third is reserved for women of those communities. It does not apply to the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Councils. Implementation is linked to delimitation after the first Census taken after the Act's commencement. The reservation lasts for fifteen years from commencement, extendable by Parliament, and rotation of seats follows each delimitation. To eliminate options, spot that statement 2 is wrong, which removes options a, c and d.
explanations: Wrong: it includes statement 2, which is incorrect, and omits statement 4.
Correct: statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct.
Wrong: it includes statement 2 and omits statements 1 and 3.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect, so not all four are correct.
keyfact: 106th Amendment: one-third seats for women in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies only, after delimitation, for 15 years.
question:
With reference to the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam), consider the following statements:
1. One-third of the seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies are to be reserved for women of those categories.
2. The reservation also applies to the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils.
3. The reservation is to come into effect only after a delimitation exercise undertaken following the first Census taken after the commencement of the Act.
4. The reservation is provided for a period of fifteen years from its commencement, which Parliament may extend.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: The Act inserted Articles 330A, 332A and 334A.
It also covers the Legislative Assembly of Delhi.
Rotation of reserved seats is to occur after each delimitation.
Implementation is linked to delimitation after the Census.
The reservation does not cover the Rajya Sabha.
statements: 1 — Correct: Women of SC and ST categories get one-third of the SC and ST seats.
2 — Incorrect: The Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils are excluded.
3 — Correct: Implementation depends on delimitation after the relevant Census.
4 — Correct: The initial period is fifteen years, extendable by Parliament.
The Act was passed in September 2023 and covers the Delhi Assembly as well. Articles 330A and 332A cover the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, and Article 334A covers commencement and duration.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct, so the answer is option b. The reservation does not extend to the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Councils.

detail: In Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa (1978), a seven-judge bench of the Supreme Court gave a wide reading of 'industry' under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act. The triple test requires: (i) systematic activity; (ii) organised by cooperation between employer and employee; and (iii) for the production or distribution of goods and services calculated to satisfy human wants and wishes. Profit motive is not essential. The decision also dealt with the exemption of some categories, such as sovereign functions and certain charitable activity. The other cases are well known on different points. Hussainbhai concerns the test of who is the real employer when labour is supplied through an intermediary. Gujarat Steel Tubes deals with the Labour Court's power over domestic inquiries. Air India Statutory Corporation concerns the absorption of contract labour. Knowing the issue each case decided is the key to elimination.
explanations: Correct: the seven-judge bench in Rajappa (1978) laid down the triple test for 'industry'.
Incorrect: Hussainbhai concerned the real employer when workers are supplied through an intermediary.

detail: Ashoka's edicts are the earliest datable royal inscriptions of India that can be read in full. Most of them are in Prakrit written in Brahmi. James Prinsep of the Asiatic Society of Bengal deciphered Brahmi in 1837, which opened up early Indian epigraphy and identified Piyadasi with Ashoka. Major Rock Edict XIII describes the conquest of Kalinga, the deaths and deportations, and the emperor's remorse and turn to dhamma. In the north-west, at places such as Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, the edicts are in Kharosthi. In Afghanistan there are Greek and Aramaic inscriptions, for example at Kandahar and Laghman. To eliminate options, you only need to know that Ashoka used scripts other than Brahmi. That rules out statement 3 and therefore options (b), (c) and (d).
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is false.
Wrong: statement 3 is false because other scripts were also used.
Wrong: it includes the false statement 3 and omits the true statement 2.
Wrong: statement 3 is false.
keyfact: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837; Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII records his remorse over the Kalinga war.
question:
With reference to the inscriptions of Ashoka, consider the following statements:
1. The Brahmi script in which most of his edicts were written was deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.
2. Major Rock Edict XIII expresses the emperor's remorse over the suffering caused by the Kalinga war.
3. All of his inscriptions found across the subcontinent are written only in the Brahmi script.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra edicts are in Kharosthi.
The Kandahar inscriptions include Greek and Aramaic.
Maski and Gujarra edicts name Ashoka explicitly.
Ashoka's edicts refer to him as Devanampiya Piyadasi.
The Kalinga edicts are the separate rock edicts found in Dhauli and Jaugada.
statements: 1 — Correct: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837.
2 — Correct: Rock Edict XIII records his remorse over the Kalinga war and his emphasis on dhamma.

3 — Incorrect: edicts in the north-west use Kharosthi, and those in Afghanistan use Greek and Aramaic. Brahmi was used for most inscriptions elsewhere. Kharosthi was written right to left, while Brahmi was written left to right.
subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: The answer is 1 and 2 only. James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi in 1837 and Rock Edict XIII records Ashoka's remorse over Kalinga. Not all Ashokan inscriptions are in Brahmi, since some in the north-west use Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic.

detail: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Article 43A (workers' participation in management) and Article 48A (environment, forests and wildlife). Article 49 requires the State to protect monuments and places of national importance. Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 is now a Fundamental Right under Article 21A. The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A and rewrote Article 45 to provide for early childhood care and education for children until they complete six years of age. The pair for Article 45 therefore uses the old, pre-2002 wording. Knowing the 86th Amendment's effect is enough to eliminate the options that treat all four pairs as correct.
explanations: Wrong: three pairs are correct.
Wrong: three pairs are correct, not two.
Correct: pairs 1, 3 and 4 match, and only pair 2 is wrong.
Wrong: Pair 2 uses the pre-2002 wording of Article 45.
keyfact: Article 45 now covers early childhood care and education below six years; education for ages 6 to 14 is a Fundamental Right under Article 21A.
question:
Consider the following pairs:

2. Article 45 : Free and compulsory education for children up to fourteen years of age
3. Article 49 : Protection of monuments and places and objects of national importance
4. Article 48A : Protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife

3 — Correct: Article 49 covers protection of monuments and places of national importance.
4 — Correct: Article 48A was inserted by the 42nd Amendment and covers environment, forests and wildlife.
subject: Polity
summary: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched. Pair 2 is wrong because Article 45 now deals with early childhood care and education for children below six years, since the 86th Amendment.

detail: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission. The proviso to Article 324(5) protects the CEC with a Supreme Court judge style removal, while other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation. Article 243K and Article 243ZA create State Election Commissions for Panchayats and Municipalities. Their commissioners are appointed by the Governor, so statement 2 is wrong. Under Article 103, the President decides questions of disqualification of MPs under Article 102(1) after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission and acts according to that opinion. Article 192 similarly gives the Governor this role for State legislators. Elimination: spotting statement 2 as false removes options a, c and d.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect, since local body elections are run by State Election Commissions.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect, so not all three hold.
keyfact: Article 103: the President acts on the Election Commission's opinion in disqualification of MPs; local body polls are run by State Election Commissions.
question:
With reference to the Election Commission of India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 324 provides that an Election Commissioner can be removed from office only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
2. The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities in the States.
3. In a question of disqualification of a Member of Parliament under Article 102(1), the President is required to obtain the opinion of the Election Commission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.
The Election Commission has no jurisdiction over elections to Panchayats and Municipalities.
Article 324(2) provides for appointment of the CEC and ECs by the President subject to a law of Parliament.
Delimitation Commission orders cannot be questioned in any court.
The Election Commission recognises political parties and allots symbols.
statements: 1 — Correct: Per the proviso to Article 324(5), any other Election Commissioner is removable only on the CEC's recommendation.
2 — Incorrect: Panchayat and Municipality elections are conducted by State Election Commissions under Articles 243K and 243ZA.
3 — Correct: Article 103(2) requires the President to obtain the Election Commission's opinion and act according to it.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Article 324(5) allows removal of an Election Commissioner only on the CEC's recommendation, and Article 103 makes the Election Commission's opinion binding on the President for MP disqualification. Local body elections belong to State Election Commissions.

detail: The Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-92) was fought by Cornwallis against Tipu, who had attacked Travancore, an ally of the British. By the Treaty of Seringapatam, Tipu ceded roughly half of his kingdom (to the British, the Marathas and the Nizam) and paid a large indemnity, with two sons held as hostages. The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) ended the Second war and was signed with Warren Hastings's government (Governor of Madras Macartney's envoys), not Cornwallis. Tipu died in 1799 in the Fourth war. Hyder Ali died in December 1782 during the Second war, and the First war (1767-69) ended with the Treaty of Madras. Each distractor changes one detail, which makes it easy to eliminate.
explanations: Correct: the 1792 treaty ended the Third war with heavy territorial and financial losses for Tipu.
Wrong: the Treaty of Mangalore (1784) ended the Second war and Cornwallis was not Governor-General then.
Wrong: Tipu Sultan was killed in 1799, in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.
Wrong: Hyder Ali died in 1782 during the Second war, and the Treaty of Madras ended the First war.
keyfact: Seringapatam 1792 ended the Third Mysore War, Mangalore 1784 the Second, and Tipu died in 1799.
options: The Treaty of Seringapatam (1792) ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War, and Tipu Sultan lost nearly half of his territory and paid a heavy war indemnity.
The Treaty of Mangalore (1784) ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War and was signed between Tipu Sultan and Lord Cornwallis.
Tipu Sultan was killed in the Third Anglo-Mysore War while defending Seringapatam.
Hyder Ali died during the First Anglo-Mysore War and the war ended with the Treaty of Madras.
question: With reference to the Anglo-Mysore Wars, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799) ended with Tipu's death and the restoration of the Wodeyars under Wellesley.
The First Anglo-Mysore War (1767-69) ended with the Treaty of Madras.
Tipu Sultan sent embassies to France, Turkey and Arabia.
Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance was imposed on Mysore after 1799.
subject: Modern History
summary: The Treaty of Seringapatam (1792) ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War. Tipu ceded about half his territory and paid an indemnity, with two of his sons held as hostages.

detail: Marine insurance in India is governed by the Marine Insurance Act, 1963, which is based on the English Marine Insurance Act, 1906. The principal classes are hull insurance, cargo insurance and freight insurance. Hull insurance protects the shipowner against loss or damage to the vessel, its machinery and equipment. Cargo insurance protects the owner of the goods, often the importer or exporter, against loss or damage during transit. Freight insurance covers the loss of freight earnings if cargo is lost. Elimination: option b reverses the definitions. Option c wrongly mixes freight and liability; crew liability is not what cargo insurance covers. Option d is wrong because cargo is not the vessel. Insurable interest must exist at the time of loss in marine insurance.
explanations: Correct. Hull covers the ship; cargo covers goods carried.
Incorrect. The definitions are reversed.
Incorrect. Freight is a separate class and cargo cover does not insure crew liability.
Incorrect. Cargo policies insure goods, not the vessel.
keyfact: Hull policy insures the vessel; cargo policy insures goods carried; the governing law is the Marine Insurance Act, 1963.
options: Hull insurance covers the vessel itself, while cargo insurance covers the goods carried on the vessel
Hull insurance covers the goods carried, while cargo insurance covers the vessel
Hull insurance covers freight earnings only, while cargo insurance covers crew liability
Both cover only the vessel but for different voyages
question: In marine insurance, a 'Hull' policy and a 'Cargo' policy differ in that:
related: The Marine Insurance Act, 1963 governs marine insurance in India.
Freight insurance covers loss of freight earnings.
In marine insurance, insurable interest must exist at the time of loss, though not necessarily at the time of contract.
General average and particular average are types of marine loss.
subject: Insurance
summary: Hull insurance covers the ship's body, machinery and equipment, while cargo insurance covers the goods transported. They are separate subject matters with different insured parties, typically the shipowner and the cargo owner.

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 carries forward the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 as amended in 2017. The benefit is 26 weeks for a woman with fewer than two surviving children, with at most 8 weeks before delivery. With two or more surviving children it is 12 weeks, with at most 6 weeks before delivery. An adopting mother (child under three months) and a commissioning mother get 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over. The eligibility condition is actual work of at least 80 days in the 12 months before the expected delivery. Examiners commonly swap 80 for a larger number such as 160 or 240. Once you spot that 3 is wrong, options (b), (c) and (d) are eliminated, because each of them includes statement 3.
explanations: Correct: statements 1, 2 and 4 match the Code, and statement 3 is the only wrong one.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and leaves out the correct statements 2 and 4.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is incorrect, and omits statement 1, which is correct.
Wrong: statement 3 misstates the 80-day qualifying period, so not all four can be correct.
keyfact: Maternity benefit: 26 weeks (max 8 weeks pre-delivery) for the first two children, 12 weeks thereafter; the qualifying period is 80 days.
question:
With reference to maternity benefit under the Code on Social Security, 2020, consider the following statements:
1. A woman with fewer than two surviving children is entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit, of which not more than 8 weeks may precede the expected date of delivery.
2. A woman who already has two or more surviving children is entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit.
3. A woman must have worked in the establishment for at least 160 days in the 12 months immediately preceding the expected date of delivery to be eligible.
4. A woman who legally adopts a child below three months of age, or a commissioning mother, is entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit from the date the child is handed over.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Qualifying period for maternity benefit is 80 days in the preceding 12 months.
Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 raised paid leave from 12 to 26 weeks.
A woman with two or more surviving children gets 12 weeks.
Adopting and commissioning mothers get 12 weeks, the child being under three months.
Maternity benefit is payable at the rate of the average daily wage.
statements: 1 — Correct: 26 weeks for fewer than two surviving children, with a maximum of 8 weeks pre-delivery.
2 — Correct: 12 weeks (maximum 6 weeks pre-delivery) where she has two or more surviving children.
3 — Incorrect: the qualifying period is 80 days of work in the preceding 12 months, not 160.
4 — Correct: 12 weeks from the date the child is handed over to an adopting or commissioning mother, the child being under three months.
subject: Social Security
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the qualifying period is 80 days in the preceding 12 months, not 160.
topic: Maternity Benefit under the Code on Social Security

detail: Articles 81 and 82 provide for the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among States and readjustment after every census. The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze the allocation of seats among States, based on the 1971 census, until the first census taken after 2000. The 84th Amendment (2001) extended this freeze, so no readjustment of the allocation among States is needed until the first census taken after 2026. It also provided for rationalising territorial constituencies within States based on the 1991 census, and the 87th Amendment (2003) substituted the 2001 census for delimitation within States, without changing the freeze. The 91st Amendment (2003) concerns the anti-defection law and limits the size of the Council of Ministers to 15 per cent of the House, so it is irrelevant here. The 42nd Amendment's freeze is the original one, not the extension, which eliminates option (a).
explanations: Incorrect: the 42nd Amendment imposed the original freeze, running only up to the first census after 2000.
Correct: the 84th Amendment extended the freeze to the first census taken after 2026.
Incorrect: the 87th Amendment substituted the 2001 census for delimitation within States and did not extend the freeze.
Incorrect: the 91st Amendment limited the size of Councils of Ministers and tightened anti-defection law.
keyfact: The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the inter-State seat freeze until the first census taken after 2026.
question: Which one of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts extended, up to the first census taken after the year 2026, the freeze on the readjustment of the allocation of Lok Sabha seats among the States?
related: Article 81 sets the maximum Lok Sabha strength at 550, comprising up to 530 State members and up to 20 Union Territory members.
The Delimitation Commission's orders have the force of law and cannot be questioned in any court.
The 104th Amendment (2019) ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies.
The 106th Amendment (2023), the Women's Reservation Act, links implementation to delimitation after the first census following its commencement.
subject: Polity
summary: The Eighty-fourth Amendment Act, 2001 extended the freeze on inter-State readjustment of Lok Sabha seats until the first census taken after 2026. The earlier freeze, imposed by the 42nd Amendment, ran only up to the first census after 2000.

detail: Salinity depends on the balance between evaporation and freshwater input from rain, rivers and ice melt. In the subtropical high-pressure belts, skies are clear, winds are dry and evaporation exceeds precipitation. This produces maximum open-ocean surface salinity, roughly at 20°–30° in both hemispheres. At the equator, heavy convectional rain and high humidity dilute the surface water, so salinity is somewhat lower. Salinity also falls towards the poles because of low evaporation and ice melt. Statement-II gives exactly the causal mechanism for Statement-I, which rules out option (b). Both statements are factually sound, which rules out (c) and (d).
explanations: Correct: both statements are true, and the evaporation-precipitation balance explains the subtropical salinity maximum.
Wrong: Statement-II is the direct explanation, not an unrelated fact.
Wrong: Statement-II is also correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Open-ocean surface salinity peaks around 20°–30° latitude, not at the equator.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Surface salinity in the open oceans is generally highest in the subtropical latitudes rather than at the equator.
Statement-II: In the subtropics evaporation exceeds precipitation, whereas the equatorial belt receives heavy rainfall and has high cloud cover.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Open-ocean salinity averages about 35 parts per thousand.
The Dead Sea and Lake Van are among the most saline water bodies.
The Baltic Sea has low salinity because of large river inflow and low evaporation.
Halocline is the zone of rapid salinity change with depth.
Salinity is lower in the Bay of Bengal than the Arabian Sea.
subject: Geography
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Open-ocean salinity peaks around 20–30° latitude because evaporation exceeds precipitation there.

detail: UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list is a favourite UPSC area, and the usual trap is to include a famous art form that has not been inscribed. Kutiyattam was proclaimed a Masterpiece in 2001 and formally inscribed in 2008. Ramman was inscribed in 2009. Garba was inscribed in 2023. Yakshagana is a prominent folk-classical theatre of coastal Karnataka, but it has no UNESCO ICH inscription. To eliminate options, a candidate who knows that Kutiyattam and Garba are inscribed can rule out 'Only one'. Knowing that Yakshagana is not inscribed rules out 'All four'. Ramman then decides between 'two' and 'three'.
explanations: Wrong: three of the four are inscribed, not one.
Wrong: Kutiyattam, Ramman and Garba are inscribed, so two undercounts.
Correct: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are right and only Yakshagana is not inscribed.
Wrong: Yakshagana is not inscribed, so not all four are correct.
keyfact: Kutiyattam, Ramman and Garba are UNESCO ICH elements; Yakshagana is not.

2. Ramman, the religious festival and ritual theatre of the Garhwal Himalayas, is an inscribed element.
3. Yakshagana of coastal Karnataka is an inscribed element.

3 — Incorrect: Yakshagana is not on the UNESCO ICH list.

detail: Before 1997 the government financed deficits through automatic monetisation using ad hoc Treasury Bills. After the 1997 agreement this was ended, and the FRBM Act, 2003, Section 5, barred the RBI from subscribing to primary issues of central government securities after 1 April 2006. Exceptions include ways and means advances and situations of exceptional circumstances as notified by the Centre. The RBI can still buy government securities in the secondary market through open market operations. The government therefore relies mostly on market borrowings through dated securities and Treasury Bills. Elimination logic: both statements are textbook facts, and the legal prohibition is the direct reason for the reliance on markets, so option (a) is right.
explanations: Correct: both are true and the FRBM prohibition explains the dependence on market borrowing.
Wrong: Statement-II does provide the explanation for Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: FRBM Act, 2003 bars RBI from subscribing to government securities in the primary market (from 2006).
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: In India, the Union Government's fiscal deficit is financed mainly through market borrowings, and the RBI is barred from directly subscribing to government securities in the primary market.
Statement-II: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 prohibits the RBI from subscribing to primary issues of Central Government securities, with certain exceptions.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The RBI can buy government securities in the secondary market through OMOs.
Ways and Means Advances are temporary loans from the RBI to the government.
The FRBM Act, 2003 was amended in 2018 to set a debt-to-GDP target.
The N.K. Singh Committee reviewed the FRBM Act.
subject: Economy
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. The FRBM Act, 2003 bars the RBI from subscribing to primary issues from 1 April 2006, with exceptions such as ways and means advances and devolvement during market stress.
topic: Fiscal Policy - FRBM and Deficit Financing

detail: Lake Baikal in southern Siberia, Russia, occupies a continental rift valley. It is the deepest lake on Earth, with a maximum depth of about 1,640 m, and the largest freshwater lake by volume. It holds roughly 20 per cent of the world's unfrozen surface freshwater. Hundreds of rivers feed it, including the Selenga. Its only major outflow is the Angara River, which flows to the Yenisei. The Lena rises close to Baikal's western shore but flows north-east to the Laptev Sea and has no connection to the lake. Statement 2 is the trap here. Eliminating it removes options (b) and (d) and leaves (c), which has statement 3 in addition to 1.
explanations: Wrong: statement 3 is also correct.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect, since the outflow is the Angara.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are right and 2 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 2 is not correct.
keyfact: Baikal drains through the Angara River (a Yenisei tributary), not the Lena.
question:
With reference to Lake Baikal, consider the following statements:

2. Its principal outflow is the Lena River.

Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake in the world.
The Angara River flows out of Baikal into the Yenisei system.
statements: 1 — Correct: Baikal is the deepest lake, at about 1,640 m, and lies in a rift.
2 — Incorrect: the outflow is the Angara River, a tributary of the Yenisei, not the Lena.
3 — Correct: it holds about 20 per cent of unfrozen surface freshwater.
subject: Geography
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Baikal drains through the Angara River, which is a tributary of the Yenisei, not the Lena.

detail: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, with M.G. Ranade and R.G. Bhandarkar as prominent leaders. Jyotirao Phule founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj in 1873 to secure social justice for the lower castes and challenge Brahmanical dominance. Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 to train national missionaries for public service. Candidates often confuse Atmaram Pandurang with Keshub Chandra Sen, who was associated with the Brahmo Samaj, or credit Ranade with founding the Samaj. Because all three attributions are correct, the answer is 'All three pairs'.
explanations: Wrong: at least two pairs are correct, and in fact all three are.
Wrong: the third pair is also correct, so two is an undercount.
Right: all three founders are correctly matched.
Wrong: every pair is correctly matched.
keyfact: Prarthana Samaj 1867 (Atmaram Pandurang); Satya Shodhak Samaj 1873 (Phule); Servants of India Society 1905 (Gokhale).

Phule wrote Gulamgiri.

statements: 1 — Correct: Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in 1867.
2 — Correct: Jyotirao Phule founded the Satya Shodhak Samaj in 1873.
3 — Correct: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905.
subject: Modern History
summary: All three pairs are correctly matched. Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj (1867), Phule the Satya Shodhak Samaj (1873) and Gokhale the Servants of India Society (1905).

detail: The BoP records all economic transactions between residents and non-residents. The current account has four components: trade in goods, trade in services, primary income, and secondary income. Primary income covers investment income, such as interest on external borrowing, and compensation of employees. Secondary income covers transfers such as remittances. Software exports are services trade and belong in the current account. The capital account in the older presentation, and the financial account in the BPM6 presentation, records cross-border investment and borrowing, including FDI, portfolio flows, and the principal of ECBs. A useful rule is that investment income (interest, dividends) goes in the current account, while the investment itself goes in the capital or financial account. So FDI inflows, though large, are not a current account item.
explanations: Incorrect: Three statements are correct, not one.
Incorrect: Only statement 3 is wrong, so three are correct, not two.
Correct: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are current account items, while FDI is not.
Incorrect: Statement 3 is incorrect, so not all four are correct.
keyfact: Investment income goes in the current account, but the investment flow itself (FDI, FPI, ECB principal) goes in the capital/financial account.
question:
With reference to India's Balance of Payments (BoP), consider the following statements:
1. Remittances received from Indian workers employed abroad are recorded in the current account.
2. Interest payments made on external commercial borrowings are recorded in the current account.
3. Foreign direct investment inflows into India are recorded in the current account.
4. Receipts from exports of software services are recorded in the current account.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Investment income such as interest and dividends is part of primary income in the current account.
Remittances are classified under secondary income.
FDI, FPI and ECB principal flows are financial/capital account items.
India usually has a merchandise trade deficit offset partly by a services surplus.
The Current Account Deficit is the net deficit on the current account.
statements: 1 — Correct: Remittances are private transfers and form part of secondary income in the current account.
2 — Correct: Interest on borrowing is investment income, which is part of primary income.
3 — Incorrect: FDI is a cross-border investment, recorded in the capital/financial account.
4 — Correct: Software exports are services trade, a current account item.
Facts: Current account = goods, services, primary income, secondary income. India usually runs a merchandise trade deficit and a services surplus, and remittances are among the largest in the world.
subject: Economy
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three'. FDI inflows are a capital (financial) account item, not a current account item.

detail: In Shankari Prasad (1951) the Court held that the amending power under Article 368 extends to Fundamental Rights and that an amendment is not 'law' under Article 13(2). Maneka Gandhi (1978) linked Articles 14, 19 and 21 and held that the procedure must be fair, just and reasonable, not merely prescribed by law. In L. Chandra Kumar (1997) the Court held that judicial review by the High Courts under Articles 226 and 227 and by the Supreme Court under Article 32 is part of the basic structure. It also held that tribunals are subject to High Court scrutiny. Minerva Mills (1980) struck down Section 4 and Section 55 of the 42nd Amendment, which had inserted Article 31C expansion and Article 368(4) and (5). It held that limited amending power is itself a basic feature. Pair 3 reverses the actual holding, so options (b), (c) and (d) are eliminated.
explanations: Correct: pairs 1, 2 and 4 are accurate, and pair 3 is wrong.
Incorrect: it includes pair 3 and excludes pairs 2 and 4, which are correct.
Incorrect: it includes pair 3 and leaves out pair 1, which is correct.
Incorrect: pair 3 is wrongly matched, so all four cannot be correct.
keyfact: Minerva Mills (1980) struck down the 42nd Amendment's curtailment of judicial review and declared limited amending power a basic feature.
question:

2. Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India — Held that the procedure under Article 21 must be fair, just and reasonable
3. Minerva Mills v. Union of India — Upheld the provisions of the 42nd Amendment curtailing judicial review of constitutional amendments

statements: 1 — Correct: Shankari Prasad (1951) held that amendments are not 'law' under Article 13.
2 — Correct: Maneka Gandhi (1978) broadened Article 21 to require fair, just and reasonable procedure.

subject: Polity
summary: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched. In Minerva Mills (1980) the Supreme Court struck down the 42nd Amendment provisions that curtailed judicial review and gave Parliament unlimited amending power.

detail: The International Solar Alliance was launched in November 2015 at Paris by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then French President François Hollande. Its Framework Agreement came into force in December 2017, making it a treaty-based international intergovernmental organisation, with headquarters in Gurugram, Haryana. Initially, membership was limited to sunshine-rich countries lying between the Tropics. The Framework Agreement was amended, and from 2020 all United Nations member states can join. ISA has observer status at the UN General Assembly but is not a UN specialised agency. To eliminate options, notice that statement 4 is wrong, which removes (b) and (c). Statement 3 is outdated, which removes (a), leaving (d).
explanations: Incorrect: Statement 3 is outdated, because membership has been open to all UN member states since the amendment.
Incorrect: Statement 4 is wrong, as ISA is not a UN specialised agency, and it omits the correct statements 1 and 2.
Incorrect: Both statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.
Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are accurate, and statements 3 and 4 are inaccurate.
keyfact: ISA: launched at COP21 (2015) by India and France, HQ Gurugram, a treaty-based organisation open to all UN member states.

detail: The IR Code recognises fixed term employment, where a worker is engaged on a written contract for a fixed period. The Code on Social Security relaxes the five-year gratuity rule for such employees, so that they are eligible pro rata after one year of service. The IR Code provides that fixed term employees receive hours of work, wages, allowances and other benefits that are not less favourable than those of permanent workers doing the same or similar work. Statement 2 fails because 'retrenchment' under the IR Code excludes termination on the expiry of a fixed term contract, so no retrenchment compensation is due merely because the contract is not renewed. Elimination is straightforward once statement 2 is recognised as false: only option (a) leaves it out.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 3 are true and statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: it includes statement 2, which is false.
Incorrect: it includes statement 2 and omits statement 3, which is true.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false, so all three cannot be correct.
keyfact: Fixed term employees get parity of benefits and pro rata gratuity after one year; non-renewal on expiry is not retrenchment.
question:
Consider the following statements regarding fixed term employment under the labour codes:

2. Non-renewal of a fixed term employment contract on its expiry is treated as retrenchment, attracting retrenchment compensation under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
3. A fixed term employee is entitled to the same working hours, wages, allowances and other benefits as a permanent employee doing the same or similar work.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Normally gratuity requires five years of continuous service, with exceptions for death or disablement.
Gratuity is payable at 15 days' wages for each completed year of service or part thereof exceeding six months.

Fixed term employment was introduced in the IR Code to give employers flexibility while maintaining parity of benefits.
statements: 1 — Correct: the Social Security Code gives gratuity to a fixed term employee after one year's service under the contract, pro rata, without the five-year condition.
2 — Incorrect: expiry of a fixed term contract without renewal is excluded from retrenchment, so compensation for retrenchment does not arise.
3 — Correct: parity in hours, wages, allowances and other benefits with comparable permanent workers is guaranteed.

Facts: fixed term employment must be by written contract. Statutory benefits are available proportionate to the service period, and the employer must give the employee the same statutory protections as permanent workers.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Industrial Relations Code excludes non-renewal of a fixed term contract on expiry from the definition of retrenchment.

detail: The 2024 Bharat Ratna recipients were Karpoori Thakur (posthumous), L. K. Advani, P. V. Narasimha Rao, Chaudhary Charan Singh and M. S. Swaminathan. Five in one year is the highest on record, and the statutory limit is a maximum of three per year, which is why the figure is notable. Statement 2 fails because Advani (Deputy PM and Home Minister) and Swaminathan (agricultural scientist) never served as Chief Ministers. Statement 4 fails because the Supreme Court in Balaji Raghavan (1996) held that national awards are not 'titles' under Article 18(1), but recipients must not use them as a prefix or suffix, and misuse can lead to forfeiture. Statements 1 and 3 are accurate, so exactly two are correct.

detail: The IIP measures short-term changes in the volume of industrial production relative to a base year. It is compiled by the NSO of MoSPI and released monthly, generally with a lag of about 28 days. It covers three broad sectors: Mining, Manufacturing and Electricity. Manufacturing carries by far the largest weight (roughly three-fourths), followed by Mining and then Electricity. The index is also classified by use-based categories such as primary goods, capital goods, intermediate goods, infrastructure/construction goods and consumer durables and non-durables. To eliminate: any option including statement 3 is wrong because Manufacturing dominates. Statement 2 is the defining feature of IIP as a quantity (volume) index, not a value index, so it must be included.

keyfact: IIP is a monthly volume index by NSO, dominated by Manufacturing weight.

subject: Indian Economy
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is wrong. The IIP is a monthly volume index compiled by NSO, and Manufacturing, not Mining, has the largest weight.

detail: The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman I, dated around 150 CE, is the earliest major inscription in classical Sanskrit and records the repair of the Sudarshana lake. The Aihole inscription at the Meguti temple was composed by the poet Ravikirti and records the victories of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, including over Harsha. The Nasik cave inscription of Gautami Balashri, the mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, celebrates her son, a Satavahana king, and not Kharavela of Kalinga, whose record is the Hathigumpha. The Allahabad pillar prashasti was composed by Harishena, a court poet of Samudragupta, so linking it with Ravikirti is a deliberate swap. Two pairs are correct.

Correct. Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched.
Incorrect. Pairs 3 and 4 are mismatched.
Incorrect. Not all pairs are correct.
keyfact: Junagadh: Rudradaman I; Aihole: Ravikirti for Pulakeshin II; Allahabad: Harishena.

summary: Only pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. The Nasik inscription of Gautami Balashri relates to Gautamiputra Satakarni, and the Allahabad prashasti was composed by Harishena.

detail: Section 139(7) provides that, in the case of a Government company or any other company owned or controlled directly or indirectly by the Central or State Government, the first auditor is appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India within 60 days from the date of registration. If the CAG does not appoint within that period, the Board of Directors appoints the auditor within the next 30 days. If the Board also fails, it must inform the members, who appoint the auditor within 60 days at an extraordinary general meeting. Option a describes the position for an ordinary company under Section 139(6), but with the further rule that if the Board fails, members act at an EGM within 90 days. Options c and d wrongly assign the power to members or the Central Government.
explanations: Incorrect: this is the rule for ordinary (non-Government) companies under Section 139(6), not for Government companies.

Incorrect: the members' EGM is the last fallback and is not the primary mechanism for a Government company.

detail: Guru Arjan Dev, the fifth Guru, compiled the Adi Granth in 1604 and installed it at the Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. It contained the compositions of the first five Gurus and of various bhagats and saints such as Kabir, Namdev, Ravidas and Sheikh Farid. Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Guru, lived after the compilation (he was executed in 1675), so his hymns could not have been in the original text. Guru Gobind Singh added them to the text. After him, the Guru Granth Sahib was declared the eternal Guru. Elimination: since Statement-II is an anachronism, options (a), (b) and (d) are ruled out. Always check dates when a later figure is claimed to appear in an earlier compilation.

Wrong. Statement-II is incorrect.

keyfact: The Adi Granth was compiled in 1604, and Tegh Bahadur's hymns were added later.

Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

subject: Medieval History
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. Guru Arjan Dev's 1604 compilation included saints like Kabir and Namdev, but Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymns were added later by Guru Gobind Singh.

detail: The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises eight classical dance forms: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Sattriya, Manipuri and Mohiniyattam. Mohiniyattam, the dance of the enchantress, is from Kerala, and Odissi is from Odisha. Manipuri, with its Raslila tradition, is from Manipur. Kuchipudi comes from Andhra Pradesh and is traditionally a dance-drama. Elimination works by recalling that Sattriya is Assamese and Mohiniyattam is Keralite, leaving (a).

detail: The clause 'even experts struggled to extract a clear recommendation' signals that the report was confusing. 'Convoluted' means intricate, twisted and difficult to follow, so it fits. 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand, and 'succinct' means brief and to the point, so both would make the sentence illogical, since a clear or concise report would not baffle experts. 'Forthright' means direct and frank, usually describing a person's manner, and it does not explain the difficulty. Use the consequence clause in a sentence as the clue to the needed tone.
explanations: Incorrect: lucid means clear, which contradicts the struggle described.
Correct: convoluted means overly complex, matching the difficulty experienced.
Incorrect: succinct means brief and clear, which would not cause confusion.
Incorrect: forthright means frank and direct, which does not explain the difficulty.
keyfact: Convoluted = intricate and hard to follow; the opposite is lucid.

subject: General English
summary: 'Convoluted' means extremely complex and hard to follow. This fits the idea that experts struggled to find a clear recommendation.

detail: X is the number of years from 2018, so X = year − 2018. With the new origin 2022, X′ = year − 2022. Therefore X = X′ + 4. Substituting into Y = 120 + 6X gives Y = 120 + 6X′ + 24 = 144 + 6X′. Only the intercept changes, because it is the trend value at the origin year (2022). The slope stays the same, since the annual increase in trend is still 6, which eliminates option b. Option c shifts the origin in the wrong direction (it would be correct for an origin of 2014). Option d ignores the shift altogether. A quick check: for the year 2022, the old equation gives 120 + 24 = 144, which matches the new intercept.
explanations: Correct. The new intercept equals the old trend value for 2022, 120 + 6×4 = 144, and the slope is unchanged.
Incorrect. The slope does not change when only the origin moves.
Incorrect. This subtracts 24, which would apply to an origin earlier than 2018.
Incorrect. It ignores the origin shift, so it is not valid for X′.
keyfact: Shifting the origin of a linear trend changes only the intercept (to the trend value at the new origin), not the slope.
question: The straight-line trend of annual sales fitted by least squares is Y = 120 + 6X, where the origin is the year 2018 and X is measured in units of one year. If the origin is shifted to the year 2022, what is the trend equation?

summary: The answer is Y = 144 + 6X′. With the new origin 2022, X = X′ + 4. Substituting gives Y = 120 + 6(X′ + 4) = 144 + 6X′.
topic: Time series: shifting the origin of a trend line

detail: The Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps) is a large, ground-nesting grassland bird. It is Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List and is in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. At the 2020 CMS Conference of Parties in Gandhinagar it was listed in Appendix I, which obliges parties to protect it strictly. Rajasthan holds the largest population, concentrated around Desert National Park and nearby areas, but the species also occurs in Gujarat (Kutch), Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. Statement 3 uses the absolute word 'only', which is a common UPSC trap, and it fails because the bird is not confined to one park. Threats include overhead power lines, habitat loss and predation of eggs and chicks.
