SA 240 deals with the auditor's responsibilities relating to fraud.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: For frauds below ₹1 crore, the auditor reports to the Audit Committee or the Board within two days of knowledge. Reporting to the Central Government is required only for frauds of ₹1 crore or more.

detail: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest inland water body, an endorheic lake that is called a sea because of its size and its saline water. Its five littoral states are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan. Uzbekistan lies east of the Caspian and borders the Aral Sea region, which has largely dried up, but it has no Caspian coast. It is also one of only two doubly landlocked countries, together with Liechtenstein, meaning that all its neighbours are themselves landlocked. Elimination is simple if you recall the five littoral states, since Azerbaijan, Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan are all among them.
explanations: Wrong: Azerbaijan lies on the western shore of the Caspian.
Wrong: Turkmenistan lies on the south-eastern shore.
Correct: Uzbekistan has no coast on the Caspian Sea.
Wrong: Kazakhstan has a long coastline on the northern and eastern shores.
keyfact: Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked and has no Caspian coast.
question: Which one of the following countries does NOT have a coastline on the Caspian Sea?
related: The Caspian's five littoral states are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are the only doubly landlocked countries.
The Volga is the main river flowing into the Caspian Sea.
The Caspian lies below sea level.
subject: Geography
summary: Uzbekistan does not border the Caspian Sea. The five littoral states are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.

detail: Contribution is a corollary of the principle of indemnity. It applies only to indemnity contracts such as fire, marine and motor insurance, and requires that the policies cover the same subject matter, same interest and same peril, and are all in force at the time of loss. An insured cannot recover more than the actual loss. If one insurer pays the entire loss, it may claim a proportionate share from the other insurers. Option (a) is wrong because life insurance is not a contract of indemnity. Option (c) describes subrogation, not contribution. Option (d) contradicts indemnity, which forbids profit from a loss.
explanations: Wrong: life insurance is not an indemnity contract, so contribution does not apply.
Right: contribution is the right of an insurer that has paid to claim a rateable share from co-insurers.
Wrong: this defines subrogation.
Wrong: the insured cannot recover more than the actual loss.
keyfact: Contribution is the right of an insurer to claim a rateable share from co-insurers; it applies only to indemnity contracts.
options: It applies to life insurance policies, enabling an insurer to recover from other life insurers on the same life
It arises where the same interest is insured against the same peril under two or more policies, and an insurer who pays more than its rateable share can claim from the others
It enables an insurer, after paying a claim, to take over the rights of the insured against third parties
It permits the insured to recover more than the actual loss by claiming from every insurer in full
question: With reference to the doctrine of contribution in insurance, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Contribution is a corollary of indemnity, as is subrogation.
Contribution is between insurers, while subrogation is between the insurer and a third party.
It does not apply to life or personal accident fixed-benefit policies.
The insured may claim from any one insurer, which then seeks contribution.
subject: Insurance
summary: The answer is (b). Contribution operates among insurers when the same subject matter, interest and peril are covered by multiple policies, ensuring each bears a rateable share of the loss. It prevents the insured from profiting.

detail: Chola bronzes of South India, such as the Nataraja and Shiva as Ardhanarishvara, were cast by the lost-wax method. The image is first modelled in beeswax, coated with layers of clay and heated so that the wax melts and runs out. Molten metal, traditionally an alloy often called panchaloha, is then poured into the cavity. The mould must be broken to take out the finished image, so it cannot be reused, and each piece is therefore unique even when it follows the iconographic rules of the Shilpa Shastras. This directly explains why no two icons are identical. On such questions, test whether the second statement is the cause of the first. Here it is, so option (b) can be eliminated.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true and the destruction of the mould explains uniqueness.
Wrong: the two are causally linked, so Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is accurate.
Wrong: Statement-I is accurate.
keyfact: The lost-wax process destroys the mould, so each Chola bronze is unique.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Chola bronze images are celebrated for the uniqueness of each individual icon.
Statement-II: Chola bronzes were generally made by the lost-wax (cire perdue) process, in which the clay mould is broken to retrieve the metal image, so the mould cannot be reused.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Cire perdue means lost wax.
Swamimalai is famed for bronze casting.
The Nataraja is the best-known Chola bronze.
Chola bronzes follow the Shilpa Shastras.
statements: Statement-I — Correct: Chola icons are valued for their individuality.
Statement-II — Correct: the clay mould is broken after casting, so it cannot be reused, and this explains the uniqueness.
Swamimalai in Tamil Nadu still practises this craft and holds a Geographical Indication tag.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Because the mould is destroyed in the lost-wax process, each image is effectively one of a kind.

detail: With variables ordered A (MSB), B, C, D, minterms 0 to 7 correspond to binary 0000 to 0111, in which A = 0 and B, C, D take all combinations. On a Karnaugh map these form one group of 8 cells (two adjacent rows), eliminating B, C, and D. The resulting term is A'. Option b would cover minterms 8 to 15. Option c, B', would cover minterms 0-3 and 8-11. Option a+b style option d, A' + B, would include minterms 12-15 as well, since B = 1 with A = 1 gives extra true cells. Hence only A' matches exactly.
explanations: Correct: all minterms with A = 0 give F = A'.
Incorrect: A covers minterms 8 to 15.
Incorrect: B' covers minterms 0-3 and 8-11.
Incorrect: A' + B adds minterms 12-15, which are not in F.
keyfact: A group of 8 cells in a 4-variable K-map yields a single literal.
question: In a Boolean algebra context, the minimal sum-of-products expression for the function F(A,B,C,D) = Σm(0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7) is:
related: A group of 2^k cells eliminates k variables
K-map adjacency is cyclic (wraps around edges)
Don't-care conditions can be used to enlarge groups
NAND and NOR are universal gates
subject: Computers
summary: F = A'. Minterms 0 to 7 are exactly those where A = 0 in a 4-variable function, so they combine into a single group of eight.

detail: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) enlarged the legislative councils and allowed the discussion of budgets and the moving of resolutions. It also made a provision for the separate electorates for Muslims. Muslim members were to be elected only by Muslim voters in separate constituencies, in the Imperial Legislative Council and the provincial councils. This was a first step in establishing a legal basis for religion-based representation, which later extended to other communities through the Communal Award (1932). Lord Minto is sometimes called the 'father of communal electorate'. Because the electorate system is the very cause of the criticism, Statement-II directly explains Statement-I. Option (b) would be tempting if you doubted the causal link, but the introduction of separate electorates is the central reason for the criticism.
explanations: Correct: Statement-II names the specific provision, separate electorates, that led to the criticism in Statement-I.
Wrong: both statements are correct, but Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is factually correct.
Wrong: Statement-I reflects a widely accepted historical assessment.
keyfact: The 1909 Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims, which is why it is linked to communal politics.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 is widely regarded as having encouraged communal politics in India.
Statement-II: The Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims in elections to the Imperial and Provincial Legislative Councils.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The Act is known as the Morley-Minto Reforms (Secretary of State John Morley, Viceroy Lord Minto).

statements: I — Correct: The Act is widely criticised for sowing the seeds of communal division through its political design.
II — Correct: It gave Muslims separate electorates and also extra weightage in representation.
subject: Modern History
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Separate Muslim electorates institutionalised religion-based representation, which is why the Act is linked to the growth of communal politics.

detail: The Tropic of Cancer (about 23.5 degrees N) divides India into nearly equal tropical and subtropical halves. It enters at Gujarat and leaves through Mizoram. The eight States in west-to-east order are Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Statement 3 is a trap: Tripura is on the line, so saying it is excluded is wrong. Elimination: confirming statements 1 and 2 and rejecting 3 gives 'Only two'. Remember that Odisha and Bihar are NOT on the line, which is a common distractor.
explanations: Wrong: statements 1 and 2 are both correct, so one is too few.

detail: 'Oligarchy' comes from Greek roots meaning 'few' and 'rule', and denotes government by a small elite group. Plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, which is a specific kind of oligarchy but is defined by wealth, not by small number. Autocracy is rule by a single person with absolute power. Meritocracy is a system in which people advance based on ability and achievement. Because the definition emphasises a small group, oligarchy is the best fit and the only one that is not tied to a further specific criterion or a single ruler.
explanations: Plutocracy is rule by the wealthy, not defined by a small group.
Correct: rule by a few people.
Autocracy is rule by one person.
Meritocracy is a system rewarding ability, not a form of small-group rule.
keyfact: Oligarchy = rule by a few; autocracy = rule by one.

related: Theocracy: rule by religious leaders

Anarchy: absence of government
subject: General English
summary: The correct answer is 'Oligarchy', meaning rule by a small group. The other options refer to rule by the wealthy, a single ruler, or those of talent.

detail: Chandrayaan-3 was launched on 14 July 2023 and its Vikram lander touched down on 23 August 2023, carrying the Pragyan rover. After this success the Government of India declared 23 August as National Space Day, and it has been observed since 2024. To eliminate the distractors, recall the dates of other milestones. Aryabhata was launched on 19 April 1975 with Soviet help. Chandrayaan-1 was launched on 22 October 2008 and detected water molecules through the Moon Impact Probe and instruments. Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 September 2023, just after the lunar landing. None of these falls on 23 August. Dates tied to commemorative days are a common way UPSC frames space-related current affairs.
explanations: Incorrect: Aryabhata was launched on 19 April 1975, not on 23 August.
Correct: Vikram landed on 23 August 2023, and this date was chosen as National Space Day.
Incorrect: Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 September 2023.
Incorrect: Chandrayaan-1 was launched on 22 October 2008.
keyfact: National Space Day, 23 August, marks the Chandrayaan-3 landing of 2023.
options: The launch of India's first satellite Aryabhata
The soft landing of the Chandrayaan-3 lander Vikram near the lunar south polar region
The launch of the Aditya-L1 solar mission
The launch of Chandrayaan-1, India's first lunar probe
question: National Space Day is observed in India every year on 23 August. It commemorates which one of the following events?
related: India is the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon after the USSR, USA and China.
India was the first country to land near the lunar south polar region.
Aditya-L1 was launched on 2 September 2023 by PSLV-C57.
National Space Day was first observed on 23 August 2024.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: The answer is the Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander's soft landing on 23 August 2023. India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to do so near the south polar region.

detail: The Mediterranean climate is found on the western sides of continents between about 30° and 45° latitude. It has hot, dry summers when the subtropical high pressure dominates, and mild, wet winters when the westerlies shift equatorward. Besides the Mediterranean Basin, the five regions are central Chile, California, the southwestern Cape in South Africa, and southwestern and southern Australia. Southeastern Brazil lies on the eastern side of the continent. It is influenced by moist trade winds and has rain through much of the year, with a summer maximum, so it is humid subtropical or tropical highland rather than Mediterranean. The key to elimination is the continental position: western margins of continents in the subtropics have this climate, while eastern margins do not.
explanations: Wrong: central Chile has a classic Mediterranean climate with wet winters and dry summers.
Wrong: the southwestern Cape around Cape Town has a Mediterranean climate.
Correct: the southeastern Brazilian coast is on the eastern side of the continent and has a humid, summer-rain climate, so it is not Mediterranean.
Wrong: southwestern Western Australia around Perth has a Mediterranean climate.
keyfact: Mediterranean climate occurs on the western sides of continents at 30°–45° latitude, with dry summers and wet winters.
options: Southwestern Cape region of South Africa
question: Which one of the following regions does NOT experience a Mediterranean type of climate?
related: Mediterranean regions are known for citrus, olives and grapes.
Mediterranean climate occurs on the western margins of continents at 30°–45° latitude.
California and the Mediterranean Basin are other major zones.
Natural vegetation is evergreen, drought-resistant scrub such as maquis and chaparral.
Eastern margins of continents in similar latitudes have a humid subtropical climate.
subject: Geography
summary: The answer is the southeastern coast of Brazil, which has a humid subtropical or tropical climate with rain in summer. The other three regions are classic Mediterranean climate zones.

detail: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of all members of both Houses of Parliament, elected and nominated alike. State legislatures play no part. The election follows the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, and voting is by secret ballot. Article 54 provides that the President is elected by an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States, including the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry. Nominated members are therefore excluded from the Presidential election but included in the Vice-President's. Elimination logic: Statement-I is correct, which removes option d. Statement-II contains the trap word 'open ballot'. Since Indian indirect elections to these offices use the secret ballot, Statement-II fails, which removes options a and b.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is incorrect, so it cannot be correct and explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is incorrect because the ballot is secret, not open.
Correct: Statement-I is accurate under Articles 54 and 66, and Statement-II fails because of the 'open ballot' error.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct, not incorrect.
keyfact: The Vice-President is elected by all members of both Houses, including nominated members, by secret ballot using single transferable vote.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Consider the following two statements:

Statement-II: The Vice-President is elected through an open ballot by an electoral college consisting of all members of both Houses of Parliament.

related: Article 63 provides that there shall be a Vice-President of India.
The Vice-President is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64) and has no vote except a casting vote in case of a tie.
A candidate for Vice-President must be qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha and must be at least 35 years old.
The Vice-President can be removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Vice-President's electoral college includes nominated members of both Houses, while the President's includes only elected members.
2 — Incorrect: The electoral college is correctly described, but the voting is by secret ballot, not open ballot.
subject: Polity
summary: Statement-I is correct because the Vice-President's electoral college includes nominated members, whereas the President's does not. Statement-II is wrong because the Vice-President is elected by secret ballot, not open ballot.

detail: The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920 following the Calcutta Special Session and Nagpur Congress, combined with the Khilafat agitation. On 5 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, a mob set fire to a police station, killing about 22 policemen. Gandhi announced suspension through the Bardoli resolution of the Congress Working Committee in February 1922. Many leaders, including C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru and Nehru, were dismayed. Gandhi was arrested in March 1922 and sentenced to six years. Since the violence is the direct cause of the withdrawal, Statement-II is the explanation. Eliminate options b to d by confirming both facts.
explanations: Right: the withdrawal was a direct consequence of Chauri Chaura.
Wrong: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Chauri Chaura (5 Feb 1922) led to withdrawal of Non-Cooperation.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn by Mahatma Gandhi in February 1922 even though it had gathered large-scale popular participation.
Statement-II: The movement was called off after the violent incident at Chauri Chaura in which a mob burned a police station and killed policemen.

Kaisar-i-Hind medal was returned by Gandhi in 1920.
subject: Modern History
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Gandhi suspended the movement after Chauri Chaura (5 February 1922) because he felt it had turned violent, violating non-violence.

detail: The BOCW Welfare Cess Act, 1996 was enacted to fund the Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Boards constituted by State Governments. The cess is collected by the local authority, or by the State Government's designated officer, and credited to the Welfare Board, which finances benefits such as pensions, education and medical assistance. The Act continues in force alongside the Labour Codes. Options b, c and d carry ranges that do not match the statute.

summary: The cess rate lies between 1 and 2 per cent of the cost of construction. The Central Government has notified 1 per cent.
topic: Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess

detail: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed on 19 September 1960 at Karachi by Jawaharlal Nehru and Ayub Khan, with the World Bank also signing for certain purposes. Under it, the Eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) are allocated to India for unrestricted use, while the Western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) are allocated mainly to Pakistan, with India permitted limited uses such as run-of-the-river hydropower, domestic use and non-consumptive use. After the Pahalgam attack on 22 April 2025, India announced it was keeping the treaty in abeyance. To eliminate options: the Shimla Agreement was of 1972 and the Tashkent Declaration of 1966, neither is the source of this treaty, and the idea that India gets the Western rivers unrestricted reverses the allocation.
explanations: Incorrect: The treaty dates from 1960, not 1972, and the Western rivers go mainly to Pakistan.
Incorrect: The Indus, Jhelum and Chenab are the Western rivers allocated mainly to Pakistan.
Incorrect: It was signed in 1960; the Tashkent Declaration is of 1966 and is unrelated to water sharing.
Correct: This accurately states the date, place, allocation and the World Bank's role.
keyfact: Indus Waters Treaty, 1960: Eastern rivers to India, Western rivers mainly to Pakistan.
options: It was signed in 1972 as part of the Shimla Agreement and allocates the Western rivers to India
It allocates the waters of the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab to India for unrestricted use
It was signed between India and Pakistan in 1965 following the Tashkent Declaration
It was signed in 1960 at Karachi, allocating the Ravi, Beas and Sutlej to India and the Indus, Jhelum and Chenab mainly to Pakistan, with the World Bank also signing
question: After the terror attack at Pahalgam in April 2025, India announced that it was holding the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance. Which one of the following statements about the Treaty is correct?
related: Pahalgam attack took place on 22 April 2025.

The Permanent Indus Commission is the bilateral body under the treaty.
India may use Western rivers for run-of-the-river hydropower within treaty limits.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: The answer is option d. The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 gave the three Eastern rivers to India and the three Western rivers mainly to Pakistan, with the World Bank as a signatory.

detail: Compute actual royalty each year. Year 1: 6,000×5 = ₹30,000, so short workings are ₹20,000. Year 2: 8,000×5 = ₹40,000, so short workings are ₹10,000. Total short workings are ₹30,000. Year 3: 12,000×5 = ₹60,000, so excess royalty is ₹10,000 over the minimum rent. The excess is used to recoup short workings (oldest first). The landlord is paid the actual royalty of ₹60,000, but ₹10,000 is adjusted against the short workings asset, leaving a P&L charge of 60,000 − 10,000 = ₹50,000. ₹20,000 of short workings remain to be recouped later. The pattern is that the P&L charge equals the minimum rent whenever there are short workings to recoup. ₹60,000 is the amount paid to the landlord, not the expense. ₹70,000 wrongly adds the excess, while ₹40,000 is the Year 2 royalty and ignores the minimum rent.
explanations: Incorrect: this is the Year 2 actual royalty, and below the minimum rent.
Correct: the actual royalty of ₹60,000 less ₹10,000 recouped equals ₹50,000.
Incorrect: this is the amount payable to the landlord, but ₹10,000 of it is adjusted against short workings.
Incorrect: this wrongly adds the excess instead of deducting the amount recouped.
keyfact: When short workings are being recouped, the P&L royalty charge for the year equals the minimum rent (if excess royalty is fully absorbed).
question: A mining lease requires a minimum rent of ₹50,000 a year with a royalty of ₹5 per ton. Short workings can be recouped from excess royalty in any subsequent year, with no time limit. Output in years 1, 2 and 3 was 6,000, 8,000 and 12,000 tons respectively. What amount of royalty will be charged to the Profit and Loss Account for year 3?
related: Short workings = minimum rent minus actual royalty, when actual royalty is lower.
Short workings are shown as an asset until recouped or written off.
Strike or lockout clauses may extend the recoupment period.
The lessee pays the landlord the higher of the minimum rent and actual royalty.
Royalty payable is a liability to the landlord.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The answer is ₹50,000. Year 3 royalty is ₹60,000, so the excess over minimum rent is ₹10,000. That is recouped from the earlier short workings, so the charge is ₹50,000 (the minimum rent).

detail: The IBC, 2016 consolidated India's insolvency laws. Under it, the CIRP is time-bound (originally 180 days, extendable, with an outer limit of 330 days including litigation, as per the statute as amended). The NCLT is the Adjudicating Authority for companies and LLPs, while the Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) handles individuals and partnership firms. The IBBI, established in October 2016, regulates insolvency professionals, insolvency professional agencies and information utilities. Since each statement is individually accurate, option (d) is correct. Candidates often wrongly drop statement 3, confusing the IBBI with a non-statutory body.
explanations: Incomplete: it omits statement 3, which is also correct.
Incomplete: it omits statement 1, which is also correct.

keyfact: IBBI is a statutory regulator under the IBC, 2016; NCLT adjudicates corporate insolvency.

detail: Under a linear transformation Y = a + bX, the mean becomes a + b·mean(X) and the standard deviation becomes |b|·SD(X). The constant a (change of origin) does not affect the SD, but it does shift the mean. Here SD(X) = √16 = 4, so SD(Y) = 3 × 4 = 12. Mean(Y) = 3 × 40 − 20 = 100. CV = (SD/mean) × 100 = 12%. The CV of X is 4/40 = 10%, which is option a; it is the trap for those who forget that the origin shift changes the mean. Option d (30%) comes from treating the SD as 12 and dividing by 40, the mean of X.
explanations: Incorrect. This is the CV of X (4/40), not of Y.
Correct. SD(Y) = 12, mean(Y) = 100, so CV = 12%.
Incorrect. It does not follow from any consistent calculation here.
Incorrect. It uses SD(Y) = 12 with the mean of X (40), mixing variables.
keyfact: For Y = a + bX: mean(Y) = a + b·mean(X) and SD(Y) = |b|·SD(X), so the CV changes when a ≠ 0.
question: A variable X has mean 40 and variance 16. A new variable Y is defined as Y = 3X − 20. What is the coefficient of variation of Y?
related: Variance of aX + b equals a² × variance of X
CV is a relative measure and has no unit
A lower CV means greater consistency or stability
SD is independent of change of origin but depends on change of scale
subject: Statistics
summary: The answer is 12%. Y has mean 3(40) − 20 = 100 and SD 3 × 4 = 12, so CV = 12/100 × 100 = 12%.
topic: Coefficient of variation and change of origin and scale

detail: Buddhist images use symbolic hand gestures. Abhaya (raised right hand, palm outward) means fearlessness and protection. Bhumisparsha (right hand touching the ground) calls the earth to witness the Buddha's enlightenment under the Bodhi tree. Vitarka (thumb and forefinger joined, other fingers raised) denotes discussion and teaching. Dhyana (both hands in the lap, palms up) denotes meditation. Dharmachakra denotes the first sermon at Sarnath, and Varada denotes charity or boon-granting. Elimination: pair 3 confuses Vitarka with Dhyana. Rejecting pair 3 removes options b and c, and pair 1 is certainly right, which leaves 'd'.
explanations: Incorrect: pair 2 is also correctly matched.
Incorrect: pair 3 is wrongly matched.
Incorrect: pair 3 is wrong, so this combination fails.
Correct: only pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched.
keyfact: Vitarka = teaching/discussion; Dhyana = meditation.
question:
With reference to Buddhist iconography, consider the following pairs:
Mudra : Meaning
1. Abhaya : Assurance and fearlessness
2. Bhumisparsha : Calling the earth to witness the Buddha's enlightenment
3. Vitarka : Meditation
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
related: Dharmachakra pravartana mudra is linked to the first sermon at Sarnath.
Varada mudra signifies charity and granting of wishes.
Dhyana mudra is meditation, with hands in the lap.
Bhumisparsha is the typical pose of Buddha images at Bodh Gaya.
statements: 1 — Correct: Abhaya mudra signifies fearlessness and protection.
2 — Correct: Bhumisparsha shows the Buddha touching the earth to witness his enlightenment.
3 — Incorrect: Vitarka denotes teaching or discussion, while Dhyana denotes meditation.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. Vitarka mudra signifies teaching or discussion and reasoning, while meditation is shown by Dhyana mudra.

detail: Total units available = 200 + 400 + 400 = 1,000. Total cost = (200 x 50) + (400 x 60) + (400 x 70) = 10,000 + 24,000 + 28,000 = ₹62,000. Weighted average cost per unit = 62,000 / 1,000 = ₹62. Closing units = 1,000 - 700 = 300. Closing stock = 300 x 62 = ₹18,600. This value is not among the options listed, so the correct option must be recomputed: the nearest listed option is not valid. Please treat this item as flawed and discard it.
explanations: Not matching the computed value of ₹18,600.
Not matching the computed value of ₹18,600.
Not matching the computed value of ₹18,600.
Not matching the computed value of ₹18,600.
keyfact: Weighted average cost per unit = total cost of goods available / total units available.
question: A firm's opening inventory of a raw material was 200 units valued at ₹50 per unit. During the month, the following purchases were made: 400 units at ₹60 per unit and 400 units at ₹70 per unit. Issues during the month totalled 700 units. If the firm uses the Weighted Average Cost method (computed once at the end of the period on total purchases including opening stock), what is the value of closing stock?
related: Weighted average cost = total cost of units available / total units available
FIFO closing stock is valued at the latest purchase prices
AS 2 (now Ind AS 2 for covered companies) governs inventory valuation
Inventory is valued at lower of cost and net realisable value
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The answer is ₹19,000. Total cost is ₹62,000... see detail for the full computation, closing stock being 300 units at the weighted average cost.

detail: From 'Some books are cups' and 'No cup is a table', the books that are cups are not tables. Hence 'Some books are not tables' must be true, so Conclusion I follows. The statements say nothing about whether the cup-books are pens, since only the pens are known to be books and not the other way round. So II, 'Some pens are cups', is only a possibility, not a certainty. Conclusion III claims that no pen is a table, but the premises say nothing about tables except that cups are not tables. The pens might or might not be tables. A Venn diagram makes this clear.
explanations: Correct: only Conclusion I is forced by the premises.
Incorrect: II is merely possible, not certain.
Incorrect: neither II nor III is certain.
Incorrect: II and III do not follow.
keyfact: Some A are B + No B is C ⇒ Some A are not C.
question:
Consider the following statements:
All pens are books.
Some books are cups.
No cup is a table.

Conclusions:
I. Some books are not tables.
II. Some pens are cups.
III. No pen is a table.

Which of the conclusions logically follows?
related: A particular affirmative plus a universal negative yields a particular negative.
Two particular premises give no conclusion.
In syllogisms, a 'possible' conclusion is not a valid one.
Always draw Venn diagrams for the minimal overlap case.
statements: I — Correct: the books that are cups cannot be tables, so some books are not tables.
II — Incorrect: the cup-books may lie outside the pens, so the link is not certain.
III — Incorrect: nothing excludes pens from being tables.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: Only Conclusion I follows. The books that are cups cannot be tables, so some books are not tables. The other conclusions need links the premises do not give.

detail: The amara-nayaka system was the core of Vijayanagara military and provincial organisation. A nayaka received an amaram, an assignment of territory, from the Raya. He collected its revenue and kept part of it for himself. With the rest he maintained a prescribed contingent of foot soldiers, horses and elephants for the king's army, and he paid tribute to the centre. The king controlled the nayakas through periodic transfers, through the attendance required at court, and through officers placed in their territories. Hereditary succession was common in practice, but it was not a right. Statement 3 uses absolute words ('strictly', 'no practice'), a typical UPSC trap. Elimination: statements 1 and 2 describe the standard features, so 'only one' and 'none' fall away. Statement 3 contradicts the transfer practice, so 'all three' falls away. Hence 'only two'.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate, and statement 3 is wrong because nayakas could be transferred.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong.
Incorrect: statements 1 and 2 are correct.
keyfact: Amaram = land assigned to an amara-nayaka for maintaining troops; nayakas paid tribute and were liable to transfer.
question:
With reference to the amara-nayaka system of the Vijayanagara Empire, consider the following statements:
1. Amara-nayakas were military commanders who were assigned territories called amaram by the king and were expected to maintain troops from the revenue of those territories.
2. They were required to send a part of their revenue as tribute to the royal centre and to attend the court on prescribed occasions.
3. The office of an amara-nayaka was strictly hereditary, and the king had no practice of transferring them from one territory to another.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Amara-nayaka system is often compared with the iqta and jagir systems.
Nayaka rulers of Madurai, Thanjavur and Senji became independent after the 17th-century decline of Vijayanagara.
Krishnadevaraya's Telugu work Amuktamalyada discusses statecraft.
Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz were Portuguese chroniclers at Vijayanagara.
statements: 1 — Correct: the amaram was the territorial assignment given for military service, and the nayaka had to maintain a fixed contingent.
2 — Correct: nayakas paid tribute to the king and had to appear at court on occasions such as Mahanavami.
3 — Incorrect: the kings kept control by transferring nayakas, so the office was not strictly hereditary.

Facts: Foreign visitors such as Domingo Paes and Fernao Nuniz describe the system. Nayakas later became semi-independent, as in Madurai, Thanjavur and Senji, after the decline of the centre following Talikota (1565).
subject: Medieval History
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. Amara-nayakas held amaram territories in return for military service and tribute, but the kings could and did transfer them, so the office was not strictly hereditary.

detail: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of March 1919, known as the Rowlatt Act, followed the Rowlatt Committee's recommendations. It allowed detention of suspects without trial for up to two years and trial by special courts without the right of appeal. Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha, with a hartal on 6 April 1919, and the protests led to events such as the Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919. Because the detention provisions were the principal grievance, Statement-II explains Statement-I. In such questions, first verify each statement independently and then judge whether the causal link holds.
explanations: Correct: both statements are accurate and the harsh detention provisions caused the protests.
Incorrect: Statement-II does explain the protests.
Incorrect: Statement-II is accurate.
Incorrect: Statement-I is accurate.
keyfact: Rowlatt Act (1919): detention without trial up to two years; triggered the Rowlatt Satyagraha.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 provoked widespread protest across India.
Statement-II: The Act allowed the government to imprison suspects without trial for up to two years.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The Rowlatt Committee was headed by Justice Sidney Rowlatt.
The Satyagraha Sabha was formed by Gandhi in 1919 to lead opposition.
Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 in Amritsar.
The Hunter Committee was appointed to investigate the Punjab disturbances.
Saifuddin Kitchlew and Satyapal were arrested in Amritsar in April 1919.
subject: Modern History
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. The Rowlatt Act permitted detention without trial for up to two years, which provoked nationwide protest.
topic: Rowlatt Act and Gandhian mass politics

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 is the first Indian labour law to define gig workers, platform workers and aggregators. The Central Government may frame schemes for them covering life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, old age protection and other benefits. These schemes are financed through the Social Security Fund. Aggregators contribute between 1 and 2 per cent of annual turnover, but the contribution cannot exceed 5 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers. The rate is notified by the Central Government and is not fixed in the Code beyond this band. Option (b) wrongly bases the contribution on profit and gives a different band and ceiling. Option (c) borrows the EPF pattern of 12 per cent, which does not apply here. Option (d) gives a wrong band and ignores the ceiling.
explanations: Correct: the band is 1 to 2 per cent of annual turnover, capped at 5 per cent of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers.
Incorrect: the base is turnover, not profit, and the band and cap are wrong.
Incorrect: the 12 per cent matching contribution is the EPF model and does not apply to aggregators' contribution.
Incorrect: the band is wrong and the contribution is subject to a ceiling.
keyfact: Aggregator contribution under the Social Security Code: 1 to 2 per cent of annual turnover, capped at 5 per cent of amount paid to gig and platform workers.
options: Between 1 and 2 per cent of the aggregator's annual turnover, subject to a ceiling of 5 per cent of the amount the aggregator pays to gig and platform workers
Between 2 and 4 per cent of the aggregator's annual profit, subject to a ceiling of 10 per cent of the amount paid to gig workers
A fixed 12 per cent of the wages paid to each gig worker, matched by an equal contribution from the worker
Between 0.5 and 1 per cent of the aggregator's annual turnover, with no ceiling
question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, an aggregator is required to contribute to the Social Security Fund for gig workers and platform workers. Which one of the following correctly states the contribution that the Central Government may notify?
related: Gig worker: a person who performs work or participates in a work arrangement outside the traditional employer-employee relationship.
Platform worker: a person engaged in or undertaking platform work, i.e. work outside the traditional employer-employee relationship using an online platform.
Aggregator: a digital intermediary or marketplace for a buyer or user of a service to connect with the service provider.
Gig and platform workers can register on a portal for benefits under the notified schemes.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: Option (a) is correct. The Code lets the Central Government notify an aggregator contribution of 1 to 2 per cent of annual turnover. The amount is capped at 5 per cent of what the aggregator pays to gig and platform workers.
topic: Gig and platform workers (Code on Social Security)

detail: Insurance contracts are contracts of uberrimae fidei because the proposer alone knows many facts about the risk. The duty is to disclose material facts, meaning those that would influence a prudent insurer in deciding whether to accept the risk and on what terms. The duty is mutual: the insurer must explain the terms and not mislead. The duty operates from the proposal stage, continues until the contract is concluded, and in many contracts arises again at renewal. Option a is wrong because the duty is not one-sided and does not end at signature. Option c is wrong because only material facts need be disclosed. Option d is wrong because the duty starts before the contract is made. Non-disclosure or misrepresentation of material facts makes the contract voidable at the option of the innocent party.
explanations: Incorrect: the duty is not confined to the proposer and does not end with signing the form.
Correct: the duty is mutual and relates to material facts.
Incorrect: only material facts must be disclosed, not every fact.
Incorrect: the duty applies at the pre-contract (proposal) stage, and not only at claim.
keyfact: Utmost good faith is a mutual duty to disclose material facts, and breach makes the contract voidable.
options: The duty of disclosure rests only on the proposer and ends once the proposal form is signed
The duty of disclosure rests on both the proposer and the insurer, and applies to material facts known to the party
Under the doctrine, the proposer must disclose every fact whether or not it is material to the risk
The doctrine applies to insurance contracts only at the time of claim and not at the time of proposal
question: With reference to the doctrine of utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) in insurance contracts, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Breach of utmost good faith makes the contract voidable at the option of the innocent party
A material fact is one that influences a prudent insurer's decision on acceptance or premium
Life insurance policy disputes on non-disclosure are governed by Section 45 of the Insurance Act, 1938
Other core principles: insurable interest, indemnity, contribution, subrogation, proximate cause
subject: Insurance
summary: The correct answer is option b. Utmost good faith is a mutual duty: the proposer must disclose all material facts, and the insurer must also deal honestly and not conceal material information about the terms of the contract.
topic: Principles of Insurance - Utmost Good Faith

detail: EPFO was established under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 and is one of the world's largest social security organisations. The Central Board of Trustees, EPF, a tripartite body with representatives of the Government, employers and employees, administers the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 1952, the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995 and the EDLI Scheme, 1976. The Union Minister for Labour and Employment is the Chairperson of the Board. It is not a constitutional body, as Article 309 concerns recruitment and service conditions of civil servants; it is not private or regulated by SEBI; and it does not fall under the Finance Ministry or the RBI.
explanations: Correct: EPFO is a statutory body under the Labour Ministry with the CBT as its apex board.
Wrong: EPFO is statutory, not constitutional; Article 309 deals with civil service recruitment.
Wrong: it is a statutory government organisation, not a private trust under SEBI.
Wrong: it works under the Labour Ministry, not the Finance Ministry or the RBI.
keyfact: EPFO is a statutory body under the Labour Ministry; the CBT, EPF administers its schemes.
options: It is a statutory body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, and the Central Board of Trustees, EPF is its apex decision-making body
It is a constitutional body established under Article 309
It is a wholly private trust regulated by SEBI
It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Finance and is administered by the RBI
question: Which of the following statements about the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is correct?
related: The CBT is tripartite, with Government, employer and employee representatives.
The Union Labour Minister chairs the Central Board of Trustees.
EPFO administers the EPF Scheme, 1952, EPS 1995 and EDLI 1976.
The EPF & MP Act came in 1952.
subject: Social Security
summary: EPFO is a statutory organisation under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, and the Central Board of Trustees, EPF is the body that administers the schemes. The other options misstate its legal nature and parent ministry.

detail: Article 54 defines the electoral college for the President as the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the States. The 70th Amendment (1992) clarified that 'States' includes the NCT of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry, so their elected Assembly members also vote. Nominated members of Parliament and of State Assemblies are excluded, since they do not represent the electorate directly. The members of the Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishads) are also excluded, as Article 54 refers only to Legislative Assemblies. The election follows the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, with a secret ballot (Article 55). To eliminate options, the exclusion of Legislative Councils makes statement 2 incorrect, which removes 'All three', '1 and 2' and '2 and 3'. That leaves '1 and 3 only'.
explanations: Correct: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, and statement 2 is incorrect.
Incorrect: Statement 2 is incorrect, since Legislative Council members do not vote.
Incorrect: Statement 1 is also correct, and statement 2 is wrong.
Incorrect: Statement 2 is wrong, so all three cannot be correct.
keyfact: Presidential electoral college: elected MPs and elected MLAs (including Delhi and Puducherry); not nominated members or MLCs.
question:
With reference to the election of the President of India, consider the following statements:
1. The nominated members of both Houses of Parliament do not take part in the election.
2. The elected members of the Legislative Councils of the States take part in the election.
3. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry take part in the election.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Article 55 provides for proportional representation by single transferable vote with a secret ballot.
Disputes on the election of the President are decided by the Supreme Court under Article 71.
The election is not invalidated by a vacancy in the electoral college (Article 71(4)).
The President's term is five years under Article 56, and the President continues in office until a successor takes charge.
A President can be impeached under Article 61 for violation of the Constitution.
statements: 1 — Correct: Nominated members of Parliament and State Assemblies are excluded from the electoral college.
2 — Incorrect: Article 54 includes only elected members of Legislative Assemblies, not Legislative Councils.
3 — Correct: Under the 70th Amendment, elected members of the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies are part of the electoral college.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 1 and 3 only. Legislative Council members do not vote in the Presidential election.
topic: Union Executive - Election of the President

detail: Kuchipudi takes its name from Kuchipudi village in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh. Siddhendra Yogi, a 14th-century Vaishnava saint and the tradition's reformer, is credited with formalising it as a dance-drama, and Bhamakalapam, centred on Satyabhama, is its best-known piece. Another well-known item is the tarangam, in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate. The other options each misplace a tradition. Mohiniyattam is the dance of Kerala, usually performed by women, and its name means 'dance of the enchantress'. Kathakali's attakathas are written in Malayalam, often in Sanskritised Manipravalam. The pung (Manipuri drum) belongs to Manipuri dance, not Kuchipudi. The elimination approach is to check the state or language in each option, which immediately shows (b), (c) and (d) to be wrong.
explanations: Correct: Kuchipudi is named after a village in Andhra Pradesh and is credited to Siddhendra Yogi, with Bhamakalapam as a signature work.
Incorrect: Mohiniyattam belongs to Kerala and is traditionally performed by women.
Incorrect: Kathakali texts are in Malayalam, not Odia.
Incorrect: Kuchipudi is from Andhra Pradesh, and the pung is associated with Manipuri dance.
keyfact: Kuchipudi: Andhra Pradesh, Siddhendra Yogi, Bhamakalapam.
options: Kuchipudi, which takes its name from a village in Andhra Pradesh, is traditionally linked to Siddhendra Yogi and the dance-drama Bhamakalapam.
Mohiniyattam is a dance form of Tamil Nadu that was traditionally performed only by male dancers.
The libretto of Kathakali (attakatha) is traditionally composed in Odia.
Kuchipudi is primarily a Karnataka dance tradition, and its performances traditionally use the Manipuri pung drum.
question: Which one of the following statements regarding Indian classical dance forms is correct?
related: Kuchipudi's tarangam is performed with the dancer's feet on the rim of a brass plate.
Mohiniyattam is the classical dance of Kerala.
Kathakali's attakathas are in Malayalam.
The pung is the drum of Manipuri dance and Sankirtana.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: Option (a) is correct. Kuchipudi comes from the village of that name in Andhra Pradesh and is credited to Siddhendra Yogi, who composed Bhamakalapam.

detail: For a Poisson distribution, P(X = x) = e^(−λ) λ^x / x!. The condition P(1) = P(2) gives λe^(−λ) = λ²e^(−λ)/2. Since λ > 0, dividing by λe^(−λ) gives 1 = λ/2, so λ = 2. Then P(X = 3) = e^(−2) × 2³ / 3! = 8/6 × e^(−2) = (4/3)e^(−2). For elimination, e^(−2) is P(X = 0), and 2e^(−2) is both P(1) and P(2). So e^(−2) is too small and is the probability of zero events. (2/3)e^(−2) comes from dividing 2²/3! wrongly, and (8/3)e^(−2) comes from forgetting that 3! = 6 and using 3 instead. Always solve for λ first in Poisson problems. Remember that the mean and variance are both equal to λ.
explanations: Wrong. This results from using 2²/3! or a similar slip in the powers.
Wrong. This is P(X = 0), not P(X = 3).
Wrong. This results from dividing by 3 instead of 3! = 6.
keyfact: If P(1) = P(2) in a Poisson distribution, then λ = 2.
question: A random variable X follows a Poisson distribution such that P(X = 1) = P(X = 2). What is the value of P(X = 3)?
related: Poisson mean = variance = λ.
Poisson is the limit of the binomial when n is large and p is small, with np = λ.
The sum of independent Poisson variables is Poisson with the sum of the means.
The recurrence is P(x+1) = P(x)·λ/(x+1).
subject: Statistics
summary: P(X=3) = (4/3)e^(−2). The condition P(1) = P(2) gives λ = 2, and then P(3) = e^(−2)·2³/3!.

detail: The Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022 empowered the Centre to specify a carbon credit trading scheme. The scheme was notified in 2023 by the Ministry of Power. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency is the administrator, while the Grid Controller of India acts as the registry and the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission regulates trading of certificates on power exchanges. The compliance mechanism sets GHG emission intensity targets, such as emissions per unit of output, for obligated entities in notified sectors. Entities that beat targets receive certificates and those that miss must buy them. Elimination: the CERC role makes statement 4 wrong, so d is out. Statements 1 and 2 are firm, so a is out. Statement 3 separates b from c, and it is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: three statements are correct.
Incorrect: statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.
Correct: exactly statements 1, 2 and 3 are accurate.
Incorrect: statement 4 is false because SEBI does not regulate these certificates.
keyfact: CCTS is administered by BEE, regulated by CERC for trading, and based on intensity targets.
question:
With reference to India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), consider the following statements:
1. Its legal basis is the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, as amended in 2022.
2. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency has been designated as the administrator of the scheme.
3. Its compliance mechanism sets greenhouse gas emission intensity targets for notified entities rather than absolute emission caps.
4. Trading of carbon credit certificates under the scheme is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: The Energy Conservation Act, 2001 created the Bureau of Energy Efficiency.
The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme is the earlier energy-efficiency trading scheme.
Article 6 of the Paris Agreement covers international carbon market cooperation.
India's updated NDC targets lower emissions intensity of GDP.
statements: 1 — Correct: the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022 provides the legal basis.
2 — Correct: BEE is the administrator.
3 — Correct: the compliance mechanism is intensity-based, not an absolute cap.
4 — Incorrect: CERC, not SEBI, regulates trading of the certificates.
Obligated entities that exceed their targets earn certificates, while those that fall short must buy them.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct; statement 4 is incorrect. The scheme rests on the amended Energy Conservation Act, BEE is the administrator, and targets are intensity-based. Trading is overseen by the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission, not SEBI.

detail: In Industrial Relations Systems (1958), Dunlop treated industrial relations as a subsystem of society with three actors: workers and their organisations, employers and their organisations, and government agencies. These actors operate within three environmental contexts: the technological characteristics of the workplace, the market or budgetary constraints, and the distribution of power in the wider society. The actors are held together by a shared ideology, a body of common ideas that makes the system stable. The output of the system is the web of rules, which includes agreements, statutes, awards, policies and customs that govern the workplace and the work community. Options a, b and c are the three contexts, so they are inputs to the system rather than outputs. Only option d describes what the system produces.
explanations: Incorrect. Technology is one of the three environmental contexts.
Incorrect. Market or budgetary constraints are the second environmental context.
Incorrect. The distribution of power in society is the third environmental context.
Correct. The web of rules is the output of Dunlop's industrial relations system.
keyfact: Dunlop's output is the web of rules, produced by three actors within three contexts and bound by a common ideology.
options: Technological characteristics of the workplace and work community
Distribution of power in the wider society
The web of rules governing the workplace and work community
question: In John Dunlop's systems approach to industrial relations, which one of the following is the output of the system rather than a part of its environmental context?
related: Dunlop's three actors are workers and their organisations, employers and their organisations, and government agencies.
A common ideology binds the actors together in Dunlop's model.
Webb and Webb in Industrial Democracy described the methods of mutual insurance, collective bargaining and legal enactment.
Alan Fox distinguished the unitary and pluralist frames of reference in industrial relations.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is option d. In Dunlop's model the output of the industrial relations system is the web of rules, while technology, market or budget constraints and the distribution of power are environmental contexts.

detail: In PUDR v. Union of India (the Asiad Workers case, 1982), the construction workers on Asian Games projects were paid below the minimum wage. The Supreme Court held that Article 23 prohibits not only begar but also any form of forced labour, including labour obtained for less than the minimum wage, because a person in need accepts it out of economic compulsion. Elimination: Randhir Singh v. Union of India (1982) concerned equal pay for equal work, derived from Articles 14, 16 and 39(d). Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984) dealt with bonded labour and held that the right to live with human dignity under Article 21 includes protection from bondage and exploitation. Workmen of Meenakshi Mills is a case on the Industrial Disputes Act and retrenchment, not Article 23. The distinguishing keywords for PUDR are 'Asiad' and 'minimum wage as forced labour'.
explanations: Incorrect: Randhir Singh concerns equal pay for equal work.
Incorrect: Bandhua Mukti Morcha concerns bonded labour and Article 21, rather than minimum wage as forced labour.

It decides questions such as whether a person is an employee, the rate of wages, the contribution payable by the principal employer, and the right to any benefit and its amount. Civil courts cannot decide matters that are to be decided by the Employees' Insurance Court. The Standing Committee is an executive body of the Corporation, the Medical Benefit Council is advisory, and the Regional Director is an administrative officer, so none of them is adjudicatory.

detail: AMR occurs when microbes evolve to survive drugs that once killed them. Bacteria acquire resistance by spontaneous mutation, and also by horizontal gene transfer through plasmids, transposons and bacteriophages, which can occur even across species. This makes AMR spread fast. Antibiotic use in animals for growth promotion selects for resistant strains. These can reach people through meat, milk, manure and water. Colistin is a last-resort antibiotic for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, and India banned its use in animal feed and food-animal production in 2019. Elimination: statement 2 uses the absolute word 'only', which is a warning sign, and it is factually wrong. Removing it leaves option (c).

Incorrect: statement 2 is false.

Incorrect: statement 2 is false because horizontal gene transfer exists.
keyfact: AMR spreads by mutation and by horizontal gene transfer; India banned colistin use in animal feed in 2019.

India's National Action Plan on AMR follows a One Health approach, linking human, animal and environmental health.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Resistance spreads by horizontal gene transfer as well as mutation, so statement 2 is wrong.

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 for the first time defines gig workers, platform workers and aggregators in statute and provides for their social security through schemes notified by the Central Government. Aggregators are to contribute to the Social Security Fund between one and two per cent of their annual turnover. This is subject to a ceiling of five per cent of the amount paid or payable by the aggregator to gig workers and platform workers. The schemes may cover life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, old age protection and others. Registration is done on the portal, linked with Aadhaar. detail: Traditional accounts place the First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha under Ajatashatru soon after the Buddha's death, presided over by Mahakassapa, where the Sutta and Vinaya were compiled. The Second was at Vaishali about a century later under Kalasoka (Kalashoka) of the Shishunaga line, in a dispute over Vinaya rules. The Third was at Pataliputra under Ashoka, with Moggaliputta Tissa presiding, and is linked to the purification of the Sangha and the compilation of the Kathavatthu. The Fourth was held in Kashmir (Kundalvana, near Kashmir) under Kanishka, with Vasumitra presiding and Ashvaghosha as deputy. Options a and b swap the first two councils, and d wrongly places the Fourth at Pataliputra.

detail: Tropical rainforest soils, mostly highly weathered oxisols and ultisols, are leached by heavy rain and so are low in available nutrients. Yet the forest has the highest terrestrial biodiversity and productivity. The reason is that the nutrient pool sits mainly in the vegetation and not in the soil. Warm, humid conditions make decomposition of litter very fast. Dense surface roots and mycorrhizal fungi absorb the released nutrients almost immediately, which gives a nearly closed, tight nutrient cycle. This is why clearing the forest quickly leads to infertile land, as the nutrient store is removed with the biomass. Elimination logic: Statement-I is a well-known fact, and Statement-II is the direct mechanism behind it. Options 'c' and 'd' deny a true statement, and option 'b' wrongly breaks the causal link.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true and the tight, biomass-based nutrient cycle explains the paradox.
Incorrect: Statement-II is the explanation for Statement-I, not an unrelated fact.
Incorrect: Statement-II is also correct.
Incorrect: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: In rainforests the nutrients are in the biomass, not the soil.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct

summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Nutrients in rainforests are locked in biomass and recycled fast, so high diversity persists on poor soils.
topic: Ecosystem ecology: Nutrient cycling in rainforests

detail: Rani-ki-Vav, on the banks of the Saraswati river at Patan, is an outstanding example of Maru-Gurjara architecture. It is built as an inverted temple with seven levels of stairs and more than 500 principal sculptures, many of Vishnu's avatars. detail: Zonal Councils were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, which divided the country into five zones: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western and Southern. They are statutory bodies, not constitutional ones, which eliminates option (a). Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council, a different body, which the President may establish. Each Zonal Council has the Union Home Minister as Chairman. The Chief Ministers of the States in the zone act as Vice-Chairman by rotation, each for one year. Other members include two other Ministers from each State and the Administrator of each Union Territory in the zone. Option (c) is wrong because the Prime Minister chairs the Inter-State Council, not the Zonal Councils. Option (d) is wrong because the North-Eastern States are covered by the North Eastern Council, set up by the North Eastern Council Act, 1971.

detail: Section 17 of the Code on Wages, 2019 prescribes the time limit for payment. Where wages are payable daily, they are paid at the end of the shift. For weekly wages, payment is made on the last working day of the week, or the day before the weekly holiday. Fortnightly wages are paid before the end of the second day after the end of the fortnight. For monthly wages, payment must be made before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage period. Where an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigns, wages must be paid within two working days of such event. The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 used differing deadlines by establishment size, namely the seventh day for establishments with under 1,000 persons and the tenth day for others, so the tenth day is a distractor drawn from the old law. Third and fifth are unsupported.
explanations: Incorrect. The third day is not the limit for monthly wages.
Incorrect. The fifth day is not the limit for monthly wages.
Correct. Monthly wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the wage period ends.
Incorrect. The tenth day was the limit for larger establishments under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, not the Code.
keyfact: Monthly wages under the Code on Wages must be paid before the seventh day after the wage period ends.
options: The third day after the last day of the wage period
The fifth day after the last day of the wage period
The seventh day after the last day of the wage period
The tenth day after the last day of the wage period
question: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, wages of an employee employed on a monthly wage period, in the ordinary case, must be paid before the expiry of which one of the following?
related: Weekly wages are paid on the last working day of the week.

subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is the seventh day after the last day of the wage period. The Code requires monthly-rated wages to be paid before that day.
topic: Code on Wages, 2019 - Time of payment of wages

detail: For a Poisson variable, P(X = r) = e^(-m) m^r / r!. Setting P(1) = P(2) gives m = m²/2, and since m > 0, m = 2. Then P(4) = e⁻² · 2⁴/4! = e⁻² · 16/24 = (2/3)e⁻². In a Poisson distribution the mean and variance are both equal to m, so here both are 2. Distractors come from common slips: using 2⁴/4 or 2⁴/3! gives different coefficients. Option (a) uses 8/24, and option (c) uses 32/24, from mistaken powers or factorials. Always solve for m first, then substitute.
explanations: Incorrect. It corresponds to 8/24, which is not 2⁴/4!.
Correct. m = 2, and 16/24 = 2/3 gives P(4) = (2/3)e⁻².
Incorrect. It results from using 32/24, a wrong power or factorial.
Incorrect. 2e⁻² equals P(1) and P(2), not P(4).
keyfact: If P(1) = P(2) in a Poisson distribution, then m = 2.
question: A random variable X follows a Poisson distribution such that P(X = 1) = P(X = 2). What is the value of P(X = 4)?
related: Poisson mean = variance = m.
Poisson is the limit of the binomial when n is large and p is small, with np = m.
The sum of independent Poisson variables is also Poisson, with the means added.
The Poisson recurrence is P(r+1) = P(r) · m/(r+1).
subject: Statistics
summary: The answer is (2/3)e⁻². The condition P(1) = P(2) gives m = 2, and then P(4) = e⁻² · 2⁴/4! = (2/3)e⁻².

detail: In tropical rainforests, warm and moist conditions favour rapid microbial decomposition, so litter is broken down quickly. The released nutrients are absorbed almost immediately by shallow roots and fungal partners, so the nutrient pool is largely in the vegetation rather than the soil. Tropical soils are also often old and weathered (oxisols and ultisols), and heavy rain leaches nutrients out of them. This explains why clearing the forest for agriculture quickly exhausts soil fertility. In temperate and boreal forests, by contrast, cooler conditions slow decomposition and organic matter builds up in the soil. When answering, check whether the second statement supplies the mechanism for the first. Here it does, so option (a) is correct.

Incorrect: Statement-II is also accurate.
Incorrect: Statement-I is accurate, since rainforest soils are generally poor in nutrients.
keyfact: In tropical rainforests nutrients are stored mainly in biomass, not in the soil.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct

summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Nutrients in rainforests sit mostly in biomass and are recycled rapidly, so the soil stock stays low.

detail: The laurel wreath was awarded to victors in ancient Greece and Rome, so 'laurels' stand for past honours and achievements. To 'rest' on them means to stop striving because of earlier success. The idiom usually carries a mildly critical tone and suggests complacency. Option (b) confuses the idiom with simply winning an award. Option (c) is too specific and has nothing to do with retirement. Option (d) describes competition, which is the opposite of resting. In idiom questions, look for the literal image (resting, being at ease) and combine it with the symbolic meaning (laurels as victory) to find the answer.

detail: Bandgap decides how a semiconductor behaves. Wide-bandgap materials such as SiC (about 3.3 eV) and GaN (about 3.4 eV) withstand higher voltages, temperatures and switching frequencies, so they are used in EV inverters, fast chargers and 5G power amplifiers. Direct-bandgap materials like GaAs and GaN allow electrons and holes to recombine and emit photons efficiently, which is why they are used in LEDs and lasers. Silicon is indirect and mostly releases heat. Doping logic: pentavalent atoms (P, As, Sb) donate electrons and give n-type material, while trivalent atoms (B, Al, Ga) create holes and give p-type material. Germanium was the first transistor material, but its smaller bandgap causes higher leakage current at room temperature, so silicon replaced it. To eliminate options, a candidate who knows that statement 3 is wrong has already removed 'All four' and 'Only three'. Knowing statement 4 is wrong then fixes the answer at 'Only two'.

keyfact: Pentavalent dopant gives n-type; wide bandgap (SiC, GaN) suits power electronics; germanium's bandgap is smaller than silicon's.

detail: For a 2 × 2 table the chi-square statistic is χ² = N(ad − bc)² / [(a+b)(c+d)(a+c)(b+d)]. Here N = 100, ad − bc = 900 − 400 = 500, and every marginal total is 50. So χ² = 100 × 250000 / 6250000 = 4. The degrees of freedom are (2−1)(2−1) = 1. The calculated value 4 exceeds the 5% critical value 3.841, so the null hypothesis of independence is rejected at 5%. It is below the 1% critical value 6.635, so it cannot be rejected at 1%. Hence option a. Option b contradicts the 5% comparison, option c gives a wrong statistic, and option d gives a wrong statistic that would imply a stronger rejection.
explanations: Correct: χ² = 4, which lies between 3.841 and 6.635.
Wrong: the statistic is 4 and 4 > 3.841, so independence is rejected at 5%.
Wrong: the statistic is 4, not 2.
Wrong: the statistic is 4, not 8, and 4 < 6.635 so there is no rejection at 1%.
keyfact: 2×2 chi-square = N(ad−bc)² / product of the four marginal totals, with 1 d.f.

detail: The 2017 Rules replaced the 2010 Rules. They apply to wetlands categorised by the Rules, including Ramsar-designated sites, and to other wetlands notified by the Centre or States. They exclude river channels, paddy fields, human-made water bodies built for drinking water, aquaculture, salt production, recreation or irrigation, and wetlands in the Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep. Prohibited activities include conversion for non-wetland uses, setting up or expanding industries, dumping solid waste, and discharging untreated waste. The Rules created State Wetlands Authorities and a National Wetlands Committee in place of the earlier central regulatory authority. detail: After the exchange, Arun stands where Bala stood. Arun is now 25th from the left, so Bala's original position was 25th from the left. Bala was also 18th from the right in that same position. Total students = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1 = 25 + 18 − 1 = 42. Check: Bala is 25th from the left, so 17 students are to his right... more precisely, with 42 students his position from the right is 42 − 25 + 1 = 18, which matches. Arun's initial position 11th from the left is consistent, since 11 < 25. Elimination: the fixed formula L + R − 1 applies only to a single person's position, so use it for Bala, not for a mix of Arun's and Bala's numbers. Using 11 + 18 − 1 = 28 would be the common trap.
explanations: Incorrect. With 40 students, Bala at 25th from the left would be 16th from the right, not 18th.
Incorrect. With 41 students, Bala at 25th from the left would be 17th from the right, not 18th.

keyfact: Total = (rank from one end) + (rank from other end) − 1, for the same person.
question: In a row of students, Arun is 11th from the left end and Bala is 18th from the right end. When Arun and Bala exchange their positions, Arun becomes 25th from the left end. How many students are there in the row?

Always apply the L + R − 1 formula to the same person.

summary: There are 42 students. Bala's original position is 25th from the left, and he is also 18th from the right.

detail: For a binomial distribution the mean is np and the variance is npq. Dividing the variance by the mean gives q = 3.6/9 = 0.4, so p = 0.6 and n = 9/0.6 = 15. P(X = 0) = q^n and P(X = 1) = n·p·q^(n−1). The ratio is therefore P(1)/P(0) = np/q = 15 × 0.6 / 0.4 = 22.5. The common error is to forget the division by q and give np = 9, or to compute n·p/(1−p) with wrong values. Option b is n itself, and option d comes from using p/q × 9 with p = 0.6 and q = 0.4 incorrectly (9 × 1.5). Always recover p, q and n first, then apply the successive-probability relation P(r+1)/P(r) = ((n−r)/(r+1))·(p/q).
explanations: Correct: np/q = 9/0.4 = 22.5.
Wrong: 15 is the value of n, not the ratio.
Wrong: 9 is the mean np; it ignores the division by q.
Wrong: 13.5 comes from 9 × (p/q) = 9 × 1.5, which wrongly uses p/q instead of 1/q; the correct ratio is np/q.
keyfact: Binomial: variance/mean = q, so q = 3.6/9 = 0.4 and P(1)/P(0) = np/q.
question: For a binomial distribution the mean is 9 and the variance is 3.6. What is the value of the ratio P(X = 1) / P(X = 0)?

For a Poisson distribution, mean = variance.
subject: Statistics
summary: From np = 9 and npq = 3.6, q = 0.4, p = 0.6 and n = 15. The ratio P(1)/P(0) = np/q = 9/0.4 = 22.5.

detail: Add the three pair rates: 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = 12/60 = 1/5 = 2(A + B + C). So A + B + C = 1/10 per day. A = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, B = 1/10 − 1/20 = 1/20 and C = 1/10 − 1/12 = 1/60. In 4 days, all three complete 4/10 = 2/5 of the work, leaving 3/5. B and C together work at 1/15 per day, so they need (3/5) × 15 = 9 days. The correct figure is therefore 9 days, which is the fourth option, not the third. Elimination: 8 days would be right only if B and C worked at 3/40 per day, and 6 or 7 days would need rates well above 1/15.
explanations: Incorrect: 8 days would need B and C to do 3/5 of the work at 3/40 per day, but their combined rate is 1/15.
Incorrect: 7 days gives a rate of 3/35 per day, which does not match 1/15.
Incorrect: this is not the result of the calculation; 3/5 ÷ 1/15 = 9, not 8.
Correct: the remaining work is 3/5 and B + C = 1/15 per day, so 9 days are needed.
keyfact: Total rate of three workers = half the sum of the three pairwise rates.
question: A and B together can complete a piece of work in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days, and A and C together in 20 days. If A, B and C all work together for 4 days and then A leaves, in how many more days will B and C complete the remaining work?

Work = rate × time; rates of workers add.
If A is twice as efficient as B, A takes half B's time.

summary: The answer is 8 days. The three-person total rate is 1/10 per day, so 4 days finish 2/5 of the work. B and C together then need 3/5 ÷ 1/15 = 9 days. Re-checking the arithmetic: the remaining 3/5 at 1/15 per day gives 9 days, so the correct option is 9 days.

detail: Subrogation follows from the principle of indemnity, which says the insured must not profit from a loss. Once the insurer has indemnified the insured, it takes over the insured's rights of recovery against third parties responsible for the loss. The insurer's right is limited to the amount it paid, and any surplus recovery belongs to the insured. The right arises only on payment of the claim, not on issue of the policy. It applies to contracts of indemnity such as fire, marine, motor and property insurance. It does not apply to life insurance or personal accident cover, which are not contracts of indemnity, because human life cannot be valued in money and the benefit is a fixed sum. To eliminate: option a ignores this limit to indemnity contracts. Option c lets the insurer profit, which contradicts indemnity. Option d ignores that the right only arises after payment.
explanations: Wrong. Life insurance is not a contract of indemnity, so the insurer has no right of subrogation against a person who caused the death.
Correct. Subrogation arises after payment of the claim and is limited to the amount paid.
Wrong. Any recovery above the amount paid by the insurer belongs to the insured, otherwise the insurer would profit.
Wrong. The right arises only after the insurer has paid the loss, not when the policy is issued.
keyfact: Subrogation arises only after the claim is paid, is capped at the amount paid, and does not apply to life insurance.
options: It applies to life insurance, so the insurer can recover the sum paid from a person who caused the death of the assured
It entitles the insurer, after paying the claim, to step into the shoes of the insured and recover from a third party responsible for the loss, limited to the amount paid
It entitles the insurer to retain the entire amount recovered from the wrongdoer even if it exceeds the claim paid
It arises as soon as the policy is issued, whether or not any claim has been paid

subject: Insurance
summary: Option b is correct. Subrogation is a corollary of indemnity: it arises only after the insurer has paid the loss, and it lets the insurer recover from the wrongdoer only up to the amount it paid.
