subject: Polity
summary: The Union Home Minister chairs each of the five Zonal Councils. They are statutory bodies, not constitutional ones. The Inter-State Council was set up by a Presidential order in 1990.

detail: Primary pollutants such as carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and particulate matter are emitted directly from sources. Secondary pollutants form in the atmosphere through chemical reactions among primary pollutants. Ground-level ozone forms when nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds react in the presence of sunlight. Other secondary pollutants include peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN) and the photochemical smog constituents. This is why ozone concentrations peak on sunny afternoons and may be higher downwind of cities than in them. Stratospheric ozone is protective and forms naturally by photolysis of oxygen. Tropospheric ozone is harmful to human lungs and to crops. Elimination logic: Statement-II claims direct emission, which contradicts the very definition of a secondary pollutant. So options (a), (b) and (d) are ruled out.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is false, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is not correct, because ozone is not emitted directly in large quantities.
Correct: ozone forms from NOx and VOCs in sunlight, so it is a secondary pollutant, and direct emission is false.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by NOx and VOCs reacting in sunlight.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

Stratospheric ozone is protective, while tropospheric ozone is a pollutant.
subject: Environment
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect, so the answer is (c). Ground-level ozone forms in the atmosphere from reactions and is not emitted directly.

detail: Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when either House of Parliament is not in session and he is satisfied that circumstances require immediate action. An ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament, but it must be laid before both Houses when Parliament reassembles and ceases to operate at the expiration of six weeks from reassembly, or earlier if both Houses pass resolutions disapproving it. Under clause (3), an ordinance cannot make any provision which Parliament is not competent to enact, otherwise it is void. Option (a) is wrong because the power is available only when Parliament is not in session. Option (b) wrongly says the ordinance lapses unless disapproved earlier, which reverses the rule. Option (d) is wrong because courts can review ordinances on broader grounds, as seen in D.C. Wadhwa (1987) and Krishna Kumar Singh (2017).
explanations: Incorrect: the power may be exercised only when either House is not in session.
Incorrect: it lapses automatically six weeks after reassembly unless approved by being replaced by an Act; wording is reversed here.
Correct: Article 123(3) makes it void to the extent it goes beyond Parliament's legislative competence.
Incorrect: ordinances are open to judicial review on grounds beyond mala fides.
keyfact: An ordinance under Article 123 cannot cover matters outside Parliament's legislative competence and expires six weeks after Parliament reassembles unless disapproved sooner.
options: An ordinance can be promulgated at any time, whether or not Parliament is in session
An ordinance must be laid before Parliament and ceases to operate at the expiration of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament unless disapproved earlier
An ordinance cannot make any provision which Parliament is not competent to enact
An ordinance promulgated by the President can be challenged only on the ground of mala fide intention and never otherwise
question: With reference to the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements regarding the President's power to promulgate ordinances under Article 123 is correct?
related: Article 213 gives the Governor a similar ordinance-making power.
Maximum gap between two Parliament sessions is six months (Article 85).
An ordinance may be withdrawn by the President at any time.
D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar (1987) condemned the re-promulgation of ordinances.
Article 123 power is co-extensive with Parliament's legislative power.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: Option (c) is correct. Article 123(3) provides that an ordinance is void to the extent it makes a provision that Parliament would not be competent to enact.

detail: Under the Code on Wages, wages are paid at intervals set by the wage period. For monthly wages, payment must be made before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding wage period. Where an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched or resigns, the wages earned must be paid within two working days of the cessation of employment. subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The answer is two working days. The Code requires settlement of wages within two working days of the employee ceasing to be in employment.
topic: Payment of wages under the Code on Wages, 2019

detail: Use rates per hour. A fills 1/12 and B fills 1/15, so together they fill 1/12 + 1/15 = 9/60 = 3/20 of the tank per hour. In 4 hours they fill 4 × 3/20 = 3/5. The remaining part is 2/5. Once C is opened, the net rate is 3/20 - 1/20 = 2/20 = 1/10 per hour, because C empties 1/20 per hour. Time for the remaining 2/5 is (2/5) ÷ (1/10) = 4 hours. Total time = 4 + 4 = 8 hours. Elimination: 7 hours would result from forgetting that C slows the filling (2/5 ÷ 3/20 is about 2.67 hours, giving roughly 6.67). 9 and 10 hours overestimate by treating the net rate incorrectly, such as using 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/20 on the full tank from the beginning, which gives 10 hours at most.
explanations: 7 hours would require the remaining 2/5 to be filled in 3 hours, a net rate of 2/15, which is more than the actual 1/10. Incorrect.
Correct. 4 hours at 3/20 per hour fills 3/5, and 4 further hours at 1/10 per hour fills 2/5.
9 hours would need the second phase to last 5 hours, giving a net rate of only 2/25. Incorrect.
10 hours is the time if all three pipes ran from the start (1/10 per hour for the full tank). Since C opened late, the tank fills sooner. Incorrect.
keyfact: In pipes and cisterns, add rates of inlets and subtract rates of outlets, then compute time for the remaining fraction.

summary: The tank is filled in 8 hours from the start. A and B fill 3/5 of the tank in 4 hours, and the remaining 2/5 is filled at a net rate of 1/10 per hour with C open, which takes 4 more hours.

The Anoop Baranwal case (2023) was decided by a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court.
Election Commissioners cannot be removed except on the recommendation of the CEC.
Article 324(2) allows the President to fix the number of Election Commissioners.
subject: Polity
summary: Option (d) is correct because it describes the Selection Committee composition under the 2023 Act. The other options misstate the Committee, the removal rule and the tenure.

detail: Utmost good faith requires the parties to disclose all material facts honestly. Because the proposer has the knowledge about the risk, the duty to disclose falls mainly on the proposer, but the duty is mutual. The insurer must also act in good faith and not conceal or misrepresent policy terms. Materiality is tested by whether the fact would influence a prudent insurer. Breach by the proposer makes the contract voidable at the insurer's option, not void automatically. The duty continues at renewal of general insurance policies, which are renewed as fresh contracts, and applies to claims as well, so statement 4 is wrong. Statement 1 is wrong because the duty is mutual.
explanations: Wrong. Statement 1 is incorrect because the duty is mutual.
Correct. Statements 2 and 3 are correct and 1 and 4 are incorrect.
Wrong. Statement 4 is incorrect because the duty applies at renewal.
Wrong. Statements 1 and 4 are incorrect.
keyfact: Utmost good faith: duty is mutual, and material non-disclosure makes the contract voidable at the insurer's option.
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the principle of utmost good faith (uberrima fides) in insurance:
1. The duty of disclosure rests only on the proposer, and the insurer owes no corresponding duty of disclosure.
2. A fact is material if it would influence a prudent insurer in deciding whether to accept the risk or in fixing the premium.
3. Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract voidable at the option of the insurer.
4. The duty of utmost good faith ends once the policy is issued and does not apply at renewal of general insurance policies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Uberrima fides is a basic principle of insurance contracts.
A material fact is one that influences a prudent insurer's decision.
Non-disclosure of a material fact makes the contract voidable, not void.
The duty of disclosure is mutual but falls more heavily on the proposer.
Ordinary contracts follow caveat emptor, but insurance contracts do not.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: the duty of good faith is mutual, so the insurer must also act honestly and not conceal or misrepresent terms.
2 — Correct: the test of materiality is the effect on a prudent insurer's decision about acceptance or premium.
3 — Correct: non-disclosure of a material fact makes the contract voidable at the insurer's option, not void.
4 — Incorrect: the duty continues at renewal of general insurance and in the claims stage.
subject: Insurance
summary: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct. Materiality is judged by the prudent insurer test, and non-disclosure of a material fact makes the contract voidable at the insurer's option.

detail: The troposphere is deeper at the equator (about 16-18 km) because strong convection lifts the tropopause. It is only about 8-9 km deep at the poles. The stratosphere warms with height because the ozone layer absorbs UV radiation, so it is stable and has little vertical mixing. The mesosphere extends to about 85-90 km, and the mesopause at its top is the coldest part of the atmosphere. The thermosphere lies above it, and the Kármán line at 100 km is conventionally taken as the boundary of space. Because the line lies above the mesopause, it is in the thermosphere. To eliminate options, confirm statements 1 and 2 first, since both are standard textbook facts. That rules out 'Only one' and 'None'. Then test statement 3 against the layer heights to rule out 'All three'.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is wrong.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong because the Kármán line lies in the thermosphere.
Incorrect: statements 1 and 2 are standard facts and are correct.
keyfact: The Kármán line (100 km) lies in the thermosphere, above the mesopause.
question:
With reference to the vertical structure of the Earth's atmosphere, consider the following statements:
1. The tropopause is, on average, higher over the equator than over the poles.
2. In the stratosphere, temperature generally increases with altitude because ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation.
3. The Kármán line, conventionally placed at 100 km above sea level, lies within the mesosphere.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: The tropopause is the boundary between the troposphere and stratosphere, and the coldest temperatures in the lower atmosphere occur there.
The ozone layer is concentrated at about 15-35 km in the stratosphere.
The mesopause is the coldest part of the whole atmosphere.
The ionosphere overlaps the mesosphere and thermosphere and reflects radio waves.
statements: 1 — Correct: Strong convection in the tropics raises the tropopause to about 16-18 km, against about 8-9 km at the poles.
2 — Correct: Ozone absorbs UV in the stratosphere, so temperature rises with height there.
3 — Incorrect: The mesosphere ends at about 85-90 km. The 100 km Kármán line is in the thermosphere.
The coldest region of the atmosphere is the mesopause. The thermosphere contains the ionosphere and is where auroras occur.
subject: Geography
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Kármán line (100 km) lies above the mesopause (about 85-90 km), so it falls in the thermosphere, not the mesosphere.

detail: The current account covers trade in goods, trade in services, primary income (such as investment income and compensation of employees) and secondary income (such as personal transfers or remittances). The capital and financial account covers FDI, portfolio investment, external commercial borrowings, banking capital, and changes in reserves. India typically runs a deficit in merchandise trade, offset partly by a surplus in services (software and business services) and remittances. To eliminate the options, note that FDI and ECB are investment flows and remittances are current transfers, which leaves services as the current account entry.
explanations: Wrong: FDI is in the financial account.
Wrong: Remittances are in the current account as secondary income.
Correct: Services trade is a current account item.
Wrong: ECBs are financial account items.
keyfact: Services trade and remittances belong to the current account; FDI and ECBs belong to the financial account.
options: Foreign Direct Investment inflows are recorded in the current account
Remittances from Indians working abroad are recorded in the capital account
Net exports of services are recorded in the current account
External Commercial Borrowings are recorded in the current account
question: With reference to the Balance of Payments (BoP) of India, which one of the following is correct?
related: Current account = trade balance + services + primary and secondary income.
Current account deficit is financed by capital account inflows.
India usually has a services trade surplus.
Foreign exchange reserves changes appear in the financial account.
subject: Economy
summary: Net exports of services are recorded in the current account. FDI and ECBs are capital or financial account items, and remittances are current account transfers.

detail: Nitrogen enters ecosystems through biological fixation (symbiotic Rhizobium; free-living Azotobacter; cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc), atmospheric fixation by lightning, and industrial fixation (Haber-Bosch). Nitrification, by Nitrosomonas (ammonia to nitrite) and Nitrobacter (nitrite to nitrate), is aerobic. Denitrification, by bacteria such as Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus, reduces nitrate to N2 (and some N2O) under anaerobic conditions such as waterlogged soils. Elimination logic: spotting that statement 3 is wrong removes options b, c and d, which all include it.
explanations: Correct: statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3 and leaves out 2 and 4.
Incorrect: it omits statement 1, which is correct, and includes statement 3.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong, so not all four can be correct.
keyfact: Nitrification is aerobic; denitrification is anaerobic and returns N2 to the atmosphere.
question:
With reference to the nitrogen cycle, consider the following statements:
1. Free-living bacteria such as Azotobacter and cyanobacteria such as Anabaena can fix atmospheric nitrogen.
2. Nitrification involves the oxidation of ammonia to nitrite and then to nitrate by chemoautotrophic bacteria.
3. Denitrification occurs mainly in well-aerated soils and converts atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.
4. Lightning contributes to the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into forms usable by plants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically in legume root nodules.
Azolla with Anabaena is used as a biofertiliser in paddy.
Nitrous oxide is a greenhouse gas that is also an ozone-depleting substance.
Haber-Bosch is the industrial route to ammonia.
statements: 1 — Correct: Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen fixer and Anabaena is a cyanobacterium that fixes nitrogen.
2 — Correct: Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are chemoautotrophs that carry out the two steps of nitrification.
3 — Incorrect: Denitrification is largely anaerobic and releases N2 to the air; it does not produce ammonia.
4 — Correct: Lightning oxidises N2 to nitrogen oxides, which reach the soil as nitrates in rain.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 reverses denitrification, which happens under anaerobic conditions and returns N2 to the atmosphere.

detail: Under Article 110 and Article 117, a Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha and can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only on the President's recommendation. Under Article 109, the Rajya Sabha may only make recommendations within fourteen days of receipt; it cannot reject or amend the Bill. Strictly, the Rajya Sabha can recommend amendments, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject; if not returned within fourteen days, the Bill is deemed passed. Statement-II as phrased is therefore accurate in that the Rajya Sabha cannot itself amend or reject it, and it must return the Bill within fourteen days. The President's recommendation is a financial-executive control, while Statement-II describes the Rajya Sabha's limited role, so neither explains the other.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II does not explain why the President's recommendation is required.
Correct: both are true but independent facts.
Wrong: Statement-II is accurate under Article 109.
Wrong: Statement-I is accurate under Article 117.
keyfact: Money Bill: Lok Sabha only, President's recommendation, Rajya Sabha has 14 days to recommend only.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: A Money Bill can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only on the recommendation of the President.
Statement-II: The Rajya Sabha has no power to reject or amend a Money Bill, and must return it to the Lok Sabha within fourteen days of its receipt.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Article 110 defines Money Bill; Speaker's certification is final.
Rajya Sabha can recommend amendments within 14 days to a Money Bill.
Financial Bills Category I also need President's recommendation for introduction.
Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
subject: Polity
summary: Both statements are correct but unrelated in reasoning. Statement-II is not the reason for the President's recommendation requirement.

detail: Cost to be capitalised = purchase price + installation = 5,00,000 + 50,000 = 5,50,000. Depreciation for year 1 at 20% WDV = 1,10,000, leaving 4,40,000. Depreciation for year 2 = 88,000, leaving 3,52,000. Sale proceeds are 3,00,000, so the loss is 3,52,000 - 3,00,000 = 52,000. The correct option is therefore a (Loss of ₹52,000). The answer key letter b is wrong. Corrected answer: a.
explanations: Correct: the WDV is ₹3,52,000 and the sale is at ₹3,00,000, so the loss is ₹52,000.
Wrong: a profit would arise only if the sale price exceeded the book value, which it does not.
Wrong: this would result from ignoring the installation cost or miscomputing depreciation.
Wrong: this reverses the sign of the actual loss.
keyfact: Capitalise installation cost; WDV depreciation is charged on the reducing balance.
question: A firm purchased a machine on 1 April 2024 for ₹5,00,000 and incurred ₹50,000 on installation. Depreciation is charged at 20% per annum on the Written Down Value method. On 31 March 2026 the machine was sold for ₹3,00,000. The profit or loss on sale is:
related: Installation charges are capitalised as part of the cost of the asset.
Under WDV, depreciation is charged on the opening book value each year.
Profit or loss on sale = sale price - WDV at the date of sale.
Under AS 10, the cost of PPE includes all costs to bring the asset to working condition.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The answer is a profit of ₹8,000. Installation cost is capitalised, so the WDV after two years is ₹3,52,000, and the sale price is ₹3,00,000, which gives a loss. Recomputing carefully shows the book value is ₹3,52,000 and the loss is ₹52,000, so option a is correct.
topic: Depreciation and disposal of fixed assets

detail: Article 280 creates the Finance Commission as a quasi-judicial constitutional body. The President constitutes it every fifth year or earlier. It has a Chairman and four other members, and Parliament by law decides their qualifications. Its main role is to recommend how the net proceeds of Union taxes are shared between the Union and the States, and among the States. It also recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid under Article 275. Since the 73rd and 74th Amendments, it also recommends measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund to supplement local body resources, based on State Finance Commission recommendations. The President lays its report before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken. The recommendations are only advisory, so the Union is not legally bound by them. In practice they are usually accepted. Eliminating statement 2 removes options c and d, and statements 1 and 3 are both accurate, which leaves b.
explanations: Incomplete: statement 3 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are accurate and statement 2 is wrong.
Wrong: it includes statement 2, which wrongly calls the recommendations binding, and leaves out statement 1.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect, so not all three statements hold.
keyfact: Finance Commission recommendations are advisory, and the Commission is a constitutional body created by Article 280.
question:
With reference to the Finance Commission under Article 280 of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. It is constituted by the President at the expiration of every fifth year from the commencement of the Constitution, or earlier if the President considers necessary.
2. Its recommendations are binding on the Union Government once they are laid before Parliament.
3. It recommends the measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities, on the basis of the recommendations of the State Finance Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Article 280(3) lists the Commission's duties on tax devolution, grants-in-aid and local body resources.
Article 275 deals with grants-in-aid to States in need.
Parliament decides the qualifications of members by law.
The Report is laid before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum on action taken.
State Finance Commissions are created under Articles 243-I and 243-Y.
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 280(1) provides for constitution every fifth year or earlier.
2 — Incorrect: The recommendations are advisory and have no binding force. The Union lays them before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum on action taken.
3 — Correct: Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) cover supplementing the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities on the basis of State Finance Commission recommendations.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 1 and 3 only. Statement 2 is wrong because Finance Commission recommendations are advisory, not binding.

detail: The ELI scheme, with an outlay of about Rs 99,446 crore, aims to create around 3.5 crore jobs. Part A supports first-time employees registered with EPFO, who get one month's wage up to Rs 15,000 in two instalments. Part B supports employers, with an incentive per additional employee for a set period. The scheme covers wages up to Rs 1 lakh per month. The first instalment is paid after six months of service and the second after twelve months, together with a financial literacy programme. The payment goes through Aadhaar-based DBT. The scheme is linked to EPFO registration, so the exam is likely to test this. Option a is wrong because it names ESIC and a wrong amount. Option c is wrong on the duration. Option d is wrong because payment is in two instalments, not on joining.
explanations: Wrong: the scheme is linked to EPFO registration, not ESIC, and the amount is up to Rs 15,000.
Correct: this matches the scheme's amount, two-instalment structure and the 1 Aug 2025 to 31 Jul 2027 window.
Wrong: it is a one-time incentive to first-time employees, not a five-year monthly subsidy.
Wrong: the payment is in two instalments, not a single instalment on joining.
keyfact: PM-VBRY (ELI): up to Rs 15,000 in two instalments to first-time EPFO-registered employees, for jobs created 1 Aug 2025 to 31 Jul 2027.
options: A one-time payment of Rs 25,000 to every employee who registers with ESIC for the first time
An incentive of up to Rs 15,000 in two instalments to first-time employees registered with EPFO, for jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027
A monthly wage subsidy of Rs 15,000 to employees for five years for jobs created up to 2030
A single instalment of Rs 15,000 paid on the day of joining to employees earning up to Rs 50,000 per month
question: The Employment Linked Incentive scheme, launched as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on 1 August 2025, provides which one of the following?
related: The scheme's outlay is about Rs 99,446 crore.
The first instalment is paid after 6 months of service and the second after 12 months.
Part A covers first-time employees and Part B covers employers.
Payment is made through Aadhaar-based DBT.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Option b is correct. The scheme gives first-time EPFO-registered employees up to Rs 15,000 in two instalments, for jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027.
topic: Social security: Employment Linked Incentive / PM-VBRY

detail: The Montreux Record is part of the Ramsar List and flags sites needing priority conservation attention because of technological developments, pollution or other human interference. It is a voluntary, cooperative tool, so entry needs the consent of the Contracting Party. In India, Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur) are on the Record. Chilika Lake was added in 1993 and removed in 2002 after restoration work, which is often cited as a success story. Elimination logic: statement 2 contradicts the sovereign, consent-based character of the convention, which leaves only 'Only two' standing once 1 and 3 are verified.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong because the Secretariat cannot list a site without the country's consent.
Incorrect: statements 1 and 3 are accurate.
keyfact: Montreux Record entry needs the concerned country's concurrence; Keoladeo and Loktak are India's listed sites.
question:
With reference to the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands and the Montreux Record, consider the following statements:
1. The Montreux Record is a register of Ramsar-listed wetland sites where changes in ecological character have occurred, are occurring or are likely to occur.
2. A site can be added to the Montreux Record by the Ramsar Secretariat even without the concurrence of the Contracting Party concerned.
3. Loktak Lake in Manipur is currently included in the Montreux Record.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Chilika Lake was the first Indian site added to the Montreux Record and the first removed from it, in 2002.
Keoladeo National Park is a Ramsar site and a Montreux Record site.
The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.
India's wetland rules are the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017.
statements: 1 — Correct: This is the standard definition of the Montreux Record, a register within the Ramsar List.
2 — Incorrect: Inclusion requires the concurrence of the Contracting Party; the Secretariat cannot act unilaterally.
3 — Correct: Loktak Lake and Keoladeo National Park are the two Indian sites currently on the Record.
Chilika was removed from the Record in 2002. Ramsar sites are designated by the Contracting Party, and the Record is a monitoring and priority-action tool.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'. Statement 2 is wrong because a site is added to the Montreux Record only with the concurrence of the country concerned.

detail: Vaccines are classified by how the antigen is presented. Live attenuated vaccines use weakened organisms: oral polio vaccine, MMR and BCG. Inactivated vaccines use killed pathogens, such as the injectable polio vaccine. Subunit and recombinant vaccines use purified or engineered antigen, as with the hepatitis B surface antigen produced in yeast. Viral vector vaccines use a harmless carrier virus to deliver the gene for an antigen. Covishield was the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine, which used a chimpanzee adenovirus (ChAdOx1) that cannot replicate in humans. BCG is made from a weakened strain of Mycobacterium bovis, so statement 3 is incorrect. Once statement 3 is rejected, options (c) and (d) fall, and since statement 4 is correct, option (a) falls too.
explanations: Incorrect. This omits statement 4, which is also correct.
Correct. Statements 1, 2 and 4 are accurate.
Incorrect. It includes statement 3, which is wrong, and leaves out statement 1.
Incorrect. It includes statement 3, which is wrong, and omits statement 2.
keyfact: BCG is live attenuated; Covishield is a non-replicating adenoviral vector vaccine; hepatitis B vaccine is recombinant.
question:
With reference to vaccines, consider the following statements:
1. The oral polio vaccine contains live attenuated polioviruses.
2. The hepatitis B vaccine in common use is a recombinant subunit vaccine.
3. The BCG vaccine is an inactivated vaccine prepared from killed bacteria.
4. The Covishield vaccine against COVID-19 used a modified non-replicating adenovirus as a vector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Injectable polio vaccine (IPV) uses inactivated virus.
MMR and varicella are live attenuated vaccines.
Typhoid conjugate vaccine links a polysaccharide antigen to a carrier protein.
Covaxin is a whole-virion inactivated vaccine.
mRNA vaccines deliver genetic instructions in lipid nanoparticles.
statements: 1 — Correct: OPV is a live attenuated vaccine and can rarely revert to cause vaccine-derived poliovirus.
2 — Correct: The hepatitis B surface antigen is produced by recombinant DNA technology, commonly in yeast.
3 — Incorrect: BCG is live attenuated, made from Mycobacterium bovis.
4 — Correct: Covishield used the ChAdOx1 non-replicating adenoviral vector. Remember that mRNA vaccines such as Pfizer and Moderna use lipid nanoparticles, not a viral vector.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because BCG is a live attenuated vaccine, not a killed one.

detail: The Barabar caves in Bihar are the earliest surviving rock-cut caves, with the highly polished Mauryan finish. Sudama cave bears Ashoka's 12th regnal year inscription recording its gift to the Ajivikas. The Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri near Bhubaneswar, written in Brahmi, records the career of the Chedi king Kharavela, so pair 2 is correct. Karla, near Lonavala in Maharashtra, has the largest and best-preserved early Buddhist chaitya hall of the Western Ghats, so pair 3 is wrong. The Pancha Rathas of Mamallapuram are monolithic temples of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I, so pair 4 is wrong. With two correct pairs, the only matching option is 'only two pairs'.
explanations: Wrong: two pairs are correctly matched, not one.
Correct: pairs 1 and 2 only.
Wrong: pair 3 is wrongly matched.
Wrong: pairs 3 and 4 are incorrect.
keyfact: Karla (Maharashtra) has the biggest early chaitya hall; Pancha Rathas are Pallava.
question:
Consider the following pairs:
Rock-cut or monument site : Association
1. Sudama cave, Barabar hills : Cave dedicated to the Ajivikas in the reign of Ashoka
2. Hathigumpha, Udayagiri (Odisha) : Inscription of Kharavela
3. Karla chaitya hall : Located in Karnataka
4. Pancha Rathas, Mamallapuram : Created under the Chalukyas of Badami
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
related: The Barabar caves have the earliest polished rock-cut interiors.
Kharavela of Kalinga was a Jaina and is known from the Hathigumpha inscription.
The Kailasa temple at Ellora was built under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I.
Bhaja, Karla and Bedsa are early Buddhist caves of western India.
Ajanta is in Maharashtra and has Buddhist paintings.
statements: 1 — Correct: Sudama cave has Ashoka's inscription dedicating it to the Ajivikas.
2 — Correct: the Hathigumpha inscription records Kharavela's achievements.
3 — Incorrect: Karla is in Maharashtra.
4 — Incorrect: the Pancha Rathas are Pallava (Narasimhavarman I). Facts: Karla is Buddhist; the Kailasa temple at Ellora is Rashtrakuta.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Only pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. Karla is in Maharashtra and the Pancha Rathas are Pallava work.

detail: PMJJBY, launched in 2015, is a one-year renewable term plan for savings bank account holders aged 18 to 50 who give auto-debit consent. Cover continues up to age 55 if premiums are paid. The sum assured is ₹2 lakh for death due to any cause. The premium was increased from ₹330 to ₹436 per year with effect from June 2022. In contrast, PMSBY covers accidental death and disability at a premium of ₹20 per year for ages 18 to 70. Elimination: (a) mixes PMSBY features, (b) wrongly gives an age band of 70 and a one-time premium, and (c) uses the old pre-2022 premium of ₹330. Only (d) is correct.
explanations: Incorrect. Accident-only cover and the ₹20 premium describe PMSBY.
Incorrect. The entry age is 18 to 50, and the premium is annual and not a one-time payment.
Incorrect. ₹330 was the earlier premium; the current premium is ₹436.
Correct. It is a renewable one-year term cover of ₹2 lakh at ₹436 per year for ages 18 to 50.
keyfact: PMJJBY: ₹2 lakh cover, any cause of death, ₹436 per year, ages 18 to 50, renewable annually.
options: It provides a life cover of ₹2 lakh only in the event of accidental death, at an annual premium of ₹20
It is open to bank account holders aged 18 to 70 years, with the premium of ₹436 payable once for lifetime cover
It provides a life cover of ₹2 lakh at an annual premium of ₹330, enrolment being possible up to age 50
It provides a renewable one-year life cover of ₹2 lakh for death due to any reason, at an annual premium of ₹436, for bank account holders aged 18 to 50 years
question: With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), which one of the following statements is correct?
related: PMJJBY and PMSBY were launched on 9 May 2015
PMJJBY cover continues up to age 55 if the premium is paid
PMSBY premium is ₹20 a year and gives ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total permanent disability
The Atal Pension Yojana was launched along with these two schemes in 2015
Premiums are auto-debited from the bank account, usually around 31 May each year
subject: Social Security
summary: PMJJBY is a one-year renewable term life insurance giving ₹2 lakh on death from any cause, with an annual premium of ₹436 and entry age of 18 to 50 years. The ₹20 premium and accident-only cover belong to PMSBY.

detail: Face value of the debentures is 10,000 × ₹100 = ₹10,00,000. Issue at a 5% discount means the company receives ₹9,50,000, so the discount on issue is ₹50,000. Redemption at a 10% premium means the company pays ₹11,00,000, so the premium on redemption is ₹1,00,000. Both amounts are a cost of borrowing to the company and are treated together as 'Loss on Issue of Debentures'. The total is ₹50,000 + ₹1,00,000 = ₹1,50,000, which is 15% of the face value. This is written off over the life of the debentures, and it may be adjusted against the securities premium account where available. Option (a) counts only the discount. Option (b) counts only the premium. Option (d) is a computational mix-up with no basis.
explanations: Incorrect. This is only the discount on issue and omits the premium on redemption.
Incorrect. This is only the premium on redemption and omits the discount on issue.
Correct. Discount on issue ₹50,000 plus premium on redemption ₹1,00,000 gives ₹1,50,000.
Incorrect. This figure has no valid basis in the computation.
keyfact: Loss on issue of debentures = Discount on issue + Premium on redemption.
question: A company issued 10,000 debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 5%, redeemable at the end of five years at a premium of 10%. What is the total amount of loss on issue of debentures to be written off over the life of the debentures?
related: Loss on issue of debentures is shown as an asset or adjusted against securities premium, and written off over the debenture life.
Debenture redemption reserve requirements are governed by the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014.
Interest on debentures is a charge against profit, not an appropriation.
Debentures issued at a discount are recorded at face value in the liability side.
Premium on redemption is a liability that arises at the time of issue.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The total loss on issue is ₹1,50,000. It is the sum of the discount on issue (₹50,000) and the premium payable on redemption (₹1,00,000).

detail: UDP is a connectionless, best-effort protocol: no handshake, no retransmission, no ordering. TCP is connection-oriented and sets up a connection with SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK. The UDP header has four 2-byte fields (source port, destination port, length, checksum) totalling 8 bytes; the TCP header has a minimum of 20 bytes, extendable to 60 with options. TCP flow control uses the receiver-advertised window in a sliding-window scheme, and congestion control is separate. Since every statement is accurate, the option covering all four is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: it omits statements 3 and 4, which are also correct.
Incorrect: it omits statement 1, which is correct.
Incorrect: it omits statement 2, which is correct.
Correct: all four statements are accurate.
keyfact: UDP header = 8 bytes; TCP header = 20 to 60 bytes.
question:
Consider the following statements about the TCP and UDP transport protocols:
1. UDP is connectionless and does not guarantee delivery or ordering of datagrams.

detail: The southwest monsoon winds, laden with moisture from the Arabian Sea, are forced up the Western Ghats. The air cools and drops heavy orographic rain on the western slopes, often over 250 cm. After crossing the crest the air descends, warms adiabatically and becomes dry, so the leeward areas of interior Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana get far less rain, often under 60 cm. This is the rain-shadow effect. The second statement therefore gives the direct cause of the contrast in the first. detail: The EDLI Scheme, 1976 gives life insurance cover to members of the EPF. The employer alone contributes to it. A 2021 amendment revised the benefit to a minimum of Rs. 2.5 lakh and a maximum of Rs. 7 lakh. At the wage ceiling of Rs. 15,000, 35 times the wage is Rs. 5.25 lakh, and adding the Rs. 1.75 lakh bonus gives Rs. 7 lakh. The minimum benefit of Rs. 2.5 lakh is payable even if the member has completed less than twelve months of continuous service, in the case of a member who dies within that period. Elimination: Rs. 2.5 lakh is the minimum, not the maximum. Rs. 6 lakh and Rs. 10 lakh are not figures in the Scheme.

detail: Annual depreciation = 10% of 5,00,000 = ₹50,000. Depreciation for 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2025 is three years, so ₹1,50,000. Book value = 5,00,000 - 1,50,000 = ₹3,50,000. Sale price = ₹3,00,000. Loss = 3,50,000 - 3,00,000 = ₹50,000. The correct answer is therefore a loss of ₹50,000, which is option (a), not option (b). Option (b) reverses the sign. detail: Total units available = 1,000 + 2,000 + 1,000 = 4,000. Total sold = 1,500 + 1,200 = 2,700. Closing = 1,300 units. Let us trace FIFO. On 25 April, 1,200 units are issued from the oldest lot, the ₹12 lot, leaving 300 units at ₹12 and 1,000 at ₹14. Closing = 300 x 12 + 1,000 x 14 = 3,600 + 14,000 = ₹17,600. Note: the closing quantity is 1,300, not 1,000. Under FIFO the answer is ₹17,600, which is not among the options, so this question's answer key is unreliable and should be revised before use.

Does not match the FIFO trace.
keyfact: Under FIFO, closing stock is made up of the most recent purchases.

detail: Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave produced by vibrating bodies, travelling as compressions and rarefactions in a medium. Because it depends on particle collisions, it cannot pass through a vacuum, unlike light. Speed is generally greatest in solids, less in liquids and least in gases, since elasticity matters more than density; thus sound is much faster in steel (about 5000 m/s) than in air (about 340 m/s). Pitch is determined by frequency, while loudness depends on amplitude. Eliminate (a) as air supports only longitudinal waves, (b) for reversing the speed order, and (d) for confusing pitch with loudness.

Incorrect: pitch depends on frequency; amplitude determines loudness.
keyfact: Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave; it needs a medium and travels fastest in solids.

detail: Article 148 provides for the CAG, appointed by warrant under the hand and seal of the President. detail: Gupta inscriptions, especially the Damodarpur copper plates, give a clear view of administrative structure. The empire was divided into bhuktis headed by an Uparika, who was often appointed by the king and sometimes held a royal title. Bhuktis were subdivided into vishayas under a Vishayapati, and the lowest units were villages under the gramika or village headman. Vishti referred to forced labour, which is evidence of how rural resources were mobilised, particularly in the Gupta and post-Gupta periods. The Sandhivigrahika (Mahasandhivigrahika) was the minister for peace and war, as seen in Samudragupta's Prayaga Prashasti, where Harishena held that office. Finance and records were handled by officials such as the Pustapala, record keeper, and the Akshapatalika, keeper of documents. Spotting the error in statement 3 gives the right count quickly.

summary: The answer is (b). Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but the Sandhivigrahika was the minister for peace and war, not for finance.

detail: Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of a persistent substance at successive trophic levels. Pollutants such as DDT, PCBs and methylmercury are lipophilic (fat-soluble) and resist metabolic degradation. They therefore accumulate in fatty tissues and are retained. Each predator eats many contaminated prey, so the burden concentrates at higher trophic levels, with top carnivores such as fish-eating birds affected most. This is why DDT caused eggshell thinning in raptors. Statement-I is therefore true. Statement-II reverses the mechanism. Water-soluble substances are readily excreted and do not biomagnify. Elimination logic: once you see that Statement-II contradicts the lipid-solubility principle, options (a), (b) and (d) are eliminated. Do not confuse biomagnification with bioaccumulation, which is build-up within one organism over time.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II is false, so it cannot explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is not correct at all.
Correct: Statement-I is true and Statement-II misstates the mechanism.
Wrong: Statement-I is true.
keyfact: Biomagnification needs pollutants that are persistent and fat-soluble, not water-soluble.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:

Statement-II: Biomagnification occurs because such pollutants are highly water-soluble and are therefore rapidly excreted by organisms.

statements: Statement-I — Correct: persistent lipophilic pollutants concentrate progressively up the trophic levels and peak in top carnivores.
Statement-II — Incorrect: the cause is fat-solubility and slow degradation or excretion, not water-solubility.
Bioaccumulation occurs within a single organism. Biomagnification occurs across trophic levels. DDT thinned the eggshells of birds of prey.
subject: Environment
summary: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. Biomagnification happens because the pollutants are fat-soluble and resist breakdown and excretion, not because they are water-soluble.

detail: A standard fire policy covers only material damage to the insured property. It does not cover the financial consequences of the interruption of business. A consequential loss (loss of profit) policy fills this gap. It covers loss of gross profit and standing charges for the indemnity period, which is the period needed to restore the business to normal after damage by an insured peril. The insurer normally insists that the material damage claim is admitted or payable under the fire policy. In practice, it is therefore issued only to an insured who holds a fire policy on the property. Option a describes the standard fire policy, not the consequential loss policy. Option b ignores the condition about the material damage policy. Option d is wrong because market-related losses are not insured perils, and the interruption must follow damage by an insured peril.

Incorrect: it does not cover market fluctuations or fall in demand, as these are not insured perils.

The Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) is for Panchayats and the Twelfth Schedule (18 functions) is for Municipalities, both added by the 73rd and 74th Amendments. Pair 4 swaps these, so it is the trap. For chronology questions, anchor on years and cause-effect relationships: the Poona Pact is a direct response to the Communal Award.

detail: Section 25F of the ID Act (now Section 70 of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020) requires one month's notice or pay in lieu, and compensation of 15 days' average pay for every completed year of service, as conditions precedent to retrenchment. The Supreme Court in Bombay Union of Journalists v. State of Bombay (1963) held these conditions mandatory. Later cases, for example State Bank of India v. N. Sundara Money (1976), dealt with the meaning of retrenchment and held it covers termination for any reason other than the listed exceptions. Bharat Forge concerned the validity of a domestic enquiry and misconduct. Bhonrilal involved regularisation and the effect of irregular appointments. Elimination: identify the case that is about the mandatory nature of Section 25F's conditions.
explanations: Incorrect: Bharat Forge Co. Ltd. v. Uttam Manohar Nakate concerned the consequences of an unfair or defective enquiry and the power of the labour court under Section 11A, not the mandatory character of Section 25F.

Incorrect: N. Sundara Money is known for the wide meaning of 'retrenchment', covering termination for any reason whatsoever except those carved out, but it is not the leading case on the mandatory nature of the conditions.
Correct: Bombay Union of Journalists treated the Section 25F conditions as mandatory, so retrenchment in breach is invalid.
Incorrect: Bhonrilal dealt with regularisation and the invalidity of irregular appointments, not the mandatory character of retrenchment conditions.
keyfact: Bombay Union of Journalists (1963): Section 25F conditions are mandatory; breach makes retrenchment void.
options: Bharat Forge Co. Ltd. v. Uttam Manohar Nakate
State Bank of India v. N. Sundara Money
Bombay Union of Journalists v. State of Bombay
Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation v. Bhonrilal

Under the IR Code, 2020, retrenchment compensation is 15 days' average pay for each completed year of service.

subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct choice is Bombay Union of Journalists v. State of Bombay (1963), which treated compliance with Section 25F as a mandatory condition precedent to a valid retrenchment. Non-compliance renders the retrenchment invalid and void.

detail: An energy pyramid shows the rate of energy flow at each trophic level. Because of the second law of thermodynamics and the roughly 10 per cent transfer rule, energy at each higher level is less than at the level below, so this pyramid is always upright. Biomass pyramids show standing crop. In a pond, phytoplankton are tiny, reproduce rapidly and are consumed quickly, so their standing biomass at any moment is less than that of the zooplankton or fish they support. The pyramid of biomass is therefore inverted. Pyramids of numbers can also be inverted, as with a single tree supporting many insects. Statement 3 wrongly applies inversion to the energy pyramid, so it is incorrect. Elimination logic: statement 1 is certain, which removes nothing alone. Statement 3 contradicts statement 1, so options (c) and (d) are eliminated. That leaves (a) and (b), and statement 2 is a standard fact, so (b) is the answer.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct, so this option is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are true and statement 3 is false.
Wrong: statement 3 is false and it also excludes statement 1.
Wrong: statement 3 is false.
keyfact: Pyramid of energy is always upright; pyramids of numbers and biomass can be inverted.
question:
With reference to ecological pyramids, consider the following statements:
1. The pyramid of energy is always upright in any ecosystem.
2. The pyramid of biomass in a pond ecosystem is generally inverted.
3. The pyramid of energy can be inverted in a pond ecosystem because phytoplankton have a short life span.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Lindeman's 10 per cent law describes energy transfer between trophic levels.
A pyramid of numbers is inverted for a tree with many insects.
Gross primary productivity minus respiration equals net primary productivity.
Detritus food chains are important in forest and estuarine ecosystems.
statements: 1 — Correct: energy is lost as heat at each transfer, so the energy pyramid is always upright.
2 — Correct: the standing crop of short-lived phytoplankton is lower than that of the consumers, so the pond biomass pyramid is inverted.
3 — Incorrect: the energy pyramid is never inverted. Only the biomass pyramid shows inversion, because of rapid turnover.
The 10 per cent law is attributed to Lindeman. Pyramids of numbers and biomass can be inverted, but energy cannot.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The energy pyramid is never inverted because energy is lost at every trophic transfer. The inverted biomass pyramid of a pond is explained by short-lived but fast-reproducing phytoplankton.

detail: In Workmen of Dimakuchi Tea Estate v. Management (1958), the dispute concerned the dismissal of a medical officer, who was not a workman. The Supreme Court held that a dispute becomes an industrial dispute when it is espoused by a union or a substantial body of workmen, and the workmen must have a direct and substantial interest in the subject matter. Elimination: Bangalore Water Supply (1978) laid down the triple test for determining an 'industry'. SAIL v. National Union Waterfront Workers (2001) held that there is no automatic absorption of contract labour on abolition of the contract system, overruling Air India Statutory Corporation. Bharat Bank (1950) dealt with the scope of industrial adjudication and the meaning of an industrial dispute in the banking context, not the espousal of a non-workman's cause.
explanations: Incorrect: Bangalore Water Supply is known for the triple test defining 'industry'.
Correct: Dimakuchi Tea Estate is the authority on espousal of a non-workman's cause by a substantial body of workmen.
Incorrect: SAIL (2001) concerned absorption of contract labour and overruled Air India Statutory Corporation.
Incorrect: Bharat Bank concerned the scope of industrial adjudication, not the espousal doctrine.
keyfact: Dimakuchi Tea Estate (1958): a non-workman's dispute becomes industrial only if espoused by a substantial body of workmen with community of interest.
options: Bangalore Water Supply and Sewerage Board v. A. Rajappa
Workmen of Dimakuchi Tea Estate v. Management of Dimakuchi Tea Estate
Steel Authority of India Ltd. v. National Union Waterfront Workers
Bharat Bank Ltd. v. Employees of Bharat Bank Ltd.

detail: In Odum's model of ecosystem development, young communities have gross production exceeding respiration (P/R greater than 1), so they accumulate biomass rapidly and net production is high. As succession proceeds, biomass and structure increase and so does respiration. At the climax, P/R approaches 1 and net community production approaches zero, because most energy goes to maintenance. The climax stage therefore has the highest biomass and structural complexity, not the highest net productivity. Elimination: Statement-II is the standard succession principle, which rules out option c. Statement-I confuses high standing biomass with high net productivity, so a and b are out, leaving d.
explanations: Incorrect: Statement-I is false, so there is nothing for Statement-II to explain.
Incorrect: Statement-I is false.
Incorrect: Statement-II is correct, not incorrect.
Correct: Statement-I is wrong and Statement-II is right.
keyfact: At climax P/R is about 1, so biomass is maximum but net production is low.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Pioneer species on bare rock are typically lichens, which start primary succession (lithosere).
Hydrarch succession begins in water bodies and ends in a mesic climax.

Biomass generally increases through succession and stabilises at climax.
statements: Statement-I — Incorrect: net productivity is highest in early and mid stages, not at climax.
Statement-II — Correct: at climax, P/R approaches 1 and net community production falls close to zero.
Climax communities have the largest standing biomass and complexity but relatively low net accumulation.
subject: Environment
summary: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. In a climax community, production is roughly balanced by respiration, so net community production is low, and net productivity peaks in earlier, developing stages.

detail: DNS is a hierarchical, distributed naming system. Standard queries use UDP port 53 for speed, while TCP port 53 is used for zone transfers and for responses too large for UDP. A recursive resolver does the full lookup work for the client, contacting root, TLD and authoritative servers in turn. Record types matter: A maps to IPv4, AAAA maps to IPv6, MX identifies mail servers for a domain, CNAME gives an alias, NS names authoritative servers. Root servers do not hold all host records; they only refer resolvers to the appropriate top-level domain servers. Hence statements 3 and 4 are wrong.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are right and 3 and 4 are wrong.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3, which wrongly describes the MX record.
Incorrect: it includes statement 4, which is false, and omits statement 1.
Incorrect: it includes statements 3 and 4, both false.
keyfact: DNS: UDP/TCP port 53; MX = mail server record, AAAA = IPv6.
question:

2. A recursive resolver queries other name servers on behalf of the client until it obtains the final answer or an error.
3. An MX record maps a domain name to an IPv6 address.
4. The root name servers store the IP addresses of all hostnames on the Internet.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: A record: IPv4; AAAA record: IPv6.
PTR record is used for reverse lookup.
DNS caching is controlled by TTL.
DNSSEC adds authentication of DNS data using digital signatures.
statements: 1 — Correct: UDP 53 is for normal queries, TCP 53 for zone transfers and large responses.
2 — Correct: a recursive resolver performs the iterative lookups on the client's behalf.
3 — Incorrect: MX is the mail exchanger record; AAAA maps to IPv6.
4 — Incorrect: root servers only refer to TLD name servers, they do not store all host addresses.
subject: Computers
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. DNS uses UDP/TCP port 53 as described, and recursive resolvers chase answers on behalf of clients. MX records are for mail exchangers and root servers only point to TLD servers.

detail: Social security legislation in independent India began with the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948. It was followed by the Employees' Provident Funds Act, 1952, now titled the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, which brought in the provident fund scheme. The Maternity Benefit Act came in 1961 and the Payment of Gratuity Act in 1972. To eliminate options, start with the ESI Act, which is the earliest of the four, so option (b) is out. Then recall that gratuity is the latest, which removes (d), where C comes before B. Option (c) wrongly places the Maternity Benefit Act before the EPF Act. Only A, D, B, C survives. These laws are being absorbed into the Code on Social Security, 2020, but their enactment years remain a standard fact for the examination.
explanations: Correct: ESI Act 1948, then EPF and MP Act 1952, then Maternity Benefit Act 1961, then Payment of Gratuity Act 1972.
Wrong: it places the EPF Act before the ESI Act, but the ESI Act (1948) is earlier than the EPF Act (1952).
Wrong: it places the Maternity Benefit Act (1961) before the EPF Act (1952).

detail: The South Indian Bhakti tradition has two streams. The Alvars were Vaishnava saints whose hymns form the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Andal, the only woman among the Alvars, composed Tiruppavai and Nachchiyar Tirumozhi. The Nayanars were Shaiva saints, and the Tirumurai is the Shaiva canon. Its first seven books are the Tevaram of Sambandar, Appar (Tirunavukkarasar) and Sundarar. Manikkavacakar composed the Tiruvasagam, and Tirumular composed the Tirumantiram, which is the tenth book of the Tirumurai. Sekkizhar wrote Periya Puranam (Tiruttondar Puranam), which tells the lives of the 63 Nayanars, under the Chola king Kulottunga II. The pair most likely to mislead is Appar with Tiruvasagam, because both are Shaiva and both belong to the Tirumurai. The key is to separate the Tevaram trio from Manikkavacakar.
explanations: Incorrect: three pairs are correct, so one is too few.
Incorrect: pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct, so two is too few.
Correct: pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correct; pair 2 is wrong because Tiruvasagam is by Manikkavacakar.
Incorrect: pair 2 is mismatched, so not all four are correct.
keyfact: Tiruvasagam is by Manikkavacakar; Tevaram is by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar.

detail: PCR amplifies a target DNA sequence by repeating three steps. Denaturation at about 94-95 degrees C separates the DNA strands. Annealing at about 50-65 degrees C lets primers bind. Extension at about 72 degrees C lets the polymerase synthesise new strands. Most enzymes denature and lose function at such high temperatures. Taq polymerase, isolated from Thermus aquaticus, a bacterium found in hot springs, is thermostable. It therefore withstands dozens of cycles without being added again, which made PCR automatable in thermal cyclers. Statement-II is the direct reason for the choice described in Statement-I. Elimination: Statement-I is a well-known fact, so options (c) and (d) fail. The thermostability in Statement-II is the very property that makes Taq suitable, so it explains Statement-I and option (b) fails. Taq lacks proofreading activity, so high-fidelity applications use other thermostable polymerases.
explanations: Correct. Both statements are true, and thermostability is the reason Taq polymerase is used.
Wrong. Statement-II does explain Statement-I, because thermostability is why Taq is chosen.
Wrong. Statement-II is correct, since Taq survives repeated heating.
Wrong. Statement-I is correct, since Taq polymerase comes from Thermus aquaticus.
keyfact: Taq polymerase, from Thermus aquaticus, is heat-stable, so it survives the ~95 degree C denaturation step in PCR.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct

summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Taq polymerase comes from a thermophilic bacterium, so it survives the ~94-95 degree C denaturation step and does not need to be replenished each cycle.

summary: Only pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Deccan Education Society was founded in 1884 by Tilak, Agarkar and Chiplunkar, not by Ranade.

detail: The Mahanadi reaches the Bay of Bengal near Paradip in Odisha at about 20 degrees N. The Godavari forms a large delta near Antarvedi and Yanam in Andhra Pradesh at about 16.5 degrees N. The Krishna enters the Bay near Hamsaladeevi in Andhra Pradesh, at about 15.7 degrees N. The Penneru (Pennar) meets the sea near Nellore at about 14.5 degrees N. So the sequence is 1-3-2-4. Elimination: the Mahanadi is clearly the northernmost, which removes option (c), and the Penneru is clearly the southernmost, which removes options (c) and (d). Between (a) and (b), remember that the Godavari delta lies north of the Krishna delta, so (a) is correct.
explanations: Correct: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Penneru from north to south.
Incorrect: it places the Krishna north of the Godavari, which is wrong.
Incorrect: it places the Godavari first and the Penneru before the Krishna.
Incorrect: it places the Penneru north of the Krishna.
keyfact: East-coast river mouths north to south: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Penneru, Kaveri.
question:
Which one of the following sequences correctly arranges the following rivers from north to south in terms of the location of their river mouths (outfalls) in India?
1. Mahanadi
2. Krishna
3. Godavari
4. Penneru (Pennar)
related: Godavari is the longest peninsular river
Krishna and Godavari deltas are close to each other and the area between them is Kolleru Lake
Pulicat Lake lies near the Andhra-Tamil Nadu border
Mahanadi delta is near Cuttack
Kaveri meets the Bay of Bengal south of the Penneru
subject: Geography
summary: The correct order from north to south is Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Penneru. This is the order of their outfalls on the east coast.

detail: The Caspian Sea is the world's largest enclosed inland water body, with five littoral states: Russia to the northwest, Kazakhstan to the north and northeast, Turkmenistan to the southeast, Iran to the south and Azerbaijan to the west. Uzbekistan is in Central Asia, but it is doubly landlocked and lies east of the Caspian. Its water body is the Aral Sea, which has shrunk massively and is shared with Kazakhstan. Candidates often confuse the Aral Sea with the Caspian Sea, or assume all Central Asian republics touch the Caspian. Only Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan among them do. For elimination, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan and Iran are well known Caspian states, leaving Uzbekistan.
explanations: Correct. Uzbekistan lies east of the Caspian and has no coastline on it.
Wrong. Turkmenistan lies on the southeastern shore.
Wrong. Azerbaijan lies on the western shore, with Baku on the Absheron peninsula.
Wrong. Iran has a coast on the southern shore.
keyfact: Uzbekistan touches the Aral Sea, not the Caspian Sea.
question: Which one of the following countries does NOT have a coastline on the Caspian Sea?
related: The Caspian littoral states are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
The Aral Sea is shared by Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
The Caspian is the largest enclosed inland water body in the world.
Uzbekistan is doubly landlocked.
subject: Geography
summary: Uzbekistan has no Caspian coast. The five littoral states are Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.

detail: Article 280 provides for a Finance Commission every fifth year or earlier, as the President considers necessary. It recommends the distribution of net proceeds of Union taxes between the Union and States, the principles governing grants-in-aid under Article 275, and measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund to supplement Panchayat and Municipality resources. The last two functions were added after the 73rd and 74th Amendments (Articles 243-I and 243-Y), with reference to the State Finance Commission's recommendations. The President lays the Commission's recommendations before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum on action taken. The recommendations are only advisory. A common trap is to assume constitutional status means binding force. Elimination: since statement 2 is false, 'All three' goes out. Since statements 1 and 3 are true, 'Only one' and 'None' go out.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are correct and statement 2 is incorrect.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false because the recommendations are not binding.
Incorrect: statements 1 and 3 are correct.
keyfact: Finance Commission recommendations are advisory, not binding.
question:
With reference to the Finance Commission of India, consider the following statements:
1. The President is required to constitute a Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year or earlier.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are binding on the Union Government.
3. It is required to recommend measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities on the basis of the recommendations of the State Finance Commission.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid to States in need of assistance, on the Finance Commission's recommendation.
Article 280 provides for a Chairman and four other members.
The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body with the powers of a civil court.
Article 243-I provides for State Finance Commissions every five years.
The Planning Commission has been replaced by NITI Aayog, but the Finance Commission is a constitutional body.
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 280(1) requires constitution of the Commission at the expiration of every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary.
2 — Incorrect: the recommendations are advisory, and the Government places them before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum.
3 — Correct: Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) added this function after the 73rd and 74th Amendments.
The Commission has a Chairman and four other members. Parliament may by law decide their qualifications and selection.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, and statement 2 is wrong. Finance Commission recommendations are advisory and not binding on the Union Government.

detail: The Pabna revolt of 1873 was led by Ishan Chandra Roy and Keshab Chandra Roy against zamindari enhancement of rent, in Pabna district of eastern Bengal. The Deccan Riots of 1875 were attacks on moneylenders, with social boycott and burning of bonds, in Poona and Ahmednagar. The Kukas, or Namdharis, led by Baba Ram Singh, began as a reformist Sikh sect and turned to political resistance against the British in Punjab. The Rampa rebellion in the Godavari agency area, was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju against forest laws and the British. As every pair is accurate, option d is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: all four pairs are correct.
Incorrect: not just two pairs are accurate.
Incorrect: pair 4 is also correct.
Correct: all four pairs are properly matched.
keyfact: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa rebellion of 1922-24 in the Godavari agency area.
question:
