detail: Section 14 of the Industrial Relations Code deals with recognition of negotiating unions. If one union has the support of at least 51 per cent of workers on the muster roll, the employer recognises it as the sole negotiating union. If no union reaches 51 per cent, the employer is to constitute a negotiating council with representatives of trade unions that each have at least 20 per cent of workers as members. Seats are allotted in proportion to membership. Elimination: 10 per cent is the threshold for union registration in some cases, and it is not the negotiating-council threshold. 25 and 33 per cent are not figures used for this purpose. Only 20 per cent matches.
explanations: Correct. A union needs at least 20 per cent membership to be represented on the negotiating council.
Incorrect. 10 per cent is a registration-related figure, not the council threshold.
Incorrect. 25 per cent is not a statutory figure for this purpose.
Incorrect. 33 per cent is not a statutory figure for this purpose.
keyfact: Sole negotiating union: 51%; negotiating council: unions with at least 20%.
options: 20 per cent of the total workers on the muster roll
10 per cent of the total workers on the muster roll
25 per cent of the total workers on the muster roll
33 per cent of the total workers on the muster roll
question: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, where no trade union in an industrial establishment has the support of 51 per cent of the workers on the muster roll to be recognised as the sole negotiating union, the appropriate Government is to constitute a negotiating council. What is the minimum share of workers that a trade union must have as members in order to be represented on this council?
related: The sole negotiating union needs the support of at least 51 per cent of workers on the muster roll.
The negotiating council is constituted with unions that each have at least 20 per cent membership.
Seats on the council are proportionate to union membership.
Recognition under the Code is intended to give one body the authority to negotiate with the employer.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is 20 per cent. Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, a union with at least 51 per cent of workers is recognised as the sole negotiating union. If there is none, a negotiating council is formed with representatives of unions that have at least 20 per cent membership.

detail: Part IX, inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, provides for Panchayats. Article 243B(1) requires Panchayats at village, intermediate and district levels. Clause (2) carves out an exception, so a State whose population does not exceed twenty lakh may choose not to constitute Panchayats at the intermediate level. Several small States and Union Territories follow a two-tier model on this basis. Statement-I uses the absolute word 'every' and ignores this exception, so it is incorrect, while Statement-II quotes the constitutional text accurately. In Statement-I/II questions, test each statement independently first. Here that eliminates options a, b and c, since only option d pairs a false first statement with a true second.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-I is incorrect because of the exemption in Article 243B(2).
Wrong: Statement-I is not correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct, which reverses this option.
Correct: Statement-I ignores the exemption, and Statement-II states it accurately.
keyfact: Article 243B(2): States with population up to 20 lakh need not constitute intermediate-level Panchayats.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Every State in India must constitute Panchayats at all three tiers, irrespective of its population.
Statement-II: Article 243B of the Constitution exempts States having a population not exceeding twenty lakh from constituting Panchayats at the intermediate level.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The 73rd Amendment Act came into force on 24 April 1993.
Article 243D provides reservation for SC, ST and women, with at least one-third seats for women.
Article 243I provides for the State Finance Commission every five years.
Article 243E fixes a five-year term for Panchayats, with elections within six months of dissolution.
The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats.
subject: Polity
summary: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. Article 243B(2) lets States with population up to twenty lakh skip the intermediate tier, so a three-tier structure is not universal.

detail: Recommendation No. 202 was adopted in 2012. It asks countries to build nationally defined social protection floors with four basic guarantees. These are access to essential health care including maternity care, basic income security for children, basic income security for persons of working age unable to earn enough, and basic income security for older persons. The guarantees are minimum, universal and not tied to earnings. The 40 per cent replacement-rate benchmark comes from Convention No. 102 of 1952, which sets minimum standards of benefits, and it is earnings-related. So option (c) is the odd one out. Options (a), (b) and (d) are all among the four guarantees. Option (d) is a paraphrase of the guarantee for people of active age. The fourth guarantee, for older persons, is not listed in the options.
explanations: Incorrect as an answer: this is the first floor guarantee.
Incorrect as an answer: this is the child income security guarantee.
Correct answer: the 40% earnings-related pension benchmark belongs to Convention No. 102, not the floor guarantees.
Incorrect as an answer: this is the guarantee for persons of working age.
keyfact: R202 (2012) has four floor guarantees: health care, child income security, working-age income security and old-age income security; the 40% benchmark is from C102.
options: Access to essential health care, including maternity care
Basic income security for children, giving access to nutrition, education and care
An earnings-related old-age pension replacing at least 40 per cent of previous earnings
Basic income security for persons of working age who are unable to earn sufficient income, particularly in cases of sickness, unemployment, maternity and disability
question: The ILO Social Protection Floors Recommendation, 2012 (No. 202) calls for nationally defined social protection floors with basic social security guarantees. Which one of the following is NOT among those basic guarantees?
related: Recommendation No. 202 was adopted in 2012
Convention No. 102 was adopted in 1952 and covers nine branches of social security
Convention No. 102 requires ratification of at least three branches
The fourth floor guarantee is basic income security for older persons
Social protection floors are minimum guarantees, and higher levels are to be reached progressively
subject: Social Security
summary: Recommendation No. 202 sets out four basic guarantees across the life cycle. An earnings-related pension at 40 per cent replacement is a benchmark under Convention No. 102, not a floor guarantee.

detail: Actual price per kg = 1,09,200 / 4,200 = ₹26. Standard price is ₹25, so the firm paid ₹1 more per kg on 4,200 kg, giving ₹4,200 Adverse. Standard quantity for actual output = 1,000 x 4 = 4,000 kg, but 4,200 kg were used. Excess 200 kg x ₹25 = ₹5,000 Adverse. Total material cost variance = 1,09,200 - 1,00,000 = ₹9,200 Adverse, which equals 4,200 + 5,000. Option d gives the total variance, not the two components asked. Options b and c wrongly flip the sign of one variance. Remember: price variance uses actual quantity; usage variance uses standard price.
explanations: Correct: price ₹4,200 A and usage ₹5,000 A.
Wrong: the price variance is adverse since actual price ₹26 exceeds standard ₹25.
Wrong: the usage variance is adverse since 4,200 kg exceeds the standard 4,000 kg.
Wrong: ₹9,200 is the total material cost variance, not the price variance.
keyfact: MPV = (SP - AP) x AQ; MUV = (SQ - AQ) x SP; both adverse here.
question: A firm's standard cost card shows: standard material for 1 unit = 4 kg at ₹25 per kg. During the month, 1,000 units were produced, 4,200 kg of material were purchased and used, and the actual cost was ₹1,09,200. What are the material price variance and material usage (quantity) variance respectively?
related: Material cost variance = Price variance + Usage variance
Material usage variance = (SQ for actual output - AQ) x SP
Material price variance = (SP - AP) x AQ
Mix variance plus yield variance equals usage variance
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: Option a is correct. Price variance = (SP - AP) x AQ = (25 - 26) x 4,200 = ₹4,200 Adverse, and usage variance = (SQ - AQ) x SP = (4,000 - 4,200) x 25 = ₹5,000 Adverse.

detail: During the polar night, the Antarctic stratosphere gets very cold and a strong polar vortex isolates the air. Polar stratospheric clouds (PSCs) form, and reactions on their surfaces convert inactive chlorine reservoirs (HCl, ClONO2) into reactive chlorine (Cl2 and others). There is no sunlight in winter to split these molecules. When sunlight returns in spring, it releases chlorine atoms, which catalytically destroy ozone. That is why the ozone hole peaks in September–October. Statement-II therefore gives the direct mechanism behind Statement-I, which rules out option b. Options c and d are ruled out because each statement is factually accurate.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true, and the PSC chemistry together with returning sunlight explains the spring peak.
Incorrect: Statement-II does provide the explanation.
Incorrect: Statement-II is accurate.
Incorrect: Statement-I is accurate.
keyfact: The ozone hole peaks in spring because PSCs prepare the chlorine in winter and sunlight triggers the destruction.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Antarctic ozone hole reaches its greatest extent in the austral spring (September–October) rather than in the polar winter.
Statement-II: Polar stratospheric clouds form in the extremely cold winter stratosphere and provide surfaces on which chlorine reservoir compounds are converted into reactive forms that destroy ozone once sunlight returns.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out ozone-depleting substances.
CFCs and halons are major ozone-depleting substances.
The Dobson Unit measures total column ozone.
The polar vortex isolates Antarctic air in winter.
subject: Environment
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Ozone destruction needs both polar stratospheric clouds and sunlight.

detail: 'Stoic' derives from the Stoic school of philosophy, which taught that virtue lies in calm endurance and self-control and in indifference to pleasure and pain. Used in everyday English, a stoic is someone who accepts hardship without complaint. A hedonist pursues pleasure as the chief aim of life, which is the reverse. An epicure is a person with refined tastes in food and drink. A cynic doubts human sincerity and believes people are motivated by self-interest. Matching each word to its core idea eliminates the three distractors.
explanations: Incorrect: a hedonist seeks pleasure above all else.
Correct: a stoic stays indifferent to pleasure and pain and practises self-restraint.
Incorrect: a cynic distrusts the motives of others.
Incorrect: an epicure enjoys refined food and drink.
keyfact: Stoic = endures pain and pleasure with calm self-control.
question: Select the option that is the correct one-word substitute for: 'A person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain and practises self-restraint'
related: Ascetic means one who practises severe self-discipline, often for religious reasons.
Misanthrope means one who hates mankind.
Philanthropist means one who loves mankind and does good.
Sybarite means a person devoted to luxury.
subject: General English
summary: A stoic is someone who endures pain and hardship without showing feeling or complaint. The other options relate to pleasure-seeking or scepticism.

detail: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 restricts de-reservation of forests and use of forest land for non-forest purposes without prior Central Government approval. The 2023 amendment, which renamed it, narrowed the Act's coverage: it applies to land declared or notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927 or under the Act itself, and to land recorded as forest in government records on or after 25 October 1980. It exempts, among others, forest land up to 0.10 hectare along a road or railway providing access to habitation, strategic linear projects of national importance within 100 km of international borders or the Line of Control, and security-related infrastructure up to a specified size. The Supreme Court's Godavarman judgment of 1996 had given a dictionary meaning of forest, which the amendment curtailed. Statement 3 is wrong as the Act is not limited to land notified under the 1927 Act, because it also covers land recorded as forest in government records after the cut-off date.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect, and statement 1 is omitted.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 2023 narrowed forest coverage and added exemptions.
question:
With reference to the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 of India, as amended in 2023 and renamed the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, consider the following statements:
1. The Act requires prior approval of the Central Government for the use of forest land for non-forest purposes.
2. The amended Act exempts certain categories of land, such as linear projects of national importance within a specified distance of borders, from its provisions.
3. The Act applies only to land notified as forest under the Indian Forest Act, 1927.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The 1996 Godavarman case expanded forest to its dictionary meaning.
The 2023 amendment also allows zoos, safaris and ecotourism facilities in forest areas.
The Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognises rights of forest dwellers.
The original Act was enacted in 1980.
statements: 1 — Correct: Prior central approval is the core requirement for diversion of forest land.
2 — Correct: The 2023 amendment exempts categories such as strategic linear projects of national importance within 100 km of borders.
3 — Incorrect: Coverage extends to land recorded as forest in government records on or after 25 October 1980, not only notified forest under the 1927 Act.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Act requires central approval for diversion of forest land, and the 2023 amendment exempts certain lands such as strategic linear projects near borders. Statement 3 is incorrect because it also covers land recorded as forest in government records.

detail: The Great Famine of 1876-78 occurred under Viceroy Lytton and killed millions in south and south-western India. The Famine Commission of 1880, headed by Richard Strachey, was the first all-India commission on the subject. It recommended a Famine Insurance Fund, public works for relief and provincial famine codes. Later commissions reviewed policy after further famines. The Campbell Commission (1866) followed the Orissa famine of 1866 and was earlier. The Lyall Commission (1898) followed the famines of 1896-97, and the MacDonnell Commission (1901) followed the famine of 1899-1900. Elimination: tie each commission to its famine. The Campbell body predates 1876, and the Lyall and MacDonnell bodies came after the 1890s, so only Strachey fits the 1876-78 famine.
explanations: Wrong: the Campbell Commission of 1866 followed the Orissa famine and came before the Great Famine of 1876-78.
Wrong: the Lyall Commission of 1898 followed the famines of 1896-97.
Wrong: the MacDonnell Commission of 1901 followed the famine of 1899-1900.
Correct: the Strachey Commission of 1880 followed the Great Famine and recommended the Famine Insurance Fund and Famine Codes.
keyfact: Strachey Commission (1880) followed the Great Famine of 1876-78 and recommended the Famine Insurance Fund and Famine Codes.
question: Which one of the following bodies recommended that provincial governments maintain a Famine Insurance Fund and drew up the first Famine Code, after the Great Famine of 1876-78?
related: The Orissa famine took place in 1866.
Lytton was Viceroy during the Great Famine of 1876-78.
The Delhi Durbar of 1877 was held during the famine.
The Famine Codes set out relief works and test-work principles.
subject: Modern History
summary: The Famine Commission of 1880 under Richard Strachey is the answer. It laid down the principles of the Famine Codes and the Famine Insurance Fund.

detail: The Economic Survey 2016-17 highlighted the Twin Balance Sheet (TBS) problem. Many infrastructure and industrial firms were over-leveraged, with weak interest coverage, and could not repay loans. Banks, especially public sector banks, accumulated high NPAs, which constrained fresh lending and depressed private investment. The policy response included the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code 2016, the Asset Quality Review of 2015, recapitalisation of PSBs, and bank mergers. Elimination: the problem is not about the Centre and States, which concerns fiscal federalism and debt. It is also not about the RBI's balance sheet or about trade accounts. Only the corporate-bank link matches.
explanations: Incorrect: Centre and State finances relate to fiscal deficit and debt, not the Twin Balance Sheet problem.
Correct: it refers to stressed corporate balance sheets and NPA-ridden bank balance sheets.
Incorrect: the RBI's balance sheet is not the subject of this concept.
Incorrect: exporters and importers relate to trade, not the TBS problem.
keyfact: Twin Balance Sheet problem means over-leveraged corporates plus NPA-laden banks (Economic Survey 2016-17).
options: The Central Government and State Governments
Over-leveraged corporates and Non-Performing Asset-laden public sector banks
question: In the context of the Indian economy, the term 'Twin Balance Sheet problem' refers to the simultaneous stress on the balance sheets of:
related: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code was enacted in 2016.
The Asset Quality Review was initiated by the RBI in 2015.
The Indradhanush plan of 2015 was for PSB reform.
The Economic Survey is presented by the Chief Economic Adviser's office in the Department of Economic Affairs.
subject: Indian Economy
summary: The Twin Balance Sheet problem describes stressed balance sheets of over-indebted corporates and of banks, mainly public sector banks, burdened with NPAs. It was popularised by the Economic Survey 2016-17.

detail: Article 243D(2) reserves not less than one-third of the total seats for women, including the seats reserved for SC and ST women, in direct elections to Panchayats. Article 243D(3) similarly reserves not less than one-third of chairperson offices for women. Article 243D(4) governs reservation of chairperson offices for SCs, STs and women. The reservation is a minimum, and many States have raised it to 50 percent. Statement-II gives the constitutional mechanism by which the one-third requirement in Statement-I operates, so it explains Statement-I.
explanations: Correct: both are accurate, and Article 243D(2) is the operative provision behind the one-third requirement.
Wrong: Statement-II is the explanation for Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is also correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is also correct.
keyfact: Article 243D: at least one-third of seats and chairperson posts in Panchayats are reserved for women.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992 requires the reservation of seats for women in Panchayats of not less than one-third of the total seats.
Statement-II: Article 243D provides that reservation for women applies to seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as well as to the seats filled by direct election generally.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Article 243D covers Panchayat reservations.
Article 243T covers Municipality reservations.
Many States provide 50 percent reservation for women in Panchayats.
Article 243K covers State Election Commissions.
subject: Polity
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Article 243D mandates not less than one-third of seats, including within SC/ST quotas, for women.

detail: The first six and last six observations together cover all 11 observations, with the sixth observation counted twice. Sum of first six = 6 × 49 = 294. Sum of last six = 6 × 52 = 312. Adding these gives 606. The total of all 11 observations = 11 × 50 = 550. The extra amount in 606 over 550 is exactly the sixth observation: 606 − 550 = 56. Elimination: the options differ only slightly, so you must compute exactly. Candidates who subtract incorrectly or treat the groups as disjoint (6 + 6 = 12 observations) get wrong values such as 55 or 58. Checking: 56 fits, as the remaining five of the first group sum to 238 and the remaining five of the last group sum to 256, so the total is 238 + 256 + 56 = 550.
explanations: Incorrect: 54 would give a combined total of 604 − 550 = 54 only if the group sums were different from those given.
Incorrect: 55 does not satisfy 606 − 550.
Incorrect: 58 does not satisfy 606 − 550.
keyfact: Overlapping group sums minus the total sum gives the common observation.
question: The average of 11 observations is 50. The average of the first six observations is 49 and the average of the last six observations is 52. What is the value of the sixth observation?
related: Sum = average × number of observations.
In overlapping-group problems, the common item equals (sum of groups) − (total sum).
Adding a constant k to every observation raises the average by k.
Weighted average = Σ(n × average)/Σn.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: The sixth observation is 56. The sixth is counted in both groups, so (6 × 49 + 6 × 52) − (11 × 50) = 606 − 550 = 56.

detail: mRNA vaccines, such as the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 vaccines, carry synthetic mRNA coding for an antigen, often wrapped in lipid nanoparticles. After injection, cells translate the mRNA into the protein, which triggers antibody and T-cell responses. The mRNA does not enter the cell nucleus and does not integrate into the host DNA, and it degrades quickly. Option a describes live attenuated vaccines, option c describes passive immunisation with antisera or monoclonal antibodies, and option d wrongly claims permanent chromosomal integration. India's first indigenous mRNA vaccine effort, by Gennova, was for COVID-19.
explanations: Wrong: that describes live attenuated vaccines.
Correct: mRNA instructs host cells to make the antigen.
Wrong: that describes passive immunisation.
Wrong: mRNA does not integrate into host chromosomes.
keyfact: mRNA vaccines make host cells produce the antigen; the mRNA does not enter the nucleus or alter DNA.
options: It introduces a weakened live pathogen into the body to trigger immunity
It delivers genetic instructions that make body cells produce an antigenic protein, which then stimulates an immune response
It injects purified antibodies produced in animals to provide immediate passive immunity
It integrates the pathogen's gene into the host's chromosomes permanently using a viral vector
question: Which one of the following best describes 'mRNA vaccine technology', which has been in the news in the context of public health?
related: Lipid nanoparticles protect mRNA and help it enter cells.
Live attenuated examples: MMR, oral polio vaccine.
Viral vector vaccines include Covishield.
Nobel Prize 2023 in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for nucleoside-modified mRNA vaccine research.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Option b is correct. An mRNA vaccine delivers messenger RNA, usually in lipid nanoparticles, so that host cells make an antigen such as the spike protein and the immune system learns to respond to it.

detail: Article 368 provides three methods of amendment: simple majority (outside Article 368), special majority, and special majority plus ratification by at least half of the State legislatures. The third category covers the federal features. These include the election of the President (Articles 54 and 55), the extent of Union and State executive power, the Supreme Court and High Courts, the distribution of legislative powers and the Seventh Schedule lists, representation of States in Parliament, and Article 368 itself. Abolishing or creating a Legislative Council under Article 169 is done by Parliament by simple majority after the State Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority, and is expressly not an Article 368 amendment. Fundamental Rights in Part III need only a special majority, subject to the basic structure doctrine. Eliminate by testing each item against the federal list: two qualify.
explanations: Incorrect: Two items, not one, need ratification.
Correct: Items 1 and 2 are federal provisions needing State ratification. Items 3 and 4 do not.
Incorrect: Neither Article 169 nor Part III needs ratification, so the count cannot reach three.
Incorrect: Items 3 and 4 do not require State ratification.
keyfact: State ratification is required only for federal features, such as President's election, Seventh Schedule, representation in Parliament and the judiciary.
question:
With reference to the amendment of the Constitution of India under Article 368, consider the following provisions:
1. The manner of election of the President of India
2. The distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the States through the Seventh Schedule lists
3. The abolition of a Legislative Council in a State under Article 169
4. The amendment of Fundamental Rights contained in Part III
How many of the above provisions can be amended only by a special majority of Parliament followed by ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the States?
related: Ratification by States has no prescribed time limit, and no specific procedure for it is laid down.
Creation of new States under Articles 3 and 4 is not an Article 368 amendment.
The Fifth and Sixth Schedules can be amended by simple majority under Paragraph 7 and Paragraph 21 respectively.
The 24th Amendment (1971) made it obligatory for the President to give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill.
statements: 1 — Correct: Election of the President is in the proviso to Article 368(2) and needs State ratification.
2 — Correct: Seventh Schedule lists and legislative distribution of powers are covered by the proviso, so ratification is needed.
3 — Incorrect: Article 169 is by a simple-majority law of Parliament and is not deemed an Article 368 amendment.
4 — Incorrect: Part III is amended by special majority only, without State ratification. Ratification is for federal provisions.
subject: Polity
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 require ratification by half of the State legislatures. Federal provisions need State ratification. Article 169 is outside Article 368, and Part III needs only a special majority.

detail: Under paragraph 6 of the Fifth Schedule, the President may by order declare an area to be a Scheduled Area, after consultation with the Governor of the State concerned. The President can also alter or rescind such areas. Under paragraph 4, a Tribes Advisory Council must be set up in each State having Scheduled Areas. The President may direct that one be set up in a State that has Scheduled Tribes but no Scheduled Areas. Statement 3 is wrong because Parliament has no role in declaring these areas. Elimination: statement 3 is the weak link, and removing it leaves option (c).
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statement 3 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule are declared by Presidential order after consulting the Governor, not by Parliament.
question:
With reference to the administration of Scheduled and Tribal Areas under the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. The Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule are declared by the President by an order, after consulting the Governor of the State concerned.
2. A Tribes Advisory Council must be established in each State having Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule.
3. The Scheduled Areas under the Fifth Schedule can be declared only by Parliament by making a law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Sixth Schedule applies to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
Article 244(1) covers the Fifth Schedule and Article 244(2) covers the Sixth Schedule.
The Tribes Advisory Council has up to 20 members, three-fourths of whom are ST representatives in the Legislative Assembly.
Autonomous District Councils exist under the Sixth Schedule.
statements: 1 — Correct: paragraph 6 of the Fifth Schedule gives the President the power by order, after consulting the Governor.
2 — Correct: paragraph 4 requires a Tribes Advisory Council in every State with Scheduled Areas.
3 — Incorrect: Scheduled Areas are declared by Presidential order, not by a law of Parliament. The Governor also has the power to direct that particular laws not apply to Scheduled Areas.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Scheduled Areas are declared by the President by order, not by Parliament by law. Each State with Scheduled Areas must have a Tribes Advisory Council.

detail: The Communal Award (August 1932) of Ramsay MacDonald gave separate electorates to the Depressed Classes. Gandhi, imprisoned in Yerwada Jail, began a fast unto death in protest. The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 by Ambedkar and Gandhi's representatives, with Malaviya, among others, facilitating the talks. It gave up separate electorates in favour of reserved seats in a joint electorate, and increased the reserved seats in provincial legislatures from 71 to 148. It also provided for a primary election system (a panel of four candidates) and reserved seats in the central legislature. Elimination logic: statement 3 is the trap, because the number of seats went up, not down. Since 3 is wrong, options c and d fall, and the choice is between a and b. Statement 1 is accurate, so a is correct.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate and statement 3 is wrong.
Incorrect: statement 1 is also correct, so 2 alone is incomplete.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong, as seats were increased, not reduced.
Incorrect: statement 3 is wrong, so all three cannot be correct.
keyfact: Poona Pact (24 Sept 1932): separate electorates dropped; reserved seats raised from 71 to 148.
question:
With reference to the Poona Pact of 1932, consider the following statements:
1. It was signed between Dr B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi, with Madan Mohan Malaviya among the prominent leaders who facilitated the agreement.
2. It replaced the separate electorates for the Depressed Classes announced in the Communal Award with reserved seats within the general electorate.
3. It reduced the number of seats reserved for the Depressed Classes in the provincial legislatures compared with the Communal Award.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Communal Award was announced on 16 August 1932 by British PM Ramsay MacDonald.
Gandhi began his fast in Yerwada Jail on 20 September 1932.
Gandhi later founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932.
The weekly Harijan was started by Gandhi in 1933.
statements: 1 — Correct: The pact was concluded in Poona (Yerwada Jail) in September 1932 between Ambedkar and Gandhi's side, with Malaviya among the key mediators.
2 — Correct: Separate electorates were abandoned in favour of reserved seats within the general electorate.

3 — Incorrect: Reserved seats rose from 71 to 148 in the provincial legislatures, and 18 percent of central seats were reserved for the Depressed Classes. The pact also introduced a primary election procedure.
subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is incorrect. The Poona Pact gave the Depressed Classes more reserved seats (148 in provincial legislatures) than the 71 under the Communal Award, while ending separate electorates.

detail: The shares have a face value of ₹10 and ₹3 per share was unpaid, so ₹7 per share was paid on share capital. The premium of ₹1 was received and is not reversed on forfeiture unless it was still unpaid. Forfeited amount = 100 x 7 = ₹700, credited to Share Forfeiture Account. On re-issue at ₹8 as fully paid-up, the discount allowed is ₹2 per share = ₹200. This is debited to Share Forfeiture Account. Balance = 700 - 200 = ₹500, which is transferred to Capital Reserve. It is a capital profit. Option (c) forgets the discount on re-issue. Option (a) is only the discount. Option (d) wrongly adds the premium.
explanations: ₹200 is the discount on re-issue, not the balance transferred to Capital Reserve.
Correct: 700 forfeited less 200 discount on re-issue.
₹700 is the forfeited amount before adjusting the discount on re-issue.
₹800 wrongly adds the premium to the forfeited amount.
keyfact: Capital Reserve on re-issue = Forfeited amount - Discount allowed on re-issue (for the same shares).
question: A company issued shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹1 per share. A shareholder holding 100 shares failed to pay the final call of ₹3 per share, and the premium had been fully received. The company forfeited the 100 shares and later re-issued all of them as fully paid-up at ₹8 per share. The amount transferred to Capital Reserve on re-issue will be:
related: Forfeited shares are credited to Share Forfeiture Account at the amount actually paid
Maximum discount on re-issue cannot exceed the forfeited amount on those shares
Gain on re-issue after forfeiture goes to Capital Reserve
Securities premium already received is not reversed on forfeiture
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The answer is ₹500. The forfeited amount is ₹700 (₹7 per share paid on share capital). The loss on re-issue is ₹200, so ₹500 goes to Capital Reserve.
topic: Company accounts - Forfeiture and re-issue of shares

detail: Bhashini, the National Language Translation Mission, is an initiative of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), implemented through the Digital India Bhashini Division. It builds AI and natural language processing models for translation, speech-to-text, text-to-speech and related tasks, and offers them through open application programming interfaces and a mobile app. The aim is to let people use the internet and government services in their own languages. It is a crowdsourcing platform too, as citizens contribute data through its Bhasha Daan initiative. Option a describes something unrelated, such as the digitisation of land records under DILRMP. Option c is ONDC, the Open Network for Digital Commerce, which is a DPIIT initiative. Option d does not exist as described, and the e-rupee is a central bank digital currency run by the RBI. Elimination logic: the word language in the name points directly to option b.
explanations: Incorrect: this is not Bhashini. Land record digitisation falls under programmes such as DILRMP.
Correct: Bhashini is an AI-based language translation and speech platform under MeitY.
Incorrect: this describes ONDC, the Open Network for Digital Commerce.
Incorrect: the digital rupee is an RBI central bank digital currency and has no connection with Bhashini.
keyfact: Bhashini is MeitY's AI-based national language translation platform for Indian languages.
options: A blockchain-based platform for digitising land records across States
An AI-enabled national language technology platform that provides translation and speech services to enable access to digital services in Indian languages
A government-backed open network protocol that connects buyers and sellers across e-commerce platforms
A consortium of public sector banks to run a common digital currency platform
question: Which one of the following best describes 'Bhashini', sometimes mentioned in the news?
related: Bhashini is run through the Digital India Bhashini Division under MeitY.
Bhasha Daan is the crowdsourcing component for language datasets.
ONDC is an open e-commerce network under DPIIT.
The e-rupee is the RBI's central bank digital currency.
BharatGen is a government-backed initiative on indigenous multimodal AI models.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Bhashini is an AI-driven language translation platform for Indian languages. It is a National Language Translation Mission initiative under MeitY, intended to widen access to digital services.

detail: Parliament passed the new Income-tax Act in August 2025 and it received assent on 21 August 2025. It is a rewrite of the six-decade-old 1961 Act, aimed at simplifying language, shortening the text and reducing litigation. It takes effect from 1 April 2026. A key structural reform is that the dual terms 'previous year' and 'assessment year' are replaced by a single concept of 'tax year', which removes a perennial source of confusion. Elimination: statement 3 contradicts the central reform, so options (c) and (d) fall away. Statements 1 and 2 hold together, which leaves (a) rather than (b).
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate and statement 3 is not.
Incomplete: statement 2 is also correct.
Wrong: includes statement 3, which is false.
Wrong: statement 3 is false.
keyfact: Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026 and introduces a single 'tax year'.
question:

summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. It does away with the 'previous year' and 'assessment year' distinction in favour of a single 'tax year', so statement 3 is wrong.

detail: Introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793 in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha, the Permanent Settlement recognised zamindars as proprietors of land who paid a fixed revenue to the Company. The aim was to secure regular revenue and create a loyal class of landlords with an incentive to invest in agriculture. The demand was fixed in perpetuity, which is the content of Statement-II. This directly causes the consequence in Statement-I, since the Company could not revise its demand upward even as cultivation expanded and prices rose. The surplus went to the zamindars and, through subinfeudation, to intermediaries. Defaulting zamindars lost their estates through the Sunset Law, under which the estate was auctioned if payment was not made by sunset on the due date. In such questions, test whether the second statement is the cause of the first. Here it is.
explanations: Correct: Both statements are true, and the perpetual fixing of the demand (II) is exactly why the Company could not share later gains (I).
Incorrect: Statement-II does explain Statement-I, as the fixed demand caused the Company's loss of future gains.
Incorrect: Statement-II is accurate, as the demand was fixed in perpetuity.
Incorrect: Statement-I is accurate, as the Company gained stable revenue but no share in later increases.
keyfact: Permanent Settlement (1793): zamindars as owners, revenue fixed forever, Sunset Law for default.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Permanent Settlement introduced in Bengal in 1793 gave the Company predictable land revenue but denied it any share in the later rise in agricultural income.
Statement-II: Under the Permanent Settlement the land revenue demand was fixed in perpetuity at the level assessed in 1793.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The Permanent Settlement was introduced by Cornwallis in 1793.
The Ryotwari system was associated with Thomas Munro in Madras and extended to Bombay.
The Mahalwari system in the North-Western Provinces was introduced under Regulation IX of 1833.
The Sunset Law led to the auction of zamindaris for arrears.
subject: Modern History
summary: The answer is (a). The Permanent Settlement fixed the revenue demand in perpetuity, so the Company got steady income. Because the demand never changed, later increases in cultivation and prices benefited zamindars and not the Company.

detail: The Insurance Ombudsman is a low-cost, informal grievance-redressal mechanism under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017. The complainant must first write to the insurer. Approaching the Ombudsman is permitted only if the insurer rejects the complaint, does not reply within 30 days, or the reply is unsatisfactory. The complaint must be filed within one year of the insurer's reply or rejection. The Ombudsman's award limit is Rs 30 lakh per claim, covering the claim amount and any compensation. Mediation by the Ombudsman is attempted first, and an award is made if mediation fails. The complaint must not be pending, or already decided, in any court, consumer forum or arbitration. This last condition makes statement 3 wrong.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct, so this is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are right, and statement 3 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect, and statement 1 is correct but left out.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: Insurance Ombudsman: award limit Rs 30 lakh; first approach the insurer; no parallel court or consumer forum case.
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Insurance Ombudsman under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017:
1. A complaint may be made to the Ombudsman only after the complainant has first approached the insurer and the insurer has rejected the complaint or not replied within 30 days.
2. The Ombudsman can deal with claims where the amount of claim, including any compensation, does not exceed Rs 30 lakh.
3. A complaint can be entertained even where the same subject matter is pending before a court or consumer forum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The complaint must be filed within one year of the insurer's reply or rejection.
Ombudsman offices are located in several cities across India.
The insured must accept the award for it to become binding on the insurer.
The insurer must comply with an accepted award within 30 days.
statements: 1 — Correct: the insurer must be approached first, and the Ombudsman can be approached if the insurer rejects the complaint or does not reply within 30 days.
2 — Correct: the Ombudsman's monetary limit is Rs 30 lakh.
3 — Incorrect: parallel proceedings before a court, consumer forum or arbitrator bar the Ombudsman from entertaining the complaint.

detail:
The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 carries forward the Trade Unions Act, 1926 rule that at least seven members must apply to register a union. It adds a representativeness test for a union of workers: the applicants must be at least 10% of the workers employed in the establishment, or 100 workers, whichever is less. The result cannot fall below seven.

For 60 workers, 10% is 6 and 100 is larger. The lower figure is 6, but the minimum of seven overrides it. The applicants therefore must number 7.

Elimination: 6 ignores the statutory floor. 10 mistakes the percentage for a fixed number. 60 confuses the number of workers with the number of applicants.
explanations: Incorrect. 10% of 60 is 6, but the Code sets a floor of seven applicants.
Correct. The lower of 10% (6) and 100 is 6, which is raised to the statutory minimum of seven.
Incorrect. Ten is not the threshold in this case. The Code uses 10% as a proportion, not as a fixed count.
Incorrect. Registration does not need all workers. It needs only the prescribed proportion, subject to a minimum of seven.
keyfact: Union registration under the IR Code needs 10% of workers or 100 workers, whichever is less, and never fewer than seven.
question: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, a trade union is to be formed in an industrial establishment that employs 60 workers. The Code requires an application for registration to be made by at least 10% of the workers or 100 workers, whichever is less, subject to a minimum number of persons. What is the minimum number of members who must apply for registration of this union?
related: A union registered under the Code is a body corporate with perpetual succession.
The Code allows the appropriate Government to recognise a union as a sole negotiating union or form a negotiating council.
The Code requires the Registrar to be appointed by the appropriate Government.
The Trade Unions Act, 1926 is subsumed in the Industrial Relations Code, 2020.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The answer is 7. The Code requires 10% of workers or 100 workers, whichever is less, but never fewer than seven members. For 60 workers, 10% is 6, which is below the floor, so seven applicants are needed.

detail: Quick Sort partitions around a pivot. If the pivot is always an extreme element, as with already sorted input and a naive pivot choice, the partitions are very unbalanced and the cost is O(n^2). Merge Sort always splits evenly, so its worst case is O(n log n), and the standard array merge uses an auxiliary array of size n. Binary search halves the search interval each step, so it takes O(log n) comparisons. Heap Sort runs in O(n log n) and sorts in place, but it is not stable, because the heap operations can reorder equal elements. Stable algorithms include Merge Sort, Insertion Sort, Bubble Sort and Counting Sort. So only statement 3 is incorrect, and option (a) is right.
explanations: Correct: statements 1, 2 and 4 are true and statement 3 is false.
Incorrect: it omits statement 4, which is true.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3, which is false, and omits statement 1.
Incorrect: it includes the false statement 3 and omits statement 2.
keyfact: Heap Sort is O(n log n) and in-place but not stable; Merge Sort is stable with O(n) extra space.
question:
Consider the following statements about sorting and searching algorithms:
1. The worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort is O(n^2), which occurs when the chosen pivot is always the smallest or largest element.
2. Merge Sort has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and, in its usual array implementation, needs O(n) extra space.
3. Heap Sort is a stable sorting algorithm.
4. Binary search on a sorted array has a worst-case time complexity of O(log n).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Quick Sort's average case is O(n log n).
Merge Sort is stable; Quick Sort and Heap Sort are typically not stable.
Insertion Sort's best case is O(n).
Binary search requires the data to be sorted.
statements: 1 — Correct: Quick Sort degrades to O(n^2) when pivots give maximally unbalanced partitions.
2 — Correct: Merge Sort is O(n log n) in every case and uses O(n) auxiliary space for arrays.
3 — Incorrect: Heap Sort is in-place but not stable.
4 — Correct: binary search needs at most about log2(n) + 1 comparisons.
Facts: Quick Sort's average case is O(n log n). Insertion Sort's best case is O(n) on sorted input. Stable sorts keep the relative order of equal keys.
subject: Computers
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because Heap Sort is not stable.

detail: The J-curve describes how a currency depreciation can first widen the trade deficit and only later narrow it, so the trade balance plotted over time resembles the letter J. Immediately after depreciation, contracts signed earlier remain in force, so import volumes and export volumes barely change. Imports, however, now cost more in domestic currency, so the import bill rises and the deficit widens. Over time, exports become cheaper abroad and imports become dearer at home, so volumes adjust and the balance improves, provided the Marshall-Lerner condition holds (the sum of the price elasticities of export and import demand exceeds one). Elimination logic: Statement-II gives the exact mechanism behind Statement-I, so option b is ruled out. Both statements are accurate, so c and d are ruled out too.
explanations: Correct: Both statements are true, and slow volume adjustment plus higher import costs explains the initial worsening.
Incorrect: Statement-II directly explains Statement-I, so it is not unrelated.
Incorrect: Statement-II is accurate, not incorrect.
Incorrect: Statement-I is accurate, as the J-curve shows.
keyfact: J-curve: after depreciation the trade balance first worsens because volumes adjust slowly, then improves if the Marshall-Lerner condition holds.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: Following a sharp depreciation of a country's currency, its trade balance may worsen in the short run before improving later.
Statement-II: In the short run, export and import volumes respond slowly to relative price changes, while the domestic-currency cost of existing import contracts rises immediately.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The J-curve shows the trade balance first worsening and then improving after depreciation.
The Marshall-Lerner condition requires the sum of export and import demand elasticities to exceed 1.
Depreciation makes exports cheaper and imports costlier.
Depreciation can raise imported inflation, especially for oil and electronics.
Devaluation refers to a deliberate cut in the official rate under a fixed regime, and depreciation to a market-driven fall.
subject: Economy
summary: Both statements are correct, and Statement-II explains Statement-I. This is the J-curve effect: volumes adjust slowly, so the higher domestic cost of imports dominates at first.
topic: Exchange rate and trade balance: J-curve

detail: Purandara Dasa (15th-16th century, Karnataka) systematised the teaching of Carnatic music through graded exercises such as sarali varisai, and his songs are signed 'Purandara Vittala'. Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri, all born in Tiruvarur, form the 'Trinity' of Carnatic music. Syama Sastri's mudra is 'Syama Krishna'. Dikshitar's mudra is 'Guruguha', and he composed mostly in Sanskrit. Tyagaraja composed chiefly in Telugu and signed his songs with his own name. The trap is statement 3, which attributes Dikshitar's language to Tyagaraja. Rejecting statement 3 removes options (c) and (d). Statement 1 is well established, so the answer is (b).
explanations: Incomplete. Statement 2 is also correct.
Correct. Statements 1 and 2 are accurate, and statement 3 fails because Tyagaraja wrote mainly in Telugu.
Wrong. It includes statement 3, which is false, and omits statement 1.
Wrong. Statement 3 is incorrect, so not all three hold.
keyfact: Tyagaraja wrote mainly in Telugu, Dikshitar in Sanskrit (mudra Guruguha), and Syama Sastri signed 'Syama Krishna'.
question:
With reference to the Carnatic music tradition, consider the following statements:

2 — Correct: Syama Sastri's mudra is 'Syama Krishna'.
3 — Incorrect: Tyagaraja composed mainly in Telugu; Dikshitar composed mostly in Sanskrit.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: The answer is 1 and 2 only. Purandara Dasa is honoured as the Pitamaha of Carnatic music, and Syama Sastri signed his works 'Syama Krishna'. Tyagaraja composed mainly in Telugu, not Sanskrit.

detail: Dhrupad is the oldest surviving major form of Hindustani vocal music. It is austere and meditative, with a long alap and a pakhawaj accompaniment. The tabla is associated with the lighter, later forms such as Khayal, thumri and tappa. Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior (late 15th to early 16th century) is widely credited with patronising Dhrupad and giving it a distinct school. Khayal existed earlier, but it rose to courtly eminence in the early 18th century under Muhammad Shah, with Sadarang and Adarang credited with its compositions. To eliminate options, spot the pakhawaj-versus-tabla error in statement 1. That removes 'All three', and the two correct statements settle the answer as 'Only two'.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is correct and statement 3 is also correct, so one correct statement undercounts.
Correct: statements 2 and 3 are correct and statement 1 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 1 is incorrect because Dhrupad uses the pakhawaj.
Wrong: statements 2 and 3 are historically established.
keyfact: Dhrupad goes with the pakhawaj; Khayal rose to court prominence under Muhammad Shah's reign.
question:
With reference to Hindustani classical music, consider the following statements:
1. Dhrupad is traditionally accompanied by the tabla as its principal percussion instrument.
2. Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior is credited with patronising and consolidating the Dhrupad tradition in the 15th-16th centuries.
3. The Khayal form gained great prominence in the Mughal court of Muhammad Shah 'Rangila' through the compositions attributed to Niyamat Khan 'Sadarang'.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Dhrupad's typical percussion is the pakhawaj.
Tansen was a court musician of Akbar and is linked with Dhrupad.
Sadarang and Adarang are associated with Khayal in Muhammad Shah's court.
The Gwalior gharana is regarded as one of the oldest Khayal gharanas.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: Dhrupad is accompanied by the pakhawaj, not the tabla. The tabla suits Khayal and lighter forms.
2 — Correct: Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior is credited with patronising Dhrupad and fostering its Gwalior tradition.
3 — Correct: Sadarang, a court musician of Muhammad Shah, is credited with popularising Khayal compositions in the Mughal court.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: Only statements 2 and 3 are correct. Dhrupad uses the pakhawaj, not the tabla, as its percussion.

detail: Wood's Despatch (1854), often called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India', was issued by Charles Wood, President of the Board of Control. It set out a comprehensive plan. A Department of Public Instruction was to be set up in each province. Universities were to be created at the three Presidency towns, and they were established in 1857. Grants-in-aid were to support private and missionary schools, and teacher training and female education were encouraged. Its language policy was graded, not exclusive. Vernacular languages were to be used at the primary stage, Anglo-vernacular in high schools, and English at the college level. The key to elimination is Statement 2, which uses the absolute word 'sole'. UPSC often plants such absolutes in statements that are otherwise broadly true. Rejecting Statement 2 leaves only option (b).
explanations: Incorrect: Statement 3 is also correct, so 'Statement 1 only' is incomplete.
Correct: Statements 1 and 3 are true. Statement 2 is false because the Despatch favoured a graded medium of instruction.
Incorrect: This includes Statement 2, which is false, and leaves out Statement 1, which is true.
Incorrect: Statement 2 is wrong, since English was not prescribed as the sole medium at every level.
keyfact: Wood's Despatch (1854): graded medium of instruction, grants-in-aid, Presidency universities (1857), Department of Public Instruction.
question:
With reference to Wood's Despatch of 1854 on education in India, consider the following statements:
1. It recommended the establishment of universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras on the model of the University of London.
2. It recommended English as the sole medium of instruction at all levels, from primary schools to universities.
3. It introduced the system of grants-in-aid to encourage private effort in education.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Wood's Despatch is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'.
The Universities of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras were founded in 1857.
The Hunter Commission (1882) reviewed education with emphasis on primary and secondary education.
The Indian Universities Act, 1904 was passed under Curzon after the Raleigh Commission.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Despatch advised universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras on the London University model. They were founded in 1857.
2 — Incorrect: The Despatch did not insist on English alone. It gave a graded scheme of vernacular, Anglo-vernacular and English instruction by level.
3 — Correct: The grants-in-aid system, which gave financial support to private and missionary schools, was introduced by the Despatch. It also linked grants to standards of inspection and teaching.
subject: Modern History
summary: The answer is (b). Wood's Despatch recommended universities on the London model and grants-in-aid, but it did not make English the sole medium. It favoured vernacular at the primary level, Anglo-vernacular in middle and high schools, and English for higher education.
topic: Education policy under the Company: Wood's Despatch

detail: When two trains cross each other completely, the distance covered is the sum of their lengths, here 150 + 100 = 250 m. Same direction: the relative speed is the difference, so v1 - v2 = 250/25 = 10 m/s. Opposite directions: the relative speed is the sum, so v1 + v2 = 250/5 = 50 m/s. Solving gives v1 = 30 m/s and v2 = 20 m/s. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5, so the slower train is 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h and the faster is 108 km/h. Elimination: 108 km/h is the faster train, a common trap when the question asks for the slower one. 54 km/h and 90 km/h do not satisfy both conditions. For example, 90 km/h = 25 m/s would require the faster train to be 35 m/s, a difference of 10 m/s but a sum of 60 m/s, which does not match the 50 m/s sum.
explanations: 54 km/h = 15 m/s would need the faster train at 25 m/s (to make the difference 10), but then the sum would be 40 m/s, not 50 m/s. Incorrect.
Correct. The speeds are 20 m/s (72 km/h) and 30 m/s (108 km/h), which satisfy both the difference of 10 m/s and the sum of 50 m/s.
90 km/h = 25 m/s would need the faster train at 35 m/s, giving a sum of 60 m/s, not 50 m/s. Incorrect.
108 km/h is the speed of the faster train, not the slower one. Incorrect.
keyfact: Trains crossing each other cover the sum of their lengths at the relative speed (sum of speeds if opposite, difference if same direction).
question: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 100 m run on parallel tracks. When they move in the same direction, the faster train takes 25 seconds to completely cross the slower one. When they move in opposite directions, they take 5 seconds to completely cross each other. What is the speed of the slower train?
related: Conversion: 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h; 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s.
Crossing a pole or a person: the distance equals the train's own length.
Crossing a platform: the distance equals train length plus platform length.
Relative speed is the sum for opposite directions and the difference for the same direction.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: The slower train runs at 72 km/h. The combined length is 250 m, so the relative speed is 10 m/s in the same direction and 50 m/s in opposite directions, which gives speeds of 30 m/s and 20 m/s.

detail: Reinsurance lets an insurer spread large or accumulated risks. It is a contract between the ceding insurer and the reinsurer, separate from the original policy. The insured is generally not a party and has no privity with the reinsurer, so he must claim from the original insurer, who in turn recovers from the reinsurer. In a quota share treaty, the reinsurer receives a fixed proportion of premiums and bears the same proportion of losses on every risk ceded. In contrast, an excess of loss treaty covers losses above a set retention. Hence statements 1 and 3 are correct, and only option c matches.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong, so any option including it fails.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are accurate.
Incorrect: statement 2 is wrong.
keyfact: Reinsurance is a separate contract between insurer and reinsurer, and the insured has no direct claim against the reinsurer.
question:
Consider the following statements regarding reinsurance:
1. Reinsurance is a contract by which an insurer transfers part of the risk it has accepted to another insurer.
2. The original insured has a direct contractual claim against the reinsurer under an ordinary reinsurance arrangement.
3. Under a quota share treaty, the reinsurer takes a fixed percentage of every risk within the treaty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: The ceding company is the original insurer
Excess of loss is a non-proportional treaty
Facultative reinsurance is arranged risk by risk
Treaty reinsurance covers a defined class of business automatically
statements: 1 — Correct: reinsurance is the transfer of part of the accepted risk to another insurer.
2 — Incorrect: there is no privity of contract between the insured and the reinsurer, so the insured cannot claim directly.
3 — Correct: a quota share reinsurer takes a fixed percentage of every ceded risk, sharing premium and loss proportionately.
subject: Insurance
summary: The answer is option c. Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is wrong because reinsurance is a separate contract between the insurer and reinsurer, so the original insured has no direct claim against the reinsurer.

detail: Goods sent on approval are sales only when the customer approves or accepts them, or when the approval period lapses. Until then, the goods still belong to the seller. Here the goods are unapproved at the year end, so the sale must be reversed and the goods added to closing stock at cost, not at selling price. The cost is ₹10,000, so adjusted closing stock is ₹60,000 + ₹10,000 = ₹70,000. Option a ignores the adjustment. Option c adds the goods at sale price, which would be ₹12,500 (cost ₹10,000 is 80% of sale price, so sale price is ₹12,500), giving ₹72,500 rather than ₹72,000, so it is wrong in any case. Option d is an arbitrary figure. The principle is that stock is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value, and unrealised profit is never recognised.
explanations: Wrong: this ignores the unapproved goods that still belong to the firm.
Correct: ₹60,000 + ₹10,000 cost of goods on approval = ₹70,000.
Wrong: this is not derived from cost; it wrongly includes a profit element or miscalculates.
Wrong: this reduces stock without any basis in the adjustment.
keyfact: Unapproved goods on approval stay in stock at cost, never at sale price.
question: A firm purchased goods worth ₹2,00,000 and the following adjustments are to be made while preparing the final accounts for the year ended 31 March 2026. Opening stock ₹40,000; closing stock (at cost) ₹60,000; goods worth ₹10,000 (cost) were sent on approval basis to customers at a profit of 20% on sales price, and as on 31 March 2026 approval for these goods had not been received. These goods were included in sales and are NOT included in the closing stock of ₹60,000. What is the amount of closing stock to be shown in the Balance Sheet after adjustment?
related: Goods on approval are sales only on acceptance or lapse of the approval period.
Stock is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
Unrealised profit is not recognised in the accounts.
Sale on approval reversal reduces sales and debtors and increases stock at cost.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The correct answer is ₹70,000. Goods sent on approval and not yet approved remain the firm's stock and are valued at cost.
topic: Goods on approval and closing stock valuation

detail: India's updated NDC of August 2022 raised the earlier 2015 targets. The emissions intensity of GDP is to fall by 45% by 2030 from the 2005 level, up from 33-35%. The share of non-fossil sources in cumulative installed electric power capacity is to reach about 50% by 2030, up from 40%, with the help of technology transfer and low-cost international finance. India also announced its long-term goal of net-zero emissions by 2070. The NDC does not specify an absolute cap on emissions, because India's stand is that its development needs and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities require flexibility. It uses intensity-based targets instead. Elimination logic: statements 1 and 2 are the standard targets, so any option leaving out one of them is wrong. Statement 3 is the trap, since an absolute cap is not part of the NDC.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 2 is also correct.
Incorrect: statement 1 is also correct.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false because there is no absolute cap.
Correct: only statements 1 and 2 are correct.
keyfact: India's 2022 NDC: 45% emissions-intensity cut by 2030 from 2005, and about 50% non-fossil power capacity, with no absolute cap.
question:
With reference to India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) submitted in 2022 under the Paris Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. It aims to reduce the emissions intensity of GDP by 45 per cent by 2030 from the 2005 level.
2. It aims to achieve about 50 per cent cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel-based energy resources by 2030, with the help of technology transfer and low-cost international finance.
3. It sets an absolute cap on India's total greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: India's net-zero target year is 2070.
The 2022 NDC added Mission LiFE as a lifestyle-based approach.
The 2015 NDC set 33-35% intensity reduction and 40% non-fossil capacity by 2030.
NDCs are submitted under Article 4 of the Paris Agreement.
Updated NDCs are submitted every five years.
statements: 1 — Correct: The 2022 NDC sets a 45% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP by 2030 from the 2005 level.
2 — Correct: It targets about 50% non-fossil installed power capacity by 2030, subject to technology and finance support.
3 — Incorrect: India's targets are intensity-based and do not impose an absolute emissions cap.
Facts: India has announced a net-zero goal for 2070. The 2015 NDC targets were 33-35% and 40%.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect, because India's NDC is an intensity-based target and not an absolute emissions cap.

detail: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of the time of Parantaka I record rules for choosing members of village committees by drawing pots (kudavolai). Rajendra I (1014-1044 CE) sent a naval expedition against Srivijaya around 1025 CE. Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE) completed the Brihadisvara (Rajarajeshvara) temple at Thanjavur around 1010 CE. Because all three are standard facts, the answer is 1, 2 and 3.
explanations: Wrong: statements 2 and 3 are also correct.
Wrong: statement 3 is also correct.
Wrong: statement 1 is also correct.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
keyfact: Rajendra I's navy attacked Srivijaya c. 1025 CE; Uttaramerur records lot-based village committees.
question:
With reference to the Chola administration and economy, consider the following statements:
1. The inscriptions at Uttaramerur describe the working of village assemblies with committees chosen by a lottery-like method.
2. The Cholas had a naval expedition that reached the Srivijaya kingdom during the reign of Rajendra I.
3. Rajaraja I built the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Rajendra I founded Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
Cholas used the terms ur, sabha and nagaram for assemblies.
Uttaramerur inscriptions belong to Parantaka I's time.
Brihadisvara temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (Great Living Chola Temples).
statements: 1 — Correct: Uttaramerur inscriptions describe assembly rules and selection by lot.
2 — Correct: Rajendra I's naval expedition reached Srivijaya c. 1025 CE.
3 — Correct: Rajaraja I built the Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur. The Cholas combined strong village institutions with maritime power.
subject: Ancient History
summary: All three statements are correct. Uttaramerur inscriptions, Rajendra I's Srivijaya expedition and Rajaraja I's Thanjavur temple are all established facts.

detail: The Sutlej rises near Mansarovar-Rakas Tal in Tibet and enters Himachal Pradesh through the Shipki La pass. The Kosi is formed by the Sun Kosi, Arun and Tamur, and the Arun rises in Tibet. It crosses Nepal and enters Bihar, where it is known for its floods and shifting course. The Teesta rises in the Pauhunri/Cho Lhamu area of Sikkim, flows through Sikkim and West Bengal, and joins the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) in Bangladesh. Elimination: each statement is well established, so none can be dropped.
explanations: Incorrect: statements 2 and 3 are also correct.
Incorrect: statement 2 is also correct.
Incorrect: statement 1 is also correct.
Correct: all three statements are true.
keyfact: The Sutlej enters India at Shipki La, and the Kosi crosses Nepal into Bihar.
question:
With reference to the Himalayan rivers, consider the following statements:
1. The Sutlej enters India through the Shipki La pass.
2. The Kosi river originates in the Tibetan region and enters Bihar after flowing through Nepal.
3. The Teesta river flows through Sikkim and joins the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) in Bangladesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Kosi is the Sorrow of Bihar.
The Sutlej is a tributary of the Indus system.
The Teesta flows through Sikkim and West Bengal.
Shipki La is in Himachal Pradesh.
statements: 1 — Correct: Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh is the entry point of the Sutlej.
2 — Correct: the Kosi's Arun branch rises in Tibet and the river flows through Nepal into Bihar.
3 — Correct: the Teesta is a tributary of the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh.
The Kosi is called the Sorrow of Bihar. The Teesta is subject to glacial lake outburst flood risk, as seen in October 2023 at South Lhonak Lake.
subject: Geography
summary: All three statements are correct. The Sutlej enters via Shipki La, the Kosi's headstreams rise in Tibet and cross Nepal into Bihar, and the Teesta flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before joining the Brahmaputra in Bangladesh.

detail: Subscription income for the current year = receipts - arrears of earlier year received - advance received for next year + outstanding at year-end. So 50,000 - 2,500 - 3,000 + 6,000 = ₹50,500. Opening arrears of ₹4,000 are not added again, because only the portion received (₹2,500) is removed from receipts and the remaining ₹1,500 relates to earlier years. The Income and Expenditure Account follows the accrual basis, so it records only the current year's income, not cash receipts. Elimination: ₹50,000 ignores adjustments, and ₹52,000 and ₹49,000 misuse the opening arrears.
explanations: Wrong: it wrongly deducts further amounts.
Wrong: it adds back the opening arrears incorrectly.
Wrong: it is the unadjusted receipt figure.
keyfact: Subscription income = receipts - previous arrears received - advance + closing outstanding.
question: In a non-trading organisation, the amount of subscriptions in arrears at the beginning of the year was ₹4,000, and subscriptions received during the year were ₹50,000. Subscriptions received in advance at the year-end were ₹3,000 (none at the start), and subscriptions outstanding at the year-end were ₹6,000. Of the amount received, ₹2,500 related to the previous year's arrears. The subscription income to be credited to the Income and Expenditure Account is:
related: Income and Expenditure Account is prepared on accrual basis.
Receipts and Payments Account is a summary of cash transactions.
Life membership fees are generally capitalised.
Entrance fees are often treated as capital receipts.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: Income for the year is ₹50,500. Start with receipts of ₹50,000, remove the arrears of ₹2,500 and the advance of ₹3,000, and add the closing outstanding of ₹6,000.

detail: The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) in Bihar was Gandhiji's first major civil disobedience-type action in India. European planters forced tenants to grow indigo on 3 out of every 20 kathas of land (the tinkathia system). Rajkumar Shukla, a local cultivator, persuaded Gandhiji to visit. Gandhiji defied an order to leave the district, and the government appointed the Champaran Agrarian Committee, of which he was a member. Based on its report, the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 abolished the tinkathia system and reduced the exactions on peasants. Elimination: since all three statements are factually sound, only the option containing 1, 2 and 3 survives. Candidates often confuse Champaran with Kheda (1918, revenue remission) and the Ahmedabad mill strike (1918).
explanations: Incomplete: it omits statement 3, which is correct.
Incomplete: it omits statement 1, which is correct.
Incomplete: it omits statement 2, which is correct.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
keyfact: Champaran (1917): tinkathia system, abolished by the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918.
question:
With reference to the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, consider the following statements:
1. It was Gandhiji's first Satyagraha in India, undertaken at the request of Rajkumar Shukla.
2. The peasants were compelled under the tinkathia system to grow indigo on a fixed portion of their land.
3. The Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 abolished the tinkathia system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Kheda Satyagraha (1918) in Gujarat was about revenue remission after crop failure.
The Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) involved Gandhiji's first fast in a labour dispute.
Gandhiji returned to India from South Africa in 1915.
Rajendra Prasad and J.B. Kripalani assisted Gandhiji in Champaran.
statements: 1 — Correct: Rajkumar Shukla invited Gandhiji, and Champaran was his first Satyagraha in India.
2 — Correct: Under tinkathia, peasants had to cultivate indigo on 3/20 of their land.
3 — Correct: The Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 abolished the tinkathia system.
Facts: Gandhiji was assisted by Rajendra Prasad, J.B. Kripalani, Mahadev Desai and others. The Champaran Agrarian Committee was appointed in 1917.
subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: All three statements are correct. Gandhiji went to Champaran at Rajkumar Shukla's invitation, the tinkathia system forced indigo cultivation, and the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918 ended it.

detail: Hydrogen is colour-coded by how it is made. Grey hydrogen comes from steam methane reforming of natural gas and emits CO2. Blue hydrogen is the same process with carbon capture and storage. Green hydrogen is made by electrolysis of water using renewable electricity, and it is the focus of India's National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023). Turquoise hydrogen comes from methane pyrolysis, which splits methane into hydrogen and solid carbon, so the carbon is not emitted as gas if the solid is used or stored. Pink (also called purple or red in some schemes) hydrogen uses nuclear power for electrolysis. Black and brown hydrogen come from coal gasification. The trap in statement 3 is that the electrolysis step is correct but the power source is wrong. Eliminating statement 3 leaves only option (a).
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are right and statement 3 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect because pink hydrogen is nuclear-powered.
Wrong: this includes statement 3 and leaves out the correct statement 2.
Wrong: statement 3 is false, so not all are correct.
keyfact: Pink hydrogen = nuclear-powered electrolysis; turquoise = methane pyrolysis giving solid carbon.
question:
With reference to the classification of hydrogen by production route, consider the following statements:
1. Grey hydrogen is produced from natural gas by steam methane reforming, with the resulting carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere.
2. Turquoise hydrogen is produced by methane pyrolysis, which yields solid carbon as a by-product instead of carbon dioxide.
3. Pink hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water using electricity generated from biomass gasification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Green hydrogen is made by electrolysis powered by renewable electricity.
Blue hydrogen is grey hydrogen combined with carbon capture and storage.
Black and brown hydrogen come from coal gasification.
The National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved in 2023.
Pink hydrogen uses nuclear electricity for electrolysis.
statements: 1 — Correct: steam methane reforming of natural gas is the grey route and releases CO2.
2 — Correct: methane pyrolysis gives hydrogen and solid carbon.
3 — Incorrect: pink hydrogen uses nuclear power for electrolysis, not biomass.

Facts: green hydrogen needs renewable electricity. Blue hydrogen is grey with carbon capture. Black and brown hydrogen come from coal. India's National Green Hydrogen Mission was approved in January 2023.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Pink hydrogen uses electrolysis powered by nuclear electricity, not biomass, so statement 3 is wrong.

detail: The Code on Wages, 2019 consolidated four earlier laws. On overtime, it requires payment at a rate not less than twice the normal rate of wages. On claims, it extended the limitation period to three years from the date the wages became payable or the deduction was made, which is more generous than the earlier Payment of Wages Act. The employer must fix the wage period as a day, a week, a fortnight or a month, but never more than a month. So a two-month wage period would be unlawful. Wages must be paid on time, for example by the seventh day after the end of the wage period in the case of monthly-paid employees. Elimination: Statement 3 is false, so options c and d are out. Statement 1 is true, so option a is incomplete. Hence option b.
explanations: Incorrect. Statement 2 is also correct, so '1 only' is incomplete.
Correct. Statements 1 and 2 are right, and statement 3 is wrong.
Incorrect. Statement 3 is wrong because wage periods cannot exceed one month, and the option leaves out statement 1.
Incorrect. Statement 3 is wrong, so all three cannot be correct.
keyfact: Code on Wages: overtime at not less than twice the normal rate, claims within three years, wage period up to one month.
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Code on Wages, 2019:
1. For overtime work, an employee is entitled to wages at a rate not less than twice the normal rate of wages.
