detail: The gratuity formula is last drawn wages × 15/26 × completed years of service. Where the fraction of a year exceeds six months, it is counted as a full year. Here 8 months is more than 6 months, so service counts as 13 years. Gratuity = 40,000 × 15 ÷ 26 × 13. Since 26 divides 13 exactly (13/26 = 1/2), this equals 40,000 × 15 × 0.5 = ₹3,00,000. This is below the statutory ceiling of ₹20 lakh, so no cap applies. Elimination: ₹2,76,923 results from wrongly taking 12 years. ₹2,88,462 results from taking 12.5 years, i.e. pro-rating the fraction. ₹3,23,077 results from taking 14 years. Only the rounding rule gives 13 years.
explanations: Correct. Service rounds up to 13 years, and 40,000 × 15/26 × 13 = ₹3,00,000.
Incorrect. This uses 12 years and ignores the rounding-up rule for a fraction above six months.
Incorrect. This uses 14 years, which has no basis.
Incorrect. This pro-rates 12.5 years, but the rule rounds fully to the next whole year, not to half years.
keyfact: Gratuity = last drawn wages × 15/26 × years, rounding up when the fraction exceeds six months.
question: An employee covered by gratuity provisions has last drawn monthly wages (basic + dearness allowance) of ₹40,000 and has rendered continuous service of 12 years and 8 months. Applying the standard gratuity formula of 15 days' wages for every completed year of service (month taken as 26 working days) and the rule that a fraction of service of more than six months is rounded up to the next year, the gratuity payable is:
related: Gratuity formula: last drawn wages × 15/26 × years of service.
A fraction of a year more than six months is counted as a full year.
The maximum gratuity payable is ₹20 lakh.
For a seasonal establishment, gratuity is 7 days' wages for each season.
Gratuity is payable on retirement, resignation, superannuation, death or disablement.
subject: Social Security
summary: The answer is ₹3,00,000. Service of 12 years 8 months is rounded up to 13 years because the fraction exceeds six months. Gratuity = 40,000 × 15/26 × 13 = ₹3,00,000.

detail: The IOD is a coupled ocean-atmosphere oscillation in the tropical Indian Ocean. In the positive phase, easterly wind anomalies along the equator weaken or reverse the usual pattern. Warm surface water piles up in the west near Africa, and cooler upwelling water appears off Sumatra and Java. The thermocline is shallow in the east and deep in the west. The Dipole Mode Index is the SST anomaly difference between the western box (50-70°E, 10°S-10°N) and the south-eastern box (90-110°E, 10°S-0°). A positive IOD usually enhances Indian monsoon rainfall, which is why it can cushion the effect of El Niño, as it did in 1997. To eliminate options, spot that statement 2 reverses the wind direction. Once it is out, 1, 3 and 4 form a consistent set.
explanations: Wrong: three statements are correct, not one.
Wrong: three statements are correct, not two. Only statement 2 is wrong.
Correct: statements 1, 3 and 4 are right and statement 2 is wrong.
Wrong: statement 2 has the wind direction reversed.
keyfact: Positive IOD: easterly wind anomalies, warm west, cool east, usually good for the Indian monsoon.

summary: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three'. Statement 2 is wrong because a positive IOD brings anomalous easterlies along the equator, which push warm water west.

detail: The DPDP Act, 2023 is India's first comprehensive personal data law. It covers digital personal data, meaning data collected digitally or digitised later. It has extraterritorial application when processing is linked to offering goods or services to people in India. It creates the roles of Data Principal, Data Fiduciary and Significant Data Fiduciary. It also sets up the Data Protection Board of India as an adjudicatory body. Board decisions can be appealed to TDSAT. The Schedule fixes penalties, with a ceiling of Rs 250 crore for failure to take reasonable security safeguards. detail: The 2016 amendment to the RBI Act, 1934 gave the MPC a statutory basis. It has six members. Three are from the RBI: the Governor (Chairperson), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, and one officer nominated by the Central Board. The other three are external members appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of a search-cum-selection committee under the Cabinet Secretary. External members hold office for four years and are not eligible for reappointment. Decisions are taken by majority of members present and voting, with a quorum of four. Each member has one vote, and the Governor has a second, casting vote in a tie. To eliminate, spot statement 3 as the trap. Terms of 'not eligible for reappointment' are a typical UPSC detail. This rules out options (c) and (d), and statement 1 is clearly correct, which rules out nothing further but confirms (b).

Correct: statements 1 and 2 are accurate and statement 3 is false.
Incorrect: statement 2 is correct, but statement 3 is false and statement 1 is also correct.

keyfact: MPC: 6 members (3 RBI + 3 external), external members serve 4 years with no reappointment, Governor has a casting vote.

detail: Article 148 provides for the CAG. He is appointed by the President by warrant under hand and seal and takes an oath before the President. His removal is on the same grounds and in the same manner as a Supreme Court Judge, that is, an address by both Houses of Parliament supported by special majority on proved misbehaviour or incapacity. His conditions of service cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment. Article 148(4) bars him from any further office under the Union or a State after he ceases to hold office, which secures his independence. Under Article 151, the Union reports go to the President, who has them laid before Parliament, and State reports go to the Governor. Elimination: statement 3 is false, so any option containing it (b, c, d) is eliminated, leaving (a).

summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so the answer is (a). Statement 3 is wrong because Article 148(4) bars the CAG from any further office under the Government of India or of any State after ceasing to hold office.

detail: The councils are a staple of UPSC ancient history. The tradition links each council to a patron, a venue, a president and an outcome. First Council (Rajagriha): Mahakassapa presided, and Ananda recited the Dhamma (Sutta) while Upali recited the Vinaya. Second Council (Vaishali): it dealt with the ten disputed practices of the Vajjiputtaka monks. Third Council (Pataliputra): it was held under Ashoka, with Moggaliputta Tissa as the leading figure and the Kathavatthu of the Abhidhamma tradition. Fourth Council (Kashmir, Kundalavana): it was held under Kanishka, with Vasumitra as president and Ashvaghosha as vice-president. To eliminate, spot the single swapped name in statement 3. Once three statements are confirmed correct and one is wrong, 'only three' is the only consistent option.

keyfact: Fourth Council (Kashmir, Kanishka): president Vasumitra, vice-president Ashvaghosha.

detail: CBAM is an EU regulation designed to prevent carbon leakage by charging importers for the embedded carbon of selected goods, equalising carbon prices between EU producers under the EU Emissions Trading System and importers. Its initial coverage is cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen. It had a transitional reporting phase beginning in October 2023, with the definitive financial phase starting in 2026. Because it is a unilateral EU measure, it is not a UNFCCC or Paris Agreement body, and developing countries including India have objected to it as a trade barrier inconsistent with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities. detail: The bandgap is the energy needed to lift an electron from the valence band to the conduction band. Silicon has a bandgap of about 1.1 eV, while SiC (about 3.3 eV for the common 4H polytype) and GaN (about 3.4 eV) are wide-bandgap materials. A wider gap means a higher breakdown electric field, lower leakage at high temperatures and faster switching, so power converters can be smaller, lighter and more efficient. This is why they are used in EV inverters, on-board chargers, fast chargers, 5G power amplifiers and solar inverters. Elimination: no known material is a room-temperature, ambient-pressure superconductor, so (b) is false. GaN and SiC are semiconductors rather than insulating thermal-barrier ceramics, which removes (c). Permanent magnets use neodymium-iron-boron or samarium-cobalt, which removes (d).
explanations: Correct. GaN and SiC are wide-bandgap semiconductors suited to high-power, high-frequency, high-temperature use.
Wrong. No material is an established superconductor at room temperature and ordinary pressure, and GaN and SiC are not superconductors.
Wrong. They are semiconductors used in electronic devices, not thermal-barrier ceramics.
Wrong. Permanent magnets use rare-earth alloys such as NdFeB, not GaN or SiC.
keyfact: GaN and SiC are wide-bandgap semiconductors, better than silicon for high-power, high-frequency use.
options: wide-bandgap semiconductors that can operate at higher voltages, temperatures and switching frequencies than silicon
superconductors that conduct electricity with zero resistance at room temperature
insulating ceramics used mainly as thermal barriers in rocket nozzles
rare-earth magnetic materials used in permanent magnet motors

subject: Science & Tech
summary: GaN and SiC are wide-bandgap semiconductors. Their larger bandgap lets devices handle higher voltage, heat and switching speed with lower losses than silicon, which makes them useful in EVs and fast chargers.

detail:
Use the formula Median = L + [(N/2 − C)/f] × h.

N = 50, so N/2 = 25. The cumulative frequencies are 5, 13, 28, 40 and 50. The first cumulative frequency of 25 or more is 28, so the median class is 20–30.

Here L = 20, C (cumulative frequency before the class) = 13, f = 15 and h = 10.

Median = 20 + (25 − 13)/15 × 10 = 20 + 8 = 28.

Elimination: 25 is just N/2 and has no meaning as a wage. 27 comes from using C = 14 wrongly. 30 is the upper limit of the median class, which is wrong because 25 is below the cumulative frequency of 28 at that limit. The correct interpolation gives 28.
explanations: 25 is simply N/2, not the median value.
Arises from a wrong cumulative frequency before the median class.
30 is the upper limit of the median class, not the interpolated median.
keyfact: Median = L + [(N/2 − C)/f] × h, with the median class identified from cumulative frequencies.
question: The frequency distribution of 50 workers by daily wages (in Rs hundred) is: 0–10: 5; 10–20: 8; 20–30: 15; 30–40: 12; 40–50: 10. What is the median wage?
related: The median class is the first class whose cumulative frequency is at least N/2.
The median is the abscissa of the intersection of the less-than and more-than ogives.
The median minimises the sum of absolute deviations.
Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean (empirical relation).
Quartiles use N/4 and 3N/4 in place of N/2.
subject: Statistics
summary: The median is 28. N/2 = 25 falls in the 20–30 class, so Median = 20 + [(25 − 13)/15] × 10 = 28.

Entry 25 covers vocational and technical training of labour. To eliminate options, match the wording. Provident funds, workmen's compensation and maternity benefits appear in the long text of Entry 24, so options a, b and d fail. The wording of the question is taken directly from Entry 24, which makes it the correct choice.

summary: The answer is Entry 24 of List III. Provident funds, employers' liability, workmen's compensation, pensions and maternity benefits are all listed under 'welfare of labour'.

detail: India's PHWRs use natural uranium as fuel and heavy water (deuterium oxide) as both moderator and coolant. The moderator's role is to slow down fast neutrons to thermal energies, which makes them far more likely to cause fission in uranium-235. Control rods contain strong neutron absorbers such as boron, cadmium or hafnium, and they regulate or shut down the chain reaction. Statement 2 reverses the role of the moderator, and this is the type of subtle reversal UPSC often uses. Eliminating it leaves statements 1 and 3, so the answer is two.
explanations: Wrong: two statements are correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are right.
Wrong: statement 2 is false.
Wrong: statements 1 and 3 are correct.
keyfact: A moderator slows neutrons; control rods absorb neutrons.
question:
With reference to the working of a nuclear reactor and radiation, consider the following statements:
1. In a pressurised heavy water reactor, heavy water is used as both moderator and coolant.
2. A moderator is used to speed up fast neutrons so that they can sustain the chain reaction.
3. Control rods in a reactor usually contain materials such as boron or cadmium that absorb neutrons.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Common moderators: heavy water, graphite, light water.
Natural uranium contains about 0.7% U-235.
India's 700 MWe PHWR is the indigenous standard design.
Fast breeder reactors do not use a moderator.
statements: 1 — Correct: PHWRs use heavy water as moderator and also as coolant in the primary circuit.
2 — Incorrect: A moderator slows down neutrons; it does not speed them up.
3 — Correct: Boron, cadmium and hafnium absorb neutrons and are used in control rods.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Only statements 1 and 3 are correct. A moderator slows down fast neutrons, rather than speeding them up.

detail: The four major events of the Buddha's life are linked with Lumbini (birth), Bodh Gaya (enlightenment), Sarnath (first sermon) and Kushinagar (Mahaparinirvana). The first Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha (Rajgir) soon after his death, under Mahakassapa, with Ajatashatru as patron. Elimination: swap each wrongly assigned event: Bodh Gaya is enlightenment, not Mahaparinirvana; Kushinagar is Mahaparinirvana, not enlightenment; Lumbini is birth, not a council venue.
explanations: Correct: the first sermon was delivered at Sarnath (Isipatana).
Incorrect: Mahaparinirvana took place at Kushinagar, while Bodh Gaya is the site of enlightenment.
Incorrect: Kushinagar is the Mahaparinirvana site; enlightenment occurred at Bodh Gaya.
Incorrect: Lumbini is the birthplace; the first Council was at Rajagriha.
keyfact: Lumbini - birth; Bodh Gaya - enlightenment; Sarnath - first sermon; Kushinagar - Mahaparinirvana.
options: Sarnath - Site of the first sermon of the Buddha
Bodh Gaya - Site of the Buddha's Mahaparinirvana
Kushinagar - Site of the Buddha's enlightenment
Lumbini - Site of the first Buddhist Council
question: Which one of the following pairs of a Buddhist or Jain site and its associated feature is correctly matched?
related: The second Buddhist Council was held at Vaishali.
The third Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka.
The Ashokan pillar at Lumbini records his visit.
The Sarnath Lion Capital is India's national emblem.
subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: Sarnath is where the Buddha delivered his first sermon (Dhammachakkappavattana). The other pairs mix up the sites of key events in his life.

detail: 248 in binary is 11111000, so the mask has 8 + 8 + 5 = 21 network bits and 11 host bits. Total addresses per subnet = 2^11 = 2048; usable hosts = 2048 - 2 = 2046 (network and broadcast addresses are excluded). The block size in the third octet is 256 - 248 = 8, so the first subnet spans 172.16.0.0 to 172.16.7.255. Its broadcast address is 172.16.7.255. Elimination: 2048 ignores reserved addresses. 172.16.8.255 is the broadcast of the second block's first /24, not the first subnet. 1022 hosts and 172.16.3.255 correspond to a /22 mask.
explanations: Correct: /21 gives 2046 usable hosts, and the range ends at 172.16.7.255.
Incorrect: 2048 counts the network and broadcast addresses as usable.
Incorrect: the broadcast is wrong; the block ends at 7.255, not 8.255.
Incorrect: these values apply to a /22 mask (255.255.252.0).
keyfact: /21 = 255.255.248.0 = 2046 usable hosts, block size 8 in the third octet.
question: An IPv4 network has the address 172.16.0.0 with the subnet mask 255.255.248.0. What is the number of usable host addresses per subnet and the broadcast address of the first subnet?
related: Usable hosts = 2^h - 2.
Block size = 256 - the interesting octet of the mask.
The network address has all host bits 0; the broadcast has all host bits 1.
CIDR notation was introduced to replace classful addressing.
subject: Computers
summary: The mask 255.255.248.0 is /21, giving 2^11 - 2 = 2046 usable hosts. The first subnet's broadcast address is 172.16.7.255.

detail: NSAP was launched in 1995 to give effect to Article 41 of the Directive Principles (right to public assistance in old age, sickness, disablement and undeserved want). It is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development. Its components are the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), the Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), the Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS), the National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) and Annapurna. NFBS is a one-time lump-sum benefit. It is paid when the primary breadwinner of a BPL household dies during the working-age band of 18 to 59 years. Eliminate 60 or more, because that is the old-age pension band covered by IGNOAPS. Options b and c shift the age limits, and the lower bound is 18, not 21, since it matches the age of majority.
explanations: Correct. NFBS applies when the primary breadwinner dies aged 18 to 59 years.
Incorrect. The upper age limit is below 60, not below 65.
Incorrect. The lower age limit is 18, not 21.
Incorrect. Age 60 and above is the band for old-age pension (IGNOAPS), not NFBS.
keyfact: NFBS: ₹20,000 lump sum on the death of a BPL household's primary breadwinner aged 18-59.
options: 18 years or more and below 60 years
18 years or more and below 65 years
21 years or more and below 60 years
question: Under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), the National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS) gives a lump-sum payment of ₹20,000 to a BPL household on the death of the primary breadwinner. For this benefit, the deceased breadwinner must have been aged:
related: NSAP was launched in 1995 and is linked to Article 41.
NSAP is administered by the Ministry of Rural Development.
NSAP components: IGNOAPS, IGNWPS, IGNDPS, NFBS and Annapurna.
NFBS gives a one-time lump sum of ₹20,000.
The old-age pension under NSAP is meant for BPL persons aged 60 years and above.
subject: Social Security
summary: The correct answer is option a. NFBS covers the death of a primary breadwinner aged 18 years or more and below 60 years (18-59). The scheme is meant to support a BPL family that loses its working-age earner.

detail: Shankari Prasad (1951) upheld Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights, and Sajjan Singh (1965) followed it. Golaknath (1967) reversed this, and the 24th Amendment and Kesavananda Bharati (1973) then restored amending power subject to the basic structure. L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held that judicial review by the High Courts under Articles 226/227 and by the Supreme Court under Article 32 is part of the basic structure. Tribunal decisions are therefore subject to scrutiny by the High Court Division Bench within whose jurisdiction the tribunal falls. I.R. Coelho (2007) held that Ninth Schedule laws enacted after 24 April 1973, the date of Kesavananda, can be reviewed against the basic structure and Fundamental Rights. In Berubari (1960) the Court held the Preamble is not part of the Constitution and is not a source of power. Kesavananda later reversed that position and held the Preamble is part of the Constitution. Eliminate pairs 2 and 4 and the answer is 'Only two'.
explanations: Incorrect: two pairs, 1 and 3, are correct.
Correct: pairs 1 and 3 are accurate and pairs 2 and 4 are wrong.
Incorrect: pairs 2 and 4 are wrongly matched.
Incorrect: pairs 2 and 4 do not state the actual holdings.
keyfact: Chandra Kumar (1997): tribunal decisions are subject to High Court review, because judicial review is part of the basic structure.
question:
Consider the following pairs of judicial decisions and the principle laid down:
1. Shankari Prasad v. Union of India : Parliament's power under Article 368 extends to amending Fundamental Rights
2. L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India : Decisions of Administrative Tribunals are immune from scrutiny by the High Courts and the Supreme Court
3. I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu : Laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to challenge on the ground of violating the basic structure
4. In re Berubari Union : The Preamble is a part of the Constitution and a source of power for Parliament
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
related: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) was decided by a 13-judge bench and held that Parliament cannot alter the basic structure.
Minerva Mills (1980) struck down parts of the 42nd Amendment, holding that limited amending power is itself a basic feature.
S.R. Bommai (1994) made Presidential proclamations under Article 356 subject to judicial review.
Indira Nehru Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975) held free and fair elections to be basic structure.
statements: 1 — Correct: Shankari Prasad (1951) upheld Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights.
2 — Incorrect: Chandra Kumar held that tribunal decisions are subject to High Court scrutiny.
3 — Correct: Coelho (2007) applied basic structure review to post-24 April 1973 Ninth Schedule laws.
4 — Incorrect: Berubari held the Preamble is not part of the Constitution, and Kesavananda reversed this.
Facts: Golaknath (1967) held Fundamental Rights could not be amended. Kesavananda (1973) gave the basic structure doctrine by a 7:6 majority.
subject: Polity
summary: Pairs 1 and 3 are correctly matched, so the answer is 'Only two'. Chandra Kumar held tribunal decisions subject to High Court review, and Berubari held the Preamble was not part of the Constitution.

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 is the first Indian statute to define gig workers, platform workers and aggregators formally. Section 114 provides for a Social Security Fund for these workers, financed largely by aggregator contributions. The contribution is a percentage of the aggregator's annual turnover, between 1% and 2%, but it cannot exceed 5% of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers. The Central Government notifies the exact rate within this range. Elimination: a profit-based levy or an EPF-style 12% wage contribution does not appear in this provision, and the Code links the levy to turnover. The 0.5% and 1% figures in option (d) are below the statutory range and misstate the cap.
explanations: Correct. This matches the turnover range of 1–2% and the 5% cap on payments to gig and platform workers.
Incorrect. The levy is linked to turnover, not profit, and it has a cap.
Incorrect. 12% of wages is the EPF employee and employer rate, which does not apply to this fund.
Incorrect. The range is 1–2%, and the cap is 5% of amounts paid or payable to workers.
keyfact: Aggregator contribution: 1–2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers.
options: 1–2% of the aggregator's annual turnover, subject to a cap of 5% of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers
5–10% of the aggregator's annual profit, with no upper cap
12% of the wages of each gig worker, matching the EPF contribution
0.5% of the aggregator's annual turnover, subject to a cap of 1% of the amount paid to workers
question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, an aggregator is required to contribute to the Social Security Fund for gig and platform workers at a rate of:
related: The Code defines gig worker, platform worker and aggregator.
The aggregator contribution is paid into the Social Security Fund.
The Central Government notifies the exact contribution rate.
Social security schemes for gig workers may cover life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, and old age protection.
Gig and platform workers can be registered through the e-Shram portal.
subject: Social Security
summary: The answer is option (a). The Code provides for an aggregator contribution of 1–2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of the amount paid or payable to gig and platform workers. The exact rate is to be notified by the Central Government.
topic: Gig and platform workers under the Code on Social Security

detail: Article 161 gives the Governor power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit or commute sentences, for offences against laws on matters within the State's executive power. The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence, although the Governor may suspend, remit or commute it. The Governor also has no power over court-martial sentences, which fall within the President's power under Article 72. The President's power covers court-martial sentences, offences against Union laws and death sentences, including pardon. Statement-II describes the scope of the Governor's power by subject matter and is true, but it does not explain why a death-sentence pardon is excluded. Elimination: both are textbook-correct, so options 'c' and 'd' fall, and the exclusion of death-sentence pardon is a separate limitation rather than a consequence of subject-matter coverage.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II describes the scope of the power by subject matter and does not explain the death-sentence exception.
Correct: both statements are true, and the exclusion in Statement-I is a separate limitation, not a result of Statement-II.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: A Governor can suspend, remit or commute but not pardon a death sentence, and has no power over court-martial sentences.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Governor of a State cannot grant a pardon to a person sentenced to death by a court in that State, though the Governor can suspend, remit or commute the sentence.
Statement-II: The pardoning power of the Governor under Article 161 extends to all offences against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the State extends.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Under Article 72 the President can pardon court-martial sentences and death sentences.
The Governor cannot grant pardon, reprieve or remission for court-martial sentences.
Article 161 power is exercised on the aid and advice of the State Council of Ministers.
The Governor can only suspend, remit or commute a death sentence, not pardon it.
statements: Statement-I — Correct: the Governor cannot pardon a death sentence, but can suspend, remit or commute it.
Statement-II — Correct: Article 161 extends to offences against laws relating to matters within the State's executive power. This does not explain why death-sentence pardon is excluded.
subject: Polity
summary: Both statements are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I. The limit on pardoning death sentences is a difference between the Governor's and the President's powers, not a result of the scope in Article 161.

detail: The International Booker Prize is awarded annually for a book translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland. The prize money is shared equally between author and translator. Banu Mushtaq's Heart Lamp is a collection of short stories about the lives of women in Muslim communities in southern India. It was written in Kannada over about three decades. Deepa Bhasthi became the first Kannada translator to win. Earlier, Geetanjali Shree's Tomb of Sand, translated from Hindi by Daisy Rockwell, won in 2022. Students should not confuse this prize with the Booker Prize for original English fiction, which David Szalay won in 2025 for Flesh. Malayalam, Tamil and Urdu are plausible distractors because they are major South Indian or Indian literary languages. None of them is the language of this book.
explanations: Incorrect: the book was not written in Malayalam.
Correct: Heart Lamp was written in Kannada.
Incorrect: the book was not written in Tamil.
Incorrect: the book was not written in Urdu.
keyfact: International Booker 2025: Banu Mushtaq's Heart Lamp, a Kannada work.
question: The International Booker Prize 2025 was won by 'Heart Lamp' by Banu Mushtaq, translated into English by Deepa Bhasthi. In which language was the book originally written?
related: Tomb of Sand (Hindi, Geetanjali Shree) won the International Booker in 2022
Deepa Bhasthi is the translator of Heart Lamp
The Booker Prize 2025 was won by David Szalay for Flesh
The International Booker prize money is split between author and translator
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Heart Lamp is a short-story collection originally written in Kannada. It won the 2025 International Booker Prize, and it was the first Kannada work to win.

detail: Varahamihira, who lived in the sixth century CE and was linked with Ujjain, wrote the Panchasiddhantika, which summarises five earlier siddhantas: Paitamaha, Vasishtha, Romaka, Paulisa and Surya. It is valuable as a record of Indian astronomy that shows influence from Greek and Roman ideas. His Brihat Samhita is a broad encyclopaedic work covering astrology, architecture, gemmology, omens and more, and does not mainly summarise astronomical schools. The Brahmasphutasiddhanta was written by Brahmagupta in 628 CE. The Aryabhatiya was composed by Aryabhata in 499 CE and presents his own system. So only the Panchasiddhantika matches the description.
explanations: Incorrect. The Brihat Samhita is an encyclopaedic work on varied subjects.
Correct. The Panchasiddhantika summarises five astronomical schools.
Incorrect. The Brahmasphutasiddhanta was written by Brahmagupta.
Incorrect. The Aryabhatiya was written by Aryabhata.
keyfact: The Panchasiddhantika of Varahamihira summarises five astronomical siddhantas.
question: Which one of the following works of Varahamihira is a compendium that summarises five earlier astronomical schools (siddhantas), including the Surya and the Paulisa?
related: Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya in 499 CE.
Brahmagupta wrote the Brahmasphutasiddhanta in 628 CE.
The Romaka and Paulisa siddhantas reflect Greek and Roman influence on Indian astronomy.
Varahamihira is traditionally counted among the Navaratnas of Vikramaditya's court.
subject: Ancient History
summary: The answer is the Panchasiddhantika. In it Varahamihira summarises five astronomical systems: Paitamaha, Vasishtha, Romaka, Paulisa and Surya. The other works are by different authors or on different subjects.

detail: The CACP recommends MSPs for a set of mandated crops, and the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs makes the final decision. MSP is an administrative policy decision. It is not a statutory right under the National Food Security Act, 2013, which deals with subsidised foodgrain entitlements under the TPDS. MSP covers a limited list of 22 mandated crops, plus a fair and remunerative price (FRP) for sugarcane. Hence statement 3 is wrong. Effective procurement in practice is concentrated in a few crops, notably wheat and rice, and in certain states.
explanations: Wrong: Statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are accurate while 3 is not.
Wrong: Statement 3 is false and statement 1 is true.
Wrong: Statement 3 is false.
keyfact: MSP is recommended by CACP and approved by CCEA, with no statutory guarantee.
question:
With reference to Minimum Support Price (MSP) in India, consider the following statements:
1. MSP is recommended by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
2. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approves the MSP.
3. MSP is legally mandated under the National Food Security Act, 2013 for all crops grown in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops.
Sugarcane has the Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP).
CACP was set up in 1965 as the Agricultural Prices Commission and renamed in 1985.
Procurement is mainly through FCI and state agencies.
statements: 1 — Correct: The CACP recommends MSPs.
2 — Correct: The CCEA gives final approval.
3 — Incorrect: The NFSA concerns food entitlements, not an MSP guarantee for all crops. MSP covers only certain mandated crops and has no statutory backing.
subject: Economy
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. MSP has no legal guarantee under the NFSA and is not mandated for all crops.

detail: The biological pump is the set of processes by which marine organisms move carbon from the sunlit surface layer to the deep ocean. Phytoplankton take up dissolved CO2 in photosynthesis. Zooplankton graze on them, and dead cells, faecal pellets and marine snow sink. Much of this material is remineralised at depth, and a small fraction is buried in sediments for long periods. Elimination: Statement-II states the mechanism that Statement-I describes, so option (b) fails because the explanation link holds. Neither statement is false, so (c) and (d) fail.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true and the second is the mechanism behind the first.
Wrong: Statement-II does explain Statement-I.
Wrong: Statement-II is true.
Wrong: Statement-I is true.
keyfact: The biological pump: phytoplankton fix CO2, and sinking organic matter carries carbon to the deep ocean.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In the open ocean, the biological pump transfers carbon from surface waters to the deep sea.
Statement-II: Phytoplankton fix carbon through photosynthesis, and part of this carbon sinks as dead organic matter and faecal pellets.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The solubility pump is the physical counterpart to the biological pump.
Blue carbon refers to carbon stored in coastal ecosystems such as mangroves, seagrasses and salt marshes.
Cold water dissolves more CO2 than warm water.
Ocean acidification results from the ocean absorbing atmospheric CO2.
statements: 1 — Correct: the biological pump moves carbon to the deep ocean.
2 — Correct: it explains the pump, since sinking organic matter carries carbon downward.
subject: Environment
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. The biological pump works because phytoplankton fix carbon and some of it sinks as organic matter.

detail: In the standard model, money supply M = m x H, where H is high-powered (reserve) money and the multiplier m = (1 + c)/(c + r), with c the currency-deposit ratio and r the reserve-deposit ratio (including CRR and excess reserves). Differentiating shows m falls when either c or r rises, because more of each rupee is held as cash or reserves rather than being redeposited and re-lent. When r is 100% and c is zero, m equals 1. Hence option a is correct. Options b and c wrongly give a positive relationship. Option d is wrong because the multiplier is defined by the reserve and cash-holding ratios, not directly by the repo rate, although the repo rate may influence them indirectly.
explanations: Correct: m = (1 + c)/(c + r) falls as either c or r rises.
Incorrect: a higher reserve ratio lowers, not raises, the multiplier.
Incorrect: a higher currency-deposit ratio also lowers the multiplier.
Incorrect: the multiplier is defined by reserve and currency ratios, not directly by the repo rate.
keyfact: Money multiplier m = (1 + c)/(c + r), falling in both c and r.
options: It is inversely related to the reserve ratio and the currency deposit ratio
It is directly related to the reserve ratio and inversely related to the currency deposit ratio
It is directly related to both the reserve ratio and the currency deposit ratio
It is independent of the reserve ratio but depends on the repo rate
question: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the stages of the 'Money Multiplier' process, in terms of what determines its value, in a fractional reserve banking system?
related: RBI's reserve money (M0) equals currency in circulation plus bankers' deposits with RBI plus other deposits with RBI.
M3 is broad money, including time deposits of the public with banks.
A CRR cut raises the money multiplier.
M1 is currency with the public plus demand deposits plus other deposits with RBI.
subject: Indian Economy
summary: The money multiplier is inversely related to both the reserve ratio and the currency-deposit ratio. A higher leakage into reserves or cash reduces credit creation.

detail: Ellora in Maharashtra has 34 caves: 12 Buddhist (south), 17 Hindu (centre) and 5 Jain (north), created roughly between the 6th and 10th centuries, mainly under the Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Yadavas. The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16), attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, was cut from a single basalt rock in a top-down method. The religious diversity at Ellora reflects patronage and a tolerant religious milieu, not the technique of carving a single monolith. Thus, in statement-pair questions, test truth of each statement first and then ask if the second is the cause. Here it is not.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-II gives no reason for the multi-religious character.
Correct: both are true; the carving method is unrelated to the religious diversity.
Wrong: Statement-II is accurate.
Wrong: Statement-I is accurate.
keyfact: Ellora: 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu, 5 Jain caves; Kailasa is a top-down monolith.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Ellora complex contains Buddhist, Hindu and Jain rock-cut monuments.
Statement-II: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was carved out of a single rock by excavating from the top downwards.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Ellora is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983).
Kailasa Temple (Cave 16) is dedicated to Shiva.
Ellora's Buddhist caves include the Vishvakarma (Carpenter's) Cave, Cave 10.
Ajanta was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1983 too.
subject: Art & Culture
summary: Both statements are correct, but the manner of carving the Kailasa Temple does not explain why Ellora has monuments of three religions. Statement-II is an independent fact.

detail: Article 324 gives the Election Commission superintendence, direction and control over the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of elections. This is the constitutional basis of its power to revise rolls. In the Bihar SIR of 2025, the Supreme Court dealt with the documents accepted for enrolment. It directed that Aadhaar be treated as an identity document alongside the other listed documents, but not as proof of citizenship. Citizenship is governed by Part II of the Constitution and the Citizenship Act, 1955, and is determined by the Central Government under that framework. The Election Commission only checks eligibility for enrolment, which under Article 326 requires citizenship, age of 18 and ordinary residence. Statement 3 is therefore wrong, which eliminates options (c) and (d). Statement 1 is certainly correct, which eliminates (a) only if statement 2 is also known to be correct.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect, and statement 1 is omitted.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
keyfact: Article 324 gives the ECI control of electoral rolls; Aadhaar is an identity document, not proof of citizenship.
question:
With reference to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls undertaken by the Election Commission of India in Bihar in 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls in the Election Commission.
2. The Supreme Court directed that Aadhaar be accepted as an additional identity document in the exercise, though not as proof of citizenship.
3. The Supreme Court held that the Election Commission has the conclusive power to determine the citizenship of persons in the electoral roll.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Article 324 creates the Election Commission as a constitutional body.
Article 326 gives adult suffrage for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections.
The Representation of the People Act, 1950 governs the preparation of electoral rolls.
The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 by the 61st Amendment (1988).
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 324 vests control of the electoral rolls in the Election Commission.
2 — Correct: Aadhaar was to be accepted as an identity document but not as proof of citizenship.
3 — Incorrect: Citizenship is determined under the Citizenship Act, 1955, not conclusively by the Election Commission.
Article 326 provides for adult suffrage, with the conditions of citizenship and age of 18. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 governs the preparation of the rolls.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is (b). The Court did not give the Election Commission conclusive power over citizenship.
topic: Electoral rolls and Special Intensive Revision

detail: Kuchipudi takes its name from Kuchipudi village in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh. Its tradition of dance-drama (Yakshagana-type presentations) was developed by Siddhendra Yogi and performed originally by male Brahmin performers. It is recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi as a classical dance. Tarangam, where the dancer balances on the edge of a brass plate, often with a pot of water on the head, is a distinctive item. The Natyashastra of Bharata is the common textual basis for classical dance in India, and Kuchipudi follows it. Statement 2 is therefore false, which eliminates options c and d. Statement 1 is true, so option b is the only remaining choice that includes statements 1 and 3.
explanations: Incorrect: it omits statement 3, which is correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are true and statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false.
keyfact: Kuchipudi: Andhra Pradesh village, Tarangam on a brass plate, with the Natyashastra as common textual basis.
question:

3. Tarangam, in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate, is a well-known item in this tradition.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises eight classical dance forms.

detail: Spearman's rank correlation coefficient is r = 1 - 6Σd²/[n(n²-1)]. With n=10 and Σd²=33, the denominator is 10 × 99 = 990 and the numerator is 6 × 33 = 198. So r = 1 - 198/990 = 1 - 0.2 = 0.80. A common error is using n³ instead of n(n²-1), or forgetting to subtract from 1, which gives 0.20. Another slip is to use n=10 as n²-1=9, giving 1 - 198/90, which is negative. The coefficient lies between -1 and +1; it equals +1 for identical rankings and -1 for exactly reversed ones, where Σd² = n(n²-1)/3. A value of 0.80 shows strong agreement between the two examiners.
explanations: 0.67 does not follow from the formula with the given data.
0.85 would need Σd² of about 24.75, not 33.
0.90 would need Σd² of 16.5, not 33.
keyfact: Spearman r = 1 - 6Σd²/[n(n²-1)].
question: Ten candidates are ranked by two examiners. The sum of squares of the differences in ranks is 33 and there are no ties. What is Spearman's rank correlation coefficient?
related: Spearman's r lies between -1 and +1.
With tied ranks, a correction factor of m(m²-1)/12 is added to Σd² for each tie group of size m.
For perfectly reversed ranks, Σd² = n(n²-1)/3.
Rank correlation suits qualitative or ordinal data.
subject: Statistics
summary: r = 1 - 6Σd²/[n(n²-1)] = 1 - 198/990 = 0.80. The formula applies directly because there are no tied ranks.

detail: Pahari painting developed in the hill states of the western Himalaya (Basohli, Guler, Kangra, Chamba and others) between the 17th and 19th centuries. Basohli was the earlier, bold style, while Kangra, which flourished under patrons such as Sansar Chand, is known for delicate, lyrical treatment, especially of Radha-Krishna and Gita Govinda themes. Elimination: the Mysore school is a south Indian tradition associated with the Wodeyars and later Tanjore-Mysore styles, not Akbar's court. The Company school developed under British patronage and showed European techniques, so describing it as purely Rajput is wrong. The Deccani school flourished under the Deccan sultanates such as Ahmadnagar, Bijapur and Golconda, not in Gujarat under Jain monks (that is the Jain or western Indian manuscript tradition).

Incorrect: The Mysore school is a southern tradition and unrelated to Akbar's court.

detail: The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017 raised paid maternity leave from 12 to 26 weeks for a woman with fewer than two surviving children. At most 8 weeks of this can be taken before the expected delivery. For a woman with two or more surviving children, the entitlement is 12 weeks, of which not more than 6 weeks may precede delivery. The amendment also gave 12 weeks to an adopting mother (child under three months) and to a commissioning mother, counted from the date the child is handed over. It made a crèche mandatory in establishments with 50 or more employees and allowed the woman four visits a day to the crèche. It also allowed work from home after maternity leave, by mutual agreement, where the nature of the work permits. To eliminate options, spot that statement 3 uses the wrong threshold (30 instead of 50). That rules out every option containing statement 3, leaving (a).

detail: Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council to inquire into and advise on disputes between States, to investigate subjects of common interest, and to make recommendations for better policy coordination. The power is discretionary, which is why a Council exists only because the President chose to create it. The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission by a Presidential Order. The Prime Minister is Chairman, and members include Chief Ministers of all States, Chief Ministers of Union Territories with legislatures, administrators of other UTs, and six Union Cabinet Ministers nominated by the PM. detail: Article 94 provides that the Speaker may be removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the House. The Speaker has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings, and to vote in the first instance on the resolution, but not in case of equality of votes. At least 14 days' notice of the resolution is required under Article 94(c). So Statement-I is false because it says he presides and cannot vote, which reverses both points. detail: REITs and InvITs are collective investment vehicles regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (Real Estate Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014 and the SEBI (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) Regulations, 2014. They are structured as trusts, not companies, and they issue units, not shares. REITs pool money to own income-generating real estate such as offices and malls, while InvITs do the same for infrastructure assets such as roads and transmission lines. Their units are listed and traded on stock exchanges, which gives investors liquidity. A defining feature is the distribution norm: not less than 90 per cent of net distributable cash flows must be distributed to unitholders, which makes them income-oriented. detail: When the government finances a larger fiscal deficit by borrowing from the domestic market, it increases demand for loanable funds. This pushes up interest rates and makes borrowing costlier for private firms, which reduces private investment and partly offsets the expansionary effect of government spending. The extent of crowding out depends on how fully the economy is employed, how interest-sensitive investment is, and the stance of the central bank. Elimination: option (b) describes a consumption response to tax cuts, not crowding out. Option (c) refers to loss of export competitiveness from currency appreciation, a different concept. Option (d) describes a monetary and trade linkage and has nothing to do with competition for funds between the public and private sectors.

keyfact: Crowding out: government borrowing raises interest rates and lowers private investment.

summary: Crowding out is the reduction in private investment because government borrowing to finance deficits pushes up interest rates. Option (a) states exactly this.

detail: In pure ALOHA a frame can collide with others sent in a vulnerable period of two frame times. Throughput S = G e^(-2G), which peaks at G = 0.5, giving S = 1/(2e) ≈ 0.184. Slotted ALOHA halves the vulnerable period, so S = G e^(-G) with a peak of 1/e ≈ 0.368 at G = 1. Frame time is 1 ms, so the channel capacity is 1000 frames per second. Maximum successful throughput = 0.184 x 1000 ≈ 184 frames per second. The link speed of 10 Mbps is not needed once the frame time is given. Option b is the slotted ALOHA value. Option c ignores contention. Option d is double the slotted ALOHA figure and is impossible.
explanations: Correct: 0.184 x 1000 frames per second of capacity gives about 184.
Incorrect: 368 corresponds to slotted ALOHA efficiency (1/e), not pure ALOHA.
Incorrect: 500 would be 50% efficiency, which no ALOHA variant achieves.
Incorrect: 736 exceeds even the slotted ALOHA limit and is not possible.
keyfact: Pure ALOHA max efficiency = 1/(2e) ≈ 18.4%; slotted ALOHA = 1/e ≈ 36.8%.
question: A 10 Mbps shared link uses pure ALOHA. If each frame takes 1 ms to transmit, what is the approximate maximum channel throughput (successful frames per second) achievable, given that the maximum efficiency of pure ALOHA is 1/(2e)?
related: Slotted ALOHA maximum efficiency is 1/e ≈ 36.8% at G = 1
Pure ALOHA vulnerable time is two frame times; slotted ALOHA's is one
CSMA/CD is used in classic wired Ethernet
CSMA/CA is used in IEEE 802.11 Wi-Fi
subject: Computers
summary: The answer is about 184 frames per second. Pure ALOHA has maximum efficiency 1/(2e) ≈ 0.184, and with a 1 ms frame time the channel can carry at most 1000 frames per second, so the maximum is about 184.

detail: Different wavelengths reveal different cosmic phenomena, and the Earth's atmosphere blocks X-rays, gamma rays and most infrared and ultraviolet radiation, so many observatories are placed in space. Fermi studies high-energy gamma-ray sources such as pulsars, blazars and gamma-ray bursts. Chandra, launched in 1999, observes X-rays from hot gas, black-hole environments and supernova remnants. Spitzer, which operated from 2003 to 2020, observed in the infrared and revealed dust-shrouded star formation and exoplanet atmospheres. The Event Horizon Telescope is an Earth-sized virtual telescope formed by linking radio dishes through VLBI at about 1.3 mm. It produced the first images of the black holes in M87 and of Sagittarius A*. Only the Spitzer pair is wrongly matched, so three pairs are correct.
