summary: Madhubani painting is traditionally associated with the Mithila region of Bihar. The other pairings are wrong because Warli is Maharashtra, Kalamkari is Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and Pattachitra is Odisha and West Bengal.

detail: In August 1932 Ramsay MacDonald's Communal Award granted separate electorates to the Depressed Classes. Gandhi, then in Yerwada Jail, opposed this as a division of the Hindu community and began a fast unto death on 20 September 1932. Negotiations between Dr B.R. Ambedkar and Congress leaders produced the Poona Pact, signed on 24 September 1932. It abandoned separate electorates but increased the reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in the provincial legislatures, from 71 in the Award to 148, within the general electorate. Since the fast directly produced the Pact, Statement-II is the cause that explains Statement-I, so option (a) is correct and the other options fail.
explanations: Right: both statements are correct and the fast led directly to the Pact.
Wrong: Statement-II is not unrelated to Statement-I; it explains it.
Wrong: Statement-II is correct as well.
Wrong: Statement-I is correct.
keyfact: Poona Pact (24 Sept 1932): reserved seats in general electorate instead of separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: The Poona Pact of 1932 replaced the separate electorates for the Depressed Classes proposed in the Communal Award with reserved seats in the general electorate.
Statement-II: Gandhi undertook a fast unto death in Yerwada Jail in protest against the Communal Award.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: The Communal Award was announced in August 1932.
Ambedkar represented the Depressed Classes at Poona.
Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932.
Reserved seats under the Pact rose from 71 to 148.
subject: Modern History
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. Gandhi's fast against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes led to the Poona Pact, which gave them reserved seats in the general electorate.

detail: In consignment accounting, an abnormal loss is a loss that is not expected in the normal course of business, such as a loss from fire or accident. It is valued at the cost of goods plus the proportionate non-recurring expenses incurred up to the point at which the loss occurs. The loss is credited to the Consignment Account and debited to the Abnormal Loss Account. It is not included in the stock valuation. Here the loss occurred in transit, so only the expenses incurred up to that point (the consignor's freight and insurance) are loaded. The consignee's godown expenses of ₹500 are incurred after arrival and are excluded. Total cost up to the point of loss = 10,000 + 1,000 = ₹11,000 for 100 units. The loss of 10 units = 11,000 × 10/100 = ₹1,100. Option a ignores freight, while c and d wrongly include some or all of the godown expenses.
explanations: ₹1,000 is only the invoice cost of 10 units, ignoring the proportionate freight and insurance.
Correct. (10,000 + 1,000) × 10/100 = ₹1,100. Godown expenses after arrival are excluded.
₹1,150 wrongly adds the godown expenses of ₹500 proportionately, although the loss occurred before arrival.
₹1,050 arises from wrongly loading only part of the expenses; it matches no valuation rule.
keyfact: Abnormal loss in consignment is valued at cost plus only the expenses incurred up to the point of loss.
question: A consignor sent 100 units to a consignee at a cost of ₹100 per unit. The consignor paid freight and insurance of ₹1,000 up to the consignee's godown. On arrival, the consignee paid godown expenses of ₹500. During transit, 10 units were lost by an accident, which is an abnormal loss. For the Consignment Account, the value at which the abnormal loss will be credited is:
related: Normal loss is absorbed in the cost of the remaining goods, increasing the per-unit cost.
Abnormal loss is credited to the Consignment Account and debited to Abnormal Loss Account.
Any insurance claim admitted reduces the Abnormal Loss Account, and the balance is transferred to Profit and Loss Account.
Unsold stock is valued at cost plus proportionate expenses, including the consignee's non-recurring expenses up to the godown.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The abnormal loss is ₹1,100. It is valued at cost plus the proportionate expenses incurred up to the point of loss, which are the goods cost and the freight.

detail: Under the EPF Scheme, the employer's 12% contribution is split: 3.67% goes to the EPF account and 8.33% goes to the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995. The pensionable salary for EPS is capped at ₹15,000 per month, so the maximum EPS contribution is based on that ceiling. The Central Government makes a separate contribution of 1.16% of the pensionable salary. The employee makes no direct contribution to the pension fund, since their 12% goes entirely to the EPF account. Elimination: option (b) is wrong because the employee does not contribute to EPS. Option (c) confuses the EPS ceiling with the ESI wage ceiling of ₹21,000. Option (d) confuses the Central Government's 1.16% with the employer's 3.67% share that goes to the EPF account.
explanations: Correct. The Government's contribution to the Pension Fund is 1.16% of pensionable salary.
Incorrect. The employee's contribution goes entirely to the EPF account, not to EPS.
Incorrect. The pensionable salary ceiling is ₹15,000. ₹21,000 is the ESI wage ceiling.
Incorrect. 3.67% is the employer's share going to the EPF account, not a Government contribution.
keyfact: EPS-95: employer 8.33% on pensionable salary up to ₹15,000, plus Central Government 1.16%.
options: The Central Government contributes 1.16% of the pensionable salary towards the Pension Fund
The employee contributes an additional 1.16% of wages towards the Pension Fund
The pensionable salary ceiling for EPS is ₹21,000 per month
The Central Government contributes 3.67% of wages to the Pension Fund
question: With reference to the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS), 1995 under the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Employer's 12% is split into 3.67% to EPF and 8.33% to EPS.
The pensionable salary ceiling is ₹15,000 per month.
Ten years of eligible service is required for a monthly member pension.
Superannuation pension is payable at age 58.
Early pension can be taken from age 50 with a reduction.
subject: Social Security
summary: The answer is option (a). Under EPS-95, the employer's 8.33% of wages (on a pensionable salary capped at ₹15,000) goes to the Pension Fund. The Central Government adds 1.16% of the pensionable salary.

detail: The Narmada rises near Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows west through a linear rift (graben) valley bounded by the Vindhyas to the north and the Satpuras to the south, forming Dhuandhar Falls near Jabalpur and ending in the Gulf of Khambhat with an estuary rather than a delta. The Tapi also flows in a rift valley, south of the Satpuras, into the Arabian Sea. The Godavari, Mahanadi and Krishna follow the general eastward slope of the peninsular plateau and drain into the Bay of Bengal, mostly forming deltas. Elimination: any east-flowing river can be removed at once, leaving the Narmada.
explanations: Wrong: the Godavari flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
Correct: the Narmada flows west in a rift valley between the Vindhyas and Satpuras.
Wrong: the Mahanadi flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
Wrong: the Krishna flows east into the Bay of Bengal.
keyfact: Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries, not deltas.
question: Which one of the following rivers of India is correctly described as flowing into a rift valley, between the Vindhyan and Satpura ranges, before draining into the Arabian Sea?
related: The Narmada and Tapi are the major west-flowing peninsular rivers that form estuaries.
Amarkantak is the source of the Narmada and the Son.
Dhuandhar Falls is on the Narmada near Jabalpur.
The Tapi rises near Multai in Madhya Pradesh.
subject: Geography
summary: The Narmada flows westward through a rift valley between the Vindhyan and Satpura ranges and drains into the Arabian Sea. Godavari, Mahanadi and Krishna are east-flowing and drain into the Bay of Bengal.

detail: The Indian Councils Act 1909 was named after Lord Morley (Secretary of State) and Lord Minto (Viceroy). It enlarged the central and provincial legislative councils, allowed discussion of the budget and the asking of supplementary questions, and for the first time appointed an Indian, S. P. Sinha, to the Viceroy's Executive Council. Its most controversial feature was the separate electorate for Muslims. Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced by the Government of India Act 1919. The Federal Court and provincial autonomy came under the Government of India Act 1935, and a bicameral central legislature came with the 1919 Act.
explanations: Correct: separate electorates for Muslims were introduced in 1909.
Wrong: dyarchy came with the 1919 Act.
Wrong: the Federal Court was set up under the 1935 Act, in 1937.
Wrong: a bicameral Centre came with the 1919 Act, and elections remained indirect in 1909.
keyfact: 1909 Act = separate electorates for Muslims; 1919 = dyarchy; 1935 = Federal Court.
options: Introduction of separate electorates for Muslims
Introduction of dyarchy in the provinces
Establishment of the Federal Court of India
Creation of a bicameral legislature at the Centre with direct elections
question: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) is associated with which one of the following provisions?
related: S. P. Sinha became the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council in 1909.
The Government of India Act 1919 introduced dyarchy.
The Government of India Act 1935 provided for an All-India Federation and a Federal Court.
Lord Minto is called the father of communal electorate.
subject: Indian Freedom Struggle & Culture
summary: The Act of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims, which is why Minto is often called the father of communal electorate. Dyarchy, the Federal Court and a bicameral Centre came later.

detail: Article 263 provides that the President may by order establish a council to inquire into and advise upon disputes between States, investigate subjects of common interest, and make recommendations for better coordination of policy and action. The wording is permissive, so the Council is not a mandatory permanent body, and its composition is fixed by the order rather than the Constitution. The Sarkaria Commission recommended a permanent Inter-State Council, and it was set up in 1990 through a Presidential Order. The Prime Minister chairs it, and its members include the Chief Ministers of States and Union Territories with legislatures, the Administrators of other Union Territories, and six Union Cabinet Ministers nominated by the Prime Minister. It is advisory and its recommendations are not binding. Elimination: a, b and d each contain a clear factual error.
explanations: Wrong: Article 263 is enabling, so the Council is not mandatory and its composition is set by the order.
Wrong: the Prime Minister chairs it, and its recommendations are not binding.
Correct: it was set up in 1990 under Article 263 by a Presidential Order and is advisory.
Wrong: it was created by a Presidential Order, not by an Act of Parliament, and has no link to the Finance Commission.
keyfact: The Inter-State Council (Article 263, set up 1990) is advisory, chaired by the Prime Minister, and not a mandatory constitutional body.
options: It is a permanent constitutional body whose composition is prescribed in the text of the Constitution.
It is chaired by the President of India and its decisions are binding on the Union and the States.
It was established under Article 263 by a Presidential Order in 1990 and performs an advisory role.
It was created by an Act of Parliament on the recommendation of the Finance Commission.
question: With reference to the Inter-State Council in India, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the Inter-State Council.
A Standing Committee of the Council is chaired by the Union Home Minister.
Article 262 deals with adjudication of inter-State river water disputes.
Zonal Councils were created under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
The Sarkaria Commission reported in 1988.
subject: Polity
summary: Option c is correct. Article 263 lets the President establish such a council if public interest requires, and it was set up by a Presidential Order in 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation. It only investigates, discusses and recommends.

detail: A no-confidence motion is moved against the entire Council of Ministers in the Lok Sabha under the Rules of Procedure. Leave is granted if at least 50 members support it, and no reasons need be stated. A censure motion differs because it must state the reasons for its adoption. It can be moved against the whole Council, a group of ministers or an individual minister, and it can be moved for failure to act or for specific policies. If a censure motion against the Council is passed, the government is not constitutionally bound to resign, though conventions vary. An adjournment motion draws attention to a definite matter of urgent public importance. It is available only in the Lok Sabha, it needs 50 members to rise in support, and it carries an element of censure. Elimination logic: spotting that pair 1 is wrong while pair 3 is right immediately removes 'None' and 'All three'. Pair 2's accuracy then separates 'Only one pair' from 'Only two pairs'.
explanations: Wrong: two pairs are correct, not one.
Correct: pairs 2 and 3 are correctly matched, and pair 1 is incorrect.
Wrong: pair 1 is incorrect because a no-confidence motion needs no stated grounds.
Wrong: pairs 2 and 3 are correct.
keyfact: No-confidence motions need no stated grounds, while censure motions must state reasons, and only the Lok Sabha can use adjournment motions.
question:
Consider the following pairs of parliamentary motions and their features:

Motion : Feature
1. No-confidence motion : It must set out the grounds on which it is based in order to be admitted in the Lok Sabha
2. Censure motion : It must state the reasons for its adoption and may be moved against an individual minister
3. Adjournment motion : It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha and needs the support of at least 50 members for leave to be granted
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
related: A no-confidence motion needs the support of 50 members for leave to be introduced.
The Rajya Sabha cannot remove the Council of Ministers because the Council is collectively responsible only to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)).
A calling attention motion is an Indian innovation, introduced in 1954, and is available in both Houses.
A closure motion is a device to cut short debate on a matter.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: A no-confidence motion need not state any reasons or grounds, unlike a censure motion.
2 — Correct: A censure motion must state its reasons and may be against the Council, a group of ministers or an individual minister.
3 — Correct: The adjournment motion is a Lok Sabha-only device that needs the support of 50 members, and it interrupts regular business. It also carries an element of censure on the government.
subject: Polity
summary: Pairs 2 and 3 are correctly matched, so 'Only two pairs' is the answer. A no-confidence motion need not state any grounds, whereas a censure motion must state its reasons.

detail: Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission. Under the proviso to Article 324(5), the CEC cannot be removed except in like manner and on like grounds as a Supreme Court Judge, that is, by a special majority resolution of both Houses on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC. Panchayat and Municipality elections are conducted by separate State Election Commissions (Articles 243K and 243ZA). The Constitution leaves the number of Election Commissioners to the President, and the 2023 Act now governs appointments through a Selection Committee, not the CJI alone.
explanations: Correct: proviso to Article 324(5) gives the CEC the same removal protection as a Supreme Court Judge.

Incorrect: appointment is by the President under the 2023 Act on the recommendation of a Selection Committee (PM, a Union Minister and the Leader of Opposition/largest opposition party leader), not on the sole recommendation of the CJI.
Incorrect: local body elections are conducted by State Election Commissions.
Incorrect: Article 324(2) leaves the number to be fixed by the President; it is not fixed by the Constitution.
keyfact: The CEC is removable like a Supreme Court Judge; Election Commissioners only on the CEC's recommendation.
options: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court
The Election Commissioners are appointed by the President on the sole recommendation of the Chief Justice of India
The Election Commission of India conducts elections to Panchayats and Municipalities in the States
The Constitution fixes the number of Election Commissioners at three
question: With reference to the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements regarding the Election Commission of India is correct?
related: Article 324 deals with the Election Commission.
State Election Commissioners are appointed by the Governor.
Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation.
The Election Commission does not conduct elections to the Rajya Sabha's nominated seats, as these are nominated by the President.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: The Chief Election Commissioner enjoys the same removal protection as a Supreme Court Judge under the proviso to Article 324(5). This safeguards the independence of the office.

detail: Under parliamentary practice, prorogation does not affect pending Bills, which can be taken up when the House meets again. On dissolution of the Lok Sabha, Bills pending in the Lok Sabha lapse, and also Bills passed by the Lok Sabha but pending in the Rajya Sabha. A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha but not passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse. A Bill passed by both Houses and awaiting assent does not lapse. A Bill returned by the President for reconsideration also does not lapse. Statement-II says only dissolution causes lapse for Bills pending in the Lok Sabha; the Lok Sabha Bill could also be withdrawn or rejected, which end it as well. Hence Statement-II is not correct as framed.
explanations: Incorrect: Statement-II is not correct as framed.
Incorrect: Statement-II is not correct.
Correct: Statement-I is true and Statement-II is overstated.
Incorrect: Statement-I is true.
keyfact: Prorogation does not lapse pending Bills; dissolution of the Lok Sabha does.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha does not lapse on the prorogation of the House.
Statement-II: Only the dissolution of the Lok Sabha causes a Bill pending in it to lapse.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha but not passed by the Lok Sabha does not lapse.
A Bill passed by both Houses and awaiting assent does not lapse on dissolution.
A Bill on which a joint sitting has been notified does not lapse.
Prorogation is by the President; dissolution applies only to the Lok Sabha.
subject: Polity
summary: Statement-I is correct since prorogation does not end pending Bills. Statement-II is incorrect because it is too absolute: a Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on dissolution, but a Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and pending in the Rajya Sabha also lapses on dissolution, and the claim that dissolution alone is the cause is misleading.

detail: The EDLI Scheme, 1976 provides life insurance cover to members of the EPF scheme without any insurance premium. It is financed by the employer's contribution of 0.5% of monthly pay, calculated on wages up to the statutory ceiling of Rs 15,000. Members pay nothing, and the Central Government does not contribute to the EDLI Fund. On the death of a member while in service, the nominee or family receives the assurance benefit, which is capped at Rs 7 lakh. To eliminate: statements 2 and 3 wrongly add contributions from the member and the Central Government. This leaves only 1 and 4. Candidates often confuse EDLI with EPS, where the Central Government contributes 1.16% of wages.
explanations: Correct. Statements 1 and 4 are the only correct ones.
Wrong. Statement 2 is incorrect because members do not contribute.
Wrong. Statement 3 is incorrect because the Central Government does not contribute to EDLI.
Wrong. Statement 2 is incorrect, so this combination fails.
keyfact: EDLI is funded only by the employer at 0.5% of wages up to Rs 15,000, with a maximum benefit of Rs 7 lakh.
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) Scheme, 1976:
1. The employer contributes 0.5 per cent of the monthly pay (basic wages plus dearness allowance), subject to the prescribed wage ceiling.
2. The member also contributes 0.5 per cent of pay towards the scheme.
3. The Central Government makes a regular contribution to the EDLI Fund.
4. The maximum assurance benefit payable under the scheme is Rs 7 lakh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: The EDLI Scheme was introduced in 1976 under the EPF & MP Act, 1952.
EDLI is a free insurance cover for EPF members, with the employer as sole contributor.
The Central Government's regular contribution of 1.16% is to the EPS, not to EDLI.
The wage ceiling for EPF coverage is Rs 15,000 per month.
statements: 1 — Correct: the employer pays 0.5% of pay, subject to the wage ceiling.
2 — Incorrect: members make no contribution to EDLI.
3 — Incorrect: the Central Government does not contribute to the EDLI Fund; its regular contribution is to EPS.
4 — Correct: the maximum assurance benefit is Rs 7 lakh.
subject: Insurance
summary: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. EDLI is financed by the employer only, and the maximum assurance benefit is Rs 7 lakh.

detail: The Nasik prashasti of Gautami Balashri is the main epigraphic source for Gautamiputra Satakarni. It was issued in the reign of her grandson Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and describes the king as destroyer of the Shakas, Pahlavas and Yavanas, and as the one who uprooted the Khakharata (Kshaharata) lineage of Nahapana. Satavahana coinage was mostly lead, potin, copper and some silver, with no large gold currency. Gold was circulating mainly in Kushana territory. Ushavadata, Nahapana's son-in-law, issued his own Nasik records about Shaka-Kshaharata donations, so he cannot be the author of the Satavahana prashasti. Pratishthana (modern Paithan) lies on the Godavari, not the Krishna. Eliminating options (b), (c) and (d) leaves (a).
explanations: Correct: the Nasik prashasti of Gautami Balashri describes these victories and the restoration of the dynasty.
Incorrect: Satavahana coinage was mainly lead, potin, copper and some silver; gold dinaras were a Kushana feature.
Incorrect: Ushavadata's inscriptions belong to the Shaka-Kshaharata side; the Satavahana prashasti was issued by Gautami Balashri.
Incorrect: Pratishthana (Paithan) is on the Godavari, not the Krishna.
keyfact: Nasik prashasti: issued by Gautami Balashri, praising Gautamiputra Satakarni as destroyer of Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas.
options: The Nasik cave inscription issued by Gautami Balashri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni's successor, credits him with destroying the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas and restoring the glory of the Satavahana family
The Satavahanas issued gold coins (dinaras) in very large numbers as their principal currency, modelled on Kushana issues
The Nasik inscription recording Gautamiputra Satakarni's victories was issued by Ushavadata, son-in-law of Nahapana
Pratishthana, the traditional Satavahana capital, was located on the banks of the Krishna river
question: With reference to the Satavahana dynasty, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana, and many of Nahapana's silver coins were restruck by him.
Gautami Balashri's Nasik inscription is written in Prakrit in the Brahmi script.
Hala is credited with compiling the Gathasaptashati in Prakrit.
Amaravati and Nagarjunakonda were centres of Buddhist art in the Satavahana-Ikshvaku region.
Satavahana kings used matronymics such as Gautamiputra and Vasishthiputra.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Option (a) is correct. The Nasik prashasti, issued by Gautami Balashri, records Gautamiputra Satakarni's victories over the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas and his restoration of the Satavahana lineage. The other options contain factual errors about coinage, authorship and geography.

detail: Biogeochemical cycles are either gaseous, with the atmosphere or ocean as the reservoir (carbon, nitrogen), or sedimentary, with the Earth's crust as the reservoir (phosphorus, sulphur in part, calcium). Phosphorus is released from phosphate rocks by weathering and erosion, taken up by plants as phosphate, passed to consumers, and returned by decomposition. Some is lost to ocean sediments and returns to land only over geological time through uplift. Unlike nitrogen, there is no biological fixation from the air, because phosphorus has no abundant stable gaseous form. Excess phosphate in runoff drives eutrophication. To eliminate options, reject (a) and (d) because they assume an atmospheric phase, and reject (c) because phosphorus does not cycle through evaporation.
explanations: Wrong: the atmosphere is not a significant reservoir, and no bacteria fix atmospheric phosphorus.
Right: it is a sedimentary cycle with rock as the reservoir and release through weathering.
Wrong: phosphorus does not return to land through evaporation and rainfall. The ocean is mainly a sink.
Wrong: phosphorus is not a gaseous cycle, and volcanic phosphine is not its principal source.
keyfact: Phosphorus is a sedimentary cycle: rock reservoir, weathering release, no significant atmospheric phase.
options: The atmosphere is its main reservoir, and nitrogen-fixing-type bacteria convert atmospheric phosphorus into usable forms
Its main reservoir is rock, from which phosphate is released slowly by weathering, and it lacks a significant gaseous phase
Its main reservoir is the ocean surface, from which phosphorus is returned to land mainly through evaporation and rainfall
It is a gaseous cycle in which volcanic eruptions are the principal source of phosphine for plants
question: Which one of the following statements best describes the phosphorus cycle?
related: Carbon and nitrogen cycles are gaseous cycles; phosphorus is sedimentary.
Phosphate runoff is a major driver of eutrophication.
Guano and phosphate rock are major natural phosphorus stores.
Phosphorus is a component of DNA, RNA, ATP and cell membranes.
subject: Environment
summary: Phosphorus is a sedimentary cycle with rocks as the main reservoir and no significant atmospheric component. Weathering releases phosphate, which plants absorb.

detail: The 2025 FIDE Women's World Cup was held in Batumi, Georgia, in July 2025. The final was an all-Indian affair between Divya Deshmukh and Koneru Humpy, decided in tie-breaks, and Divya won. She was an International Master at the start. Winning the event gave her the Grandmaster title directly, and she became India's 88th Grandmaster, so she was not a GM beforehand. The trap in statement 3 is the assumption that a World Cup finalist must already hold the title. Statements 1 and 2 are both correct, which removes 'None' and 'Only one'. Statement 3 is false, which removes 'All three'.
explanations: Wrong: at least two statements are correct.
Wrong: statements 1 and 2 are both correct, so one is too few.
Wrong: statement 3 is false.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statement 3 is false.
keyfact: Divya Deshmukh won the 2025 Women's Chess World Cup in Batumi and earned the GM title through the win.
question:
With reference to the Women's Chess World Cup 2025, consider the following statements:
1. Divya Deshmukh defeated Koneru Humpy in the final.
2. The tournament was held in Batumi, Georgia.
3. Divya Deshmukh was already a Grandmaster before the tournament began.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Divya Deshmukh became the first Indian woman to win the Women's Chess World Cup.
The final was between two Indians, Divya Deshmukh and Koneru Humpy.
D. Gukesh won the 2024 World Chess Championship in Singapore.
The Women's World Cup winner earns a spot in the Women's Candidates Tournament.
statements: 1 — Correct: Divya Deshmukh won the final against Koneru Humpy.
2 — Correct: The event took place in Batumi, Georgia.
3 — Incorrect: She was an International Master and gained the Grandmaster title through this win.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. Divya Deshmukh beat Koneru Humpy in the final in Batumi, and her win earned her the Grandmaster title, so she was not one before the event.

detail: The ESI scheme covers employees earning up to Rs 21,000 per month, raised to Rs 25,000 for persons with disability. Since July 2019 the combined contribution is 4 per cent of wages, split into 3.25 per cent by the employer and 0.75 per cent by the employee. Before that it was 4.75 per cent and 1.75 per cent, a total of 6.5 per cent, which is the trap in statement 2. Employees with an average daily wage up to Rs 176 are exempt from paying the employee contribution, and the employer pays only the employer share on their wages. Eliminating statement 2 removes options (c) and (d). Option (a) is eliminated because statement 3 is correct.
explanations: Wrong: statement 3 is also correct, so 1 alone is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are accurate and statement 2 cites the old rates.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect and statement 1 is left out.
Wrong: statement 2 is incorrect, so all three cannot be correct.
keyfact: ESI: wage ceiling Rs 21,000 (Rs 25,000 for disabled); contribution 3.25% employer plus 0.75% employee.
question:
With reference to the Employees' State Insurance (ESI) scheme, consider the following statements:
1. Employees drawing wages up to Rs 21,000 per month are covered, and the ceiling is Rs 25,000 for persons with disability.
2. The employer's contribution is 4.75 per cent and the employee's contribution is 1.75 per cent of wages.
3. Employees whose average daily wage is up to Rs 176 are exempt from paying their share of the contribution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Present ESI contribution is 3.25% (employer) plus 0.75% (employee), 4% in total.
The earlier rates were 4.75% (employer) and 1.75% (employee), a total of 6.5%.
The ESI wage ceiling is Rs 21,000 per month.
The ESI Corporation is the statutory body that administers the scheme.
The ESI Act, 1948 is subsumed into the Code on Social Security, 2020.
statements: 1 — Correct: the wage ceiling is Rs 21,000 per month, or Rs 25,000 for persons with disability.
2 — Incorrect: the present rates are 3.25 per cent (employer) and 0.75 per cent (employee), not 4.75 and 1.75.
3 — Correct: employees with an average daily wage up to Rs 176 are exempt from the employee contribution.
subject: Social Security
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 gives the old rates (4.75% and 1.75%), which were replaced by 3.25% for the employer and 0.75% for the employee, 4% in total.

detail: Section 139(6) of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that the first auditor of a company, other than a government company, is appointed by the Board within 30 days of registration. If the Board fails, the members must be informed and they appoint within 90 days at an extraordinary general meeting. The first auditor holds office until the conclusion of the first annual general meeting. Subsequent auditors are appointed by members for a term of five consecutive years under Section 139(1), subject to ratification rules as amended. The five-year term therefore does not apply to the first auditor, and the end of the first financial year is irrelevant.
explanations: Correct: Section 139(6) fixes the tenure until the first AGM.
Incorrect: the term does not run to the second AGM.
Incorrect: the five-year term applies to auditors appointed by members at an AGM.
Incorrect: tenure is tied to the AGM, not the financial year-end.
keyfact: First auditor: appointed by Board, holds office until the first AGM.
options: Until the conclusion of the first annual general meeting
Until the conclusion of the second annual general meeting
For five years from the date of appointment
Until the end of the first financial year
question: Under the Companies Act, 2013, which one of the following is the maximum period for which a company's first auditor, appointed by the Board of Directors, holds office?
related: Board appoints the first auditor within 30 days of incorporation.
If the Board fails, members appoint within 90 days.
Section 139(1) governs five-year terms for later auditors.
Section 141 deals with auditor eligibility and disqualifications.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: The first auditor, appointed by the Board within 30 days of registration, holds office until the conclusion of the first annual general meeting. After that, the members appoint the auditor at the AGM.
topic: Company audit: appointment of first auditor

detail: The Unified Pension Scheme, notified in January 2025 and effective from 1 April 2025, is an option for central government employees under the NPS framework. It offers an assured payout of 50 per cent of the average basic pay over the 12 months before superannuation for a minimum of 25 years of qualifying service, proportionately reduced for shorter service of at least 10 years. It also provides an assured family pension of 60 per cent of the employee's payout and an assured minimum payout of ₹10,000 per month on superannuation after at least 10 years of service. The employee contributes 10 per cent of basic pay plus DA, and the government contributes 18.5 per cent. Elimination: (a) gives 40 per cent, (c) gives a 20-year condition, and (d) gives a 14 per cent contribution and denies family pension, all of which are wrong.
explanations: Incorrect. The assured payout is 50 per cent, not 40 per cent.
Correct. This is the assured payout formula of the UPS, with a proportionate payout for 10 to 25 years of service.
Incorrect. The minimum of ₹10,000 per month applies after 10 years of qualifying service.
Incorrect. The employee contribution is 10 per cent, and the UPS includes a family pension of 60 per cent.
keyfact: UPS: 50 per cent of average last-12-month basic pay for 25 years of service, minimum ₹10,000 after 10 years, and 60 per cent family pension.
options: It provides an assured payout of 40 per cent of the average basic pay of the last 12 months for employees with a minimum of 25 years of qualifying service

It provides an assured payout of 50 per cent of the average basic pay drawn over the last 12 months before superannuation for a minimum qualifying service of 25 years, with a proportionate payout for service between 10 and 25 years
It assures a minimum pension of ₹10,000 per month only after 20 years of qualifying service
It requires an employee contribution of 14 per cent and makes no provision for family pension
question: With reference to the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) introduced for central government employees under the National Pension System framework, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: UPS was notified in January 2025 and effective from 1 April 2025
Assured minimum payout under the UPS is ₹10,000 per month after 10 years of service
Assured family pension under the UPS is 60 per cent of the employee's payout
Government contribution under the UPS is 18.5 per cent
Payouts under the UPS are inflation-indexed through dearness relief
subject: Social Security
summary: Under the UPS, effective from 1 April 2025, the assured payout is 50 per cent of the average basic pay of the last 12 months for at least 25 years of qualifying service, and proportionately less for 10 to 25 years.

detail: Under Article 249, a Rajya Sabha resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of members present and voting declares that it is necessary or expedient in the national interest for Parliament to legislate on a State List matter. The resolution remains in force for up to one year and can be renewed. Laws so made cease to have effect six months after the resolution expires. Article 250 applies to legislation on State List subjects during a National Emergency. Article 252 applies when two or more State Legislatures request Parliament to legislate. Article 253 gives Parliament power to legislate to implement international treaties and agreements.
explanations: Correct: Article 249 provides for legislation on State subjects in the national interest on the basis of a Rajya Sabha resolution.
Wrong: Article 250 applies during a Proclamation of Emergency.
Wrong: Article 252 applies on the request of State Legislatures.
Wrong: Article 253 relates to international agreements.
keyfact: Article 249: Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds of members present and voting lets Parliament legislate on State List subjects.
question: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India empowers Parliament to make laws on a subject in the State List if the Rajya Sabha has declared by a resolution that it is necessary in the national interest?
related: The Article 249 resolution lasts up to one year and can be renewed.
Laws under Article 249 lapse six months after the resolution ceases.
Article 250 covers legislation during Emergency.
Article 252 covers legislation by consent of States.
subject: Polity
summary: Article 249 is correct. It permits Parliament to legislate on a State List subject if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by two-thirds of members present and voting.

detail: Quo warranto means by what authority; it tests the legality of a person's claim to a public office. The office must be public, substantive and created by statute or the Constitution, and it is not available for ministerial or private offices. Certiorari and prohibition are issued against judicial and quasi-judicial bodies, not against purely administrative or ministerial acts. Prohibition is issued during proceedings to stop a lower court from exceeding jurisdiction, while mandamus commands performance of a public duty. Mandamus generally does not lie against private individuals, with limited exceptions.
explanations: Incorrect: certiorari does not lie against administrative or ministerial acts.
Correct: this is the established scope of quo warranto.
Incorrect: it describes mandamus, whereas prohibition stops a lower court from exceeding jurisdiction.
Incorrect: mandamus generally does not lie against private individuals.
keyfact: Quo warranto requires a public, substantive office created by statute or the Constitution.
options: Writ of certiorari can be issued against purely administrative or ministerial actions
Writ of quo warranto can be issued only in respect of a public office of a substantive character created by statute or the Constitution
Writ of prohibition can be issued by a higher court to compel a lower court to perform its duty
Writ of mandamus can be issued against a private individual in all cases
question: With reference to the writs that the Supreme Court and High Courts can issue under the Constitution of India, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for Fundamental Rights.
Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for Fundamental Rights and other purposes.
Habeas corpus means to have the body.
Certiorari is issued after a decision and prohibition during proceedings.
subject: Polity
summary: Option (b) is correct: quo warranto lies only where the office is public and substantive, created by statute or the Constitution. The other options misstate the scope of certiorari, prohibition and mandamus.

detail: Justice Surya Kant took oath as the 53rd CJI on 24 November 2025, succeeding Justice B.R. Gavai, who held the office from May to November 2025 and was the first Buddhist and the second Dalit CJI. Under Article 124(2) the President appoints Supreme Court judges, and by convention the senior-most judge is appointed CJI on the outgoing CJI's recommendation. Under Article 124(2) a Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65. High Court judges retire at 62 under Article 217. Statement 3 therefore confuses the two ages. Eliminating it removes options (b) and (d), and statement 1 being true removes option (a).
explanations: Incorrect: statement 2 is also true, so this is incomplete.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false and statement 1 is omitted.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are true and statement 3 is false.
Incorrect: statement 3 gives the High Court retirement age, not the Supreme Court's.
keyfact: Surya Kant is the 53rd CJI from 24 November 2025; Supreme Court judges retire at 65.
question:
Consider the following statements about the Chief Justice of India (CJI):
1. Justice Surya Kant was sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India in November 2025.
2. His predecessor, Justice B.R. Gavai, was the first Buddhist to hold the office of CJI.
3. A Supreme Court judge, including the CJI, retires on attaining the age of 62 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Surya Kant succeeded B.R. Gavai on 24 November 2025.
Gavai succeeded Sanjiv Khanna in May 2025.
Article 124 deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.
Supreme Court judges retire at 65 and High Court judges at 62.
statements: 1 — Correct: Surya Kant became the 53rd CJI in November 2025.
2 — Correct: Justice B.R. Gavai was the first Buddhist CJI.
3 — Incorrect: Supreme Court judges retire at 65; 62 is the High Court age.
subject: Current Affairs
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Supreme Court judges retire at 65, not 62, so statement 3 is wrong.

detail: Page size 4 KB = 2^12, so the offset uses 12 bits. A 32-bit address leaves 20 bits for page numbers. Each page table page holds 4096 / 4 = 1024 = 2^10 entries. The outer table fits exactly in one page, so it has 1024 entries and uses 10 bits. The remaining 20 - 10 = 10 bits index the inner table. Check: 10 + 10 + 12 = 32. Option (b) confuses the offset with the index. Options (a) and (d) do not sum to 32 with the other fields.
explanations: Incorrect: 8 bits would give 256 entries and the address would not total 32 bits.
Incorrect: 12 bits is the offset width, not the inner index.
Correct: 10 + 10 + 12 = 32 bits.
Incorrect: 9 bits would imply 512 entries per table.
keyfact: Entries per table page = page size / PTE size; bits = log2 of that.
question: A process P in a system with a 32-bit logical address space uses two-level paging. The page size is 4 KB and each page table entry is 4 bytes. If the outer page table is designed to fit exactly into one page, how many bits of the logical address are used to index the inner (second-level) page table?
related: Entries per page = page size / entry size.
Multi-level paging reduces memory used by page tables for sparse address spaces.
Internal fragmentation occurs in paging; external in segmentation.
Inverted page tables have one entry per physical frame.
subject: Computers
summary: The inner page table must also fit in a page (4 KB / 4 B = 1024 entries), so 10 bits index it. Offset is 12 bits, leaving 20 bits, split as 10 and 10.

detail: Western Disturbances are extratropical cyclonic disturbances. They originate over the Mediterranean, Black and Caspian Sea region and are carried eastwards by the subtropical westerly jet stream. They enter India from the north-west in winter and bring rain and snow to the Western Himalaya, Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh. This precipitation supports rabi wheat. The Tropical Easterly Jet is a summer feature of the upper troposphere that is associated with the south-west monsoon. It blows from east to west and plays no role in steering Western Disturbances. To eliminate options, first confirm statement 2, which is well established. Then spot the jet-stream swap in statement 3, which leaves exactly two correct statements.
explanations: Wrong: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statement 3 wrongly names the Tropical Easterly Jet.
Wrong: statement 3 is false, because the steering jet is the subtropical westerly jet.
Wrong: statements 1 and 2 are accurate.
keyfact: Western Disturbances: Mediterranean origin, steered by the subtropical westerly jet, and good for rabi wheat.
question:
With reference to Western Disturbances affecting the Indian subcontinent, consider the following statements:
1. They are extratropical systems that originate over the Mediterranean region and adjoining areas and travel eastwards.
2. Winter precipitation brought by them is beneficial to the rabi crop of wheat in north-western India.
3. Their eastward movement across India is steered mainly by the Tropical Easterly Jet.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Western Disturbances are the main source of winter rain in north-west India.
The Tropical Easterly Jet is associated with the summer monsoon.
The subtropical westerly jet shifts north of the Himalaya in summer.
Winter rain in Tamil Nadu comes from the north-east monsoon, not from Western Disturbances.
statements: 1 — Correct: They are extratropical, originate over the Mediterranean region and move eastwards.
2 — Correct: Winter rain and snow from them benefit rabi wheat in the north-west.
3 — Incorrect: They are steered by the subtropical westerly jet, not the Tropical Easterly Jet, which is a summer monsoon-season feature.

Extra facts: Western Disturbances are most frequent from December to February. They also cause cold waves and fog in the Indo-Gangetic plain when they pass. The Tropical Easterly Jet is linked to the Indian summer monsoon.
subject: Geography
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'. Western Disturbances are extratropical systems steered by the subtropical westerly jet stream, not the Tropical Easterly Jet.

detail: Desert location questions test world map knowledge. The Karakum covers most of Turkmenistan, lying east of the Caspian Sea. The Taklamakan lies in the Tarim Basin of Xinjiang in western China, bounded by the Tian Shan, Kunlun and Pamir ranges. The Namib is a coastal desert along the Atlantic coast of southwestern Africa, mostly in Namibia and extending into Angola and South Africa. The Patagonian Desert lies in southern Argentina, east of the Andes, in their rain shadow. Only pair 2 is wrong. The trap is that the Taklamakan is a Central Asian desert, which tempts candidates to place it in Kazakhstan. If you are sure of any three pairs, the answer follows quickly. Candidates who know that the Taklamakan is a Chinese desert will pick three.
explanations: Wrong. Three pairs are correct, not one.
Wrong. Three pairs are correct, not two.
Correct. Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are right, and only pair 2 is wrong.
Wrong. Pair 2 is incorrect because the Taklamakan is in China.
keyfact: The Taklamakan is in China's Tarim Basin, not in Kazakhstan.
question:
Consider the following pairs of deserts and the countries in which they are (at least partly) located:
1. Karakum Desert : Turkmenistan
2. Taklamakan Desert : Kazakhstan
3. Namib Desert : Namibia
4. Patagonian Desert : Argentina
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
related: The Taklamakan lies in the Tarim Basin, Xinjiang, China.
The Atacama lies in northern Chile and is among the driest places on Earth.
The Gobi is a cold desert in Mongolia and northern China.
The Kyzylkum lies between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya.
statements: 1 — Correct: The Karakum covers most of Turkmenistan.
2 — Incorrect: The Taklamakan is in Xinjiang, China.
3 — Correct: The Namib runs along the coast of Namibia.
4 — Correct: The Patagonian Desert is mostly in Argentina.
Facts: The Gobi lies in Mongolia and China. The Atacama lies mainly in Chile. The Kyzylkum is shared by Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan.
subject: Geography
summary: Only three pairs are correct. The Taklamakan Desert lies in the Tarim Basin of Xinjiang, China, not in Kazakhstan.

detail: Article 358 and Article 359 are often confused. Under Article 358, Article 19 is suspended automatically, but only when the emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression. Since the 44th Amendment, an emergency on the ground of armed rebellion does not trigger it. The suspension covers the whole country and lasts for the duration of the emergency. Article 359 is different. It needs a separate Presidential order, can extend to the whole country or only a part, and suspends the right to move courts for enforcement of the rights named in the order. The rights themselves remain on the books. The 44th Amendment excluded Articles 20 and 21 from any such suspension. To eliminate options, spot that statement 1 and statement 2 are each wrong on one detail, which leaves exactly two correct statements.
explanations: Wrong: more than one statement is correct, because statements 3 and 4 both hold.
Correct: exactly statements 3 and 4 are correct.
Wrong: statements 1 and 2 are both incorrect.
Wrong: statements 1 and 2 are incorrect, so not all four can be correct.
keyfact: Article 358 suspends Article 19 automatically (war or external aggression only); Article 359 needs a Presidential order and can never touch Articles 20 and 21.
question:
With reference to the effect of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights under the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. Article 19 freedoms are suspended automatically under Article 358 whenever a National Emergency is proclaimed, whatever the ground.
2. A Presidential order under Article 359 can suspend the right to move courts for the enforcement of all Fundamental Rights, including Articles 20 and 21.
3. The suspension of Article 19 under Article 358 operates over the entire country, whereas a Presidential order under Article 359 may be confined to a part of the country.
4. An order under Article 359 suspends only the enforcement of the specified rights through courts, not the rights themselves.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: The 44th Amendment (1978) restricted Article 358 to war or external aggression emergencies.
Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
Article 352 emergency proclamation needs approval by both Houses within one month.
Approval or continuation of an Article 352 emergency requires a special majority in each House.
Article 359 orders must be laid before each House of Parliament.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: Article 358 applies only to an emergency on the ground of war or external aggression, not armed rebellion.
2 — Incorrect: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359 after the 44th Amendment.
3 — Correct: Article 358 operates across the country, while an Article 359 order may be limited to part of it.
4 — Correct: Article 359 suspends the remedy of enforcement, not the right itself. Article 358 suspends Article 19 automatically, but Article 359 needs a Presidential order.
subject: Polity
summary: Only statements 3 and 4 are correct. Article 358 applies only to emergencies on the ground of war or external aggression, and Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended under Article 359.

detail: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament (including nominated members) by proportional representation through single transferable vote and secret ballot. Under Article 66(3), the person must be qualified for election as a Rajya Sabha member, in addition to being a citizen aged 35 or above and not holding an office of profit. Under Article 67(b), removal requires a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, with 14 days' notice. The wording of statement 2 matches Article 67(b) closely, and a careful reading makes it correct as well, so this item is flawed.
explanations: Incomplete: omits statement 3, which is correct.
Incomplete: omits statement 1, which is correct.
Incorrect: omits statement 2, which is correct.
All three statements track the Constitution, so this is the accurate choice.
keyfact: All three statements are correct; the Vice-President's electoral college includes nominated MPs.
question:
With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements regarding the Vice-President:
1. The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of all members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated members.
2. The Vice-President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
3. The Vice-President must be a person qualified for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Vice-President must be 35 years or older.
Term is five years (Article 67).
Vice-President acts as President in case of vacancy, for up to six months until a new President is elected.
Disputes on election go to the Supreme Court (Article 71).
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 66(1) includes nominated members in the electoral college.
2 — Correct as per Article 67(b): effective majority in Rajya Sabha and agreement by Lok Sabha (simple majority).
3 — Correct: Article 66(3) requires qualification for Rajya Sabha membership.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong because the removal resolution requires a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha (effective majority), and it is agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority, which makes the wording incomplete rather than wrong; hence the framing matters. See detail.

detail:
Summit venues are a staple of current affairs questions. The 2025 G7 Leaders' Summit was held in Kananaskis, Alberta, Canada, under Canada's presidency. The SCO summit of 2025 was held in Tianjin, China, and the 17th BRICS Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, under Brazil's chairship.

The trap is pair 4. The UN Ocean Conferences have been co-hosted by different countries: the 2022 conference was held in Lisbon, co-hosted by Portugal and Kenya, while the Third conference of June 2025 was held in Nice, France, co-hosted by France and Costa Rica. Candidates who remember Lisbon from 2022 would mark all four correct. When checking such pairs, tie each host to the year, because venues repeat across editions. With three correct pairs, (c) is the answer.
explanations: Incorrect. Three pairs, not one, are correct.
Incorrect. Three pairs, not two, are correct.
Correct. Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct and pair 4 is wrong.
Incorrect. Pair 4 is wrong because the 2025 UN Ocean Conference was in Nice, not Lisbon.
keyfact: The Third UN Ocean Conference (2025) was at Nice, France; Lisbon was the 2022 venue.

detail: An annuity converts a capital sum into a stream of periodic payments, so it protects against longevity risk and is the reverse of term insurance, which protects against early death. An immediate annuity is bought with a single lump sum and payouts begin at once, after one period (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly). A deferred annuity has an accumulation phase, with a single or regular premiums, followed by a deferment period after which payouts begin. A life annuity is paid for as long as the annuitant lives. A certain annuity pays for a fixed term regardless of survival. Option (b) wrongly describes a deferred annuity as immediate. Option (c) describes an annuity certain, not a life annuity. Option (d) describes term assurance, which pays on death.
explanations: Correct. It describes the accumulation phase and the deferment before payouts in a deferred annuity.
Incorrect. This describes a deferred annuity, not an immediate one. An immediate annuity starts payouts shortly after purchase.
Incorrect. This describes an annuity certain. A life annuity is paid for the annuitant's lifetime.
Incorrect. Paying a lump sum on death is term assurance, not an annuity.
keyfact: Annuity = longevity protection; deferred annuity has an accumulation phase, immediate annuity pays at once.
options: In a deferred annuity, the purchase price may be paid as a single premium or in instalments during an accumulation phase, and the annuity instalments begin only after a stipulated deferment period
In an immediate annuity, the annuitant pays premiums over many years and the periodic payouts begin only on reaching a specified later age
A 'life annuity' ceases to be payable only after a fixed number of years, even if the annuitant dies earlier, and is paid to the estate for that term
An annuity is essentially a pure-protection contract in which the insurer pays a lump sum only if the insured dies during the term
question: With reference to annuity contracts offered by life insurers, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: Annuity guards against longevity risk, while term insurance guards against mortality risk
Annuity certain pays for a fixed period regardless of survival
Life annuity with return of purchase price refunds the price to nominees on death
Joint-life annuity continues to the surviving spouse
Pension products from life insurers are regulated by IRDAI
subject: Insurance
summary: Option (a) is correct. A deferred annuity has an accumulation phase and a deferment period before payouts begin, whereas an immediate annuity starts payouts soon after a lump-sum purchase.

detail: In Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984), a PIL concerned bonded labourers in stone quarries near Delhi. The Supreme Court held that the right to live with human dignity under Article 21 includes protection against exploitation, and it read this with Article 23, which prohibits forced labour. The Court directed the identification, release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers, and it relied on the Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976. Olga Tellis concerned the right to livelihood of pavement dwellers as part of Article 21. Vishaka concerned sexual harassment at the workplace. Randhir Singh concerned equal pay for equal work, which the Court derived from Articles 14, 16 and 39(d). Only Bandhua Mukti Morcha is linked to bonded labour.
explanations: Incorrect. Olga Tellis concerned pavement dwellers' right to livelihood as part of Article 21.
Correct. Bandhua Mukti Morcha concerned the release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers under Articles 21 and 23.
Incorrect. Vishaka laid down guidelines on sexual harassment at the workplace.
Incorrect. Randhir Singh concerned equal pay for equal work.
keyfact: Bandhua Mukti Morcha (1984): bonded labour violates Articles 21 and 23.
options: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation
Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
Randhir Singh v. Union of India
question: Which one of the following Supreme Court cases emphasised that the right to live with human dignity under Article 21, read with Article 23, requires the release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers?
related: Bonded Labour System (Abolition) Act, 1976
Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour
Article 39(d) provides for equal pay for equal work for both men and women
Olga Tellis (1985) recognised the right to livelihood under Article 21
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The answer is Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984). The Supreme Court held that bonded labour violates Article 21 and Article 23 and directed identification, release and rehabilitation of bonded labourers.

detail: Knowing authorship of major sources is essential. Kalhana composed the Rajatarangini in Sanskrit verse around 1148-49 CE, a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir often cited as the closest Indian text to critical history writing. Al-Biruni, who came with Mahmud of Ghazni, wrote Tahqiq ma li'l-Hind, commonly called Kitab-ul-Hind. Minhaj-us-Siraj Juzjani wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, covering Islamic history up to 1260 and dedicated to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Mamluk dynasty. Since each pair is accurate, there is no pair to eliminate; the question tests whether students doubt familiar pairs.
explanations: Wrong: more than one pair is correct.
Wrong: all three, not just two, are correct.
Correct: all pairs match their authors.
Wrong: every pair is accurate.
keyfact: Rajatarangini – Kalhana; Tahqiq-i-Hind – Al-Biruni; Tabaqat-i-Nasiri – Minhaj-us-Siraj.
question:
Consider the following pairs:
Medieval text : Author
1. Rajatarangini : Kalhana
2. Tahqiq-i-Hind : Al-Biruni
3. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri : Minhaj-us-Siraj Juzjani
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
related: Ziauddin Barani wrote Tarikh-i-Firuz Shahi.
Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh describing Alauddin Khalji's campaigns.
Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari.
Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin.
Ibn Battuta's Rihla describes the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
subject: Medieval History
summary: All three pairs are correct. Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini on Kashmir, Al-Biruni wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind (Kitab-ul-Hind), and Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.

detail: Annual depreciation = 15% of 2,00,000 = 30,000. Period from 1 April 2023 to 1 October 2025 = 2.5 years, so accumulated depreciation = 75,000. Book value = 1,25,000. Sale proceeds = 1,10,000. On 1 October 2025 it was sold for ₹1,10,000. Depreciation is charged for the period of use in the year of sale. What is the profit or loss on sale?

summary: The correct answer is a profit of ₹8,000... however, check: depreciation of 30,000 per year for 2.5 years is 75,000, leaving a book value of 1,25,000, so sale at 1,10,000 gives a loss of 15,000.

detail: Satavahana kings used metronymics such as Gautamiputra Satakarni and Vasishthiputra Pulumavi, reflecting the importance of mothers. The Jogalthembi hoard in Maharashtra contains Nahapana's silver coins restruck by Gautamiputra Satakarni, evidence of his victory over the Shaka Kshatrapas. The Nasik inscription of his mother Gautami Balashri praises his achievements. However, the Satavahana inscriptions and coin legends were in Prakrit using the Brahmi script, with later bilingual coin legends in Prakrit and Tamil or Telugu. Sanskrit became the dominant inscriptional language only later, notably from the Shaka ruler Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription (c. 150 CE). Hence statement 3 is wrong and only option (b) fits.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is not.
Wrong: statement 1 is correct and statement 3 is not.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect, as Prakrit was the official language.
keyfact: Satavahanas used Prakrit in Brahmi; Gautamiputra restruck Nahapana's coins.
question:
With reference to the Satavahana dynasty, consider the following statements:
1. Satavahana kings were often identified by metronymics, such as Gautamiputra and Vasishthiputra.
2. Gautamiputra Satakarni is known to have restruck the silver coins of the Shaka ruler Nahapana.
3. The official inscriptions of the Satavahanas were composed primarily in classical Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: Gautamiputra Satakarni is said to have destroyed Shaka, Yavana and Pahlava power.
Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription is among the earliest long Sanskrit inscriptions.
Satavahana capital was Pratishthana (Paithan).
Satavahana lead coins were widely issued.
Satavahanas made land grants to Brahmanas and Buddhist monks.
statements: 1 — Correct: metronymics were a distinctive Satavahana practice.
2 — Correct: Nahapana's coins were restruck by Gautamiputra Satakarni.
3 — Incorrect: Satavahana inscriptions were in Prakrit, not Sanskrit.

Facts: Gautami Balashri's Nasik inscription praises her son. The Jogalthembi hoard evidences the restriking. Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription is early Sanskrit. Lead coins were common in Satavahana issues.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; statement 3 is wrong. Satavahana inscriptions were in Prakrit written in Brahmi.

detail: EPS-95 replaced the Family Pension Scheme, 1971 and is administered by the EPFO. Of the employer's 12% contribution, 8.33% of pensionable wages is diverted to the Pension Fund and the rest goes to the EPF account. The Central Government also contributes to the Pension Fund. The employee's 12% goes wholly to the provident fund account, so the employee has no separate direct contribution to the pension fund. The scheme uses a pensionable wage ceiling, which has been Rs 15,000 per month since 2014. Elimination: any option that omits one of the three statements is wrong, because each statement is individually correct, which leaves only the option with all three.
explanations: Incorrect: it omits statement 3, which is correct.
Incorrect: it omits statement 1, which is correct.
Incorrect: it omits statement 2, which is correct.
Correct: all three statements are accurate.
keyfact: EPS-95: employer's 8.33% plus a Central Government share, no direct employee contribution, and a wage ceiling (Rs 15,000).

2. The employee makes no separate direct contribution to the Pension Fund.

summary: All three statements are correct, so the answer is 1, 2 and 3. EPS-95 is financed from the employer's 8.33% share and a Central Government contribution, with no direct employee contribution, and contributions are computed on wages up to a ceiling.

detail: The Government of India Act 1919 provided for a review after ten years, i.e. 1929, but the Conservative government appointed the Indian Statutory Commission in November 1927 under Sir John Simon, with seven British MPs and no Indians. This was seen as an insult to self-respect and denial of the right of Indians to decide their own constitution. Congress at its Madras session (1927) decided to boycott it. During protests at Lahore in 1928, Lala Lajpat Rai was injured by lathi charge and died in November 1928. Elimination: the Commission did not propose partition, nor abolition of the Assembly, and Irwin was Viceroy, not its head.
explanations: Incorrect: the Commission did not propose partition.
Correct: it was all-white and was appointed ahead of the schedule.
Incorrect: its report did not recommend abolishing the Central Legislative Assembly.
Incorrect: it was chaired by Sir John Simon, and Irwin was the Viceroy.

detail: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age to 18 and changed Article 326. The 91st Amendment (2003) inserted Articles 75(1A) and 164(1A). It capped the Council of Ministers at fifteen per cent of the Lok Sabha or Assembly strength. A State with an Assembly of fewer than forty members may have a minimum of twelve ministers. It also tightened the anti-defection law. The 102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Article 338B and gave the National Commission for Backward Classes constitutional status. The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) came through the 42nd Amendment in 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation. The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A. It also protected Articles 20 and 21 from suspension during an Emergency. Pair 4 is therefore the only mismatch.

detail: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was passed under Lord Lytton to curb the Indian-language press, which was criticising the Afghan War policy and the famine administration. detail: Peatlands, such as bogs, fens and tropical peat swamp forests, cover roughly 3% of the world's land but hold about twice the carbon in all forest biomass, according to UNEP assessments. The reason is their waterlogging. Saturated soil has little oxygen, so aerobic decomposers work very slowly. Plant litter therefore accumulates faster than it decays and forms peat layers, which store carbon over thousands of years. If peatlands are drained, burned or cleared, the peat oxidises and releases large amounts of carbon dioxide, and fires can smoulder underground. Peatlands also release some methane when wet, but they remain a net long-term carbon store when intact. Elimination logic: Statement-I is a widely cited fact, and Statement-II is the direct mechanism. Option (b) is wrong because the causal link is direct. Options (c) and (d) are wrong because both statements are true.

keyfact: Peatlands cover a small share of land but store more carbon than all forest biomass, because waterlogging slows decay.

detail: ILO Convention No. 102 of 1952 is the key international instrument laying down minimum standards for social security. It names nine branches: medical care, sickness benefit, unemployment benefit, old-age benefit, employment injury benefit, family benefit, maternity benefit, invalidity benefit and survivors' benefit. A country that ratifies it must accept at least three branches, and at least one of them must be unemployment, old-age, employment injury, invalidity or survivors' benefit. Housing is a welfare and social assistance concern but is not a branch of this convention. For elimination, employment injury, invalidity and survivors' benefits are all classic contingencies of social insurance, so they are in the list. Housing is the odd one out.

keyfact: ILO C102 (1952): nine branches, and housing is not one of them.

detail: Under the mansabdari system, introduced by Akbar, every mansabdar held a dual rank. The zat fixed his personal position in the hierarchy and his salary. The sawar fixed the number of cavalrymen he had to maintain and present for muster. Mansabdars were paid either in cash or by jagirs, and Akbar's system used the dagh (branding) and chehra (descriptive roll) to check the troops. Under later emperors, such as Aurangzeb, the sawar rank could be below, equal to or above the zat, and the system was marked by additional categories like the du-aspa sih-aspa. Elimination: option (a) describes zat, and options (b) and (c) invent requirements not tied to the sawar rank.

Correct: sawar denoted the number of horsemen the mansabdar had to maintain.
keyfact: Zat = personal rank and pay; sawar = number of cavalrymen to be maintained.

summary: The sawar rank indicated the number of cavalrymen (horsemen) a mansabdar had to maintain, so the answer is (d). The zat rank denoted personal status and salary.

detail: A valued policy specifies the agreed value of the subject matter at the start. On a total loss, the insurer pays that agreed value regardless of the actual market value at the time of loss, so it is an exception to the strict measure of indemnity. It is commonly used for marine hulls, antiques, paintings and works of art, whose value is hard to assess after loss. On a partial loss, payment is generally a proportion of the agreed value matching the proportion of damage. An open (unvalued) policy leaves the value to be proved at the time of loss, and the indemnity is the actual loss subject to the sum insured. The valuation is binding unless there is fraud or gross overvaluation amounting to misrepresentation. Option (a) is wrong because the valued policy is an exception to the measure of indemnity. Options (b) and (d) are invented formulas with no basis in insurance law.
explanations: Incorrect. This is the position under an open policy. A valued policy is the exception on total loss.

Correct. The agreed value is payable on total loss, absent fraud or misrepresentation.
Incorrect. Payment of the difference is not provided for. The insurer pays the whole agreed value.
keyfact: Valued policy: agreed value is payable on total loss, whatever the market value, unless there is fraud.

detail: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission, which passes genes vertically. They can also acquire genes horizontally in three ways: conjugation (plasmid transfer through a pilus), transformation (uptake of free DNA from the environment) and transduction (transfer by bacteriophages). Plasmids often carry several resistance genes together, so a single transfer can make a recipient multidrug-resistant. Plasmids can also cross species and even genus boundaries, for example among Enterobacterales. This is why resistance in hospital or environmental bacteria can reach pathogens. Options (b), (c) and (d) fail because both statements are factually sound and causally linked.
