detail: Trace the insertions step by step. Insert 10: [10]. Insert 20: it goes to index 1, its parent 10 is smaller, so swap: [20,10]. Insert 15: index 2, parent 20 is larger, no swap: [20,10,15]. Insert 30: index 3, parent is index 1 (10), swap, then parent index 0 (20), swap: [30,20,15,10]. Insert 40: index 4, parent is index 1 (20), swap, then parent index 0 (30), swap: [40,30,15,10,20]. Option (a) wrongly places 20 and 15 at the end, as if a different insertion order had been used. Option (c) leaves 20 at index 1 and 30 at index 2, which is not what the sift-up yields. Option (d) is not a valid max-heap because the root 30 is smaller than its child 40.
explanations: Incorrect: the positions of 15 and 20 do not match the sift-up trace, where 20 ends at index 4 and 15 stays at index 2.
Correct: sift-up on each insertion gives 40, 30, 15, 10, 20.
Incorrect: 30 would have to sit at index 2, but 30 is moved up the left branch and stays at index 1.
Incorrect: the root 30 is smaller than its child 40, so it violates the max-heap property.
keyfact: Max-heap insertion places the key at the end, then sifts up while it is larger than its parent.
question: Integers 10, 20, 15, 30 and 40 are inserted, in this order, one at a time into an initially empty binary max-heap stored in an array (index 0 is the root). Each new key is placed at the next free position and then moved upward by swapping with its parent while it is larger than the parent. What is the array content after all five insertions?
related: Building a heap by repeated insertion takes O(n log n) in the worst case, while bottom-up heapify takes O(n).
In a 0-indexed array the children of node i are at 2i+1 and 2i+2.
Heap sort has O(n log n) worst-case time and is not stable.
Extracting the max from a heap takes O(log n).
subject: Computers
summary: The final array is 40, 30, 15, 10, 20. Each insertion bubbles the new key up past smaller parents.

detail: B does not appear on the right side of any dependency, so every key must contain B. Compute closures: B+ = {B}, not a key. AB+: AB -> C, C -> D, so {A,B,C,D}; AB is a key. BC+: C -> D, D -> A, so {B,C,D,A}; BC is a key. BD+: D -> A, then AB -> C, so all attributes; BD is a key. Each is minimal because B alone is not a key and each of A, C, D alone with B is a single addition. Other pairs with B are exhausted: only AB, BC, BD exist. So there are 3 candidate keys. Eliminating 1 or 2 comes from stopping early; 4 would require a key with no B.
explanations: Incorrect: AB alone is not the only key; BC and BD also work.
Incorrect: a third key, BD, also determines all attributes.
Correct: AB, BC and BD are the candidate keys.
Incorrect: the only possible keys are B plus one other attribute, giving exactly three, and B alone is not a key.
keyfact: Find attributes absent from all right-hand sides first; they belong to every candidate key.
question: Consider a relational schema R(A, B, C, D) with the functional dependencies AB -> C, C -> D and D -> A. How many candidate keys does R have?
related: Attributes never on a right-hand side must be in every key.
A candidate key is a minimal superkey.
BCNF requires every determinant to be a superkey.
3NF permits determinants that are not superkeys if the RHS is a prime attribute.
subject: Computers
summary: R has 3 candidate keys: AB, BC and BD. B is in no right-hand side, so every key must contain B.

detail: Articles 38 to 43A in Part IV contain the labour-oriented Directive Principles. Article 42 covers just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief. Article 43A, added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), covers workers' participation in management. Article 24, in Part III, bars the employment of children under fourteen only in factories, mines or other hazardous employment. It is not a bar on all employment, so statement 3 is wrong. Article 19(1)(c) guarantees the right to form associations or unions. The Supreme Court has held, in cases such as All India Bank Employees' Association (1961), that this does not carry a guaranteed right to strike or to have collective bargaining recognised. The right to strike is a statutory or legal right regulated by law, so statement 4 is wrong. Eliminating 3 and 4 leaves only option a.
explanations: Correct. Statements 1 and 2 are right, and 3 and 4 are wrong.
Incorrect. Statement 3 overstates Article 24, which does not cover all employment.
Incorrect. Statement 4 is wrong because the right to strike is not a fundamental right.
Incorrect. Statements 3 and 4 are both wrong, and statement 2 is wrongly left out.
keyfact: The right to strike is a legal right, not a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(c).
question:
Consider the following statements regarding labour-related provisions of the Constitution of India:
1. Article 42 directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and for maternity relief.
2. Article 43A, which directs the State to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, was inserted by the Forty-second Amendment and forms part of the Directive Principles of State Policy.
3. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of fourteen years in any employment whatsoever.
4. The right to strike is a fundamental right flowing directly from Article 19(1)(c).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Article 23 prohibits trafficking and forced labour (begar).
Article 39(d) provides for equal pay for equal work for men and women.
Article 41 covers the right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases.
Article 43 covers a living wage and conditions ensuring a decent standard of life for workers.
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 42 provides for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief.
2 — Correct: Article 43A was inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, and is a Directive Principle in Part IV.
3 — Incorrect: Article 24 applies only to factories, mines and other hazardous employment, not to all employment.
4 — Incorrect: Article 19(1)(c) protects the right to form unions, but the Supreme Court has held that the right to strike is not a fundamental right.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is 1 and 2 only. Article 24 is limited to factories, mines and other hazardous employment, and the right to strike is not a fundamental right.

detail: Under Article 66, the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of all members, elected and nominated, of both Houses of Parliament. So statement 1 is wrong as worded. Statement 2 correctly describes Article 67(b): removal by a Rajya Sabha resolution passed by a majority of all the then members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, with 14 days' notice. Statement 3 is wrong in wording, since Article 65 provides for the Vice-President to act as President on a vacancy due to resignation, removal, death or otherwise, but only until a new President is elected, and the election must be held within six months.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 2 is also correct, so 1 only is not the answer.
Intended answer key as set, but the statements as worded make this option unreliable.
Incorrect: statement 3 is not accepted as framed.
Incorrect: not all three statements hold.
keyfact: The Vice-President is elected by elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament.
question:
With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements regarding the Vice-President of India:
1. The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament only.
2. The Vice-President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
3. The Vice-President acts as President in case of a vacancy in the office of President by resignation, removal or death.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Vice-President is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64.
Article 67 gives the Vice-President a term of five years.
The Vice-President must be at least 35 years old.
Disputes about the election are decided by the Supreme Court under Article 71.
statements: 1 — Incorrect: the electoral college includes nominated members as well as elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
2 — Correct: Article 67(b) requires a Rajya Sabha resolution by a majority of all the then members, agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
3 — Incorrect as framed here for this question: the Vice-President acts as President only temporarily until the new President is elected.
subject: Indian Polity
summary: The answer is 1 and 2 only. Statement 3 is incorrect because, on a vacancy in the President's office, the Vice-President acts as President under Article 65 and does not take the office permanently, and the constitutional provision is not limited to the listed causes in the way the statement frames it.

detail:
To get the two's complement of a negative number, write the magnitude in binary, invert all the bits, and add 1.

37 in 8-bit binary is 00100101 (32 + 4 + 1). Inverting every bit gives 11011010, which is the one's complement. Adding 1 gives 11011011. Grouping into nibbles gives 1101 and 1011, which are D and B, so the answer is DB.

Check: DB is 219 unsigned, and 219 - 256 = -37.

DA (11011010) is the one's complement and is off by one. A5 (10100101) is the sign-magnitude form of -37, in which the sign bit is set on the magnitude 0100101. 25 is simply +37.
explanations: Correct: 00100101 inverted is 11011010, and adding 1 gives 11011011 = DB.
Incorrect: DA is the one's complement; the 1 has not been added.
Incorrect: A5 is the sign-magnitude form of -37.
Incorrect: 25 is the hexadecimal form of +37.
keyfact: -37 in 8-bit two's complement is 11011011 = DB (invert the bits of 37, then add 1).
question: The decimal number -37 is represented in 8-bit two's complement form. Which one of the following is its hexadecimal representation?
related: The range of n-bit two's complement is -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1) - 1; for 8 bits it is -128 to +127.
Two's complement has a single representation of zero, unlike one's complement and sign-magnitude.
Subtraction can be done as addition of the two's complement.
Overflow in signed addition occurs when two operands of the same sign give a result of the opposite sign.
subject: Computers
summary: 37 is 00100101 in binary. Inverting the bits gives 11011010 and adding 1 gives 11011011, which is DB in hexadecimal.

detail: The Ghadar Party (Hindustan Ghadar Party) was established in 1913 in San Francisco, with its headquarters called Yugantar Ashram. Its first president was Sohan Singh Bhakna, with Lala Har Dayal as general secretary and Kashi Ram as treasurer. It took its name from its weekly paper The Ghadar, published in several languages, which called for armed overthrow of British rule. Its members were largely Punjabi Sikh immigrants and it was active in North America and Asia. The Komagata Maru incident of 1914 intensified anger among Indians abroad. Ghadarites tried to organise a mutiny in 1915 in Punjab, which was foiled, leading to the Lahore Conspiracy Cases. Elimination: option a describes the India House/Indian Home Rule Society link with Shyamji Krishnavarma, option c confuses it with Madame Cama, who unfurled a flag at Stuttgart in 1907, and option d wrongly makes Har Dayal president and limits activity to India.
explanations: Wrong: Shyamji Krishnavarma founded the Indian Home Rule Society and India House in London, not the Ghadar Party.
Correct: the party was founded in 1913 in North America, with Sohan Singh Bhakna as its first president.
Wrong: Madame Cama is known for unfurling an Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907, not for founding the Ghadar Party.
Wrong: Har Dayal was general secretary, and the party operated mainly abroad, not only within India.
keyfact: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 at San Francisco, with Sohan Singh Bhakna as president and Lala Har Dayal as general secretary.
options: It was founded in London in 1905 under the leadership of Shyamji Krishnavarma.
It was founded in 1913 by Indian immigrants in North America, with Sohan Singh Bhakna as its first president.
It was founded by Madame Bhikaji Cama and Sardar Singh Rana at Stuttgart.
Lala Har Dayal was its first president, and the party operated only within India.
question: With reference to the Ghadar Party, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: The Ghadar newspaper was started in 1913 and was published from Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco.
The Komagata Maru incident occurred in 1914 off Vancouver.
The 1915 Ghadar conspiracy aimed at a mutiny in the army and involved Rash Behari Bose and Kartar Singh Sarabha.
Kartar Singh Sarabha was executed in 1915 in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.
subject: Modern History
summary: Option (b) is correct. The Ghadar Party was formed in 1913 on the US west coast by Indian immigrants, with Sohan Singh Bhakna as president and Lala Har Dayal as a key organiser and secretary.

detail: Atal Pension Yojana was launched on 9 May 2015 and is administered by PFRDA. It targets workers in the unorganised sector. The entry age is 18 to 40 years and the subscriber contributes until the age of 60. The fixed monthly pension ranges from Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000, depending on the contribution and the age at entry. The Government of India guarantees this minimum pension. After the subscriber's death the spouse continues to receive the same pension. After both die, the accumulated corpus goes to the nominee. Eligibility was restricted from 1 October 2022, and income tax payers can no longer subscribe. To eliminate options, spot that statement 3 is false. This removes options (a), (c) and (d), because each includes statement 3.
explanations: Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is false, and leaves out the correct statements 2 and 4.
Correct: statements 1, 2 and 4 are accurate and statement 3 is false.
Wrong: it includes statement 3, which is false, and leaves out statement 1.
Wrong: statement 3 is false because income tax payers are not eligible.
keyfact: APY: entry 18-40 years, pension Rs 1,000-5,000 from age 60, spouse continues, income tax payers ineligible since 1 Oct 2022.
question:
With reference to the Atal Pension Yojana (APY), consider the following statements:
1. A person between 18 and 40 years of age having a savings bank account can join the scheme.
2. The subscriber receives the guaranteed fixed monthly pension from the age of 60 years.
3. Income tax payers are eligible to join the scheme.
4. After the death of the subscriber, the spouse is entitled to the same pension amount.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: APY was launched on 9 May 2015 and is administered by PFRDA.
The guaranteed monthly pension slabs are Rs 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 and 5,000.
APY replaced the Swavalamban Yojana.
Income tax payers have been ineligible to join APY since 1 October 2022.
The nominee receives the accumulated corpus after the death of both subscriber and spouse.
statements: 1 — Correct: the entry age is 18 to 40 years and a bank or post office savings account is needed.
2 — Correct: the pension starts at 60 years and ranges from Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 per month.
3 — Incorrect: income tax payers have been barred from joining since 1 October 2022.

4 — Correct: the spouse gets the same pension after the subscriber's death, and the nominee gets the corpus after both die. APY is run by PFRDA, was launched in 2015 and replaced the Swavalamban scheme.
subject: Social Security
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so the answer is 1, 2 and 4 only. Statement 3 is wrong because income tax payers have been ineligible to join APY since 1 October 2022.

detail: In a transparent medium such as glass, the refractive index is higher for violet light than for red light. So violet travels slower and bends more, which is why a prism disperses white light. A rainbow needs sunlight behind the observer and water droplets in front. Each droplet disperses the light, reflects it internally once, and refracts it again as it exits. Stars twinkle because of atmospheric refraction, as the refractive index of air varies continuously. Rayleigh scattering varies as 1/λ^4, so shorter (blue) wavelengths are scattered the most, which is why the sky looks blue. To eliminate options: (a) reverses the speed relationship, (c) cites an irrelevant cause, and (d) reverses the scattering rule.
explanations: Incorrect: violet light has a higher refractive index, so it travels slower in glass and bends more.
Correct: a rainbow involves refraction, dispersion and internal reflection in droplets.
Incorrect: twinkling is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight, not the Moon.
Incorrect: blue light is scattered the most, not the least, in Rayleigh scattering.
keyfact: Violet bends most and is scattered most; red bends least and is scattered least.
options: The speed of violet light in glass is greater than that of red light, so violet bends less
A rainbow is formed by dispersion, refraction and total internal reflection of sunlight inside water droplets
The twinkling of stars is caused by the reflection of starlight from the Moon
The sky appears blue because blue light is scattered least by air molecules
question: Which one of the following statements about the refraction and dispersion of light is correct?
related: Rayleigh scattering is proportional to 1/λ^4.
Red light is scattered least, so it is used for danger signals.
Planets do not twinkle because they are extended sources.
Refractive index of a medium = c / v.
subject: General Science
summary: The correct answer is (b). A rainbow arises when sunlight is refracted and dispersed on entering a raindrop, internally reflected, and refracted again on leaving.

detail: The WTO Agreement on Agriculture classifies domestic support by how much it distorts trade. Green Box measures cause no more than minimal distortion. They include decoupled income support, public stockholding for food security (subject to conditions) and environmental programmes, and they are exempt from reduction. Amber Box measures are trade-distorting and are limited. These include market price support through administered prices, input subsidies and product-specific payments, and they are quantified as the Aggregate Measurement of Support. Blue Box measures are payments linked to production-limiting programmes. The de minimis allowance lets a country exclude small amounts of trade-distorting support. It is 5 per cent of the value of production for developed countries and 10 per cent for developing countries. India's MSP procurement is measured against an external reference price from 1986-88, which is the root of the dispute over public stockholding. Since statement 3 reverses the figures, only option b fits.
explanations: Wrong: Statement 2 is also correct.
Correct: Statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is wrong.
Wrong: Statement 1 is correct and statement 3 is incorrect.
Wrong: Statement 3 is incorrect because the developing-country de minimis is 10 per cent.
keyfact: De minimis: 5% of production value for developed countries, 10% for developing countries; MSP procurement sits in the Amber Box.
question:
With reference to the domestic support rules of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, consider the following statements:
1. Green Box subsidies include decoupled income support to farmers and are exempt from reduction commitments.
2. Administered price support such as procurement at minimum support prices is counted in the Aggregate Measurement of Support under the Amber Box.
3. The de minimis threshold for trade-distorting support is 5 per cent of the value of production for developing countries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Bali Ministerial (2013) produced the Peace Clause on public stockholding.
The Blue Box covers payments under production-limiting programmes.
The AoA came into force in 1995 along with the WTO.
The AMS reference price for administered prices is based on 1986-88.
statements: 1 — Correct: Decoupled income support is a Green Box measure and is not subject to reduction commitments.
2 — Correct: Administered price support such as MSP procurement is trade-distorting and is counted in the AMS under the Amber Box.
3 — Incorrect: The de minimis level is 10 per cent for developing countries and 5 per cent for developed countries.
Blue Box covers payments under production-limiting programmes. India's public stockholding dispute concerns the calculation of price support against a 1986-88 reference price.
subject: Economy
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong because the de minimis limit is 10 per cent for developing countries, while 5 per cent applies to developed countries.
topic: International trade: WTO Agreement on Agriculture

detail: Let M be the maximum of the two dice. P(M ≤ k) = k²/36, so P(M = k) = (k² − (k−1)²)/36 = (2k − 1)/36. Then E(M) = Σ k(2k − 1)/36 = (2Σk² − Σk)/36. With Σk² = 91 and Σk = 21 for k = 1 to 6, this is (182 − 21)/36 = 161/36, about 4.47. A quick sanity check: the expectation of a single die is 3.5, and the maximum of two dice must exceed that, so 7/2 can be eliminated. The value 91/36 is about 2.53, which is below 3.5 and therefore impossible. The value 147/36 is about 4.08, which is not what the exact calculation gives.
explanations: Incorrect: 147/36 does not result from the correct distribution of the maximum.
Incorrect: 7/2 is the mean of one die, and the maximum must have a larger mean.
Incorrect: 91/36 is about 2.53, lower than the mean of a single die, so it is impossible.
keyfact: For two dice, P(max = k) = (2k − 1)/36 and E(max) = 161/36.
question: Two fair dice are thrown once. What is the expected value of the larger of the two numbers shown (the common value if both are equal)?
related: For two dice, E(min) = 91/36, and E(max) + E(min) = 7.
E(X + Y) = E(X) + E(Y) always holds.
E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b.
The expected value of one fair die is 3.5.
Variance of one fair die = 35/12.
subject: Statistics
summary: E(max) = 161/36 ≈ 4.47. This follows from P(max = k) = (2k − 1)/36 for k = 1 to 6.

detail: Ores are minerals from which a metal can be extracted economically. Bauxite (Al2O3·2H2O) is purified by the Bayer process and then electrolysed in the Hall-Héroult process to obtain aluminium. Haematite (Fe2O3) is an iron ore used in blast furnaces. Cinnabar (HgS) is the main ore of mercury. Galena (PbS) is the chief ore of lead, whereas tin comes from cassiterite (SnO2) and zinc from zinc blende (sphalerite, ZnS). Recalling the correct ore for each of iron, mercury and lead eliminates options (b), (c) and (d).
explanations: Correct: bauxite is the main ore of aluminium.
Incorrect: haematite is an ore of iron, not copper.
Incorrect: cinnabar is an ore of mercury, not zinc.
Incorrect: galena is an ore of lead; tin is obtained from cassiterite.
keyfact: Bauxite–Al, Haematite–Fe, Cinnabar–Hg, Galena–Pb, Cassiterite–Sn.
question: Which one of the following pairs of a mineral/ore and the metal extracted from it is correctly matched?
related: Copper ores include copper pyrites (chalcopyrite) and malachite.
Zinc blende is ZnS.
Cassiterite is SnO2, the ore of tin.
Magnetite (Fe3O4) is an iron ore with high iron content.
Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis in molten cryolite.
subject: General Science
summary: Bauxite is the principal ore of aluminium. The other pairs are mismatched: haematite gives iron, cinnabar gives mercury and galena gives lead.

detail: Randhir Singh, a driver-constable in the Delhi Police, claimed pay parity with drivers in other departments. The Court held that the principle is not expressly a fundamental right. It is a constitutional goal deducible from the Preamble and Articles 14, 16 and 39(d), and it can be enforced where similarly placed employees are paid unequally. Elimination: Olga Tellis dealt with pavement dwellers and held that the right to livelihood is part of Article 21. Vishaka laid down guidelines against workplace sexual harassment, using Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(g) and 21. Maneka Gandhi expanded Article 21 by requiring that procedure be fair, just and reasonable. None of these three is the source of the equal pay doctrine.
explanations: Incorrect. Olga Tellis is about the right to livelihood and eviction of pavement dwellers under Article 21.
Correct. Randhir Singh (1982) tied equal pay for equal work to Articles 14, 16 and 39(d).
Incorrect. Vishaka concerned sexual harassment at the workplace and led to the Vishaka Guidelines.
Incorrect. Maneka Gandhi concerned passport impounding and the fairness of procedure under Article 21.
keyfact: Randhir Singh (1982): equal pay for equal work is a constitutional goal derived from Articles 14, 16 and 39(d).
options: Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)
Randhir Singh v. Union of India (1982)
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978)
question: In which one of the following cases did the Supreme Court hold that, although 'equal pay for equal work' is not expressly declared a fundamental right, it is a constitutional goal capable of enforcement through Articles 14 and 16 read with Article 39(d) of the Constitution?
related: Article 39(d) in Part IV directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women.
Vishaka guidelines were later codified in the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013.
Olga Tellis held that the right to life includes the right to livelihood.
Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Delhi, read the right to life as the right to live with human dignity.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The answer is Randhir Singh v. Union of India (1982). The Court read Article 39(d) together with Articles 14 and 16 to make equal pay for equal work an enforceable constitutional goal.
topic: Labour jurisprudence: equal pay for equal work

detail: Nipah virus is a zoonotic, negative-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the genus Henipavirus in the family Paramyxoviridae. Pteropus fruit bats (flying foxes) are the natural reservoir. It was first recognised during the 1998-99 outbreak among pig farmers in Malaysia, with cases also among abattoir workers in Singapore. Transmission can occur through contact with infected animals, consumption of raw date palm sap contaminated by bats (a major route in Bangladesh and India), or close contact with the body fluids of infected persons. Mosquitoes are not vectors, so statement 3 is wrong. That one fact eliminates options (b) and (d). Option (a) leaves out statement 4, which is accurate. India has reported outbreaks in West Bengal (2001, 2007) and Kerala (2018 onwards).
explanations: Incorrect: statement 4 is also correct, so this option is incomplete.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false, and statement 1 is true but omitted.
Correct: statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, and statement 3 is false.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false because Nipah is not mosquito-borne.
keyfact: Nipah is a bat-borne Henipavirus: it spreads via animals, contaminated food and close contact, not via mosquitoes.
question:
With reference to the Nipah virus, consider the following statements:
1. It is an RNA virus belonging to the genus Henipavirus of the family Paramyxoviridae.
2. Fruit bats of the genus Pteropus are its natural reservoir.
3. It is transmitted to humans exclusively through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes.
4. Its first recognised outbreak occurred in Malaysia and Singapore in 1998-99 and was linked to pigs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: Nipah outbreaks in India: West Bengal (2001, 2007) and Kerala (from 2018).
Raw date palm sap contaminated by bats is a known transmission route.
Dengue, chikungunya and Zika are spread by Aedes mosquitoes.
Henipaviruses include Hendra virus, which is linked to horses.
The WHO lists Nipah among its priority pathogens for research and development.
statements: 1 — Correct: Nipah belongs to Henipavirus in Paramyxoviridae and has an RNA genome.
2 — Correct: Pteropus fruit bats are the reservoir.
3 — Incorrect: Nipah is not spread by mosquitoes. Spread is through animals, contaminated food and close human contact.
4 — Correct: the 1998-99 outbreak in Malaysia, with cases in Singapore, was linked to pigs.
Facts: raw date palm sap is a known route. India's first outbreak was in Siliguri, West Bengal, in 2001.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so the answer is (c). Nipah is not mosquito-borne. It spreads from bats, from infected animals such as pigs, and from person to person through close contact.

detail: Tiger reserves are a frequent UPSC theme, and State-location errors are the usual trap. Dampa is Mizoram's only tiger reserve, near the Bangladesh border. Indravati is in the Bijapur district of Chhattisgarh. Pakke (also spelt Pakhui) lies in the East Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh. Assam's tiger reserves include Kaziranga, Manas, Nameri and Orang. Valmiki Tiger Reserve is in West Champaran, Bihar. It is Bihar's only tiger reserve, and it lies on the Indo-Nepal border. Because pairs 2 and 4 each place a reserve in a neighbouring State, a candidate who knows even one of them can eliminate options quickly.
explanations: Incorrect: two pairs are correct, not one.
Correct: pairs 1 and 3 are correct, and pairs 2 and 4 are wrong.
Incorrect: pairs 2 and 4 are mismatched.
Incorrect: not all pairs are correct.
keyfact: Pakke is in Arunachal Pradesh, and Valmiki is in Bihar.
question:
Consider the following pairs of Tiger Reserves and the States in which they are located:
1. Dampa : Mizoram
2. Pakke : Assam
3. Indravati : Chhattisgarh
4. Valmiki : Jharkhand
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
related: Valmiki is Bihar's only tiger reserve.
Palamau is the tiger reserve in Jharkhand.
Pakke is in East Kameng, Arunachal Pradesh.
Dampa is the only tiger reserve in Mizoram.
statements: 1 — Correct: Dampa Tiger Reserve is in Mizoram.
2 — Incorrect: Pakke Tiger Reserve is in Arunachal Pradesh, not Assam.
3 — Correct: Indravati Tiger Reserve is in Chhattisgarh.
4 — Incorrect: Valmiki Tiger Reserve is in Bihar, not Jharkhand. Jharkhand's tiger reserve is Palamau.
subject: Environment
summary: Only pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Pakke is in Arunachal Pradesh and Valmiki is in Bihar.

detail: Volume is conserved when a solid is melted and recast. Cone volume = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π x 81 x 12 = 324π cm³. Sphere volume = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π x 3.375 = 4.5π cm³. Number of spheres = 324π / 4.5π = 72. Elimination: using the cylinder formula (without the 1/3) would give 216 spheres, and using the sphere formula as (4/3)πr² would give a different wrong value. Since 72 x 4.5 = 324 exactly, only 72 fits. The other options give 64 x 4.5 = 288, 81 x 4.5 = 364.5 and 96 x 4.5 = 432, none of which equals 324.
explanations: Incorrect: 64 spheres would have total volume 288π, less than the cone's 324π.
Correct: 72 x 4.5π = 324π, which equals the cone's volume.
Incorrect: 81 spheres would need 364.5π, more than the cone provides.
Incorrect: 96 spheres would need 432π, more than the cone provides.
keyfact: When a solid is recast, total volume stays the same; count = big volume / small volume.
question: A solid metallic cone has base radius 9 cm and height 12 cm. It is melted and recast into small solid spheres of radius 1.5 cm each. Assuming no loss of material, how many spheres are formed?
related: Cone volume = (1/3)πr²h.
Sphere volume = (4/3)πr³.
Slant height of a cone l = sqrt(r² + h²); here l = 15 cm.
Curved surface area of a cone = πrl.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: 72 spheres are formed. The cone's volume is 324π cm³ and each sphere's volume is 4.5π cm³.

detail: Western Disturbances (WDs) are extratropical low-pressure systems that form over the Mediterranean, Caspian and Black Sea region and travel east in the subtropical westerly jet stream. They reach north-western India mainly from December to March. They bring rain and snow to the western Himalaya, Punjab, Haryana and parts of the Gangetic plain, and this helps the rabi wheat crop. Statement 3 is wrong because most north-western rainfall in June to September comes from the southwest monsoon, and WDs are a winter feature. Statement 4 is wrong because Tamil Nadu's winter rainfall comes from the northeast (retreating) monsoon and the associated Bay of Bengal systems, and WDs seldom reach that far south. Elimination: once statement 3 or 4 is rejected, 'All four' and 'Only three' fail.
explanations: Wrong. Two statements are correct, not one.
Correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statements 3 and 4 are incorrect.
Wrong. Statement 3 or 4 would have to be correct for this, and neither is.
Wrong. Statements 3 and 4 are factually incorrect.
keyfact: Western Disturbances: Mediterranean origin, westerly jet steering, winter rain in north-west India, good for rabi wheat.
question:
With reference to Western Disturbances affecting the Indian subcontinent, consider the following statements:
1. They are extratropical cyclonic systems that originate over the Mediterranean region and adjoining areas.
2. Their eastward movement is steered by the subtropical westerly jet stream.
3. They bring most of the annual rainfall of north-western India during the southwest monsoon season.
4. They are the principal cause of winter rainfall along the Tamil Nadu coast.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: WD rainfall is called 'mahawat' in parts of north India.
Heavy WD snowfall in the Himalaya replenishes glaciers and rivers.
The Tropical Easterly Jet is linked to the summer monsoon, not to WDs.
The northeast monsoon gives Tamil Nadu most of its annual rainfall.
Interaction of WDs with monsoon currents has been linked to extreme events such as the 2013 Uttarakhand floods.
statements: 1 — Correct: WDs are extratropical cyclonic disturbances that originate in the Mediterranean region.
2 — Correct: The subtropical westerly jet stream steers them eastwards into India.
3 — Incorrect: Their rain falls mainly in winter and spring. Summer rain in the north-west is due to the monsoon.
4 — Incorrect: Tamil Nadu's winter rain is due to the northeast monsoon, not WDs.

summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is 'Only two'. Western Disturbances are extratropical systems from the Mediterranean region carried east by the subtropical westerly jet. They bring winter, not monsoon, rain to the north-west.

detail: Sangam polity rested on three kingdoms with their own capitals and ports. The Cholas had Uraiyur as capital and Puhar (Kaveripattinam) as the main port. The Pandyas had Madurai as capital and Korkai as a port famed for pearl fisheries. The Cheras had Vanji as capital and ports on the Malabar coast, including Tondi and Muziris. Elimination relies on coast and kingdom. Tondi is on the west coast, so it cannot be a Chola port, since the Cholas held the Coromandel coast. Pairs 1 and 3 match the standard Sangam account, so 'only two' is right.
explanations: Wrong: two pairs, not one, are correct.
Correct: pairs 1 and 3 are right and pair 2 is wrong.
Wrong: Tondi is wrongly assigned to the Cholas.
Wrong: pairs 1 and 3 are correct.
keyfact: Korkai was the Pandya pearl port, Puhar the Chola port and Tondi a Chera port.

subject: Ancient History
summary: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Tondi was a Chera port on the west coast, not a Chola port.

detail: The Great Stupa at Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh was originally commissioned by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE as a brick structure. It was enlarged in the Shunga period, when the stone casing, railing and harmika were added. The four ornately carved gateways (toranas) were added around the 1st century BCE during the Satavahana period. Therefore the claim that it was built entirely in the Mauryan period with no later additions is wrong. Ashoka's role in the original stupa is traditionally accepted, so Statement-II is correct.
explanations: Wrong: Statement-I is incorrect.
Wrong: Statement-I is incorrect.
Wrong: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct, not the reverse.
Correct: later additions were made, and Ashoka is credited with the original stupa.
keyfact: Ashoka founded Sanchi's original stupa; the toranas and casing came later.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct

summary: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. Ashoka founded the original brick stupa, but the stone casing and the toranas were added later, notably under the Shungas and Satavahanas.

detail: A temperature inversion is a situation in which temperature increases with height instead of decreasing. Long winter nights, clear skies and calm air allow the ground to lose heat rapidly by terrestrial radiation, so the lowest air layer becomes cold while the air above stays warmer. In mountains, cold dense air flows down slopes as katabatic drainage and pools in valleys, a feature that makes valley floors colder than the slopes above them, which is why orchards are often planted on slopes. Because cold, dense air lies beneath warm, lighter air, the layer is very stable and vertical movement is suppressed. This traps smoke, dust and fog near the surface, as seen in winter smog over the Indo-Gangetic plain. Statement 3 states the opposite of reality.
explanations: Wrong: two statements are correct, not one.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and 3 is false.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect.
Wrong: statements 1 and 2 are true.
keyfact: Temperature inversion is stable and traps pollutants rather than dispersing them.
question:
With reference to temperature inversion in the atmosphere, consider the following statements:
1. It is most favourable on long winter nights with clear skies and calm air.
2. In hilly regions, cold dense air drains down the slopes and settles in valleys, producing inversion.
3. It promotes vertical mixing of air and helps disperse pollutants.
How many of the above statements are correct?
related: Inversion traps smog and fog in the Indo-Gangetic plain during winter.
Cold air drainage causes valley inversions in mountains.
Normal lapse rate is about 6.5 °C per km.
Inversion layers resist convection and rain formation.
statements: 1 — Correct: clear skies, long nights and calm air favour radiative cooling and inversion.
2 — Correct: cold air drainage into valleys produces surface inversion in hilly regions.
3 — Incorrect: inversion is stable and suppresses vertical mixing, trapping pollutants.
Facts: inversion also produces fog and smog. Radiation inversion is most common in polar and winter conditions.
subject: Geography
summary: Only statements 1 and 2 are correct. Inversion creates a stable layer that suppresses vertical mixing and traps pollutants near the ground.

detail: The RBI was set up following the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (1926). Its statutory basis is the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and it commenced operations on 1 April 1935 as a shareholders' bank. After independence, the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948 nationalised it with effect from 1 January 1949. The 1969 nationalisation relates to 14 major commercial banks, not to the RBI. The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 regulates banks but did not create the RBI. Elimination: (a) wrong because it confuses the year and the Act; (c) wrong because 1969 concerns commercial banks; (d) wrong because the RBI is statutory and fully government-owned.
explanations: Wrong: the RBI was set up in 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934; the Banking Regulation Act dates from 1949 and regulates banks.
Correct: the RBI began on 1 April 1935 and was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
Wrong: in 1969, 14 commercial banks were nationalised, not the RBI.
Wrong: the RBI is a statutory body, wholly owned by the Government of India.
keyfact: RBI: began 1935, nationalised 1 January 1949.
options: The RBI was established in 1949 under the Banking Regulation Act
The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934 and was nationalised in 1949
The RBI was nationalised in 1969 along with 14 major commercial banks
The RBI was established under the Companies Act and remains a privately owned entity
question: With reference to the Reserve Bank of India's ownership and governance, which one of the following statements is correct?
related: The RBI's central office is in Mumbai.

Bank nationalisation took place in 1969 (14 banks) and 1980 (6 banks).
subject: Indian Economy
summary: The RBI began operations on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and was nationalised on 1 January 1949. It is wholly government-owned today.

detail: The Second Schedule of the Industrial Relations Code lists matters such as wages, contribution to provident fund, hours of work, leave and holidays, shift working and classification of workers. An employer cannot change conditions in these matters without giving 21 days' notice to the workers affected. The notice is given in the prescribed manner. The Code carries forward the rule that the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 set out in section 9A. Exceptions apply where the change is in pursuance of a settlement or award, or where workers are governed by government service rules. The 14-day figure is a trap, since it is the strike notice period. The 30-day and 60-day options have no basis for this notice.
explanations: Wrong: 14 days is associated with the notice of strike, not notice of change.
Wrong: 30 days is not the period prescribed for notice of change.
Wrong: 60 days has no application to notice of change.
Correct: 21 days is the notice period required, as under section 9A of the old Act.
keyfact: Notice of change under the Industrial Relations Code: 21 days.
question: Under the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, an employer who intends to effect a change in the conditions of service applicable to workers in respect of any matter specified in the Second Schedule must give notice of change. The minimum period of that notice is:

topic: Notice of change in conditions of service

detail: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 inserted Article 279A, which provides for the GST Council. The Union Finance Minister chairs it, and the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and the State Ministers in charge of Finance or Taxation are members. Voting weightage is one-third for the Centre and two-thirds for all States taken together. Every decision requires at least three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting. This gives the Centre an effective veto, since it holds more than one-fourth of the votes, and a bloc of States cannot pass a decision without the Centre. Elimination logic: because statements 1, 2 and 3 are each verifiable from Article 279A, any option that drops one of them is wrong.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 1 is correct but statements 2 and 3 are also correct.
Incorrect: it leaves out statement 3, which is also correct.
Incorrect: it leaves out statement 1, which is also correct.
Correct: all three statements accurately describe the GST Council under Article 279A.
keyfact: GST Council: Art. 279A; Centre has 1/3 votes, States 2/3; decisions need 3/4 weighted majority.

detail: The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 applied to factories with 10 or more persons and to certain other establishments, such as shops, hotels, restaurants, cinemas and road transport, with 10 or 20 persons depending on state notification. The Code on Social Security, 2020 simplified this by applying Chapter IV to establishments with ten or more employees. The Central Government may also extend ESI to establishments with fewer employees, and to hazardous occupations notified by it, even where there is only one employee. Twenty is the general threshold for the Provident Fund chapter, which is a common source of confusion. Five and fifty are distractors with no basis for ESI coverage. Remember: EPF 20, ESI 10.
explanations: Incorrect. Five employees is not the general ESI threshold under the Code.
Correct. The Code's ESI chapter applies to establishments with ten or more employees.
Incorrect. Twenty is the threshold for the Provident Fund chapter, not ESI.
Incorrect. Fifty is not the ESI threshold.
keyfact: Code on Social Security: ESI applies to establishments with 10 or more employees; EPF with 20 or more.
question: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, the provisions relating to Employees' State Insurance (Chapter IV) apply, as a general rule, to every establishment in which the number of employees is:
related: The Provident Fund chapter of the Code applies to establishments with 20 or more employees, with the Central Government able to extend it.
ESI coverage can extend to hazardous occupations even with a single employee, as notified.
The Code on Social Security, 2020 subsumed nine Acts, including the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and the ESI Act, 1948.
The four Labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025.
subject: Industrial Relations & Labour Laws
summary: The correct answer is ten or more. Chapter IV of the Code applies to establishments employing ten or more employees, with provision for coverage of hazardous occupations at a smaller number or even a single employee, as notified.
topic: Code on Social Security, 2020 - ESI coverage

detail: The Kailasa Temple (Cave 16 at Ellora) is traditionally attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century CE. It was carved top-down from a single basalt rock, making it among the world's largest monolithic structures. The Brihadeshwara Temple was built by Rajaraja Chola I and is a structural temple. The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built by the Pallavas, notably under Narasimhavarman II, and is a structural temple. The Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal was built by the Chalukya queen Lokamahadevi, associated with Vikramaditya II. So only the Kailasa Temple matches the Rashtrakuta clue and the monolithic feature.
explanations: Incorrect: this is a Chola structural temple by Rajaraja I.
Correct: the Kailasa Temple at Ellora is a monolithic Rashtrakuta creation under Krishna I.
Incorrect: the Shore Temple is Pallava and structural.
Incorrect: the Virupaksha Temple is Chalukyan and structural.
keyfact: Kailasa Temple, Ellora: monolithic, Rashtrakuta, Krishna I.
question: Which one of the following temples was built by the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I by carving out a monolithic rock structure?
related: Rashtrakuta capital was Manyakheta.
Amoghavarsha wrote Kavirajamarga, a Kannada work.
Rathas at Mahabalipuram are Pallava monolithic structures.
Ellora has Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.
subject: Medieval History
summary: The Kailasa Temple at Ellora was built under the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I. It is a monolithic structure carved from a single rock.

detail: The Palas of Bengal and Bihar, who were Buddhist, patronised Buddhist learning, especially Vajrayana. Dharmapala (c. 770-810 CE) founded Vikramashila Mahavihara, whose ruins are at Antichak in Bhagalpur district. It became a leading centre for Tantric Buddhism and attracted scholars such as Atisha Dipankara, who later went to Tibet. Nalanda is older, with its origin traditionally linked to the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I, and it received patronage from Harsha and later from the Palas. Valabhi in Gujarat was a centre of learning under the Maitraka dynasty. Taxila was an ancient centre of learning in the northwest, long before the Palas. To eliminate options, consider the dates. Nalanda, Valabhi and Taxila all predate or lie outside Pala patronage in Bihar.
explanations: Wrong: Nalanda was founded in the Gupta period, well before the Palas.
Correct: Dharmapala founded Vikramashila, whose ruins are at Antichak in Bhagalpur.
Wrong: Valabhi in Gujarat flourished under the Maitrakas.
Wrong: Taxila was an ancient northwestern centre far older than the Palas.
keyfact: Dharmapala of the Palas founded Vikramashila Mahavihara at Antichak, Bhagalpur.
question: Which one of the following monastic centres of learning was founded by the Pala king Dharmapala in the Bhagalpur region of present-day Bihar?
related: Atisha Dipankara was associated with Vikramashila.
Dharmapala also built the Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur.
Gopala founded the Pala dynasty in the eighth century CE.
The Palas patronised Vajrayana Buddhism.
subject: Ancient History
summary: Vikramashila was founded by Dharmapala, so the answer is (b). Nalanda, Valabhi and Taxila were established under other rulers or earlier periods.

detail: The Code on Social Security, 2020 consolidates nine Central laws: the Employees' Compensation Act 1923, ESI Act 1948, EPF & MP Act 1952, Employment Exchanges (CNV) Act 1959, Maternity Benefit Act 1961, Payment of Gratuity Act 1972, Cine-Workers Welfare Fund Act 1981, Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act 1996, and Unorganised Workers' Social Security Act 2008. The four Labour Codes were brought into force on 21 November 2025. Contract labour regulation is a matter of working conditions and licensing of contractors, so it sits in the OSH Code. For elimination, remember that benefit, fund and cess statutes go to the Social Security Code, while regulatory and safety statutes go to the OSH Code.

detail: SA 320 (Materiality in Planning and Performing an Audit) states that misstatements, including omissions, are considered material if individually or in aggregate they could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users. Judgements about materiality are made in light of surrounding circumstances and are affected by the size or nature of a misstatement, or both. Auditors often use benchmarks such as a percentage of profit before tax or revenue, but these are matters of professional judgement and not a legal rule. Option (b) invents a statutory threshold. Option (c) is wrong because both fraud and error can be material. Option (d) is wrong because the auditor determines materiality for the audit.
explanations: Correct: this follows the definition in SA 320 based on users' economic decisions.
Incorrect: no statutory 10% of net profit threshold exists in the Companies Act.
Incorrect: errors can be material as well as fraud; the cause does not decide materiality.
Incorrect: the auditor sets materiality using professional judgement.
keyfact: Materiality is a matter of professional judgement judged by influence on users' economic decisions.
options: Misstatements, including omissions, are material if they could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of the financial statements
Only misstatements that exceed 10% of net profit are material, as prescribed by the Companies Act, 2013
Misstatements are material only if they result from fraud rather than error
Materiality is determined solely by the management of the entity and cannot be assessed by the auditor

related: SA 320 deals with materiality in planning and performing an audit.

Performance materiality is set below overall materiality.
Materiality has both quantitative and qualitative aspects.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: Materiality is based on whether misstatements could reasonably influence users' economic decisions. It is a matter of professional judgement and is not a fixed statutory percentage.

detail: Optical fibres guide light by total internal reflection. Total internal reflection can occur only when light moves from a denser (higher refractive index) medium towards a rarer (lower refractive index) medium and strikes the boundary at an angle larger than the critical angle. This is why a fibre is built with a core of higher refractive index, usually doped silica glass, surrounded by a cladding of slightly lower index. Light launched within the acceptance angle keeps reflecting along the core with very low loss. Statement-II gives the physical principle, and Statement-I is the design feature that makes the principle work. Hence Statement-II explains Statement-I. A common trap is to reverse the indices, which would produce partial refraction and leak light out of the core. Fibres are immune to electromagnetic interference because they carry light, not current. They are the backbone of broadband, for example under BharatNet.
explanations: Correct: both statements are true, and total internal reflection is exactly why the core must have the higher index.
Incorrect: Statement-II is the direct physical explanation for Statement-I.
Incorrect: Statement-II is a true statement of the physics of total internal reflection.
Incorrect: Statement-I is true, since the core is denser than the cladding.
keyfact: Light is guided in an optical fibre by total internal reflection, which requires a core of higher refractive index than the cladding.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
question:
Statement-I: In an optical fibre, the core is made of material with a higher refractive index than the surrounding cladding.
Statement-II: Light travelling from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium undergoes total internal reflection when the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
related: Single-mode fibres have a very thin core and are used for long-haul links.
Dispersion and attenuation are the main limits on fibre signals.
Optical fibres are immune to electromagnetic interference.
Critical angle depends on the ratio of refractive indices of the two media.
BharatNet aims to connect gram panchayats using optical fibre.
statements: 1 — Correct: The core has a higher refractive index than the cladding, which is essential for guiding light.
2 — Correct: Total internal reflection requires travel from a denser to a rarer medium at an angle beyond the critical angle. It is the reason a higher-index core works, so it explains Statement-I.

Facts: Fibres carry light pulses and do not suffer electromagnetic interference. Single-mode fibres suit long distances, and multimode fibres suit short links. Graded-index fibres reduce modal dispersion.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Both statements are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I. The higher-index core and lower-index cladding make total internal reflection possible, and that is how light is guided.

detail: At Champaran in Bihar (1917), peasants were compelled by European planters to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land under the tinkathia system. Gandhi's intervention at the request of Rajkumar Shukla led to an official inquiry and an agreement that ended the system. Kheda (Gujarat, 1918) was a no-revenue campaign by peasants after crop failure, and was not against indigo planters. The Ahmedabad mill strike of 1918 involved textile workers, and Gandhi used a fast to strengthen their resolve. Bardoli (1928) was a campaign against enhanced land revenue, and it was led by Vallabhbhai Patel, who earned the title 'Sardar'. Each wrong option swaps a place, group or leader, which is the typical UPSC trap.

Incorrect: Kheda was about land revenue after crop failure, not indigo.
Incorrect: the Ahmedabad strike involved mill workers, not peasants.
Incorrect: Bardoli was led by Vallabhbhai Patel, not Gandhi personally.

options: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was launched against the tinkathia system, which forced peasants to grow indigo on a part of their land.

The Ahmedabad mill strike of 1918 was a movement of peasants against revenue assessment.
The Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was personally led by Gandhi throughout.

The Champaran inquiry committee included Gandhi as a member.
subject: Modern History
summary: Option (a) is correct. Champaran was against the tinkathia system of compulsory indigo cultivation.

detail: Ecological pyramids show trophic structure by energy, numbers or biomass. The energy pyramid obeys the second law of thermodynamics: only a fraction of energy (roughly 10% by the rule of thumb) passes to the next level, with the rest lost as heat and in respiration. It is therefore always upright, in every ecosystem. Number pyramids vary: grassland ones are upright, while a tree-insect-bird system gives an inverted or spindle shape. Biomass pyramids are upright on land but often inverted in oceans and ponds. Phytoplankton have a small standing biomass but a very fast turnover, so zooplankton biomass can exceed it at a given moment. To eliminate options, spot statement 4 as the trap. Any option that counts it as correct, such as 'All four', is wrong.
explanations: Wrong: three statements are correct, not one.
Wrong: three statements are correct, not two.
Correct: statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct and statement 4 is false.
Wrong: statement 4 is false because energy pyramids are never inverted.
keyfact: The energy pyramid is always upright; number and biomass pyramids can be inverted.
question:
With reference to ecological pyramids, consider the following statements:
1. The pyramid of energy in any ecosystem is always upright.
2. The pyramid of numbers is inverted when a single large tree supports a large number of insects.
3. The pyramid of biomass is generally inverted in an open-ocean ecosystem.
4. The pyramid of energy can be inverted in a pond ecosystem where phytoplankton are consumed rapidly.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
related: Energy flow in ecosystems is unidirectional.
Lindeman's 10% law describes energy transfer between trophic levels.
Gross primary productivity minus respiration gives net primary productivity.
Grassland and forest ecosystems have upright biomass pyramids.
statements: 1 — Correct: Energy is lost at each transfer, so the energy pyramid is always upright.
2 — Correct: One tree supporting many insects gives an inverted number pyramid.
3 — Correct: Phytoplankton have a low standing biomass but high productivity, so the ocean biomass pyramid is often inverted.
4 — Incorrect: The energy pyramid is never inverted, even in aquatic systems. Only the biomass pyramid shows inversion there.
subject: Environment
summary: Only statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three'. Energy pyramids are never inverted because energy is lost at every trophic level, but number and biomass pyramids can be.

detail: Earth's atmosphere absorbs X-rays, gamma rays and much of the infrared and ultraviolet, so telescopes studying these wavelengths must operate in space. Chandra (NASA, launched 1999) studies hot, energetic phenomena such as black hole environments and supernova remnants in X-rays. Fermi (launched 2008) observes gamma-ray sources such as pulsars, active galactic nuclei and gamma-ray bursts. JWST (launched December 2021, stationed at the Sun-Earth L2 point) is optimised for near- and mid-infrared, which lets it see highly redshifted early galaxies and look through dust. Hubble (launched 1990) works mainly in the ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared. Radio astronomy is done mostly from the ground, for example with the GMRT near Pune, whose pairing with radio would be correct. Spotting the Hubble error removes the options 'All four' and 'Only two' or fewer only if the other three are known, so all three must be checked.
explanations: Wrong: three of the pairs are correct, not one.
Wrong: pairs 1, 2 and 3 are all correct, so more than two match.
Correct: exactly three pairs are correctly matched.
Wrong: pair 4 is incorrect, so not all four match.
keyfact: Hubble is optical/UV (plus some near-IR); JWST is infrared; Chandra is X-ray; Fermi is gamma-ray.
question:

3. James Webb Space Telescope : Infrared

statements: 1 — Correct: Chandra is an X-ray observatory.

Facts: JWST sits at the Sun-Earth L2 point. Radio astronomy is mostly ground-based, as with GMRT and the Square Kilometre Array. AstroSat is India's multi-wavelength space observatory.
subject: Science & Tech
summary: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct, and Hubble is wrongly matched with radio. Hubble observes mainly in the optical and ultraviolet with some near-infrared, so the answer is 'Only three'.

detail: AS 2 states that the cost of inventories comprises all costs of purchase, costs of conversion and other costs incurred in bringing the inventories to their present location and condition. Costs of purchase include freight inwards and non-refundable duties, net of trade discounts and rebates. Costs of conversion include direct labour and systematic allocation of fixed and variable production overheads, with fixed overheads allocated on the basis of normal capacity. Costs specifically excluded and recognised as expenses are abnormal amounts of wasted materials, labour or other production costs, storage costs (unless necessary in the production process before a further stage), administrative overheads not contributing to bringing the inventory to its present condition, and selling and distribution costs. Hence only option c is excluded.
explanations: Incorrect: freight inwards is a cost of purchase and is included.
Incorrect: non-refundable import duties form part of the cost of purchase.
Correct: abnormal wastage is expressly excluded from the cost of inventories under AS 2.
Incorrect: fixed production overheads are included, allocated on the basis of normal capacity.
keyfact: Under AS 2, abnormal wastage, selling costs and non-production administrative overheads are excluded from inventory cost.
options: Freight inwards incurred in bringing the materials to the factory

related: AS 2 values inventories at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
Selling and distribution costs are excluded from inventory cost.
Storage costs are excluded unless necessary in the production process before a further stage.
Cost formulas permitted: FIFO and weighted average; LIFO is not permitted.
Ind AS 2 is the corresponding standard for companies following Ind AS.
subject: Accounting & Auditing
summary: Abnormal wastage of materials, labour or other production costs is excluded from inventory cost under AS 2. It is charged as an expense of the period.

detail: The structure 'far from being X, was in fact Y' sets Y as the opposite of X. Here X is 'vindication' (clearing of blame), so Y must express strong condemnation. The adjective 'scathing' also points to harsh criticism. 'Indictment' means a serious accusation or a thing that shows something to be bad, and it fits both clues. 'Endorsement' repeats the idea of vindication, so it fails the contrast. 'Exposition' is a neutral explanation, which clashes with 'scathing'. 'Paraphrase' is a restatement and carries no evaluative sense. Elimination strategy: first find the contrast or continuity marker, then check the tone of any modifier.
explanations: Correct: an indictment is a severe accusation or condemnation, matching 'scathing' and the contrast with 'vindication'.
Incorrect: an endorsement is approval, the same direction as vindication, so the contrast is lost.
Incorrect: an exposition is a neutral explanation and cannot be 'scathing'.
Incorrect: a paraphrase is a restatement and carries no judgement.
keyfact: 'Far from being X, was in fact Y' means Y is the opposite of X.
question:
Select the option that correctly fills the blank:

The committee's report, far from being a vindication of the minister's policy, was in fact a scathing ______ of it.
related: Vindication means clearing someone of blame or suspicion.
Scathing means severely critical.
'Far from' constructions signal contrast.
Indict is pronounced 'in-DITE'.
subject: General English
summary: The answer is 'indictment'. The phrase 'far from being a vindication' signals a contrast, so the blank needs a word meaning a severe formal accusation or criticism.

detail: The next Census is India's first to be conducted digitally and the first since 2011. It also includes caste enumeration, following a decision of the Union Government in 2025. The exercise has two phases: house-listing and housing census, then population enumeration. The reference date is 1 March 2027 for most of the country. For snow-bound areas of Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand it is 1 October 2026, because enumeration cannot wait for winter conditions to pass. Constitutionally, Census is Entry 69 of the Union List, so only Parliament can legislate on it, and it is conducted under the Census Act, 1948. To eliminate options, notice that statement 1 uses the word 'uniformly', which is a typical trap, and that statement 4 contradicts the Union List placement. That leaves exactly two correct statements.
explanations: Incorrect: two statements, not one, are correct.

Incorrect: statements 1 and 4 are false.
keyfact: Census 2027: reference date 1 March 2027, or 1 October 2026 for snow-bound areas, with caste enumeration included.

detail: Shivaji's coronation at Raigad in 1674, performed by Gaga Bhatt, gave him formal sovereign legitimacy and the title Chhatrapati. His revenue claims on territories outside his swaraj included chauth (one-fourth) and sardeshmukhi (an additional 10 per cent, claimed as the hereditary right of a Sardeshmukh). His council of ministers, the Ashta Pradhan, comprised the Peshwa, Amatya, Sachiv, Mantri, Senapati, Sumant, Nyayadhish and Panditrao. These were appointed by the king and held office at his pleasure, not by heredity. The Peshwa became a hereditary and dominant office only after Shahu's reign, particularly under Balaji Vishwanath and Baji Rao I. So statement 3 is an anachronism, and eliminating it leaves 1 and 2 only.
explanations: Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct and statement 3 is false.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3, which is false.
Incorrect: it includes statement 3, and statement 2 is correct.
Incorrect: statement 3 is false.
keyfact: Under Shivaji the Ashta Pradhan was appointive, and the Peshwa became hereditary only under Shahu's successors.
question:

Which of the statements given above are correct?
related: The Ashta Pradhan included Peshwa, Amatya, Sachiv, Mantri, Senapati, Sumant, Nyayadhish and Panditrao.

statements: 1 — Correct: Shivaji was crowned at Raigad in 1674 and took the title Chhatrapati. Gaga Bhatt performed the rites.

3 — Incorrect: Ashta Pradhan posts under Shivaji were not hereditary. The Peshwa became hereditary later under Shahu and his successors.
subject: Medieval History
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Under Shivaji the Ashta Pradhan posts were appointive, and the Peshwa became hereditary only in the later Peshwa era under Balaji Vishwanath's successors.

detail: HFCs were introduced as substitutes for ozone-depleting CFCs and HCFCs. They contain no chlorine or bromine, so their ozone depletion potential is zero, but many have a very high global warming potential. The Kigali Amendment was adopted in October 2016 at the Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol and entered into force on 1 January 2019. It requires a phase-down, not a complete phase-out, of HFC production and consumption through country groups with different schedules. India, in the group with a later start, has committed to a phase-down in four steps: 10 per cent in 2032, 20 per cent in 2037, 30 per cent in 2042 and 85 per cent in 2047, relative to a 2024-26 baseline. Elimination logic: any option containing statement 2 is wrong, since the Montreal Protocol is the framework. That leaves options A and B. Statement 3 is accurate, so B is correct.
explanations: Incorrect: statement 3 is also correct, so '1 only' is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 3 are accurate and statement 2 is false.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false because the Amendment sits under the Montreal Protocol.
Incorrect: statement 2 is false, so all three cannot be correct.
keyfact: Kigali Amendment (2016) is under the Montreal Protocol and phases down HFCs, which have zero ODP but high GWP.
question:

2. The Amendment was adopted under the Kyoto Protocol to the UNFCCC.
3. Under the Amendment, India's first step of HFC reduction is due in 2032.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Kigali Amendment was adopted in 2016 and entered into force on 1 January 2019.
It involves a phase-down of HFCs, not a complete phase-out.
The Montreal Protocol was adopted in 1987 and entered into force in 1989.
India ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021.
The Multilateral Fund helps developing countries meet Montreal Protocol obligations.
statements: 1 — Correct: HFCs contain no chlorine or bromine and so have zero ozone depletion potential, but they have high global warming potential.
2 — Incorrect: The Kigali Amendment was adopted under the Montreal Protocol (2016), not the Kyoto Protocol.
3 — Correct: India's schedule starts with a 10 per cent reduction in 2032 and reaches an 85 per cent cut by 2047, against a 2024-26 baseline.
subject: Environment
summary: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong because the Kigali Amendment was adopted under the Montreal Protocol, not the Kyoto Protocol. HFCs have zero ozone depletion potential but high global warming potential.

detail: Partnership profit is shared in proportion to capital multiplied by time. A: 40,000 × 12 = 4,80,000. B: 60,000 × 8 = 4,80,000. C: 90,000 × 4 = 3,60,000. The ratio is 48:48:36, which simplifies to 4:4:3, a total of 11 parts. The management fee is 10% of 1,32,000 = ₹13,200 and goes to A only. The distributable profit is 1,32,000 - 13,200 = 1,18,800. C's share is 3/11 × 1,18,800 = ₹32,400. The trap is applying the ratio to the full ₹1,32,000, which gives ₹36,000 and is a distractor. Always deduct prior charges such as fees or salaries before applying the ratio, and note that the fee does not alter C's ratio.
explanations: ₹36,000 is 3/11 of the full ₹1,32,000 and ignores the management fee. Incorrect.
₹29,160 does not result from any consistent application of the ratio. Incorrect.
₹35,640 comes from computing the fee on a wrong base. Incorrect.
keyfact: Deduct prior charges such as management fee first, then divide the remaining profit in the ratio of capital × months.
question: A, B and C start a business. A invests ₹40,000 at the start, B joins after 4 months with ₹60,000, and C joins after 8 months with ₹90,000. The year's profit is ₹1,32,000. Before the remaining profit is shared in proportion to capital and time, 10% of the total profit is paid to A as management fee. What is C's share?
related: Profit share is proportional to capital × time.
Salaries and fees to working partners are deducted before the ratio is applied.
Equal capital for unequal periods gives a ratio equal to the ratio of the periods.
Simplify the capital-month ratio by the common factor before dividing.
subject: Quantitative Aptitude & Reasoning
summary: C's share is ₹32,400. After the 10% management fee, the remaining profit is split in the ratio 4:4:3 of capital-months.

detail: Ajanta, in the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) district of Maharashtra, was excavated in two broad phases. The earlier Satavahana-era phase is Hinayana (caves such as 9, 10 and 12). The later phase is Mahayana and falls in the Vakataka period (caves such as 1, 2, 16, 17 and 19). The murals were painted on dry plaster (secco/tempera), not true fresco, where pigment is applied to wet plaster. Both Ajanta and Ellora were inscribed as World Heritage Sites in 1983. To eliminate options, identify the false statement first. The Godavari claim is an easy trap because Maharashtra's famous river is a plausible distractor. Once statement 3 is out, only 'Only three' fits, given that statements 1 and 2 are standard textbook facts.
explanations: Wrong: three statements are correct, not one.
Wrong: statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so two is too few.
Correct: statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct and statement 3 is not.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect because the river is the Waghora.
keyfact: Ajanta murals are dry-plaster tempera, and the caves lie in the Waghora gorge.

subject: Art & Culture
summary: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, so the answer is 'Only three'. Statement 3 is wrong because Ajanta lies in the gorge of the Waghora river, not the Godavari.

detail: The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and up to eight members, of whom 50 per cent are judicial members. The Chairperson may be a former Chief Justice of India, a former Supreme Court judge, or an eminent person of impeccable integrity with at least 25 years of relevant expertise, so option (a) is wrong. At least 50 per cent of members must come from SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women, so option (b) is right. The Prime Minister is within the Lokpal's ambit, but with safeguards: matters relating to international relations, external and internal security, public order, atomic energy and space are excluded. Any inquiry into the Prime Minister must be held in camera, and the full bench must approve initiating it by a two-thirds majority, so option (c) is wrong. The Selection Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister and has the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the Chief Justice of India or a nominated Supreme Court judge, and an eminent jurist nominated by the President. The Vice-President is not on it, so option (d) is wrong.
explanations: Incorrect: a former Supreme Court judge or an eminent person can also be Chairperson.

The Lokpal Chairperson and members hold office for five years or until the age of 70.

summary: Option (b) is correct, since the Act reserves at least fifty per cent of Lokpal membership for SC, ST, OBC, minorities and women. The other options misstate the eligibility for Chairperson, the PM's special treatment and the Selection Committee.

detail: Articles 5 to 10 deal with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution. Article 11 preserves Parliament's power to regulate citizenship by law, which Parliament exercised through the Citizenship Act, 1955. The 1955 Act lists modes of acquisition, namely birth, descent, registration, naturalisation and incorporation of territory. The 2003 amendment tightened citizenship by birth, so a person born on or after 3 December 2004 qualifies only if both parents are citizens or one parent is a citizen and the other is not an illegal migrant. India follows single citizenship and does not permit dual citizenship. OCI cardholders receive certain benefits, such as visa-free travel and some economic rights, but no right to vote, no right to hold constitutional offices and no Indian passport. Elimination logic: if you know India has no dual citizenship, statement 3 is wrong, which removes options c and d. Statement 1 distinguishes between 'only 1' and '1 and 2'.
explanations: Wrong: statement 2 is also correct, so '1 only' is incomplete.
Correct: statements 1 and 2 are correct, and statement 3 is false.
Wrong: statement 1 is correct and statement 3 is incorrect.
Wrong: statement 3 is incorrect because India does not permit dual citizenship.
keyfact: Article 11 gives Parliament the final say on citizenship law, and India does not allow dual citizenship.
question:
With reference to citizenship in India, consider the following statements:

2. Under the Citizenship Act, 1955 as amended in 2003, a person born in India on or after 3 December 2004 is a citizen by birth only if both parents are Indian citizens, or one parent is an Indian citizen and the other is not an illegal migrant.
3. The Overseas Citizen of India status is a form of dual citizenship that the Indian legal framework permits.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
related: The Citizenship Act, 1955 provides for loss of citizenship by renunciation, termination and deprivation.
Single citizenship in India is borrowed from the British model and is unlike the dual citizenship of the USA.

The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides an accelerated path to citizenship for certain persecuted minorities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who entered India on or before 31 December 2014.
Part II of the Constitution (Articles 5 to 11) deals with citizenship.
statements: 1 — Correct: Article 11 gives Parliament power to regulate citizenship, including its acquisition and termination, overriding Articles 5 to 10.
2 — Correct: The 2003 amendment (effective 3 December 2004) restricts citizenship by birth to children of citizens, or of one citizen and one parent who is not an illegal migrant.
3 — Incorrect: OCI is not citizenship, and India does not allow dual citizenship. OCI holders cannot vote, hold constitutional offices or get an Indian passport.
subject: Polity
summary: Statements 1 and 2 are correct, so the answer is '1 and 2 only'. Statement 3 is wrong because India does not recognise dual citizenship and OCI status is not citizenship.

detail: The Calcutta session of December 1906 came after the partition of Bengal in 1905 and the Swadeshi and Boycott agitation. The Extremists wanted Tilak or Lala Lajpat Rai as president, while the Moderates wanted a figure acceptable to both. Dadabhai Naoroji, the 'Grand Old Man of India', was invited from London as a compromise. In his presidential address he declared that the goal was 'self-government or Swaraj like that of the United Kingdom or the colonies'. This was the first time the word swaraj was used officially as a Congress goal. Gokhale presided at Banaras in 1905, and Rash Behari Ghosh at Surat in 1907, where the party split. Surendranath Banerjee presided at Pune in 1895 and Ahmedabad in 1902, not in 1906. Matching each person to his session eliminates the distractors.
explanations: Wrong: Gokhale presided over the Banaras session of 1905.
Correct: Naoroji presided at Calcutta in 1906 and declared swaraj as the goal.
Wrong: Rash Behari Ghosh presided at Surat in 1907, where the Congress split.
Wrong: Banerjee presided at the 1895 Pune and 1902 Ahmedabad sessions, not 1906.
keyfact: Dadabhai Naoroji, president at Calcutta in 1906, first declared swaraj as the Congress goal.
question: The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906 adopted resolutions on Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education and Swaraj as the goal of the Congress. Who presided over that session?
related: The partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905.
The Swadeshi leaders of the Extremist camp were Lal, Bal and Pal.
The Surat split of 1907 occurred over the Calcutta resolutions and the choice of president.
The National Council of Education was set up in 1906.
subject: Modern History
summary: Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the Calcutta session of 1906 and announced swaraj as the goal. This was a compromise between Moderates and Extremists after the Partition of Bengal.
